34.tq: Test a complete constitutional list while avoiding substitution of a neighbouring office.
34.sec: Charged vs voted expenditure  [APPSC]

34.s: Which grant is intended to meet an advance requirement for only part of a financial year until the Appropriation Act is passed?
34.x: A vote on account provides an advance for a part of the year, generally about two months or one-sixth of the year, until the Appropriation Act is passed.
34.tq: Match the grant with its immediate temporary purpose.
34.sec: Vote on account, vote of credit, exceptional, supplementary and excess grants  [APPSC]

34.s:
Consider the following statements about a vote on account:
1. It is provided under Article 116.
2. It generally covers about two months or one-sixth of the year.
3. In election years, it may cover three to five months.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
34.x: All three statements are correct. A vote on account is an advance for part of the year and may cover a longer period in an election year.
34.tq: Check article, duration and election-year variation together.
34.sec: Vote on account, vote of credit, exceptional, supplementary and excess grants  [APPSC]

34.s: A demand of an unexpected nature and indefinite magnitude is met through a:
34.x: A vote of credit under Article 116 is granted for an unexpected demand whose magnitude or character cannot be stated in detail.
34.tq: Distinguish an indefinite emergency demand from an inadequacy in an existing grant.
34.sec: Vote on account, vote of credit, exceptional, supplementary and excess grants  [APPSC]

34.s: An exceptional grant is one which:
o: Provides an advance for the first two months of the year
Is not part of the current service of any year
Is sanctioned after expenditure has exceeded the grant
Meets a new service not included in the Budget
34.x: An exceptional grant is made for a purpose that is not part of the current service of any financial year.
34.tq: Separate the exact meanings of exceptional, additional and excess grants.
34.sec: Vote on account, vote of credit, exceptional, supplementary and excess grants  [APPSC]

34.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Grant)
A. Supplementary grant
B. Additional grant
C. Excess grant
D. Vote of credit

List-II (Purpose)
1. Expenditure exceeds the amount already granted
2. New service not included in the Budget
3. Sanctioned amount is insufficient
4. Unexpected demand of indefinite magnitude or character

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
34.x: A supplementary grant meets an insufficiency; an additional grant covers a new service; an excess grant relates to expenditure beyond the amount granted; and a vote of credit meets an unexpected indefinite demand.
34.tq: Start from the sure pair and match each grant with its distinctive purpose.
34.sec: Vote on account, vote of credit, exceptional, supplementary and excess grants  [APPSC]

34.s: An excess grant becomes relevant when:
o: The expenditure is not part of the current service of any year
A new service is proposed in the current Budget
The sanctioned amount is insufficient before expenditure is incurred
Expenditure has exceeded the amount originally granted and prior approval of the Public Accounts Committee is required
34.x: An excess grant is required when expenditure has exceeded the amount granted. It requires prior scrutiny and approval by the Public Accounts Committee.
34.tq: Distinguish an excess already incurred from a supplementary requirement anticipated during the year.
34.sec: Vote on account, vote of credit, exceptional, supplementary and excess grants  [APPSC]

34.s: Which one of the following correctly states the purpose of an additional grant?
o: To meet a new service not provided for in the Budget
To meet expenditure already exceeding the grant
To express disapproval of a policy
To provide an advance until the Appropriation Act
34.x: An additional grant is sanctioned for a new service not included in the original Budget.
34.tq: Reject neighbouring purposes and identify the grant linked to a new service.
34.sec: Vote on account, vote of credit, exceptional, supplementary and excess grants  [APPSC]

34.s: Since the presentation of the Union Budget was advanced to 1 February, a vote on account is ordinarily required only in:
o: Years in which the Rajya Sabha is dissolved
Years in which there is no Finance Bill
34.x: After the Budget date was advanced to 1 February, a vote on account is generally needed only when an interim Budget is presented, particularly in an election year.
34.tq: Apply the change in the Budget calendar to determine when temporary spending authority is needed.
34.sec: Vote on account, vote of credit, exceptional, supplementary and excess grants  [APPSC]

34.s: A token grant is associated with:
o: An emergency demand of indefinite magnitude
A fresh withdrawal from the Public Account without parliamentary approval
A reduction of a Demand for Grant to Re 1
Re-appropriation and approval by the Lok Sabha
34.x: A token grant relates to re-appropriation and must also be voted by the Lok Sabha.
34.tq: Distinguish the budgetary token grant from the token cut motion.
34.sec: Vote on account, vote of credit, exceptional, supplementary and excess grants  [APPSC]

34.s: A policy cut motion is intended to express:
o: Approval of additional expenditure on a new service
Approval of the policy behind a Demand for Grant
A demand for expenditure from the Contingency Fund
Disapproval of the policy behind a Demand for Grant
34.x: A policy cut proposes to reduce the demand to Re 1, thereby expressing disapproval of the policy underlying the demand.
34.tq: Link the form of reduction with the political purpose of the motion.
34.sec: Cut motions - policy, economy, token  [other exams]

34.s: Under an economy cut motion, the Demand for Grant is:
34.x: An economy cut seeks a reduction by a specified amount to suggest economy in expenditure.
34.tq: Separate the three cut motions by their precise reduction amounts.
34.sec: Cut motions - policy, economy, token  [other exams]

34.s: A token cut motion is moved to:
o: Reduce a demand to Re 1 and reject its policy
Authorize expenditure on a new service
Reduce a demand by Rs 100 to ventilate a specific grievance
Reduce a demand by any amount to secure economy
34.x: A token cut reduces the demand by Rs 100 and is intended to ventilate a specific grievance.
34.tq: Use the exact numerical amount to distinguish a token cut from a policy cut.
34.sec: Cut motions - policy, economy, token  [other exams]

34.s:
Consider the following statements about cut motions:
1. They are moved only in the Lok Sabha.
2. They are moved during voting on Demands for Grants.
3. Passage of a cut motion indicates loss of confidence in the Council of Ministers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
34.x: Cut motions are moved only in the Lok Sabha during voting on Demands for Grants. If passed, they indicate that the government has lost the confidence of the House.
34.tq: Combine the location, stage and political consequence of a cut motion.
34.sec: Cut motions - policy, economy, token  [other exams]

34.s: Under which Article of the Constitution is the Consolidated Fund of India provided for?
34.x: Article 266(1) provides for the Consolidated Fund of India. It includes revenues received by the Union, loans raised by it and loan repayments received by it.
34.tq: Use the Article-number distinction between the two parts of Article 266 and Article 267.
34.sec: Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, Public Account

34.s: Which one of the following expenditures from the Consolidated Fund of India requires an appropriation law?
o: Withdrawal for an unforeseen expenditure pending parliamentary approval
Withdrawal of amounts credited to the Consolidated Fund for government expenditure
Remittance of money held temporarily in the Public Account
Withdrawal of public deposits held by the government as trustee
34.x: Money can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India only under an appropriation made by law. The Contingency Fund and Public Account follow different rules.
34.tq: Identify the fund first, then apply its withdrawal rule.
34.sec: Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, Public Account

34.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Consolidated Fund of India:
1. It includes all revenues received by the Union Government.
2. It includes loans raised by the Union Government, including Treasury Bills and internal or external loans.
3. It includes repayments of loans received by the Union Government.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
34.x: All three statements are correct. The Consolidated Fund comprises Union revenues, loans raised through specified sources and loan repayments received by the Union.
34.tq: Check whether each statement covers a separate component of the same constitutional fund.
34.sec: Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, Public Account

34.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched with the Public Account of India?
1. Provident funds — amounts held by the government in a fiduciary capacity
2. Small savings — amounts credited to the Public Account
3. Deposits and remittances — transactions included in the Public Account
4. Withdrawal — requires an appropriation law in every case
34.x: Provident funds, small savings, deposits and remittances are credited to the Public Account. Withdrawal from it does not require appropriation in the same manner as withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund, making statement 4 incorrect.
34.tq: Find the statement that reverses the constitutional rule applicable to the Public Account.
34.sec: Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, Public Account

34.s: In relation to the Public Account of India, the Government primarily acts as a
34.x: The Government acts as a banker or trustee in respect of money credited to the Public Account, such as provident funds, deposits and small savings.
34.tq: Test the functional role associated with the fund rather than merely its contents.
34.sec: Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, Public Account

34.s: The Contingency Fund of India is intended primarily for meeting
o: routine departmental expenditure included in the annual budget
expenditure from public deposits without legislative scrutiny
unforeseen expenditure pending approval by Parliament
repayment of all external loans raised by the Union
34.x: The Contingency Fund is used for unforeseen expenditure when immediate action is necessary, pending authorisation by Parliament.
34.tq: Distinguish emergency advances from routine budgetary expenditure and loan transactions.
34.sec: Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, Public Account

34.s:
Consider the following statements about the Contingency Fund of India:
1. It is provided for under Article 267 of the Constitution.
2. It was established under the Contingency Fund of India Act, 1950.
3. It is held by the Finance Secretary in the Department of Expenditure.
4. It is at the disposal of the President of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
34.x: All four statements are correct. Article 267 provides for the Fund, which was established by the 1950 Act, is held by the Finance Secretary in the Department of Economic Affairs, and is placed at the President’s disposal.
34.tq: Separate the constitutional provision, establishing law, custody and operational authority.
34.sec: Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, Public Account

34.s: What is the corpus of the Contingency Fund of India stated for the financial year 2021-22 onwards?
34.x: The corpus of the Contingency Fund of India was raised to ₹30,000 crore from the financial year 2021-22.
34.tq: Distinguish the present corpus from the earlier corpus and from larger budgetary figures.
34.sec: Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, Public Account

34.s: Which one of the following statements regarding audit of government funds is correct?
o: The CAG audits all three funds of the Union and the States.
The CAG audits the Consolidated and Public Accounts but not Contingency Funds.
The Finance Secretary audits all three funds and reports to the CAG.
The CAG audits only the Consolidated Fund of India.
34.x: The Comptroller and Auditor General audits the Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund and Public Account of both the Union and the States.
34.tq: Watch for the exclusion of one fund and identify the constitutional audit authority.
34.sec: Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, Public Account

34.s: The Railway Budget was merged with the Union Budget in
34.x: The separate Railway Budget was merged with the Union Budget in 2017. It had been separated in 1924 on the recommendation of the Acworth Committee.
34.tq: Use the paired historical dates to distinguish separation from merger.
34.sec: Railway budget merger, outcome budget, gender budget

34.s: The separation of the Railway Budget from the General Budget in 1924 was based on the recommendation of the
34.x: The Railway Budget was separated from the General Budget in 1924 on the recommendation of the Acworth Committee.
34.tq: Apply the wrong-committee trap to a well-known budget reform.
34.sec: Railway budget merger, outcome budget, gender budget

34.s: Which one of the following changes was associated with the Union Budget from 2017-18?
o: Introduction of the first Outcome Budget
Introduction of the Railway Budget as a separate document
Dropping of the Plan and Non-Plan distinction
Restoration of the Plan and Non-Plan distinction
34.x: The Plan and Non-Plan distinction was dropped from 2017-18. This was distinct from the earlier introduction of the Outcome Budget in 2005.
34.tq: Discriminate between reforms introduced in different years.
34.sec: Railway budget merger, outcome budget, gender budget

34.s: The Outcome Budget, also known as the Output-Outcome Framework, was introduced in
34.x: The Outcome Budget was introduced in 2005 and is treated as a budget document under the Output-Outcome Framework.
34.tq: Separate the year of introduction from the later Railway Budget and Plan distinction reforms.
34.sec: Railway budget merger, outcome budget, gender budget

34.s: Which of the following best describes gender budgeting?
o: Allocation of the entire budget exclusively to women-specific departments
Allocation of resources with reference to gender where disparities are chronic
Allocation of funds only for female employment schemes
Preparation of a separate budget for women outside the Union Budget
34.x: Gender budgeting involves making allocations with reference to gender in areas where gender disparities are chronic. It is not restricted to an entirely separate or women-only budget.
34.tq: Reject the extreme ‘entirely’ and ‘only’ interpretations of a policy concept.
34.sec: Railway budget merger, outcome budget, gender budget

34.s: The Gender Budget Statement has been presented since
34.x: The Gender Budget Statement has been presented since 2005-06 as part of the gender-budgeting process.
34.tq: Distinguish the financial year of the statement from the year of Railway Budget merger.
34.sec: Railway budget merger, outcome budget, gender budget

34.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Performance budgeting — First Hoover Commission and Administrative Reforms Commission
2. Zero-Based Budgeting — Peter Pyhrr
3. First use of Zero-Based Budgeting in government — Jimmy Carter
4. Outcome Budget — Acworth Committee
34.x: Performance budgeting is associated with the First Hoover Commission in the USA and the Administrative Reforms Commission in India. Zero-Based Budgeting is associated with Peter Pyhrr and was first used by Jimmy Carter; the Acworth Committee was related to the Railway Budget separation, not Outcome Budget.
34.tq: Use the person-committee-purpose trap by matching each reform with its proper association.
34.sec: Railway budget merger, outcome budget, gender budget

34.s: The Union Budget for 2026-27 was presented on
34.x: The Union Budget 2026-27 was presented on 1 February 2026. The date 14 February 2026 relates to the presentation of the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026-27.
34.tq: Separate closely placed Union and State budget dates.
34.sec: Universal angles

34.s: Which group of Articles is identified as containing budget-related provisions?
34.x: The budget-related provisions identified here are Articles 109 to 117 and Articles 265 to 267, covering financial legislation, public revenues and the principal government funds.
34.tq: Check the complete range rather than selecting an option containing only familiar financial Articles.
34.sec: Universal angles

34.s: The second batch of Supplementary Demands for Grants for 2025-26 approved by the Lok Sabha is associated with
34.x: Supplementary, additional or excess grants are provided for under Article 115. The second batch of Supplementary Demands for Grants for 2025-26 was approved by the Lok Sabha.
34.tq: Use the Article-function association and distinguish supplementary grants from the Annual Financial Statement.
34.sec: Universal angles

34.s: The proposed Economic Stabilisation Fund of ₹1 lakh crore was intended to address
o: only agricultural subsidies in the States
capital expenditure on railway tracks alone
repayment of all public-sector bank loans
34.x: The proposed Economic Stabilisation Fund of ₹1 lakh crore was intended to respond to global shocks and disruptions in supply chains.
34.tq: Match the proposed fund with its stated purpose and reject narrow or absolute alternatives.
34.sec: Universal angles

34.s: Who presented the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026-27?
34.x: The Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026-27 was presented on 14 February 2026 by Finance Minister Payyavula Keshav.
34.tq: Apply the office-holder trap by distinguishing the Finance Minister, the Agriculture Minister and the Governor.
34.sec: Universal angles

34.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026-27:
1. A separate Agriculture Budget was presented by K. Atchannaidu.
2. The session opened with the address of Governor S. Abdul Nazeer to both Houses.
3. The Budget was presented on 14 February 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
34.x: All three statements are correct. K. Atchannaidu presented the separate Agriculture Budget, Governor S. Abdul Nazeer addressed both Houses at the opening, and the State Budget was presented on 14 February 2026.
34.tq: Verify the date, presenter and opening constitutional act as separate facts before choosing the combination.
34.sec: Universal angles

35.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the financial committees of Parliament:
1. Members of these committees are elected annually by proportional representation through the single transferable vote.
2. The term of the members is one year.
3. Ministers are eligible to serve as members of these committees.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
35.x: Members are elected annually by proportional representation through the single transferable vote and hold office for one year. Ministers are ineligible to serve on these committees.
35.tq: Identify the true procedural statements and reject the eligibility trap.
35.sec: Financial committees - PAC, Estimates, COPU: strength, RS membership, chairman

35.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the composition of the Estimates Committee?
o: 30 members, all elected from the Lok Sabha
22 members, including 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha
22 members, all elected from the Lok Sabha
30 members, including 20 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha
35.x: The Estimates Committee has 30 members, all of whom are drawn from the Lok Sabha. The Rajya Sabha has no representation in it.
35.tq: Use the composition figures to distinguish the three financial committees.
35.sec: Financial committees - PAC, Estimates, COPU: strength, RS membership, chairman

35.s:
Which of the following statements correctly describes the Committee on Public Undertakings?
1. It consists of 22 members.
2. It includes 15 members from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha.
3. Its chairman is appointed from among the Lok Sabha members by the Speaker.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
35.x: All three statements are correct. The Committee on Public Undertakings has 22 members, including 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha, and its chairman is appointed by the Speaker from the Lok Sabha members.
35.tq: Check the complete composition-and-chairman combination rather than one isolated figure.
35.sec: Financial committees - PAC, Estimates, COPU: strength, RS membership, chairman

35.s: The chairperson of the Estimates Committee is appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and is invariably from which political grouping?
o: A party represented only in the Rajya Sabha
35.x: The Speaker appoints the chairperson of the Estimates Committee, who is invariably a member of the ruling party.
35.tq: Distinguish the convention for the Estimates Committee from the Opposition-chairman convention of the PAC.
35.sec: Financial committees - PAC, Estimates, COPU: strength, RS membership, chairman

35.s: The three financial committees of Parliament maintain an unremitting vigil primarily over which of the following?
35.x: The Estimates Committee, Public Accounts Committee and Committee on Public Undertakings exercise continuing oversight over expenditure and governmental performance.
35.tq: Match the collective role with the subject domain of the committees.
35.sec: Financial committees - PAC, Estimates, COPU: strength, RS membership, chairman

35.s:
Consider the following statements about parliamentary financial control:
1. The budget exercises control before expenditure takes place.
2. The financial committees exercise control after expenditure has taken place.
3. Parliamentary financial committees replace the budgetary process entirely.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
35.x: The budget provides control before expenditure, while the financial committees examine expenditure and performance after the event. They complement, rather than replace, the budgetary process.
35.tq: Track the time sequence of control and reject the extreme replacement claim.
35.sec: Financial committees - PAC, Estimates, COPU: strength, RS membership, chairman

35.s: The Public Accounts Committee primarily scrutinises which combination of documents?
o: Election expenditure statements, census reports and Finance Commission reports
Appropriation Bills, Money Bills and constitutional amendment Bills
Annual reports of political parties and reports of the Union Public Service Commission
Appropriation Accounts, Finance Accounts and reports of the Comptroller and Auditor-General
35.x: The Public Accounts Committee examines the Appropriation Accounts, Finance Accounts and audit reports submitted by the Comptroller and Auditor-General.
35.tq: Use the document-based function to separate PAC work from legislative scrutiny.
35.sec: Public Accounts Committee - reports, reporting, chairman

35.s: In examining government expenditure, the Public Accounts Committee checks whether money was spent:
o: Within the scope of the demand for grant
Only after approval by the Supreme Court
35.x: The PAC checks whether expenditure remained within the scope of the demand for grant approved by Parliament.
35.tq: Apply the committee’s audit function to a spending situation.
35.sec: Public Accounts Committee - reports, reporting, chairman

35.s: Which one of the following is NOT an area ordinarily examined by the Public Accounts Committee?
o: Formulation of the original policy itself
35.x: The PAC examines execution and the financial consequences of policy, but it cannot examine the policy itself. It may identify waste, extravagance, loss and nugatory expenditure and assess efficiency, economy and propriety.
35.tq: Find the option that crosses the boundary between policy execution and policy formulation.
35.sec: Public Accounts Committee - reports, reporting, chairman

35.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Public Accounts Committee:
1. It may take up certain matters on its own.
2. Its recommendations are binding on the government.
3. It examines not merely legality but also efficiency, economy and propriety.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
35.x: The PAC may take up matters on its own and examines efficiency, economy and propriety in addition to legality. Its recommendations are not binding on the government.
35.tq: Reject the legal-effect trap while retaining the two functional statements.
35.sec: Public Accounts Committee - reports, reporting, chairman

35.s:
Assertion (A): The chairperson of the Public Accounts Committee is generally selected from the Opposition.
Reason (R): The selection of an Opposition member as chairperson is a constitutional rule applicable in every case.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
35.x: The Opposition chairpersonship of the PAC is a convention followed since 1967, not a constitutional or statutory rule applicable in every case.
35.tq: Separate a parliamentary convention from a binding constitutional requirement.
35.sec: Public Accounts Committee - reports, reporting, chairman

35.s: Who is the chairperson of the Public Accounts Committee for 2026–27?
35.x: K. C. Venugopal is the chairperson of the Public Accounts Committee for 2026–27.
35.tq: Use the precise current-year office-holder rather than a person associated with another parliamentary function.
35.sec: Public Accounts Committee - reports, reporting, chairman

35.s: Which committee is popularly described as the ‘Ombudsman’ of Parliament?
35.x: The Committee on Petitions is popularly described as the Ombudsman of Parliament because it considers petitions on bills and matters of public interest.
35.tq: Match the distinctive nickname with the committee’s grievance-related function.
35.sec: Committee nicknames and reform area

35.s: The Estimates Committee is commonly known as the:
35.x: The Estimates Committee is known as the Continuous economy committee and suggests economies and alternative policies.
35.tq: Discriminate among the committee nicknames instead of matching only by financial subject.
35.sec: Committee nicknames and reform area

35.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Committee — Characterisation
1. Public Accounts Committee — Watchdog on departmental expenditure and irregularities
2. Estimates Committee — Suggests economies and alternative policies
3. Committee on Petitions — Examines only public accounts

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
35.x: The PAC is described as a watchdog on departmental expenditure and irregularities, and the Estimates Committee suggests economies and alternative policies. The Committee on Petitions deals with petitions on bills and public-interest matters, not only public accounts.
35.tq: Locate the single function mismatch in a set of closely related committee descriptions.
35.sec: Committee nicknames and reform area

35.s: Which of the following groups consists of committees regarded as part of the parliamentary watchdog group?
o: Subordinate Legislation, Government Assurances, Estimates, PAC, COPU and DRSCs
Committee on Petitions, Supreme Court, PAC and Finance Commission
Rules Committee, Election Commission, Estimates and CAG
Finance Commission, UPSC, Election Commission, PAC and COPU
35.x: The watchdog group comprises the Committee on Subordinate Legislation, Committee on Government Assurances, Estimates Committee, PAC, COPU and Departmentally Related Standing Committees.
35.tq: Check the complete group and exclude constitutional bodies that are not parliamentary committees.
35.sec: Committee nicknames and reform area

35.s: The Public Accounts Committee originated in 1921 under the:
35.x: The Public Accounts Committee originated in 1921 under the Government of India Act, 1919.
35.tq: Use the year–enactment pair to avoid confusion among the constitutional reform Acts.
35.sec: Origin years and recommending bodies

35.s:
Consider the following statements about Departmentally Related Standing Committees:
1. They were introduced in 1993 with 17 committees.
2. Their number became 24 from 2004.
3. Their establishment was based on the recommendation of the Rules Committee.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
35.x: All three statements are correct: DRSCs began in 1993 with 17 committees, expanded to 24 from 2004, and were introduced on the recommendation of the Rules Committee.
35.tq: Combine the origin year, numerical expansion and recommending body in one verification set.
35.sec: Origin years and recommending bodies

35.s: Which committee considers petitions relating to Bills and matters of public interest?
35.x: The Committee on Petitions examines petitions relating to Bills and matters of public interest.
35.tq: Match the petition-related function with the exact committee name.
35.sec: Other standing committees - function, strength, date

35.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched regarding the strength of standing committees?
o: Committee on Petitions: Lok Sabha 15, Rajya Sabha 10
Committee on Subordinate Legislation: Lok Sabha 10, Rajya Sabha 15
Committee on Government Assurances: Lok Sabha 10, Rajya Sabha 15
Committee of Privileges: Lok Sabha 10, Rajya Sabha 10
35.x: The Committee on Petitions has 15 members from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha. The Committee on Subordinate Legislation has 15 members from each House, while Government Assurances and Privileges have 15 in the Lok Sabha and 10 in the Rajya Sabha.
35.tq: Start with the sure House-wise strength pair and eliminate the reversed figures.
35.sec: Other standing committees - function, strength, date

35.s: The Committee on Subordinate Legislation is concerned with:
o: Checking the exercise of delegated rule-making power
35.x: The Committee on Subordinate Legislation checks how delegated rule-making powers are exercised.
35.tq: Distinguish delegated legislation from assurances, ethics and business scheduling.
35.sec: Other standing committees - function, strength, date

35.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Ethics Committee of the Rajya Sabha was established on 4 March 1997.
2. The Ethics Committee of the Lok Sabha was established on 16 May 2000.
3. The Ethics Committees examine the conduct of members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
35.x: The Rajya Sabha Ethics Committee dates from 4 March 1997, the Lok Sabha Ethics Committee from 16 May 2000, and their subject is the conduct of members.
35.tq: Verify both dates first, then connect the committees to their common function.
35.sec: Other standing committees - function, strength, date

35.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Committee on Government Assurances — Exercises delegated rule-making power
Business Advisory Committee — Allots time for government and other business
Committee of Privileges — Examines members’ conduct
Ethics Committee — Considers questions of privilege
35.x: The Business Advisory Committee allots time for government and other business. Questions of privilege belong to the Committee of Privileges, members’ conduct to the Ethics Committee, and delegated rule-making to the Committee on Subordinate Legislation.
35.tq: Find the only correctly assigned function among neighbouring standing committees.
35.sec: Other standing committees - function, strength, date

35.s: Which of the following committees is chaired by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
35.x: The Speaker chairs the Lok Sabha Business Advisory Committee, which allots time for government and other business.
35.tq: Use the authority–function relationship to identify the committee chaired by the Speaker.
35.sec: Other standing committees - function, strength, date

35.s:
Consider the following statements regarding other standing committees:
1. The Committee on Private Members’ Bills and Resolutions is a Lok Sabha-only committee.
2. The Committee on Absence of Members is a Lok Sabha-only committee.
3. The Committee on Empowerment of Women consists of members of both Houses and was established on 29 April 1997.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
35.x: All three statements are correct. The two specified committees are exclusive to the Lok Sabha, while the Committee on Empowerment of Women is a committee of both Houses established on 29 April 1997.
35.tq: Check House jurisdiction separately from the establishment date.
35.sec: Other standing committees - function, strength, date

35.s: The Committee on Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes consists of:
o: 31 members: 21 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha
30 members: 20 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha
22 members: 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha
30 members: 15 from the Lok Sabha and 15 from the Rajya Sabha
35.x: The Committee on Welfare of SCs and STs has 30 members, comprising 20 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha.
35.tq: Compare the committee’s 20–10 composition with the similar 21–10 DRSC figure.
35.sec: Committee on Welfare of SCs and STs

35.s: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Committee on Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes?
o: Reviewing welfare programmes for SCs and STs in Union ministries and bodies
Determining the composition of the National Commissions for SCs and STs
Examining reports of the National Commissions for SCs and STs
35.x: The committee examines commission reports, constitutional safeguards and welfare programmes. It does not determine the composition of the National Commissions.
35.tq: Find the option that assigns a constitutive power instead of an oversight function.
35.sec: Committee on Welfare of SCs and STs

35.s:
Consider the following statements about the Committee on Welfare of SCs and STs:
1. A Minister may serve as a member of the committee.
2. It examines the working of welfare programmes for SCs and STs in Union ministries and bodies.
3. It examines reports of the National Commissions for SCs and STs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
35.x: The committee examines welfare programmes and the reports of the National Commissions. Ministers are ineligible to serve on it, making statement 1 incorrect.
35.tq: Apply the common ministerial-ineligibility rule while retaining the committee’s substantive functions.
35.sec: Committee on Welfare of SCs and STs

35.s: Each Departmentally Related Standing Committee consists of:
o: 25 members: 15 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha
31 members: 21 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha
22 members: 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha
30 members: 20 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha
35.x: Each DRSC has 31 members, comprising 21 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha.
35.tq: Distinguish the DRSC composition from the 30-member SC/ST Welfare Committee.
35.sec: Departmentally Related Standing Committees

35.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Departmentally Related Standing Committees is correct?
1. There are 24 DRSCs.
2. Sixteen are under the Lok Sabha and eight are under the Rajya Sabha.
3. Their quorum is 11.
4. Ministers are eligible to serve on them.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
35.x: There are 24 DRSCs, with 16 under the Lok Sabha and 8 under the Rajya Sabha; their quorum is 11. Ministers are ineligible, so statement 4 is false.
35.tq: Use the ministerial-eligibility statement as the decisive false element.
35.sec: Departmentally Related Standing Committees

35.s:
The Departmentally Related Standing Committees scrutinise which of the following?
1. Demands for grants
2. Bills referred to them
3. Annual reports of ministries
4. Long-term policy of the ministries
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
35.x: DRSCs scrutinise demands for grants, referred Bills, annual reports and the long-term policy of the ministries under their jurisdiction.
35.tq: Recognise the full range of DRSC scrutiny rather than limiting it to grants.
35.sec: Departmentally Related Standing Committees

35.s: Which of the following statements about ad hoc parliamentary committees is correct?
o: They cease to exist once they have submitted their reports.
They are constituted only for financial legislation.
They can be created only by the President.
They continue permanently after submitting their reports.
35.x: Ad hoc committees are temporary and cease to exist after submitting their reports.
35.tq: Use the life-cycle feature of an ad hoc committee to reject permanent-status claims.
35.sec: Ad hoc committees - select, joint committees, JPCs

35.s: Ad hoc committees of Parliament are broadly of which two kinds?
o: Inquiry committees for a subject, and Select or Joint Committees on Bills
35.x: The two broad kinds are inquiry committees set up for a particular subject and Select or Joint Committees constituted to examine Bills.
35.tq: Classify the two categories before considering specific examples.

35.s: A Bill is referred to a Select Committee or a Joint Committee by:
o: A direction of the Comptroller and Auditor-General
An order of the President without parliamentary motion
A resolution of the Supreme Court

A. 2G spectrum
B. Bofors
C. Ketan Parekh
D. Harshad Mehta securities scam
E. Soft-drink pesticides
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
35.x: The investigations occurred in the order Bofors (1987), Harshad Mehta securities scam (1992), Ketan Parekh (2001), soft-drink pesticides (2003) and 2G spectrum (2011).

o: The original 1950 form of the Estimates Committee
Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 relating to simultaneous elections

35.s: Which of the following best describes a criticism of the Public Accounts Committee?
o: It replaces the budget and prevents all unauthorised expenditure in advance.
It is a post-mortem check, and frequent use of the guillotine can weaken financial control.
It can examine only the legality of expenditure and never its propriety.
It is a pre-expenditure approving authority whose recommendations automatically bind the government.
35.x: The PAC is criticised as a post-mortem mechanism because it examines expenditure after it occurs; frequent guillotine of demands can further weaken financial control. Its recommendations are not binding.
35.tq: Contrast post-expenditure scrutiny with pre-expenditure budgetary control and reject absolute claims.

36.s: The 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985 amended which of the following Articles in connection with vacation of seats and disqualification?
36.x: The 52nd Amendment amended Articles 101, 102, 190 and 191 concerning vacation of seats and disqualification.

36.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the anti-defection law:
1. It applies to members of both Houses of Parliament.
2. It applies to members of State Legislative Assemblies and Legislative Councils.
3. It operates on the legislature party.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
36.x: The law covers MPs, MLAs and MLCs, and its provisions operate on the legislature party. Therefore, all three statements are correct.
36.tq: Check the coverage across both Union and State legislatures before selecting the complete combination.
36.sec: Anti-defection law - Schedule, amendments, coverage

36.s: The principal objective of the anti-defection law is to
o: curb defections induced by the lure of office and promote stable governments
abolish political parties from the legislative process
transfer legislative control from parties to the Election Commission
36.x: The law was intended to curb horse-trading and defections for office, thereby promoting party discipline and stable governments.
36.tq: Identify the purpose from the cause-effect relationship rather than from the constitutional location of the law.
36.sec: Anti-defection law - Schedule, amendments, coverage

36.s: The expression “Aaya Ram, Gaya Ram”, associated with frequent defections, became prominent in the political context of
36.x: The expression became associated with rampant defections in Haryana in 1967, a phenomenon that contributed to the enactment of the anti-defection law.
