62.sec: Composition and status - number, CEC vs EC powers, decision rule, tenure, salary, removal  [APPSC]

62.s: In which case did the Supreme Court describe Article 324 as a “reservoir of power”?
o: Mohinder Singh Gill v. Chief Election Commissioner
S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
62.x: In Mohinder Singh Gill v. CEC (1978), the Supreme Court described Article 324 as a reservoir of power.
62.tq: Match the constitutional principle with the case that established or described it.
62.sec: Powers of Election Commission - Article 324, elections, parties and symbols, disqualification advice  [APPSC]

62.s: The reservoir of power under Article 324 may be used by the Election Commission primarily when:
o: A State Election Commission requests it in every case
No law holds the field on the matter concerned
A law already completely occupies the field
The President delegates legislative power to it
62.x: Article 324 operates as a reservoir where no law holds the field; it cannot ordinarily override an existing law governing the matter.
62.tq: Apply the condition attached to residual constitutional power.
62.sec: Powers of Election Commission - Article 324, elections, parties and symbols, disqualification advice  [APPSC]

62.s:
Under Article 324(1), the superintendence, direction and control of elections extends to elections to:
1. Parliament and State Legislatures
2. The offices of President and Vice-President
3. Panchayats and Municipalities
Which of the statements given above are correct?
62.x: Article 324(1) covers elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, President and Vice-President. Panchayat and municipal elections are conducted under the State Election Commission framework.
62.tq: Separate the jurisdiction of the ECI from that of State Election Commissions.
62.sec: Powers of Election Commission - Article 324, elections, parties and symbols, disqualification advice  [APPSC]

62.s: Which one of the following is NOT a type of function performed by the Election Commission of India?
62.x: The Election Commission performs administrative, advisory and quasi-judicial functions; it is not a legislative body.
62.tq: Find the institutionally incompatible function rather than a function expressly associated with the Commission.
62.sec: Powers of Election Commission - Article 324, elections, parties and symbols, disqualification advice  [APPSC]

62.s: The Election Commission recognises political parties and allots election symbols under the:
62.x: Party recognition and symbol allotment are governed by the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968, issued under the Representation of the People Act, 1951 and Article 324.
62.tq: Match a power with its exact legal instrument and year.
62.sec: Powers of Election Commission - Article 324, elections, parties and symbols, disqualification advice  [APPSC]

62.s: When a dispute arises regarding an election symbol or party recognition, the Election Commission exercises which nature of jurisdiction?
o: Advisory jurisdiction to the Governor only
62.x: The Commission settles disputes relating to party recognition and election symbols in its quasi-judicial capacity.
62.tq: Infer the nature of jurisdiction from the dispute-resolution function.
62.sec: Powers of Election Commission - Article 324, elections, parties and symbols, disqualification advice  [APPSC]

62.s:
The Election Commission gives advice on the disqualification of:
1. Members of Parliament to the President under Article 103
2. Members of State Legislatures to the Governor under Article 192
3. Members of Parliament in anti-defection cases to the Speaker under the Tenth Schedule
Which of the statements given above are correct?
62.x: The ECI advises the President under Article 103 and the Governor under Article 192. Anti-defection cases are decided by the Speaker or Chairman under the Tenth Schedule, not by the ECI.
62.tq: Use the wrong-authority trap to distinguish Articles 103 and 192 from the Tenth Schedule.
62.sec: Powers of Election Commission - Article 324, elections, parties and symbols, disqualification advice  [APPSC]

62.s: Which one of the following sequences best represents the broad electoral process over which the Election Commission exercises control?
o: Results, polling, announcement of election, nominations
Announcement of election, nominations, polling, results
Nominations, results, announcement of election, polling
Polling, announcement of election, results, nominations
62.x: The Commission controls the electoral process from the announcement of the election through nominations and polling to the declaration of results.
62.tq: Arrange the stages by identifying the natural first and last steps.
62.sec: Powers of Election Commission - Article 324, elections, parties and symbols, disqualification advice  [APPSC]

62.s: The Election Commission may cancel a poll when there is:
o: A delay in the formation of a State Cabinet
A reduction in the number of registered voters
A disagreement between two political parties over their manifestos
62.x: The Commission can cancel polls in cases such as rigging or booth capturing to protect the integrity of the electoral process.
62.tq: Identify the immediate electoral-integrity ground among unrelated administrative events.
62.sec: Powers of Election Commission - Article 324, elections, parties and symbols, disqualification advice  [APPSC]

62.s: Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls is ordered under:
o: Article 280 and Section 21 of the Delimitation Act, 2002
Article 324 and Section 21 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950
Article 243K and Section 11 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951
Article 326 and Section  Representation of the People Act, 1950
62.x: Special Intensive Revision is ordered under Article 324 and Section 21 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
62.tq: Match the electoral exercise with both its constitutional and statutory bases.
62.sec: Powers of Election Commission - Article 324, elections, parties and symbols, disqualification advice  [APPSC]

62.s: Which district achieved 100 per cent digitalisation of Special Intensive Revision forms?
62.x: ASR district achieved 100 per cent digitalisation of Special Intensive Revision forms.
62.tq: Test the exact district-name abbreviation rather than a generic description of digitisation.
62.sec: Powers of Election Commission - Article 324, elections, parties and symbols, disqualification advice  [APPSC]

62.s: In State of Karnataka v. Prathik Parasrampuria (2026), the Supreme Court held that which of the following is a core duty of the Election Commission?
o: Preparing the Union Budget for elections
Conducting municipal elections in every State
62.x: The Supreme Court held in the 2026 case that removing black money from elections is a core duty of the Election Commission.
62.tq: Link the judicial decision with the specific electoral-governance duty stated in it.
62.sec: Powers of Election Commission - Article 324, elections, parties and symbols, disqualification advice  [APPSC]

62.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Model Code of Conduct is correct?
o: It rests on Article 324 and applies from the day the election schedule is announced
It applies only to municipal elections under Article 243ZA
It is a statute enacted by Parliament and applies only after polling begins
It is enforced exclusively by the State Legislature after results are declared
62.x: The Model Code of Conduct is not a statute; it rests on Article 324 and applies from the announcement of the election schedule, as recognised in Harbans Singh Jalal (1997).
62.tq: Discriminate between a non-statutory code and a parliamentary statute, including its point of commencement.
62.sec: Powers of Election Commission - Article 324, elections, parties and symbols, disqualification advice  [APPSC]

62.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. J&K delimitation — Commission under Justice Ranjana Desai
2. Assam delimitation — Election Commission of India
3. Enforcement of the Model Code of Conduct — State Legislature alone
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
62.x: J&K delimitation was conducted by a Commission under Justice Ranjana Desai in 2022, while Assam was delimited by the ECI with effect from August 2023. The Model Code is not enforced by the State Legislature alone.
62.tq: Start with the two correct institution-location pairs and reject the wrong authority.
62.sec: Powers of Election Commission - Article 324, elections, parties and symbols, disqualification advice  [APPSC]

62.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Function)
A. Preparation and revision of electoral rolls
B. Scrutiny of nominations
C. Regulation of election expenses
D. Delimitation of territorial constituencies

List-II (Description)
1. Examination of candidates' nomination papers
2. Determination of electoral boundaries under the Delimitation Commission Act
3. Maintenance and updating of voter lists
4. Monitoring expenditure incurred during elections

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
62.x: Electoral-roll revision concerns voter lists, scrutiny concerns nomination papers, expense regulation concerns election expenditure, and delimitation concerns territorial boundaries.
62.tq: Start from the sure pair and complete the one-to-one matching.
62.sec: Powers of Election Commission - Article 324, elections, parties and symbols, disqualification advice  [APPSC]

62.s: Which one of the following is the official designation of the district-level election authority referred to in the Election Commission's state machinery?
62.x: The official designation is District Election Officer, although the APPSC usage may refer to the Collector as the District Returning Officer. The district authority appoints Returning and Presiding Officers.
62.tq: Test the exact official designation against a plausible but non-official title.
62.sec: Powers of Election Commission - Article 324, elections, parties and symbols, disqualification advice  [APPSC]

62.s: Which of the following correctly describes the election machinery at the State and district levels?
o: The State Election Commissioner functions as the Chief Electoral Officer for Parliamentary elections
The Election Commission appoints every Presiding Officer directly from New Delhi
The Governor functions as the Chief Electoral Officer and the Chief Secretary appoints Presiding Officers
The Chief Electoral Officer functions at the State level, while the District Election Officer appoints Returning and Presiding Officers
62.x: Each State has a Chief Electoral Officer, and at the district level the Collector or District Election Officer appoints Returning and Presiding Officers.
62.tq: Apply the who-does-this-job test to distinguish levels of election administration.
62.sec: Powers of Election Commission - Article 324, elections, parties and symbols, disqualification advice  [APPSC]

62.s: Regional Election Commissioners may be appointed by the President after consultation with the:
62.x: The President may appoint Regional Election Commissioners after consulting the Election Commission.
62.tq: Identify the constitutionally relevant consulting authority rather than the appointing authority alone.
62.sec: Composition and status - number, CEC vs EC powers, decision rule, tenure, salary, removal  [APPSC]

62.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Chief Election Commissioners of India:
1. V.S. Ramadevi was the first woman Chief Election Commissioner.
2. V.S. Ramadevi served in 1990.
3. V.S. Ramadevi was the tenth Chief Election Commissioner.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
62.x: V.S. Ramadevi was the first and only woman Chief Election Commissioner and served in 1990. T.N. Seshan, not Ramadevi, was the tenth CEC.
62.tq: Split the statements using the office-holder and numerical designation.
62.sec: Chief Election Commissioners - FIRST, FIRST woman, reform era; National Voters' Day

62.s: Which one of the following Chief Election Commissioners is particularly associated with election reforms, enforcement of the Model Code of Conduct and introduction of Elector Photo Identity Cards?
62.x: T.N. Seshan, the tenth CEC, is associated with major election reforms, enforcement of the Model Code of Conduct and Elector Photo Identity Cards.
62.tq: Match the notable reform with the correct office-holder.
62.sec: Chief Election Commissioners - FIRST, FIRST woman, reform era; National Voters' Day

62.s: The headquarters of the Election Commission of India is located at:
62.x: The Election Commission of India has its seat at Nirvachan Sadan, New Delhi.
62.tq: Test the exact institutional location rather than a nearby central-government building.
62.sec: Chief Election Commissioners - FIRST, FIRST woman, reform era; National Voters' Day

62.s: Which one of the following is the training arm of the Election Commission of India?
o: Law Commission of India, New Delhi
62.x: The India International Institute of Democracy and Election Management (IIIDEM), New Delhi, is the training arm of the Election Commission of India.
62.tq: Distinguish an institution's training arm from its headquarters.
62.sec: Chief Election Commissioners - FIRST, FIRST woman, reform era; National Voters' Day

62.s:
Arrange the following milestones in chronological order:
A. Establishment of the Election Commission of India
B. Golden Jubilee of the Election Commission
C. Diamond Jubilee of the Election Commission
D. Completion of 75 years of the Election Commission
62.x: The Election Commission was established in 1950, its Golden Jubilee was in 2001, Diamond Jubilee in 2010 and 75 years were completed in 2025.
62.tq: Anchor the sequence with the establishment year and then compare the anniversary years.
62.sec: Chief Election Commissioners - FIRST, FIRST woman, reform era; National Voters' Day

62.s: The Election Commission of India was established on:
62.x: The Election Commission of India was established on 25 January 1950.
62.tq: Separate the foundation date from neighbouring national and electoral dates.
62.sec: Chief Election Commissioners - FIRST, FIRST woman, reform era; National Voters' Day

62.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
62.x: The Golden Jubilee was observed in 2001. The Diamond Jubilee was in 2010 and 75 years were completed in 2025.
62.tq: Use anniversary arithmetic to eliminate swapped milestone years.
62.sec: Chief Election Commissioners - FIRST, FIRST woman, reform era; National Voters' Day

62.s:
With reference to post-retirement restrictions on Election Commissioners, consider the following statements:
1. The Constitution expressly bars retiring Election Commissioners from receiving any further government appointment.
2. The Constitution contains a bar on the post-retirement appointment of the Comptroller and Auditor General.
3. Article 319 deals with post-retirement restrictions relating to the Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
62.x: The Constitution does not expressly bar retiring Election Commissioners from further government appointment. Constitutional restrictions apply to the CAG under Article 148(4) and the UPSC Chairman under Article 319.
62.tq: Identify the constitutional-bar trap and distinguish ECs from CAG and UPSC provisions.
62.sec: Post-retirement restrictions - constitutional position

62.s: Which one of the following correctly states the constitutional position regarding the qualifications and tenure of the Election Commissioners?
o: The Constitution prescribes a five-year term and qualifications equivalent to those of a Supreme Court judge.
The Constitution prescribes both detailed qualifications and a fixed six-year tenure.
The Constitution prescribes qualifications but leaves tenure entirely to the President.
The Constitution prescribes neither qualifications nor a term of office for them.
62.x: The Constitution prescribes neither qualifications nor a term of office for the Election Commissioners; these matters are dealt with through the applicable legal framework.
62.tq: Watch for the constitutional-versus-statutory distinction.
62.sec: Post-retirement restrictions - constitutional position

62.s: The CEC and Other ECs (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023 is identified as:
o: Act No. 49 of 2023, replacing the 1975 Act
Act No. 29 of 2023, replacing the 1991 Act
Act No. 49 of 2022, replacing the 1991 Act
Act No. 49 of 2023, replacing the 1991 Act
62.x: The 2023 law is Act No. 49 of 2023 and replaced the 1991 Act.
62.tq: Check both the Act number and the legislation it replaced.
62.sec: CEC and Other ECs Act 2023 - selection committee, search committee, service conditions

62.s: Under the CEC and Other ECs Act, 2023, the Search Committee is headed by:
62.x: The Search Committee is headed by the Law Minister.
62.tq: Apply the 'who performs this institutional job?' method.
62.sec: CEC and Other ECs Act 2023 - selection committee, search committee, service conditions

62.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Search Committee under the 2023 Act:
1. It is headed by the Law Minister.
2. It includes two members of Secretary rank or above.
3. It prepares a shortlist of five names.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
62.x: The Search Committee is headed by the Law Minister, has two Secretary-rank or above members, and shortlists five names.
62.tq: Treat each composition and numerical detail as a separate statement.
62.sec: CEC and Other ECs Act 2023 - selection committee, search committee, service conditions

62.s: Under the CEC and Other ECs Act, 2023, which statement is correct regarding the Selection Committee?
o: It must select only from the five names shortlisted by the Search Committee.
It has no role in recommending names to the President.
It may select a person only after approval by the Chief Justice of India.
It may select names other than those included in the shortlist prepared by the Search Committee.
62.x: The Selection Committee may choose names outside the shortlist prepared by the Search Committee. It recommends the names for appointment by the President.
62.tq: Test the exception to the normal shortlist-based selection process.
62.sec: CEC and Other ECs Act 2023 - selection committee, search committee, service conditions

62.s: The eligibility requirement under the 2023 Act includes which of the following?
o: A sitting Supreme Court judge with administrative experience
Only a serving Chief Secretary of a State with judicial experience
Present or past Secretary to the Government of India rank with election-management experience
Any member of Parliament with electoral experience
62.x: An eligible person must hold or have held a post equivalent to Secretary to the Government of India and possess election-management experience.
62.tq: Look for the exact rank-plus-experience combination.
62.sec: CEC and Other ECs Act 2023 - selection committee, search committee, service conditions

62.s: The tenure of the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners under the 2023 Act is:
o: Until the age of 70 years or five years, whichever is later
Five years or until the age of 62 years, whichever is earlier
Six years or until the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier
62.x: The tenure is six years or until attaining 65 years of age, whichever is earlier. Reappointment is not permitted.
62.tq: Compare both components of a compound tenure rule and note 'whichever is earlier'.
62.sec: CEC and Other ECs Act 2023 - selection committee, search committee, service conditions

62.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the service conditions of the CEC and ECs:
1. They are paid on a par with a Judge of the Supreme Court.
2. The CEC and the other Election Commissioners receive equal salaries.
3. Their service conditions may be varied to their disadvantage after appointment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
62.x: The CEC and ECs receive equal salaries on a par with a Supreme Court judge. Their service conditions cannot be varied to their disadvantage, making statement 3 false.
62.tq: Find the reversed-protection statement in a service-conditions question.
62.sec: CEC and Other ECs Act 2023 - selection committee, search committee, service conditions

62.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the removal of the Chief Election Commissioner?
o: The CEC may be removed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister alone.
The CEC may be removed by the Chief Justice of India on a judicial recommendation.
The CEC is removed by a simple majority of the Lok Sabha alone.
The CEC is removed in the same manner as a Supreme Court judge, through a special-majority address by both Houses of Parliament.
62.x: The CEC is removed like a Supreme Court judge, on a special-majority address passed by both Houses of Parliament.
62.tq: Use the 'who would perform this constitutional removal?' test.
62.sec: CEC and Other ECs Act 2023 - selection committee, search committee, service conditions

62.s: With regard to the removal of Election Commissioners other than the CEC, which one of the following is correct?
o: They can be removed only on the recommendation of the Chief Justice of India.
They can be removed by the Union Cabinet without any recommendation.
They can be removed only on the recommendation of the CEC.
They enjoy an absolute constitutional immunity from removal.
62.x: Election Commissioners other than the CEC can be removed only on the recommendation of the CEC. Section 11 of the 2023 Act provides the removal procedure.
62.tq: Distinguish the removal safeguards applicable to the CEC and other ECs.
62.sec: CEC and Other ECs Act 2023 - selection committee, search committee, service conditions

62.s: Article 324(2) of the Constitution provides that the Election Commissioners are appointed by the President subject to:
o: A recommendation of the State Election Commission
A resolution of the Supreme Court
62.x: Article 324(2) vests appointment in the President, subject to the provisions of a law made by Parliament.
62.tq: Match the constitutional article with its exact statutory qualification.
62.sec: CEC and Other ECs Act 2023 - selection committee, search committee, service conditions

62.s: In Anoop Baranwal v. Union of India (2023), the interim selection panel directed by the Constitution Bench consisted of:
o: Prime Minister, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and Chief Justice of India
Prime Minister, Law Minister and Chief Justice of India
President, Prime Minister and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha
Prime Minister, Speaker of the Lok Sabha and Chief Justice of India
62.x: Until Parliament enacted a law, the Constitution Bench directed selection by a panel comprising the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition or leader of the largest opposition party in the Lok Sabha, and the Chief Justice of India.
62.tq: Separate the interim judicial mechanism from the later statutory mechanism.
62.sec: Anoop Baranwal case - interim selection mechanism

62.s: Which one of the following was the principal change made by the 2023 Act in relation to the interim mechanism in Anoop Baranwal?
o: The entire Selection Committee was replaced by the Search Committee.
The Prime Minister was replaced by the President.
The Leader of Opposition was replaced by the Law Minister.
The Chief Justice of India was replaced by a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister.
62.x: The 2023 Act replaced the Chief Justice of India on the selection panel with a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister.
62.tq: Discriminate between the CJI in the interim panel and the Cabinet Minister in the statutory panel.
62.sec: Anoop Baranwal case - interim selection mechanism

62.s: Before the judgment in Anoop Baranwal v. Union of India, the appointment of the CEC and ECs was made by the President on the advice of:
o: The Prime Minister, Leader of Opposition and Chief Justice of India jointly
62.x: Before the interim mechanism laid down in Anoop Baranwal, the President appointed the CEC and ECs on the advice of the Prime Minister alone.
62.tq: Arrange the institutional position before, during and after the judicial intervention.
62.sec: Anoop Baranwal case - interim selection mechanism

62.s: The Tarkunde Committee, which proposed a selection panel comprising the Prime Minister, Leader of Opposition and Chief Justice of India, was set up in:
62.x: The Tarkunde Committee was set up in 1975 by Jayaprakash Narayan and proposed a three-member selection panel and a three-member Election Commission.
62.tq: Link the committee's year with its distinctive proposed composition.
62.sec: Anoop Baranwal case - interim selection mechanism

62.s: Who set up the Tarkunde Committee?
62.x: The Tarkunde Committee was set up by Jayaprakash Narayan in 1975.
62.tq: Test the person associated with the committee rather than its recommendation.
62.sec: Anoop Baranwal case - interim selection mechanism

62.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Tarkunde Committee:
1. It proposed a three-member Election Commission.
2. It proposed a selection panel of the Prime Minister, Leader of Opposition and Chief Justice of India.
3. It was constituted under the CEC and Other ECs Act, 2023.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
62.x: The Tarkunde Committee proposed both a three-member Commission and the PM–LoP–CJI selection panel. It was set up in 1975, not under the 2023 Act.
62.tq: Reject the anachronistic statutory attribution in statement 3.
62.sec: Anoop Baranwal case - interim selection mechanism

62.s: The constitutional challenge to the 2023 selection framework was pending, as of May 2026, in:
o: Anoop Baranwal v. Union of India
S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
Jaya Thakur v. Union of India
62.x: The 2023 Act was challenged in Jaya Thakur v. Union of India, and the matter remained pending as of May 2026.
62.tq: Distinguish the later statutory challenge from the earlier Anoop Baranwal judgment.
62.sec: CEC and Other ECs Act 2023 - selection committee, search committee, service conditions

62.s: Which concern was raised in the proceedings concerning the 2023 selection committee?
o: The use of a three-member Election Commission
The government having a 2–1 majority and the absence of one absolutely neutral person
The absence of any role for the President in appointment
The Search Committee having more members than the Selection Committee
62.x: The framework was criticised for giving the government a 2–1 majority. The Supreme Court also questioned the absence of one absolutely neutral person and asked whether the Leader of Opposition was merely ornamental.
62.tq: Identify the institutional-balance concern rather than a formal appointment step.
62.sec: CEC and Other ECs Act 2023 - selection committee, search committee, service conditions

62.s: What was the status of the Election Commission of India during January 1990?
o: It was replaced by the State Election Commissions
The posts of Election Commissioners were abolished and it became a single-member body again
Its functions were transferred to the Law Commission
It functioned with the CEC and two Election Commissioners
62.x: In January 1990, the posts of the additional Election Commissioners were abolished and the Election Commission again became a single-member body.
62.tq: Test the short-lived institutional reversal between the 1989 expansion and the later multi-member arrangement.
62.sec: Multi-member commission history - T.N. Seshan era reforms

62.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Election Commission of India:
1. Since October 1993, it has functioned as a multi-member body consisting of the CEC and two Election Commissioners.
2. Decisions in the multi-member Commission are taken by majority.
3. The Chief Election Commissioner has an absolute veto over every decision of the Commission.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
62.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because decisions are governed by the majority rule and the CEC does not possess an absolute veto over every decision.
62.tq: Reject the absolute-power statement and identify the majority-rule principle.
62.sec: Multi-member commission history - T.N. Seshan era reforms

62.s: The constitutional validity of the multi-member Election Commission and the majority rule was upheld in which case?
o: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
Mohinder Singh Gill v. Chief Election Commissioner
ADR v. Election Commission of India
T.N. Seshan v. Union of India
62.x: The Supreme Court upheld the multi-member structure and majority rule in T.N. Seshan v. Union of India (1995).
62.tq: Use the case-name association to distinguish institutional-structure litigation from election-process cases.
62.sec: Multi-member commission history - T.N. Seshan era reforms

62.s: Which one of the following was NOT associated with the election reforms of the T.N. Seshan era?
o: Transfer of election petitions from High Courts to the Election Commission
Strict enforcement of the Model Code of Conduct in 1991
Introduction of Electors Photo Identity Cards
62.x: Election petitions were not transferred to the Election Commission; they are tried by the High Courts in the case of Parliamentary and State Legislature elections. The other three measures were associated with the Seshan era.
62.tq: Find the institutional power wrongly transferred to the Election Commission.
62.sec: Multi-member commission history - T.N. Seshan era reforms

62.s: During the enforcement of the Model Code of Conduct in 1991, which action was associated with the T.N. Seshan era?
o: All political parties were dissolved by the President
Voting was restricted to holders of Electors Photo Identity Cards
Politicians violating the Code were arrested and partisan police officers were removed
Election petitions were decided by the Election Commission
62.x: The Seshan-era enforcement included arresting politicians who violated the Model Code of Conduct and removing partisan police officers.
62.tq: Match the reformer with the specific enforcement actions rather than with unrelated constitutional powers.
62.sec: Multi-member commission history - T.N. Seshan era reforms

62.s:
With reference to Article 329 of the Constitution, consider the following statements:
1. Laws relating to delimitation of constituencies cannot be questioned in any court.
2. The allotment of seats to constituencies cannot be questioned in any court.
3. An election to Parliament or a State Legislature can be questioned only through an election petition.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
62.x: Article 329(a) bars judicial challenge to laws relating to delimitation and allotment of seats, while Article 329(b) requires an election to be challenged only through an election petition.
62.tq: Split Article 329 into its two clauses and test both the delimitation bar and the election-petition rule.
62.sec: Disputes regarding election - EC vs courts, Article 329 bar

62.s: An election to Parliament or a State Legislature may be challenged under Article 329(b) through an election petition under which law?
o: The Representation of the People Act, 1951
The Representation of the People Act, 1950
62.x: Article 329(b) operates with the election-petition mechanism provided under the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
62.tq: Distinguish the two Representation of the People Acts by linking election petitions with the 1951 Act.
62.sec: Disputes regarding election - EC vs courts, Article 329 bar

62.s: Which of the following correctly describes the judicial forum and appellate route for an election petition concerning a Parliamentary or State Legislative election?
o: It is tried by the Election Commission, with appeal to the High Court
It is tried by the Governor, with appeal to the Election Commission
It is tried by the High Court, with appeal to the Supreme Court
It is tried directly by the Supreme Court, with appeal to the President
62.x: Election petitions concerning Parliament or State Legislatures are tried by the High Court, and an appeal lies to the Supreme Court.
62.tq: Apply the 'who would do this job?' method to separate the Election Commission from the judicial forum.
62.sec: Disputes regarding election - EC vs courts, Article 329 bar

62.s: Which one of the following functions is performed by the Election Commission of India rather than by a court hearing an election petition?
o: Adjudicating disputes concerning the election of the President under Article 71
Hearing an appeal from a High Court judgment in an election petition
Deciding disputes relating to political parties and election symbols
62.x: The Election Commission decides disputes concerning political parties and election symbols and advises on disqualification. It does not try election petitions or decide presidential election disputes.
62.tq: Separate the Commission's administrative and quasi-judicial functions from the courts' election-petition jurisdiction.
62.sec: Disputes regarding election - EC vs courts, Article 329 bar

62.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. By convention, courts generally do not interfere once the election process has begun.
2. The Election Commission can review the result of an election after it has been declared.
3. The Election Commission does not try election petitions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
62.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is false because the Election Commission cannot review an election result; challenges must follow the election-petition route.
62.tq: Use the negative institutional-power trap: the Commission conducts elections but does not review declared results or try petitions.
62.sec: Disputes regarding election - EC vs courts, Article 329 bar

62.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Provision)
A. Article 329(a)
B. Article 329(b)
C. Article 71

List-II (Subject)
1. Election disputes concerning President and Vice-President
2. Bar on questioning delimitation and allotment of seats in court
3. Challenge to an election only by an election petition

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
62.x: Article 329(a) concerns the bar on challenges to delimitation and seat allotment, Article 329(b) requires an election petition, and Article 71 covers disputes regarding Presidential and Vice-Presidential elections.
62.tq: Start from the sure Article 71 pair and then distinguish the two clauses of Article 329.
62.sec: Disputes regarding election - EC vs courts, Article 329 bar

62.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Institution or authority)
A. Chief Electoral Officer
B. State Election Commission
C. District Collector
D. Election Commission of India

List-II (Function or position)
1. District Election Officer/District Returning Officer
2. Conducts elections to Panchayats and municipalities
3. Conducts elections to Parliament and State Legislatures
4. State-level officer for elections under the control of the Election Commission of India

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
62.x: The Chief Electoral Officer is the state-level officer under the ECI; the SEC conducts local-body elections; the Collector serves as District Election Officer/District Returning Officer; and the ECI conducts Parliamentary and State Legislative elections.
62.tq: Build the answer from the sure district-level pair and then separate ECI elections from SEC elections.
62.sec: Chief Electoral Officer of the state and AP State Election Commission - distinction

62.s: The Chief Electoral Officer of a State is appointed by the Election Commission of India from among which category?
o: Senior civil servants of the State
Judges of the concerned High Court
Members of the State Legislative Assembly
62.x: The Chief Electoral Officer is appointed by the Election Commission of India from among senior civil servants of the State.
62.tq: Test the appointing authority and source cadre together, avoiding confusion with the Governor's appointment of the State Election Commissioner.
62.sec: Chief Electoral Officer of the state and AP State Election Commission - distinction

62.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Chief Electoral Officer and the State Election Commission:
1. The Chief Electoral Officer functions under the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
2. The State Election Commission functions under Articles 243K and 243ZA.
3. The Chief Electoral Officer is removed like a High Court judge.
4. The State Election Commissioner is removable only in the manner applicable to a High Court judge.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
62.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is false: the Chief Electoral Officer is removed by the Election Commission, whereas the State Election Commissioner enjoys protection comparable to that of a High Court judge.
62.tq: Compare the two offices line by line, especially the easily swapped removal provisions.
62.sec: Chief Electoral Officer of the state and AP State Election Commission - distinction

62.s: Which of the following elections is conducted by the State Election Commission rather than by the Election Commission of India?
o: Election to a State Legislative Council
62.x: Municipal elections, along with Panchayat elections, are conducted by the State Election Commission under Articles 243K and 243ZA.
62.tq: Use the body-versus-election distinction to identify the local-government election.
62.sec: Chief Electoral Officer of the state and AP State Election Commission - distinction

62.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Election Commission of India — President and Vice-President elections
Election Commission of India — Election of Speaker of a State Legislative Assembly
62.x: The Speaker is elected by the House itself, not by the Election Commission of India. The ECI conducts elections to the offices of President and Vice-President, while State Election Commissions conduct Panchayat and municipal elections.
62.tq: Identify the wrong authority by asking who elects an office from within the House itself.
62.sec: Chief Electoral Officer of the state and AP State Election Commission - distinction

62.s: Who appoints the State Election Commissioner, and what protection governs removal from office?
o: The Election Commission of India; removal at the pleasure of the President
The Governor; removal only in the manner applicable to a High Court judge
The Chief Minister; removal by the State Legislative Assembly
The President; removal by the Supreme Court
62.x: The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor and can be removed only in the manner applicable to a High Court judge under Article 243K(2).
62.tq: Pair the appointing authority with the constitutional removal safeguard instead of confusing it with the CEO's position.
62.sec: Chief Electoral Officer of the state and AP State Election Commission - distinction

62.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Initiative)
A. SVEEP
B. cVIGIL
C. Saksham
D. Voter Helpline

List-II (Purpose)
1. Registration, corrections, roll search and complaints
2. Reporting Model Code violations through geo-tagged photographs or videos
3. Voter education and electoral participation
4. Assistance and facilities for voters with disabilities

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
62.x: SVEEP promotes voter education and turnout; cVIGIL reports Model Code violations; Saksham assists voters with disabilities; and Voter Helpline provides registration, correction, search and complaint services.
62.tq: Start with the distinctive cVIGIL geo-tagging function and eliminate codes that misplace the remaining apps.
62.sec: Voter facilitation apps and campaigns

62.s: SVEEP, launched in 2009, is primarily associated with which objective?
62.x: SVEEP stands for Systematic Voters' Education and Electoral Participation and is a voter education and turnout programme launched in 2009.
62.tq: Expand the acronym and connect it with the programme's stated objective and launch year.
62.sec: Voter facilitation apps and campaigns

62.s: A citizen wants to report a suspected violation of the Model Code of Conduct by uploading a geo-tagged video. Which platform is most appropriate?
62.x: cVIGIL enables citizens to report Model Code of Conduct violations using geo-tagged photographs or videos.
62.tq: Map the practical scenario to the app whose defining feature is geo-tagged complaint reporting.
62.sec: Voter facilitation apps and campaigns

62.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Special Intensive Revision is correct?
o: The Bihar SIR removed about 70 lakh names and the subsequent turnout was the highest since Independence.
The Bihar SIR concerned only municipal elections.
The Bihar SIR removed about 7 lakh names and produced the lowest turnout since Independence.
The Bihar SIR was conducted exclusively through the Saksham application.
62.x: The Bihar Special Intensive Revision removed about 70 lakh names, and the turnout that followed was reported as the highest since Independence.
62.tq: Distinguish the similar figures 7 lakh and 70 lakh and retain the correct turnout comparison.
62.sec: Voter facilitation apps and campaigns

62.s: Which district in Andhra Pradesh achieved 100 per cent digitalisation of Special Intensive Revision enumeration forms?
62.x: ASR district in Andhra Pradesh achieved 100 per cent digitalisation of SIR enumeration forms.
62.tq: Test the exact district associated with the complete digitalisation milestone.
62.sec: Voter facilitation apps and campaigns

62.s:
Consider the following statements regarding VVPAT:
1. It is attached to the Electronic Voting Machine.
2. It prints a slip containing the serial number, name and symbol of the selected candidate.
3. The voter can see the printed slip for seven seconds.
4. The slip is handed over to the voter for personal custody.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
62.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the voter views the slip through the VVPAT window; it is not handed over to the voter.
62.tq: Use the operational sequence and reject the plausible but incorrect claim that the voter receives the paper slip.
62.sec: VVPAT - working, verification rules

62.s: The use of VVPAT was permitted through an amendment to which rules?
o: The Representation of the People Rules, 1950
62.x: VVPAT use was permitted through an amendment to the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961.
62.tq: Identify the exact subordinate-rules framework instead of confusing it with the Representation of the People Acts.
62.sec: VVPAT - working, verification rules

62.s: VVPAT was first used in an election at which location in 2013?
62.x: VVPAT was first used in 2013 at 51-Noksen in Nagaland. The 70-Parur reference relates to the first EVM pilot in 1982.
62.tq: Separate the two easily confused first-use locations: VVPAT at 51-Noksen and EVM pilot at 70-Parur.
62.sec: VVPAT - working, verification rules

62.s: EVMs and VVPATs used by the Election Commission of India are manufactured by which organisations?
62.x: Electronic Voting Machines and VVPATs are manufactured by Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL) and Electronics Corporation of India Limited (ECIL).
62.tq: Recall the paired public-sector manufacturers without substituting other electronics or defence organisations.
62.sec: VVPAT - working, verification rules

62.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the early use of Electronic Voting Machines?
o: They were first piloted at 70-Parur, Kerala, in 1982 and used universally in the 2004 Lok Sabha election.
They were first piloted at 51-Noksen, Nagaland, in 2013 and used universally in 2009.
They were first piloted in Delhi in 1991 and used universally in 1996.
They were first piloted in Andhra Pradesh in 1989 and used universally in 1999.
62.x: EVMs were first piloted at 70-Parur in Kerala in 1982 and were used universally in the 2004 Lok Sabha election.
62.tq: Keep the EVM timeline distinct from the later VVPAT timeline by checking both the location and year.
62.sec: VVPAT - working, verification rules

62.s: Under the Supreme Court's 2019 verification arrangement, how many randomly chosen VVPATs are counted per Assembly segment?
62.x: The slips of five randomly chosen VVPATs are counted in each Assembly segment under the Supreme Court's 2019 arrangement.
62.tq: Test the prescribed numerical standard directly and distinguish it from the later 100 per cent counting demand.
62.sec: VVPAT - working, verification rules

62.s: Which of the following was the decision of the Supreme Court in ADR v. Election Commission of India in April 2024?
o: It abolished the use of VVPAT machines.
It ordered compulsory counting of 100 per cent of VVPAT slips in every election.
It rejected the demand for 100 per cent VVPAT counting.
It transferred VVPAT verification entirely to State Election Commissions.
62.x: In ADR v. ECI (April 2024), the Supreme Court rejected the demand for counting 100 per cent of VVPAT slips.
62.tq: Spot the reversal trap involving a demand for total counting and the Court's actual decision.
62.sec: VVPAT - working, verification rules

62.s: Candidates placed second and third in an election may seek verification of what proportion of EVMs' burnt memory per Assembly segment, and within what period after the result?
62.x: Candidates placed second and third may seek verification of 5 per cent of EVMs' burnt memory per Assembly segment within seven days of the result.
62.tq: Pair both numerical conditions—percentage and time limit—to avoid selecting an option with only one correct figure.
62.sec: VVPAT - working, verification rules

62.s: The Opposition's removal motion against which Chief Election Commissioner was described as the first such motion against a CEC appointed under the 2023 Act?
62.x: The removal motion was moved against CEC Gyanesh Kumar and was described as the first such motion against a CEC appointed under the 2023 Act.
62.tq: Use the current-affairs association between the office-holder and the specific constitutional controversy.
62.sec: Universal angles

62.s: V. S. Ramadevi is associated with which distinction in the Election Commission of India?
o: First Chief Election Commissioner appointed under the 2023 Act
First Chief Election Commissioner of India
First State Election Commissioner for local-body elections
First woman Chief Election Commissioner of India
62.x: V. S. Ramadevi was the first woman Chief Election Commissioner of India.
62.tq: Discriminate between closely related firsts by matching the person with the exact distinction.
62.sec: Universal angles

62.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Election Commission of India — Article 324 — elections to Parliament and State Legislatures
Election Commission of India — Article 243K — elections to local bodies
State Election Commission — Article 324 — elections to Parliament and State Legislatures
State Election Commission — Article 280 — elections to local bodies
62.x: The Election Commission of India derives its constitutional basis from Article 324 and conducts elections to Parliament and State Legislatures. The State Election Commission functions under Article 243K for local-body elections.
62.tq: Split the options by checking both the constitutional Article and the level of elections involved.
62.sec: Universal angles

62.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the selection panel under the 2023 law relating to the Election Commission of India:
1. The Supreme Court stated in May 2026 that the place of the Chief Justice of India on the panel was only temporary, pending a law.
2. Petitions by the Association for Democratic Reforms and Jaya Thakur challenge the government majority in the Selection Committee.
3. The challenged composition of the Selection Committee gives the government a 2:1 majority.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
62.x: All three statements are correct. The Supreme Court described the CJI's place as temporary pending legislation, while the petitions challenge the 2:1 government majority in the Selection Committee.
62.tq: Check each statement separately, especially the composition ratio and the precise status of the CJI's membership.
62.sec: Universal angles

62.s:
Assertion (A): The Supreme Court observed in May 2026 that the Chief Justice of India's place on the Election Commission selection panel was only temporary.
Reason (R): Petitions challenge the 2:1 government majority in the Selection Committee under the 2023 Act.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
62.x: Both the Assertion and the Reason are true. However, the challenge to the government's 2:1 majority does not by itself explain the Supreme Court's observation that the CJI's place was temporary pending a law.
62.tq: Separate the truth of the two propositions from whether the Reason actually explains the Assertion.
62.sec: Universal angles

62.s: A petition alleges that the Prime Minister's national broadcast during Assembly elections violated which part of the Model Code of Conduct?
o: Part I, dealing with general conduct of candidates
Part IX, dealing with election expenditure
Part VII, dealing with the conduct of the party in power
Part III, dealing with polling-day arrangements
62.x: The petition alleged a violation of Part VII of the Model Code of Conduct, which concerns the conduct of the party in power.
62.tq: Exact-part questions are solved by matching the alleged conduct with the relevant subject of the Code.
62.sec: Universal angles

62.s:
Consider the following statements about the institutional limitations and demands concerning the Election Commission of India:
1. The Election Commission depends on the Department of Personnel and Training, the Law Ministry and the Home Ministry.
2. It has no power over inner-party democracy or party finances.
3. There is a demand that its expenses should be charged on the Consolidated Fund.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
62.x: All three statements are correct. The Commission's dependence on these ministries and its limited authority over internal party democracy and party finances have generated criticism, including the demand for charging its expenses on the Consolidated Fund.
62.tq: Identify the institutional-criticism cluster and verify whether each limitation or reform demand is included.
62.sec: Universal angles

62.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched in the context of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Anil Chandra Punetha — new State Election Commissioner for local-body polls
Anil Chandra Punetha — first Chief Election Commissioner of India
Gyanesh Kumar — State Election Commissioner for local-body polls in Andhra Pradesh
Sukumar Sen — officer associated with 100% SIR digitalisation in ASR district
62.x: Anil Chandra Punetha was identified as the new State Election Commissioner for local-body polls. The other pairs wrongly assign unrelated national or district-level roles.
62.tq: Use the level of jurisdiction to distinguish the State Election Commissioner from the national Election Commission and district administration.
62.sec: Universal angles

63.s: The first pilot use of an Electronic Voting Machine in India was conducted in which constituency and year?
o: Anantnag Assembly constituency, Jammu and Kashmir, in 1998
63.x: EVMs were first used on a pilot basis in the 70-Parur Assembly constituency of Kerala in 1982.
63.tq: Use the exact place-year combination rather than confusing a pilot with a wider trial or statewide use.
63.sec: EVM and VVPAT - FIRST use, EVM statements, VVPAT, SC verification rules  [APPSC]

63.s: The wider trial of Electronic Voting Machines in 1998 covered how many Assembly seats in Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Delhi?
63.x: The wider trial in 1998 covered 16 Assembly seats across Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Delhi.
63.tq: Fix the specific numerical milestone in the EVM timeline.
63.sec: EVM and VVPAT - FIRST use, EVM statements, VVPAT, SC verification rules  [APPSC]

63.s: Electronic Voting Machines were used at all polling stations in a Lok Sabha general election for the first time in:
63.x: The 2004 general election was the first Lok Sabha election in which EVMs were used at all polling stations.
63.tq: Distinguish nationwide polling-station coverage from the first state-level use.
63.sec: EVM and VVPAT - FIRST use, EVM statements, VVPAT, SC verification rules  [APPSC]

63.s: Which of the following statements regarding the manufacture and legal framework of EVMs and VVPATs is correct?
o: They are manufactured only by the Election Commission of India under the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
They are manufactured by BEL and ECIL, and the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 were amended to permit VVPATs.
They are manufactured by the Reserve Bank of India, and the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 prohibit VVPAT use.
They are manufactured by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, and VVPATs were authorised by the Constitution.
63.x: Bharat Electronics Limited and Electronics Corporation of India Limited manufacture the machines. The Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 were amended to enable VVPAT use.
63.tq: Check both the manufacturing bodies and the specific legal instrument instead of accepting a constitutional or ministry attribution.
63.sec: EVM and VVPAT - FIRST use, EVM statements, VVPAT, SC verification rules  [APPSC]

63.s: In N. Chandrababu Naidu v. Union of India (2019), VVPAT slips of how many randomly selected EVMs per Assembly segment were directed to be counted?
63.x: The Supreme Court directed counting of VVPAT slips from five randomly selected EVMs in each Assembly segment.
63.tq: Identify the court case through its distinctive verification number.
63.sec: EVM and VVPAT - FIRST use, EVM statements, VVPAT, SC verification rules  [APPSC]

63.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Supreme Court's 2024 decision in ADR v. ECI:
1. The demand for ballot paper voting and counting of 100 per cent VVPAT slips was rejected.
2. Symbol-loading units are to be sealed and preserved for 45 days.
3. A runner-up in second or third position may seek checking of 5 per cent of EVMs per segment within seven days.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
63.x: All three statements correctly describe the verification rules associated with ADR v. ECI in April 2024.
63.tq: Test a cluster of linked judicial safeguards using the coded combination options.
63.sec: EVM and VVPAT - FIRST use, EVM statements, VVPAT, SC verification rules  [APPSC]

63.s: VVPAT slips must be counted in which of the following circumstances?
o: Whenever EVM data and Form 17C do not match
Whenever postal ballots exceed the number of EVM votes
Only in constituencies using postal ballots
Only when the winning candidate requests it after the declaration of results
63.x: VVPAT slips are required to be counted wherever the EVM data and Form 17C do not match.
63.tq: Apply the verification rule to a specific discrepancy rather than to a general recount demand.
63.sec: EVM and VVPAT - FIRST use, EVM statements, VVPAT, SC verification rules  [APPSC]

63.s: Which one of the following features was specified for EVMs in relation to candidate identification?
o: They must display the candidates' party manifestos.
They must show black-and-white photographs of polling agents.
They must show colour photographs of the candidates.
They must display only the candidates' election symbols without names.
63.x: EVMs are to display colour photographs of the candidates.
63.tq: Use the precise official feature and reject nearby but unsupported display requirements.
63.sec: EVM and VVPAT - FIRST use, EVM statements, VVPAT, SC verification rules  [APPSC]

63.s:
Which of the following is the correct order of counting-related procedures?
A. Counting of postal ballots
B. Counting of the penultimate EVM/VVPAT round
C. Counting of the final EVM/VVPAT round
63.x: Postal ballots are counted before the penultimate EVM/VVPAT round; the final EVM/VVPAT round follows subsequently.
63.tq: Arrange the procedure by identifying the expressly stated precedence of postal-ballot counting.
63.sec: EVM and VVPAT - FIRST use, EVM statements, VVPAT, SC verification rules  [APPSC]

63.s:
With reference to totalisers, consider the following statements:
1. A totaliser combines the counting of several EVMs.
2. It is intended to conceal booth-wise voting trends.
3. The Election Commission has stated that a legal framework for totalisers already exists.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
63.x: A totaliser combines several EVM counts to hide booth-wise trends. The ECI stated that no legal framework for totalisers exists, making statement 3 false.
63.tq: Spot the reversed institutional position in the third statement.
63.sec: EVM and VVPAT - FIRST use, EVM statements, VVPAT, SC verification rules  [APPSC]

63.s: Which one of the following pairs relating to Delimitation Commissions is NOT correctly matched?
63.x: The 1973 Commission was chaired by Justice J.L. Kapur. Justice Kuldip Singh chaired the 2002 Commission.
63.tq: Find the swapped chairperson in a date-person matching question.
63.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

63.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the years of the Delimitation Acts from the years in which the corresponding Commissions were constituted?
63.x: The Delimitation Acts were enacted in 1952, 1962, 1972 and 2002, while the Commissions were constituted in 1952, 1963, 1973 and 2002.
63.tq: Separate the closely related years of legislation from the years of constitution of the Commissions.
63.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

63.s:
Read the following statements:
1. Article 82 deals with readjustment of Lok Sabha constituencies after each census.
2. Article 170 deals with readjustment of State Legislative Assembly constituencies after each census.
3. Articles 330 and 332 relate to reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
63.x: Articles 82 and 170 provide for readjustment relating to Parliament and State Assemblies, while Articles 330 and 332 concern SC/ST seat reservation.
63.tq: Match constitutional Articles with their institutional subject before selecting the coded combination.
63.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

63.s: Delimitation primarily refers to:
o: Fixing the number of seats and the boundaries of Lok Sabha and Assembly constituencies
Allocating ministerial portfolios among political parties
Determining the expenditure limit of each political party
Preparing the electoral roll for municipal elections only
63.x: Delimitation is the fixing of the number of seats and boundaries of Lok Sabha and State Assembly constituencies.
63.tq: Choose the definition that covers both the numerical and territorial aspects of delimitation.
63.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

63.s: The constitutional principle underlying delimitation is best expressed as:
o: One State, one vote, one value
One district, one representative, one value
One party, one constituency, one value
One person, one vote, one value
63.x: Delimitation rests on the principle of ‘one person, one vote, one value’, associated with uniformity of representation under Article 81(2).
63.tq: Discriminate among similar-looking formulations of the electoral equality principle.
63.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

63.s:
Which of the following statements about the Delimitation Commission is correct?
1. It is constituted under an Act of Parliament.
2. It works with the Election Commission of India.
3. Its orders may be modified by either House of Parliament.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
63.x: The Commission is constituted under parliamentary legislation and works with the ECI. Its orders cannot be modified by the Lok Sabha or State Legislative Assemblies, so statement 3 is false.
63.tq: Use the ‘wrong authority’ trap to test who can modify delimitation orders.
63.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

63.s: Which of the following statements regarding the legal status of delimitation orders is correct?
o: They require approval by each State Assembly before becoming effective.
They cannot be challenged in a court and cannot be modified by the Lok Sabha or State Assemblies.
They can be challenged before any High Court as a matter of right.
They can be modified by the Lok Sabha through a simple resolution.
63.x: Delimitation Commission orders enjoy finality: they cannot be challenged in court or modified by the Lok Sabha or State Legislative Assemblies.
63.tq: Test the exceptional finality of a statutory Commission’s orders.
63.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

63.s:
Arrange the following Delimitation Commissions in chronological order:
A. Commission chaired by Justice Kuldip Singh
B. Commission chaired by Justice J.L. Kapur constituted in 1963
C. Commission chaired by Justice N. Chandrasekhara Aiyar
D. Commission chaired by Justice J.L. Kapur constituted in 1973
63.x: The Commissions were constituted in 1952, 1963, 1973 and 2002 respectively: N. Chandrasekhara Aiyar, J.L. Kapur, J.L. Kapur and Kuldip Singh.
63.tq: Anchor the sequence to the four constitution years rather than the repeated name of the chairperson.
63.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

63.s: Which Constitutional Amendment froze inter-State allocation of seats until 2000 on the basis of the 1971 Census?
63.x: The 42nd Amendment of 1976 froze inter-State seat allocation until 2000, using the 1971 Census as the basis.
63.tq: Link the amendment number with both its year and the census basis.
63.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

63.s:
Consider the following statements about the 84th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2001:
1. It extended the freeze on inter-State seat allocation until after the first census following 2026.
2. It permitted rationalisation of constituencies on the basis of the 1991 Census.
3. It changed the total number of Lok Sabha seats on the basis of the 2001 Census.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
63.x: The 84th Amendment extended the freeze and allowed rationalisation using the 1991 Census. It did not change the total number of seats on the basis of the 2001 Census.
63.tq: Separate rationalisation of boundaries from alteration of the total number of seats.
63.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

63.s: The principal effect of the 87th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 was to:
o: Use the 2001 Census for redrawing boundaries without changing the total number of seats
End the freeze on inter-State seat allocation immediately
Restore the 1971 Census as the basis for delimitation and increase total seats
Abolish the Delimitation Commission and transfer its functions to Parliament
63.x: The 87th Amendment substituted the 2001 Census for boundary redrawing while keeping the total number of seats unchanged.
63.tq: Distinguish boundary redrawing from an increase in the total seat allocation.
63.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

63.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Jammu and Kashmir Delimitation Commission — Justice Ranjana Desai
2. Assam delimitation — Election Commission of India
3. Assam delimitation became effective — August 2023
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
63.x: The Jammu and Kashmir Commission was headed by Justice Ranjana Desai, while Assam was delimited by the ECI with effect from August 2023.
63.tq: Combine the authority, chairperson and effective date to avoid state-wise confusion.
63.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

63.s: The orders of the Jammu and Kashmir Delimitation Commission headed by Justice Ranjana Desai became effective in:
63.x: The Jammu and Kashmir delimitation orders became effective in March and May 2022.
63.tq: Retain the paired effective months rather than only the year of the Commission’s work.
63.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

63.s: Which one of the following statements about the Tamil Nadu Assembly resolution is NOT correct?
o: It proposed freezing the Lok Sabha at 543 seats permanently.
It proposed retaining a 2.2:1 Lok Sabha to Rajya Sabha ratio.
It linked the proposed women’s quota to delimitation from 2029.
It proposed women’s quota from 2029 without linking it to delimitation.
63.x: The resolution proposed women’s reservation from 2029 without linking it to delimitation. It also proposed a permanent freeze at 543 Lok Sabha seats and retention of the 2.2:1 ratio.
63.tq: Locate the reversal of an expressly stated condition in a policy-resolution question.
63.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

63.s: The present number of elected Lok Sabha seats, as distinguished from the constitutional ceiling mentioned, is:
63.x: The Lok Sabha has 543 elected seats against a ceiling of 550, comprising 530 seats for States and 20 for Union Territories in the stated allocation framework.
63.tq: Distinguish the existing elected strength from the maximum ceiling.
63.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

63.s: The ceiling of 550 Lok Sabha seats mentioned in the constitutional framework consists of:
o: 500 seats for States and 50 seats for Union Territories
543 seats for States and 7 seats for Union Territories
520 seats for States and 30 seats for Union Territories
530 seats for States and 20 seats for Union Territories
63.x: The stated ceiling comprises 530 seats for the States and 20 seats for the Union Territories.
63.tq: Break a total into its State and Union Territory components.
63.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

63.s: Since which year have the per-State Lok Sabha seat numbers remained unchanged, as stated in the context of delimitation?
63.x: The per-State Lok Sabha seat numbers have remained unchanged since 1976.
63.tq: Separate the year of the constitutional freeze from the census years associated with it.
63.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

63.s: Which of the following statements about the former Anglo-Indian representation in the Lok Sabha is correct?
o: The two Anglo-Indian seats ended in 2020, making the older ceiling description outdated.
The Anglo-Indian seats were transferred to the Rajya Sabha in 2020.
The Anglo-Indian seats were increased from two to twenty in 2020.
The two Anglo-Indian seats continue to form part of the present elected strength.
63.x: The two Anglo-Indian nominated seats ended in 2020. Therefore, the older description of a maximum of 552 seats including two Anglo-Indians is stale.
63.tq: Identify the time-sensitive constitutional change behind an outdated numerical claim.
63.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

63.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the relationship between Articles 81(2), 82 and 170 in delimitation?
o: Article 81(2) expresses uniformity of representation, while Articles 82 and 170 provide for constituency readjustment for Parliament and State Assemblies respectively.
Articles 82 and 170 prescribe the powers of the Election Commission but not constituency readjustment.
Article 81(2) deals only with Panchayat elections, while Articles 82 and 170 concern presidential elections.
Article 82 concerns Rajya Sabha elections and Article 170 concerns municipal elections.
63.x: Article 81(2) embodies uniformity of representation, while Articles 82 and 170 provide the constitutional basis for readjustment of Lok Sabha and Assembly constituencies.
63.tq: Map each Article to its distinct constitutional function rather than its broad election subject.
63.sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

63.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the NETA app is correct?
o: It enables voters to rate their elected representatives and was built by a private start-up.
It is used exclusively for filing election petitions before the High Courts.
It was conceptualised and developed by the Election Commission of India.
It enables citizens to report Model Code of Conduct violations with geo-tagged photographs.
63.x: The NETA app allows voters to rate their representatives and was built by a private start-up, not conceptualised by the Election Commission of India.
63.tq: Distinguish the private NETA app from official Election Commission applications.
63.sec: Voter facilitation - ECI apps, postal ballot, election ink

63.s:
Consider the following statements regarding cVIGIL:
1. It enables citizens to report violations of the Model Code of Conduct.
2. Photographs or videos accompanying a complaint may be geo-tagged.
3. The system provides for action within 100 minutes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
63.x: cVIGIL enables citizens to report Model Code violations using geo-tagged photographs or videos, with action envisaged within 100 minutes.
63.tq: Check whether all three operational features belong to the same application.
63.sec: Voter facilitation - ECI apps, postal ballot, election ink

63.s: ECINET is associated with which one of the following functions?
o: Merging more than 40 Election Commission applications and websites into one platform
Issuing election petitions directly to the Supreme Court
Providing only postal ballots to service voters
63.x: ECINET is a unified platform that merges more than 40 Election Commission applications and websites.
63.tq: Identify the precise institutional function of the named digital platform.
63.sec: Voter facilitation - ECI apps, postal ballot, election ink

63.s:
The Voter Helpline app is primarily used for which of the following purposes?
1. Searching for a name in the electoral roll
2. Filing forms and complaints
3. Reporting violations through geo-tagged videos only
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
63.x: The Voter Helpline app helps users search the electoral roll and file forms and complaints. Reporting Model Code violations through geo-tagged photographs or videos is associated with cVIGIL.
63.tq: Separate closely related functions of different Election Commission apps.
63.sec: Voter facilitation - ECI apps, postal ballot, election ink

63.s:
Which of the following categories of electors are entitled to use postal ballots?
1. Service voters
2. Special voters
3. Electors on election duty
4. Persons in preventive detention
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
63.x: The listed categories—service voters, special voters, electors on election duty and persons in preventive detention—are covered by postal-ballot provisions.
63.tq: Test completeness of a statutory-category list rather than recalling a single category.
63.sec: Voter facilitation - ECI apps, postal ballot, election ink

63.s: The indelible election ink used in India is manufactured by which organisation and is based on which substance?
o: Mysore Paints and Varnish Ltd; silver nitrate
63.x: Indelible election ink is manufactured by Mysore Paints and Varnish Ltd and is based on silver nitrate.
63.tq: Use the manufacturer–ingredient pair to avoid a two-part factual trap.
63.sec: Voter facilitation - ECI apps, postal ballot, election ink

63.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Voter Helpline app — Search name in electoral roll
ECINET — Exclusive platform for election petitions
63.x: ECINET is a unified platform merging more than 40 Election Commission applications and websites; it is not an exclusive platform for election petitions.
63.tq: Find the mismatched purpose among closely related electoral initiatives.
63.sec: Voter facilitation - ECI apps, postal ballot, election ink

63.s:
Consider the following measures relating to polling stations:
1. The maximum number of electors assigned to a polling station is 1,200.
2. A facility is provided for depositing mobile phones at polling booths.
3. Candidate booths are to be located just beyond 100 metres from the polling station.
4. Candidate photographs on EVMs have been redesigned in colour.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
63.x: The measures include a 1,200-elector cap, mobile-deposit facilities, colour candidate photographs on EVMs and candidate booths just beyond 100 metres from polling stations.
63.tq: Treat each administrative measure as an independent statement and verify the complete set.
63.sec: Voter facilitation - ECI apps, postal ballot, election ink

63.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 330 — Reservation of seats for SCs and STs in State Legislative Assemblies
Article 332 — Reservation of seats for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha
Article 330 — Reservation of seats for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha
Article 334 — Establishment of the Election Commission
63.x: Article 330 provides for reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha, while Article 332 concerns State Legislative Assemblies.
63.tq: Use the Article–institution pairing and reject neighbouring-Article swaps.
63.sec: Reserved and special constituencies - SC/ST seats, floating constituencies

63.s:
With reference to reserved Lok Sabha constituencies in Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. Amalapuram is a Scheduled Caste-reserved constituency.
2. Araku is a Scheduled Tribe-reserved constituency.
3. Tirupati is a Scheduled Tribe-reserved constituency.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
63.x: Amalapuram and Tirupati are Scheduled Caste-reserved constituencies in Andhra Pradesh, whereas Araku is the Scheduled Tribe-reserved constituency.
63.tq: Discriminate between SC and ST constituencies within the same State.
63.sec: Reserved and special constituencies - SC/ST seats, floating constituencies

63.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the reservation pattern in the Lok Sabha for Telangana?
63.x: Telangana has three Scheduled Caste-reserved and two Scheduled Tribe-reserved Lok Sabha constituencies.
63.tq: Compare the State-wise SC/ST figures without reversing the categories.
63.sec: Reserved and special constituencies - SC/ST seats, floating constituencies

63.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (State)
A. Andhra Pradesh — Lok Sabha
B. Andhra Pradesh — Legislative Assembly
C. Telangana — Lok Sabha
D. Telangana — Legislative Assembly

List-II (Number of SC/ST reserved seats)
1. 4 / 1
2. 29 / 7
3. 3 / 2
4. 19 / 12

Code:
63.x: Andhra Pradesh has 4 SC and 1 ST Lok Sabha seats and 29 SC and 7 ST Assembly seats. Telangana has 3 SC and 2 ST Lok Sabha seats and 19 SC and 12 ST Assembly seats.
63.tq: Start with the sure State–House pair and then complete the numerical matching.
63.sec: Reserved and special constituencies - SC/ST seats, floating constituencies

63.s:
Which of the following statements correctly describes the allocation of SC and ST reserved constituencies?
1. ST seats are generally located where the share of the ST population is highest.
2. SC seats are spread across the State and rotated at each delimitation.
3. All voters in a reserved constituency, and not merely voters belonging to the reserved community, may vote.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
63.x: ST seats are concentrated in areas with the highest ST population share, SC seats are spread and rotated at delimitation, and reserved constituencies have a common electorate of all voters.
63.tq: Combine location, rotation and electorate principles in one reservation question.
63.sec: Reserved and special constituencies - SC/ST seats, floating constituencies

63.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Article 334 is correct?
o: The original period of reservation was 5 years and it ended in 1955.
The Article deals exclusively with reservation in local bodies.
The provision originally applied for 20 years, up to 1970, without later extension.
The original period of reservation was 10 years, up to 1960, and it has been repeatedly extended.
63.x: Article 334 originally provided for a ten-year period, up to 1960, and the reservation period has been repeatedly extended by constitutional amendments.
63.tq: Use the original time limit and the subsequent-extension feature together.
63.sec: Reserved and special constituencies - SC/ST seats, floating constituencies

63.s:
Which of the following statements about Anglo-Indian representation is correct?
1. The President could nominate two Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha.
2. The Governor could nominate one Anglo-Indian to a State Legislative Assembly.
3. These provisions were ended by the 104th Constitutional Amendment.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
63.x: Articles 331 and 333 provided for nomination of two Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha by the President and one to a State Assembly by the Governor. The 104th Amendment ended these provisions.
63.tq: Check the authority, number and constitutional termination together.
63.sec: Reserved and special constituencies - SC/ST seats, floating constituencies

63.s:
The constitutional provision for reservation of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies under the 106th Amendment provides for which of the following?
1. One-third reservation of seats
2. Reservation for 15 years
3. Rotation after each delimitation
4. Immediate operation irrespective of census and delimitation
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
63.x: The 106th Amendment provides one-third reservation for 15 years, with rotation after each delimitation. Its operation begins only after the next census and delimitation; therefore statement 4 is false.
63.tq: Spot the false immediacy claim in a statement about commencement of constitutional reservation.
63.sec: Reserved and special constituencies - SC/ST seats, floating constituencies

63.s: A constituency having no fixed geographical boundary, such as the Sangha seat in Sikkim, is known as a:
63.x: A floating constituency has no fixed geographical boundary. The Sangha constituency in Sikkim is an example in which only registered Buddhist monks vote and contest.
63.tq: Identify the exact electoral term from its defining geographical feature.
63.sec: Reserved and special constituencies - SC/ST seats, floating constituencies

63.s:
With reference to the Sangha constituency in Sikkim, consider the following statements:
1. It is an example of a floating constituency.
2. Only registered Buddhist monks can vote and contest in it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
63.x: The Sangha seat has no fixed geographical boundary and is restricted to registered Buddhist monks as electors and candidates.
63.tq: Test both defining features of a special constituency rather than just its name.
