63.sec: Reserved and special constituencies - SC/ST seats, floating constituencies

63.s:
Match the type of election with its description:

List-I
A. General election
B. Mid-term election
C. By-election

List-II
1. Election to a legislature dissolved before expiry of its normal term
2. Election held for a single vacancy, ordinarily within six months
3. Election held at the normal end of the legislature’s term

Code:
63.x: A general election is held at the normal end of a legislature’s term, a mid-term election follows premature dissolution, and a by-election fills a single vacancy, ordinarily within six months.
63.tq: Match each election type with its timing and purpose.
63.sec: Reserved and special constituencies - SC/ST seats, floating constituencies

63.s: Under Section 80 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, an election can be called in question only by means of:
o: A writ petition before the District Court
A reference by the Election Commission
63.x: Section 80 provides that no election can be called in question except by an election petition. The constitutional basis is Article 329(b).
63.tq: Distinguish the statutory bar in Section 80 from the filing period in Section 81.
63.sec: Election petitions - RPA 1951 Section 81, court, grounds

63.s: An election petition under Section 81 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, must ordinarily be presented within:
o: 45 days of the election of the returned candidate
60 days of the declaration of poll
30 days of the notification of election
90 days of the constitution of the House
63.x: Section 81 requires an election petition to be presented within 45 days of the election of the returned candidate.
63.tq: Separate the 45-day filing period from the separate Section 80 rule and Section 100 grounds.
63.sec: Election petitions - RPA 1951 Section 81, court, grounds

63.s: Which court ordinarily tries an election petition under the Representation of the People Act, 1951?
o: Supreme Court in the first instance
63.x: Under Section 80A, an election petition is tried by the High Court. An appeal lies to the Supreme Court.
63.tq: Identify the court of original trial and distinguish it from the appellate court.
63.sec: Election petitions - RPA 1951 Section 81, court, grounds

63.s:
Consider the following grounds for declaring an election void under Section 100 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951:
1. The returned candidate was not qualified or was disqualified.
2. A corrupt practice was committed.
3. A nomination was improperly rejected.
4. Improper acceptance of votes or breach of the Constitution or the Act affected the result.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
63.x: All four circumstances are recognised grounds under Section 100 for declaring an election void, subject to the statutory requirements concerning their effect on the election result where applicable.
63.tq: Test the complete statutory list of grounds rather than relying on a single familiar ground.
63.sec: Election petitions - RPA 1951 Section 81, court, grounds

63.s: Which one of the following statements regarding disposal of election petitions is correct?
o: The Supreme Court tries every election petition directly and no appeal is permitted.
The Election Commission must decide the petition within six months, with no appeal.
The District Court must decide the petition within three months, with appeal to the High Court.
The High Court is required to try to decide the petition within six months, and an appeal lies to the Supreme Court.
63.x: The High Court should try to decide an election petition within six months, and an appeal lies to the Supreme Court.
63.tq: Use the court hierarchy and time expectation to reject authority swaps.
63.sec: Election petitions - RPA 1951 Section 81, court, grounds

63.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the present legal location of electoral offences such as bribery, undue influence and personation?
o: They remain in IPC Chapter IXA only.
They are contained in BNS Chapter IX, Sections 169 to 177, from 1 July 2024.
They are dealt with only under Section 81 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
They are contained in the Constitution under Article 329(b).
63.x: From 1 July 2024, electoral offences such as bribery, undue influence and personation are placed in Chapter IX of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, Sections 169–177. Earlier, they were in Chapter IXA of the IPC.
63.tq: Track the transition from the IPC provision to the corresponding BNS chapter and sections.
63.sec: Election petitions - RPA 1951 Section 81, court, grounds

63.s:
Match the following provisions of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 with their contents:

List-I
A. Section 80
B. Section 80A
C. Section 81
D. Section 100

List-II
1. Grounds for declaring an election void
2. Petition to be presented within 45 days
3. No election may be called in question except by an election petition
4. Election petition to be tried by the High Court

Code:
63.x: Section 80 contains the election-petition bar, Section 80A specifies the High Court, Section 81 prescribes 45 days, and Section 100 lists grounds for declaring an election void.
63.tq: Start with the distinctive Section 80 and Section 100 pairs, then resolve the two procedural provisions.
63.sec: Election petitions - RPA 1951 Section 81, court, grounds

63.s:
Assertion (A): The rule that an election cannot be called in question except by an election petition is contained in Section 80 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
Reason (R): Section 81 prescribes the period within which an election petition must be presented.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
63.x: Both statements are true, but the 45-day filing period under Section 81 does not explain the separate rule in Section 80 requiring an election petition to question an election.
63.tq: Separate two true neighbouring statutory provisions and test whether the Reason actually explains the Assertion.
63.sec: Election petitions - RPA 1951 Section 81, court, grounds

63.s: Recognition of political parties under the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968 is distinct from registration under which provision?
o: Section 19 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950
Paragraph 16A of the Election Symbols Order, 1968
Section 29A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951
63.x: Recognition is governed by the Election Symbols Order, 1968, whereas registration of political parties is under Section 29A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
63.tq: Separate the similar-looking concepts of registration and recognition by identifying the governing provision.
63.sec: National and state party recognition - criteria, number of national parties  [APPSC]

63.s: Which one of the following is a valid criterion for recognition as a National Party?
o: Securing 8% of valid votes in one State
Recognition as a State Party in four or more States
Winning one Lok Sabha seat for every 25 seats allotted to a State
Recognition as a State Party in two or more States
63.x: Recognition as a State Party in four or more States is one of the alternative criteria for recognition as a National Party.
63.tq: Distinguish the national-party threshold from the nearby state-party thresholds.
63.sec: National and state party recognition - criteria, number of national parties  [APPSC]

63.s:
Which of the following combinations correctly represents criteria for recognition as a State Party? 

1. Six per cent of votes in the Assembly election and two seats
2. Six per cent of votes in the Lok Sabha election and one Lok Sabha seat
3. Three per cent of Assembly seats or three seats, whichever is more
4. Eight per cent of valid votes

Select the correct answer:
63.x: All four listed conditions are alternative criteria for recognition as a State Party, including the Assembly, Lok Sabha, seat-share and 8% vote conditions.
63.tq: Check each alternative threshold independently before selecting the coded combination.
63.sec: National and state party recognition - criteria, number of national parties  [APPSC]

63.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Model Code of Conduct:

1. It is a set of guidelines issued by the Election Commission for political parties, candidates and the ruling government.
2. It is a statutory law enacted by Parliament.
3. Its authority is associated with the plenary power of the Election Commission under Article 324.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
63.x: The Model Code is a set of ECI guidelines and is supported by the Commission's plenary power under Article 324. It is not a statutory law enacted by Parliament.
63.tq: Spot the wrong legal-status statement while retaining the correct authority-based statements.
63.sec: Model Code of Conduct - legal status, authority, enforcement  [APPSC]

63.s:
Arrange the following milestones relating to the Model Code of Conduct in chronological order:

A. Part VII relating to the party in power was added
B. The Code was first drafted by the Kerala Government
C. The Code was revised
D. The Code was formalised by the Election Commission

Select the correct sequence.
63.x: The sequence is 1960 drafting by Kerala, 1968 formalisation by the ECI, 1974 revision, and 1979 addition of Part VII.
63.tq: Fix the earliest and latest milestones first, then place the 1968 and 1974 events.
63.sec: Model Code of Conduct - legal status, authority, enforcement  [APPSC]

63.s: The Model Code of Conduct was first used in which election?
63.x: The Model Code of Conduct was first used in the 1960 Kerala Assembly election.
63.tq: Distinguish first use from later formalisation and revision dates.
63.sec: Model Code of Conduct - legal status, authority, enforcement  [APPSC]

63.s: Who enforced the Model Code of Conduct with particular strictness in 1991?
63.x: Chief Election Commissioner T. N. Seshan enforced the Model Code of Conduct with rigour in 1991.
63.tq: Apply the wrong-person-with-the-deed trap to distinguish election officials and judges.
63.sec: Model Code of Conduct - legal status, authority, enforcement  [APPSC]

63.s: According to the ruling in Harbans Singh Jalal v Union of India, the Model Code of Conduct comes into force:
o: On the date of publication of election results
On announcement of the election schedule
63.x: The Punjab and Haryana High Court held in 1997 that the Model Code comes into force when the election schedule is announced.
63.tq: Identify the operative trigger instead of confusing it with nomination, polling or result dates.
63.sec: Model Code of Conduct - legal status, authority, enforcement  [APPSC]

63.s: Which one of the following is NOT a restriction under Part VII of the Model Code of Conduct?
o: Introducing new schemes or grants after announcement of polls
Using official machinery or transport for campaigning
Continuing ordinary official visits without combining them with electioneering
63.x: Part VII restricts combining official visits with electioneering, using official machinery or transport for campaigning, and introducing new schemes or grants after polls are announced.
63.tq: Find the option that does not describe a prohibited act under the specific part of the Code.
63.sec: Model Code of Conduct - legal status, authority, enforcement  [APPSC]

63.s: Part VII of the Model Code of Conduct primarily governs the conduct of:
o: Candidates who have lost the election
63.x: Part VII, added in 1979, contains provisions concerning the party in power and the use of governmental machinery during elections.
63.tq: Link a named part of the Code with its specific institutional subject.
63.sec: Model Code of Conduct - legal status, authority, enforcement  [APPSC]

63.s: Which of the following may be imposed for violation of the Model Code of Conduct?
o: Dissolution of Parliament by the Chief Election Commissioner
Censure and, in serious cases, suspension or withdrawal of recognition under Paragraph 16A
Cancellation of the Constitution by the President
Automatic imprisonment by the Election Commission
63.x: The Election Commission may censure a party and may suspend or withdraw recognition under Paragraph 16A of the Symbols Order in appropriate cases.
63.tq: Ask who can impose which sanction and reject powers that belong to no election authority.
63.sec: Model Code of Conduct - legal status, authority, enforcement  [APPSC]

63.s:
With reference to the Model Code of Conduct, consider the following statements:

1. It was formalised by the Election Commission in 1968.
2. Part VII was added in 1979.
3. It is lifted immediately when polling ends, even before declaration of results.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
63.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Code is lifted once results are declared, not immediately when polling ends.
63.tq: Use the time-word trap in statement 3 while verifying the two historical milestones.
63.sec: Model Code of Conduct - legal status, authority, enforcement  [APPSC]

63.s: The Model Code of Conduct was lifted in Assam, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal and Puducherry on 7 May 2026, except in respect of:
63.x: The Code was lifted in the listed jurisdictions on 7 May 2026, except for the Falta re-poll seat.
63.tq: Use precise exception-based recall for a date-linked administrative action.
63.sec: Model Code of Conduct - legal status, authority, enforcement  [APPSC]

63.s: Under Article 326, the right to vote in elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies is based on:
63.x: Article 326 provides for elections based on universal adult suffrage, with the voting age being 18 years.
63.tq: Separate the constitutional voting principle from outdated age and qualification conditions.
63.sec: Right to vote - Article 326, nature, first-past-the-post  [other exams]

63.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the legal nature of the right to vote in India?
o: It is a statutory right under the Representation of the People Acts
It is a constitutional right enforceable only through Article 32
It is an absolute natural right outside the Constitution and statutes
It is a Fundamental Right under Article 19
63.x: The right to vote is a statutory right under the Representation of the People Acts and is not a Fundamental Right.
63.tq: Discriminate among constitutional, fundamental and statutory rights using the exact legal classification.
63.sec: Right to vote - Article 326, nature, first-past-the-post  [other exams]

63.s: A citizen who is disqualified on grounds of non-residence, unsoundness of mind, crime or corrupt or illegal practice is:
o: Entitled to vote only in Rajya Sabha elections
Excluded from the right to vote under the qualifications and disqualifications governing Article 326
Entitled to vote if the person deposits a security amount
Automatically entitled to vote under Article 326
63.x: Article 326 permits voting by citizens aged 18 or above subject to disqualifications such as non-residence, unsoundness of mind, crime and corrupt or illegal practice.
63.tq: Apply the general rule to a fact pattern by checking the stated statutory disqualifications.
63.sec: Universal adult franchise - Article 326, voting age  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

63.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the first-past-the-post system used for Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections?
o: The candidate is elected only after securing more than half of the valid votes.
Seats are distributed strictly in proportion to the total votes polled by each party.
The candidate securing a majority of all registered voters wins.
The candidate securing the highest number of votes in a single-member constituency wins.
63.x: Under the territorial single-member first-past-the-post system, the candidate with the highest plurality of votes wins; an absolute majority is not required.
63.tq: Distinguish plurality from majority and proportional representation.
63.sec: Right to vote - Article 326, nature, first-past-the-post  [other exams]

63.s:
Proportional representation through the single transferable vote is used for elections to which of the following?

1. Rajya Sabha
2. Legislative Councils
3. President and Vice-President
4. Lok Sabha

Select the correct answer:
63.x: Single transferable vote-based proportional representation is used for the Rajya Sabha, Legislative Councils, President and Vice-President. Lok Sabha elections use first-past-the-post.
63.tq: Separate the institutions using proportional representation from those using territorial first-past-the-post.
63.sec: Right to vote - Article 326, nature, first-past-the-post  [other exams]

63.s: Which of the following is NOT cited as a reason for rejecting proportional representation for Lok Sabha elections?
o: It may encourage fragmentation and unstable governments.
It guarantees a direct election in every single-member constituency.
It weakens the voter–Member of Parliament link.
It may be difficult for voters to understand.
63.x: Difficulty for voters, fragmentation, unstable governments, expense, absence of by-elections and a weaker voter–MP link are cited concerns. Guaranteeing direct election in every single-member constituency is not such a reason.
63.tq: Find the option that is outside the stated list of objections to proportional representation.
63.sec: Right to vote - Article 326, nature, first-past-the-post  [other exams]

63.s: A candidate's security deposit is forfeited when the candidate secures less than:
63.x: The security deposit is forfeited if the candidate obtains less than one-sixth of the valid votes.
63.tq: Recall the exact fractional threshold and distinguish it from common one-fourth and one-third distractors.
63.sec: Right to vote - Article 326, nature, first-past-the-post  [other exams]

63.s: The Supreme Court directed the inclusion of a NOTA option on all Electronic Voting Machines in:
o: Harbans Singh Jalal v Union of India, 1997
Mohinder Singh Gill v Chief Election Commissioner, 1978
Kuldip Nayar v Union of India, 2006
63.x: In PUCL v Union of India on 27 September 2013, the Supreme Court directed that a NOTA button be provided on all EVMs.
63.tq: Match the election-related judicial direction with the correct case and year.
63.sec: NOTA - PUCL case, year, effect on result

63.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the electoral effect of NOTA?
o: NOTA votes are transferred to the candidate placed second.
Even if NOTA receives the highest number of votes, the candidate with the highest votes among the contesting candidates is declared elected.
The election is automatically cancelled if NOTA receives the highest votes.
A re-poll is compulsory whenever NOTA exceeds the winning candidate's votes.
63.x: NOTA has no electoral effect on the result. Even when NOTA receives the most votes, the highest-scoring contesting candidate wins.
63.tq: Apply the no-electoral-effect rule to a hypothetical result scenario.
63.sec: NOTA - PUCL case, year, effect on result

63.s: Which of the following statements about the NOTA symbol and its first Lok Sabha use is correct?
o: It is a blank ballot, designed by the Supreme Court, and was first used in 2013.
It is a ballot with a black cross, designed by Parliament, and was first used in 2024.
It is a ballot with a black cross, designed by NID Ahmedabad, and was first used in 2014.
It is a ballot with a red star, designed by the Election Commission, and was first used in 2019.
63.x: The NOTA symbol is a ballot with a black cross, designed by the National Institute of Design, Ahmedabad; it was first used in a Lok Sabha election in 2014.
63.tq: Combine symbol, designing institution and first-use year without confusing the judicial-order year with the implementation year.
63.sec: NOTA - PUCL case, year, effect on result

63.s: The first general election to the Lok Sabha in India was held in:
63.x: India's first general election was held in 1951–52.
63.tq: Distinguish the first election period from the year in which the First Lok Sabha was constituted.
63.sec: Lok Sabha general elections - number, Lok Sabha to year, FIRST election  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

63.s: The 18th Lok Sabha was elected in which year?
63.x: The 18th Lok Sabha was elected in 2024; the 17th Lok Sabha was elected in 2019.
63.tq: Separate consecutive Lok Sabha numbers from their corresponding election years.
63.sec: Lok Sabha general elections - number, Lok Sabha to year, FIRST election  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

63.s:
Match the following Lok Sabhas with the years of their election.

List-I
(a) 1st Lok Sabha
(b) 9th Lok Sabha
(c) 11th Lok Sabha
(d) 16th Lok Sabha

List-II
(i) 1996
(ii) 1952
(iii) 2014
(iv) 1989

Select the correct answer using the code below:
63.x: The 1st, 9th, 11th and 16th Lok Sabhas correspond respectively to 1952, 1989, 1996 and 2014.
63.tq: Start with the fixed 1st Lok Sabha–1952 pair and eliminate codes around it.
63.sec: Lok Sabha general elections - number, Lok Sabha to year, FIRST election  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

63.s: Which one of the following correctly gives the total number of Lok Sabha general elections held so far and the election year of the 17th Lok Sabha?
63.x: There have been 18 Lok Sabha general elections so far, and the 17th Lok Sabha was elected in 2019; the 18th was elected in 2024.
63.tq: Keep the total count separate from the year of the immediately preceding Lok Sabha.
63.sec: Lok Sabha general elections - number, Lok Sabha to year, FIRST election  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

63.s: The Delimitation Order, 2008, presently governing the constituencies of Andhra Pradesh was based on which Census and Commission combination?
o: 1991 Census and Delimitation Commission constituted in 2002
2001 Census and Delimitation Commission constituted in 2008
2011 Census and Delimitation Commission constituted in 2002
2001 Census and Delimitation Commission constituted in 2002
63.x: The Delimitation Order, 2008 was based on the 2001 Census and the Delimitation Commission constituted in 2002.
63.tq: Separate the Census year from the year of the Commission.
63.sec: Delimitation in AP - Delimitation Order 2008, AP Reorganisation Act 2014

63.s: After the reorganisation of Andhra Pradesh, the number of Assembly and Lok Sabha constituencies presently governed by the Delimitation Order, 2008 is respectively:
63.x: The present Andhra Pradesh has 175 Assembly constituencies and 25 Lok Sabha constituencies under the Delimitation Order, 2008 after the 2014 reorganisation.
63.tq: Match the two figures as a constituency pair.
63.sec: Delimitation in AP - Delimitation Order 2008, AP Reorganisation Act 2014

63.s: Section 26 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 provided for increasing the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly seats from 175 to:
63.x: Section 26 envisaged increasing the Andhra Pradesh Assembly strength from 175 to 225, subject to Article 170.
63.tq: Check the proposed figure against the existing strength.
63.sec: Delimitation in AP - Delimitation Order 2008, AP Reorganisation Act 2014

63.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the proposed increase in Assembly seats under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014:
1. Andhra Pradesh Assembly seats were proposed to increase from 175 to 225.
2. Telangana Assembly seats were proposed to increase from 119 to 153.
3. The increase operates independently of Article 170 of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
63.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the proposal is subject to Article 170.
63.tq: Reject the statement that removes an expressly stated constitutional condition.
63.sec: Delimitation in AP - Delimitation Order 2008, AP Reorganisation Act 2014

63.s: Article 170(3) of the Constitution freezes the number of Assembly seats until:
63.x: Article 170(3) freezes Assembly numbers until the first Census after 2026. An earlier increase would require a constitutional amendment.
63.tq: Focus on the exact constitutional time reference.
63.sec: Delimitation in AP - Delimitation Order 2008, AP Reorganisation Act 2014

63.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
63.x: Article 325 provides for one general electoral roll and prohibits exclusion on grounds of religion, race, caste or sex. Article 324 concerns the Election Commission, Article 326 adult suffrage, and Article 329 court-related bars.
63.tq: Use the Article-subject pairing rather than relying on familiar article numbers.
63.sec: Electoral provisions in the Constitution - Part XV, Articles 324-329

63.s: Which Article of the Constitution vests the superintendence, direction and control of elections in the Election Commission of India?
63.x: Article 324 vests the superintendence, direction and control of elections in the Election Commission of India.
63.tq: Identify the constitutional provision from its distinctive power.
63.sec: Electoral provisions in the Constitution - Part XV, Articles 324-329

63.s: Under Article 329, which of the following is correct?
o: Only the Election Commission can decide disputes concerning delimitation laws.
Elections can be challenged only by an election petition, while delimitation laws are barred from being questioned in court.
Delimitation laws may be questioned in any subordinate court.
All election disputes may be directly challenged before any court before polling begins.
63.x: Article 329 bars courts from questioning delimitation laws and provides that an election may be challenged only through an election petition.
63.tq: Choose the option preserving both limbs of the constitutional bar.
63.sec: Electoral provisions in the Constitution - Part XV, Articles 324-329

63.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the qualifying dates for revision of electoral rolls?
63.x: The four qualifying dates are 1 January, 1 April, 1 July and 1 October. 1 December is not a qualifying date.
63.tq: Find the date outside the four-date set.
63.sec: Electoral rolls - qualifying dates, overseas electors, revisions

63.s: The four qualifying dates for enrolment in electoral rolls, introduced through the Election Laws (Amendment) Act, 2021, are:
63.x: The qualifying dates are 1 January, 1 April, 1 July and 1 October.
63.tq: Recall the complete four-date sequence rather than one isolated date.
63.sec: Electoral rolls - qualifying dates, overseas electors, revisions

63.s: An overseas Indian elector may enrol in the electoral roll at:
o: the address of the Indian embassy in the foreign country
any address selected by the elector
the last place of employment in India בלבד
the address of the Indian passport
63.x: Under Section 20A of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, an overseas elector may enrol at the address given in the Indian passport.
63.tq: Apply the special registration rule to the overseas-elector scenario.
63.sec: Electoral rolls - qualifying dates, overseas electors, revisions

63.s: Which one of the following correctly describes a Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls?
o: It rebuilds the electoral roll comprehensively.
It is undertaken only after a general election result.
It is conducted only for overseas electors.
It is an annual summary correction without rebuilding the roll.
63.x: A Special Intensive Revision rebuilds the electoral roll, whereas summary revision is conducted annually.
63.tq: Distinguish the comprehensive revision from the routine annual revision.
63.sec: Electoral rolls - qualifying dates, overseas electors, revisions

63.s: An exit poll is best described as:
o: A survey conducted before the election notification to assess voter intention
A poll of voters taken immediately after they leave the polling station
A survey conducted only among political party workers
A statistical report prepared after the declaration of results
63.x: An exit poll is conducted among voters immediately after they leave the polling station; it is different from an opinion poll.
63.tq: Separate the timing of an exit poll from that of an opinion poll.
63.sec: Exit polls and opinion polls - Section 126A

63.s: Under Section 126A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the prohibition on conducting or publishing exit polls extends from:
o: 48 hours before the first phase until the close of the last phase
the issue of the election notification until the declaration of results
the first nomination date until the last counting day
the start of polling in the first phase until half an hour after the close of polling in the last phase
63.x: Section 126A prohibits conducting or publishing exit polls from the commencement of polling in the first phase until half an hour after polling closes in the last phase.
63.tq: Track both the starting point and the precise end point.
63.sec: Exit polls and opinion polls - Section 126A

63.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes the restrictions on opinion polls and exit polls?
o: Opinion polls are barred for 48 hours before the close of poll, whereas Section 126A covers exit polls across multi-phase polling.
Exit polls are barred only for 48 hours before the close of poll, whereas opinion polls are barred from the first phase.
Both are barred only after the declaration of results.
Neither is subject to a statutory restriction.
63.x: Opinion polls are barred during the 48 hours before the close of poll under Section 126, while Section 126A governs the longer phase-to-phase restriction on exit polls.
63.tq: Compare the two restrictions by both subject and time period.
63.sec: Exit polls and opinion polls - Section 126A

63.s: The formula for election indelible ink is associated with the:
63.x: The formula for the indelible ink comes from the National Physical Laboratory, while Mysore Paints and Varnish Limited manufactures it.
63.tq: Use the manufacturer-versus-formula distinction.
63.sec: Indelible ink - manufacturer, finger, composition

63.s: Indelible ink is ordinarily applied to the:
63.x: Election indelible ink is applied to the left forefinger.
63.tq: Recall the precise finger rather than the general hand.
63.sec: Indelible ink - manufacturer, finger, composition

63.s: The key chemical responsible for the indelible character of election ink is:
63.x: Silver nitrate is the key chemical in election indelible ink.
63.tq: Identify the distinctive chemical component.
63.sec: Indelible ink - manufacturer, finger, composition

63.s: Indelible ink was first used in the Indian general election of:
63.x: Indelible ink was first used in the 1962 general election. The claim that it was first used in Mysore in 1960 is incorrect.
63.tq: Reject the nearby but incorrect preliminary-use year.
63.sec: Indelible ink - manufacturer, finger, composition

63.s: For a Lok Sabha election, the notification commencing the election process is issued by the:
o: Governor, on the recommendation of the Election Commission
President, on the recommendation of the Election Commission
Chief Election Commissioner, without executive recommendation
Union Home Minister, on the recommendation of the President
63.x: Under Section 14 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the President issues the notification for a Lok Sabha election on the Election Commission's recommendation.
63.tq: Ask which constitutional authority issues the notification at Union level.
63.sec: Commencement of the election process - Sections 14 and 15 RPA

63.s: For an Assembly election, the notification commencing the election process is issued by the:
63.x: Under Section 15 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the Governor issues the notification for a State Assembly election on the Election Commission's recommendation.
63.tq: Match the level of election with the issuing authority and section.
63.sec: Commencement of the election process - Sections 14 and 15 RPA

63.s: Which authority fixes the election schedule and nomination dates?
63.x: The Election Commission fixes the election schedule and nomination dates, while the President or Governor issues the formal notification as applicable.
63.tq: Distinguish the authority fixing the schedule from the authority issuing the notification.
63.sec: Commencement of the election process - Sections 14 and 15 RPA

63.s: A by-election to fill a casual vacancy is ordinarily required to be held within:
63.x: A by-election is ordinarily held within six months of a vacancy, subject to the stated exceptions.
63.tq: Recall the statutory time limit before considering exceptions.
63.sec: Commencement of the election process - Sections 14 and 15 RPA

63.s: The six-month requirement for a by-election does NOT apply when:
o: the vacancy occurs in a reserved constituency
the election is held during the monsoon season
the constituency has more than one polling station
the remaining term is under one year or the Election Commission certifies difficulty after consulting the Centre
63.x: The exceptions are where the remaining term is less than one year or the Election Commission, after consulting the Central Government, certifies difficulty in holding the election.
63.tq: Look for the option containing both statutory exceptions.
63.sec: Commencement of the election process - Sections 14 and 15 RPA

63.s: Which of the following persons is eligible for the absentee-voter postal ballot category on the basis of age?
o: A citizen aged 90 years or above only
A citizen aged 80 years or above
A citizen aged 75 years or above
A citizen aged 85 years or above
63.x: The senior-citizen threshold for the absentee-voter postal ballot category is 85 years or above, raised from 80 years.
63.tq: Notice the revised threshold rather than the former age limit.
63.sec: Postal ballot and home voting - eligible categories and age

63.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the listed categories eligible for postal ballot or home voting?
o: All private-sector employees irrespective of election duty
Persons with benchmark disability of 40 per cent or more
63.x: The listed categories include senior citizens aged 85 or above, persons with benchmark disability of 40 per cent or more, essential-service staff on duty, service voters, election-duty electors and persons under preventive detention.
63.tq: Identify the overbroad category that is not recognised in the specified list.
63.sec: Postal ballot and home voting - eligible categories and age

63.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the election officer's role?
o: Returning Officer — conducts the poll in a constituency and declares the result
District Election Officer — manufactures indelible ink
Chief Electoral Officer — issues election petitions
Electoral Registration Officer — appoints the Election Commission
63.x: The Returning Officer conducts the poll in a constituency and declares the result. The other roles are incorrectly assigned.
63.tq: Start with the officer whose constituency-level function is distinctive.
63.sec: Election machinery - CEO, DEO, Returning Officer, observers

63.s: The District Election Officer is generally the:
63.x: At the district level, the District Election Officer is usually the Collector.
63.tq: Match the district-level election designation with the usual administrative office.
63.sec: Election machinery - CEO, DEO, Returning Officer, observers

63.s: Under Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, expense accounts are received within 30 days by the:
63.x: The District Election Officer receives election expense accounts within 30 days under Section 78.
63.tq: Pair the statutory section with the responsible officer.
63.sec: Election machinery - CEO, DEO, Returning Officer, observers

63.s: Which of the following is NOT a category of observer appointed by the Election Commission under Section 20B?
63.x: The listed observer categories are general, police and expenditure observers. Judicial observer is not among them.
63.tq: Find the role outside the three-member observer set.
63.sec: Election machinery - CEO, DEO, Returning Officer, observers

63.s:
Consider the following statements about election machinery:
1. The Chief Electoral Officer assists the Election Commission in each State or Union Territory.
2. Electoral Registration Officers and Booth Level Officers are associated with electoral rolls.
3. Booth Level Officers now carry standard photo identity cards.
4. The Election Commission has no control over officers deployed on poll duty.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
63.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the Election Commission controls officers on poll duty and may transfer them or act against partisan conduct.
63.tq: Reject the absolute statement denying the Election Commission's supervisory control.
63.sec: Election machinery - CEO, DEO, Returning Officer, observers

63.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Representation of the People Act, 1951 — only Panchayat elections
Representation of the People Act, 1950 — corrupt practices and election petitions
Representation of the People Act, 1951 — allocation of seats and electoral rolls
Representation of the People Act, 1950 — electoral rolls and delimitation
63.x: The Representation of the People Act, 1950 deals with allocation of seats, delimitation and electoral rolls. The 1951 Act deals with the conduct of elections, corrupt practices and election petitions.
63.tq: Separate the administrative electoral-roll statute from the election-conduct statute.
63.sec: RPA 1950 vs RPA 1951 - subjects

63.s: Which of the following subjects is governed primarily by the Representation of the People Act, 1951?
o: Registration of political parties under Section 29A
Revision of electoral rolls under Section 21
63.x: Section 29A, concerning registration of political parties, belongs to the Representation of the People Act, 1951. Electoral-roll eligibility, roll revision, allocation of seats and delimitation are associated with the 1950 Act.
63.tq: Use the section number to identify the correct Act.
63.sec: RPA 1950 vs RPA 1951 - subjects

63.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Section 19, RPA 1950 — voter eligibility
2. Section 21, RPA 1950 — revision of electoral rolls
3. Section 8, RPA 1951 — disqualifications
4. Sections 77–78, RPA 1951 — election expense accounts
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
63.x: All four pairs are correctly matched: Sections 19 and 21 belong to the 1950 Act, while Sections 8 and 77–78 belong to the 1951 Act.
63.tq: Verify each section-Act pairing before selecting the combined option.
63.sec: RPA 1950 vs RPA 1951 - subjects

63.s: The Supreme Court hearing on EVM totalisers, referred to in the context of election transparency, was scheduled on which date?
63.x: The Supreme Court hearing on EVM totalisers was scheduled for 2 September 2026.
63.tq: Use the exact-date distinction among closely related current-affairs developments.
63.sec: Universal angles

63.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Tamil Nadu Assembly's position on delimitation in August 2026?
o: It supported delimitation exclusively on the basis of the 2011 Census without any freeze.
It demanded a permanent freeze at 543 Lok Sabha seats and a 2.2:1 Lok Sabha–Rajya Sabha ratio.
It proposed abolishing the Rajya Sabha after delimitation.
It demanded an increase of Lok Sabha seats to 850 and a 1:2.2 Lok Sabha–Rajya Sabha ratio.
63.x: The Tamil Nadu Assembly asked for a permanent freeze at 543 Lok Sabha seats and proposed a 2.2:1 Lok Sabha–Rajya Sabha ratio.
63.tq: Separate the specific institutional demand from broader positions on delimitation.
63.sec: Universal angles

63.s:
With reference to Andhra Pradesh's representation in the Lok Sabha, consider the following statements:
1. Andhra Pradesh has four reserved Lok Sabha seats for Scheduled Castes.
2. Andhra Pradesh has one reserved Lok Sabha seat for Scheduled Tribes.
3. Both categories of reserved seats are equal in number.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
63.x: Andhra Pradesh has four Scheduled Caste-reserved Lok Sabha seats and one Scheduled Tribe-reserved Lok Sabha seat. Therefore, the two categories are not equal in number.
63.tq: Split the numerical comparison from the two individual figures.

63.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding significant milestones in India's election system.

List-I
 a. EVM first used at Parur
 b. VVPAT first used at Noksen
 c. NOTA introduced

List-II
 i. 1982
 ii. 2013
 iii. 2013

63.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026:
1. It proposed raising the Lok Sabha ceiling from 550 to 850.
2. It proposed delimitation on the basis of the 2011 Census.
3. It was passed by the Lok Sabha with the required special majority.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
63.x: The Bill proposed increasing the Lok Sabha ceiling from 550 to 850 and conducting delimitation on the 2011 Census. It was defeated, not passed with the required special majority.
63.tq: Identify the false outcome statement while retaining the two substantive proposals.
63.sec: Universal angles

63.s: Why have southern States expressed apprehension regarding population-based delimitation?
o: They oppose the use of electronic voting machines in parliamentary elections.
They fear that States such as Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Rajasthan may gain seats at their expense.
They fear that the Rajya Sabha will become a directly elected chamber.
They fear that all Lok Sabha seats reserved for Scheduled Castes will be abolished.
63.x: Southern States fear that population-based delimitation would transfer political representation towards more populous States such as Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Rajasthan.
63.tq: Link the policy principle of population-based delimitation with its regional representation effect.
63.sec: Universal angles

63.s: The EAC-PM proposal of August 2026 relating to Lok Sabha representation envisaged which of the following?
o: Increasing the Lok Sabha ceiling directly from 550 to 850 without changing constituencies
Merging 170 constituencies to reduce the Lok Sabha to 543 seats
Splitting 170 oversized constituencies to reach 824 seats
63.x: The EAC-PM proposal envisaged splitting 170 oversized constituencies in order to reach a total of 824 Lok Sabha seats.
63.tq: Check both components of the proposal—the number of constituencies and the proposed total.
63.sec: Universal angles

63.s: With reference to delimitation and Andhra Pradesh–Telangana representation, which one of the following is correct?
o: The increase in seats under Section 26 awaits the census after 2026.
The increase in seats under Section 26 is unrelated to any future census.
Section 26 concerns only the abolition of reserved seats in Andhra Pradesh.
The increase in seats under Section 26 was completed on the basis of the 2001 Census.
63.x: The Andhra Pradesh–Telangana seat increase under Section 26 awaits the census conducted after 2026.
63.tq: Match the statutory reference with the qualifying time condition instead of treating the provision as immediately operative.
63.sec: Universal angles

63.s: In State of Karnataka v. Prathik Parasrampuria (2026), removal of black money from elections was described as which of the following?
o: A function of the Delimitation Commission alone
An exclusive duty of the Finance Commission
A core duty of the Election Commission of India
A responsibility transferred entirely to political parties
63.x: The Supreme Court case identified removing black money from elections as a core duty of the Election Commission of India.
63.tq: Ask which constitutional authority is associated with the responsibility described in the case.
63.sec: Universal angles

63.s: The Election Commission of India delisted how many Registered Unrecognised Political Parties in 2026?
63.x: The Election Commission delisted 808 Registered Unrecognised Political Parties in 2026.
63.tq: Use the exact administrative figure and distinguish it from nearby delimitation numbers.
63.sec: Universal angles

63.s:
Consider the following statements about the Election Commission of India:
1. It was constituted in 1950.
2. It is a permanent independent constitutional body.
3. Its IIIDEM trains election managers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
63.x: The Election Commission was constituted in 1950, is a permanent independent constitutional body, and its IIIDEM provides training to election managers.
63.tq: When all three statements describe distinct institutional features, test whether the inclusive option is warranted.
63.sec: Universal angles

63.s: Which district in Andhra Pradesh achieved 100 per cent digitisation of SIR enumeration forms in July 2026?
63.x: Alluri Sitharama Raju district achieved 100 per cent digitisation of SIR enumeration forms in July 2026.
63.tq: Test the precise place associated with the administrative achievement.
63.sec: Universal angles

64.s: The Tarkunde Committee on electoral reforms was appointed in which year and submitted its report in which year?
64.x: The Tarkunde Committee was appointed in 1974 and submitted its report in 1975.
64.tq: Use the paired-year distinction to avoid confusing the appointment year with the report year.

64.s: Which of the following recommendations was associated with the Tarkunde Committee?
o: A three-member Election Commission and voting age of 18 years
64.x: The Tarkunde Committee recommended a three-member Election Commission and lowering the voting age to 18 years.
64.tq: Match the committee with its distinctive institutional recommendations.

64.s: The Tarkunde Committee proposed that appointments to the Election Commission should be made by a panel consisting of:
o: The President, the Vice-President and the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition and the Chief Justice of India
The Prime Minister, the Home Minister and the Chief Election Commissioner
The Chief Justice of India, the Law Minister and the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
64.x: The proposed appointing panel comprised the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition and the Chief Justice of India.
64.tq: Test the exact composition of an appointing panel; do not substitute nearby constitutional authorities.

64.s: Which one of the following committees undertook the broadest review of electoral reforms in 1990?
64.x: The Dinesh Goswami Committee, constituted in 1990, is described as undertaking the broadest review of electoral reforms.
64.tq: Use the distinctive descriptive phrase to identify the committee.

64.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Dinesh Goswami Committee:
1. It examined time limits for bye-elections.
2. It dealt with strengthening the Election Commission.
3. It flagged the role of musclemen in elections.
4. It recommended rotation of seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
64.x: All four statements describe recommendations or concerns associated with the Dinesh Goswami Committee.
64.tq: Check each recommendation independently before selecting the comprehensive combination.

64.s: The Vohra Committee, constituted in 1993, primarily examined:
o: The financing of political parties by the State
The nexus between crime and politics
64.x: The Vohra Committee examined the nexus between criminals and politicians, or the crime-politics nexus.
64.tq: Discriminate between committees by their central subject rather than their common electoral-reform setting.

64.s: Which committee or report is correctly matched with its principal subject?
o: Vohra Committee — State funding of elections
Indrajit Gupta Committee — State funding of elections
J.S. Verma Committee — Simultaneous elections only
64.x: The Indrajit Gupta Committee of 1998 dealt with state funding of elections. The Vohra Committee examined the crime-politics nexus, while the Tarkunde and J.S. Verma Committees had different areas of focus.
64.tq: Find the correctly matched pair among closely related electoral-reform committees.

64.s:
With reference to the Indrajit Gupta Committee, consider the following statements:
1. It was constituted in 1998.
2. It dealt with state funding of elections.
3. Its recommendation on state funding has not been adopted.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
64.x: The Indrajit Gupta Committee was constituted in 1998, examined state funding of elections, and its recommendation has not been adopted.
64.tq: Combine a year, subject and implementation-status fact in one coded question.

64.s: The Law Commission's 170th Report, submitted in 1999, dealt with which of the following?
o: Only the appointment of the Election Commission
Reform of electoral laws, including internal party democracy
64.x: The 170th Report of the Law Commission dealt with electoral-law reform and included internal party democracy among its concerns.
64.tq: Reject options that narrow a broad report to an unrelated single subject.

64.s:
Which of the following was associated with the Law Commission's 170th Report of 1999?
1. Partial list seats under proportional representation
2. Disqualification on the framing of charges
3. Internal party democracy
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
64.x: The 170th Report covered internal party democracy, partial-list proportional-representation seats and disqualification on the framing of charges.
64.tq: Treat each listed recommendation as a separate proposition before using the code.

64.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
64.x: The Law Commission's 255th Report was issued in 2015, whereas its 170th Report was issued in 1999.
64.tq: Separate the two easily confused Law Commission report numbers and years.

64.s: The Second Administrative Reforms Commission, chaired by Veerappa Moily, examined the theme of:
64.x: The Second Administrative Reforms Commission's relevant work for electoral reform was under the theme “Ethics in Governance.”
64.tq: Associate the committee with its named report theme rather than a related recommendation.

64.s: Which one of the following was associated with the Second Administrative Reforms Commission's recommendations?
o: Appointment of all Election Commissioners by the Chief Justice of India
Partial state funding and barring persons charged with serious offences
64.x: The Second Administrative Reforms Commission recommended partial state funding and barring persons charged with serious offences.
64.tq: Distinguish a recommendation from the broader subject title of the commission.

64.s: The J.S. Verma Committee of 2013 was primarily associated with:
o: Simultaneous elections to Parliament and State Assemblies
64.x: The J.S. Verma Committee dealt with criminal-law reform concerning sexual offences and also urged restrictions on candidates charged with such offences.
64.tq: Avoid swapping the J.S. Verma Committee's criminal-law subject with other electoral-reform committees.

64.s: Which committee recommended barring candidates charged with sexual offences?
64.x: The J.S. Verma Committee urged that candidates charged with sexual offences should be barred.
64.tq: Identify the person-associated recommendation rather than the committee's year alone.

64.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order of the year associated with the committee or report:
A. Vohra Committee
B. Law Commission's 170th Report
C. Indrajit Gupta Committee
D. J.S. Verma Committee
64.x: The correct sequence is Vohra Committee (1993), Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998), Law Commission 170th Report (1999), and J.S. Verma Committee (2013).
64.tq: Fix the earliest and latest items first, then distinguish 1998 from 1999.

64.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The 170th Law Commission Report backed simultaneous elections.
2. The 2018 draft Law Commission report also backed simultaneous elections.
3. Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections were held together from 1951-52 to 1967.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
64.x: All three statements are correct: both the 170th Report and the 2018 draft report supported simultaneous elections, and simultaneous Lok Sabha–Assembly polls were held from 1951-52 to 1967.
64.tq: Link two recommendations with the historical period in which simultaneous elections occurred.
64.sec: One Nation One Election - committee, 129th Amendment Bill

64.s: Who chaired the High-Level Committee constituted in 2023-24 on simultaneous elections?
64.x: The High-Level Committee on simultaneous elections was chaired by former President Ram Nath Kovind.
64.tq: Identify the chairperson separately from the other prominent members.
64.sec: One Nation One Election - committee, 129th Amendment Bill

64.s: Which of the following persons was NOT listed as a member of the Ram Nath Kovind High-Level Committee on simultaneous elections?
64.x: Amit Shah, Ghulam Nabi Azad and N.K. Singh were listed as members. Dinesh Goswami was not listed as a member of this committee.
64.tq: Find the outsider in a list of persons associated with the committee.
64.sec: One Nation One Election - committee, 129th Amendment Bill

64.s: Which one of the following sets contains only members listed for the Ram Nath Kovind High-Level Committee?
o: B.R. Gavai, U.U. Lalit, Sanjiv Khanna and Amit Shah
Dinesh Goswami, Amit Shah, Harish Salve and Sanjay Kothari
Amit Shah, Ghulam Nabi Azad, N.K. Singh and Subhash C. Kashyap
Veerappa Moily, N.K. Singh, Subhash C. Kashyap and Dinesh Goswami
64.x: Amit Shah, Ghulam Nabi Azad, N.K. Singh and Subhash C. Kashyap were among the listed members of the committee.
64.tq: Check every name in the set against the committee membership list.
64.sec: One Nation One Election - committee, 129th Amendment Bill

64.s: The Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 was introduced in the Lok Sabha in:
64.x: The Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 was introduced in the Lok Sabha in December 2024.
64.tq: Distinguish the year in the Bill's title from the month and year of introduction.

64.s:
The Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 proposes amendments to which of the following Articles?
1. Article 83
2. Article 172
3. Article 327
4. Article 280
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
64.x: The Bill proposes amendments to Articles 83, 172 and 327. Article 280 is not among the Articles identified for amendment.
64.tq: Eliminate the unrelated Article and retain the three Articles expressly connected with the Bill.
64.sec: One Nation One Election - committee, 129th Amendment Bill

64.s: Which of the following correctly describes the phased rollout recommended by the Ram Nath Kovind High-Level Committee?
o: Local-body elections first, followed by Lok Sabha elections after five years
All elections to be held on the same day without any transitional phase
Rajya Sabha and Legislative Council elections together first, followed by Assembly elections
Lok Sabha and Assembly elections together first, followed by local-body elections within 100 days
64.x: The committee recommended holding Lok Sabha and Assembly polls together initially, followed by local-body elections within 100 days.
64.tq: Track the sequence and the specific 100-day interval in the proposed phased model.
64.sec: One Nation One Election - committee, 129th Amendment Bill

64.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the constitutional provisions discussed in connection with simultaneous elections:
1. Article 83 concerns the duration of the Houses of Parliament.
2. Article 172 concerns the duration of State Legislatures.
3. Article 327 concerns Parliament's power relating to elections.
4. Article 356 concerns President's Rule.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
64.x: All four statements correctly identify the subjects of Articles 83, 172, 327 and 356.
64.tq: Separate the Articles expressly amended by the Bill from other Articles mentioned in the surrounding constitutional debate.
64.sec: One Nation One Election - committee, 129th Amendment Bill

64.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched in relation to the constitutional provisions discussed in connection with simultaneous elections?
o: Article 83 — Duration of Houses of Parliament
Article 85 — Dissolution and related parliamentary matters
Article 174 — Dissolution and related matters concerning State Legislatures
Article 356 — Appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner
64.x: Article 356 concerns President's Rule, not appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner. Articles 83, 85 and 174 were among the provisions mentioned in the debate in relation to duration or dissolution.
64.tq: Use the wrong constitutional subject to identify the incorrectly matched pair.
64.sec: One Nation One Election - committee, 129th Amendment Bill

64.s: A proposed safeguard for maintaining governmental accountability under simultaneous elections is based on which model?
o: The Westminster model of an unelected executive
The American model of judicial review
The German model of a constructive vote of no-confidence
64.x: The proposed safeguard is a constructive no-confidence motion modelled on the German system.
64.tq: Match the institutional safeguard with the country model specifically associated with it.
64.sec: One Nation One Election - committee, 129th Amendment Bill

64.s:
Which of the following has been cited as a criticism of the simultaneous-election proposal?
1. It may weaken federalism.
2. It would require very large numbers of EVMs and security forces.
3. It would eliminate the need for State Legislative Assemblies.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
64.x: The criticisms identified are that simultaneous elections may weaken federalism and require huge numbers of EVMs and forces. The proposal does not eliminate State Legislative Assemblies.
64.tq: Accept the two stated criticisms and reject the extreme claim that the institutions themselves would be abolished.
64.sec: One Nation One Election - committee, 129th Amendment Bill

64.s: At the Joint Parliamentary Committee hearings in 2026, which former Chief Justice of India stated that the Bill did not violate the Basic Structure?
64.x: Former Chief Justice of India B.R. Gavai told the Joint Parliamentary Committee that the Bill did not violate the Basic Structure.
64.tq: Distinguish the specific opinion expressed from the separate views of other former Chief Justices.
64.sec: One Nation One Election - committee, 129th Amendment Bill

64.s: Which pair of former Chief Justices of India raised doubts concerning the Basic Structure in the 2026 Joint Parliamentary Committee hearings?
64.x: U.U. Lalit and Sanjiv Khanna raised Basic Structure doubts, whereas B.R. Gavai stated that the Bill did not violate the Basic Structure.
64.tq: Separate the two dissenting or doubtful views from the contrary opinion expressed by another former CJI.
64.sec: One Nation One Election - committee, 129th Amendment Bill

64.s: Electoral bonds were introduced through amendments made by which legislative measure?
64.x: The Electoral Bond Scheme was introduced through amendments made by the Finance Act, 2017.
64.tq: Identify the legislative route through which the scheme was introduced.

64.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the institution authorised to sell electoral bonds?
o: The Ministry of Finance through its designated offices
Any scheduled commercial bank authorised by the Election Commission
64.x: Electoral bonds were sold only by the State Bank of India.
64.tq: Use the exclusive-authority trap and identify who performed the specified function.

64.s: The Electoral Bond Scheme was notified in which year?
64.x: The scheme was notified in 2018, although the enabling amendments were made through the Finance Act, 2017.
64.tq: Distinguish the year of notification from the year of the enabling legislation.

64.s: Which of the following was the highest denomination in which electoral bonds were issued?
64.x: Electoral bonds were issued in denominations ranging from ₹1,000 to ₹1 crore.
64.tq: Test the upper limit in a range of denominations.

64.s:
Consider the following statements regarding electoral bonds:
1. They were bearer instruments.
2. They were valid for 15 days.
3. They could be encashed by every registered political party.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
64.x: Electoral bonds were bearer instruments and were valid for 15 days. Statement 3 is false because only registered parties securing at least 1% of the votes in the last election could encash them.
64.tq: Find the qualifying condition hidden behind the broad phrase 'every registered political party'.

64.s: A political party could encash electoral bonds only if it had secured at least what percentage of votes in the last election?
64.x: Only a registered political party that had secured at least 1% of the votes in the last election could encash electoral bonds.
64.tq: Recall the statutory eligibility threshold rather than the general registration requirement.

64.s: Which of the following statements about the donor under the Electoral Bond Scheme is correct?
o: The donor could remain anonymous only when donating below ₹20,000.
The donor's identity was hidden from the public.
The donor's identity was disclosed only to the Election Commission before purchase.
The donor's identity was disclosed to the public along with the party's annual report.
64.x: The donor's identity was not disclosed to the public under the scheme.
64.tq: Discriminate between public disclosure and institutional disclosure.

64.s:
With reference to the electoral bond judgment of 2024, consider the following statements:
1. The judgment was delivered by a five-judge Constitution Bench.
2. The decision to strike down the scheme was unanimous.
3. The Court directed the State Bank of India to provide donor data to the Election Commission of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
64.x: All three statements are correct: a five-judge Constitution Bench unanimously struck down the scheme and directed SBI to provide donor data to the ECI.
64.tq: When all three statements describe distinct features of one judgment, verify the bench, outcome and direction separately.

64.s: The Supreme Court's decision in Association for Democratic Reforms v. Union of India also invalidated which change associated with electoral political funding?
o: Abolition of political party registration under the RPA
Removal of the corporate donation cap under the Companies Act
Compulsory disclosure of all cash donations by parties
Restriction on donations by individual citizens
64.x: The Court struck down the removal of the corporate donation cap from the Companies Act.
64.tq: Identify the allied legal provision affected by the judgment, not merely the main scheme.

64.s: According to the cited assessment of party funding for 2004–2023, what proportion of party funds came from undisclosed sources?
64.x: The cited assessment stated that 60% of party funds during 2004–2023 came from undisclosed sources, amounting to ₹19,083 crore.
64.tq: Link the percentage with the period and monetary figure instead of treating it as a general estimate.

64.s: The amount of ₹19,083 crore, cited in the context of political funding, refers to which of the following?
o: The corporate donation cap removed by Parliament
The total value of electoral bonds issued in one year
The expenditure limit for all Lok Sabha candidates
64.x: ₹19,083 crore was the amount corresponding to the reported 60% of party funds from undisclosed sources during 2004–2023.
64.tq: Use the associated figure and time period to identify the correct context.

64.s: Under the current expenditure limits, the maximum expenditure permitted for a Lok Sabha candidate in a larger State or Union Territory is:
64.x: The current limit for a Lok Sabha candidate in a larger State or Union Territory is ₹95 lakh.
64.tq: Separate current limits from the earlier figures and compare the State categories.

64.s: The current expenditure limit for a Lok Sabha candidate in a smaller State or Union Territory is:
64.x: The current Lok Sabha expenditure limit in a smaller State or Union Territory is ₹75 lakh; the earlier limit was ₹54 lakh.
64.tq: Test the smaller-State figure against the commonly remembered older limit.

64.s: For a candidate contesting an Assembly election in a larger State or Union Territory, the current expenditure limit is:
64.x: The current Assembly expenditure limit in a larger State or Union Territory is ₹40 lakh; it was earlier ₹28 lakh.
64.tq: Distinguish the Assembly ceiling from the Lok Sabha ceiling and the earlier value.

64.s: Which one of the following correctly states the current expenditure limit for an Assembly candidate in a smaller State or Union Territory?
64.x: The current limit for an Assembly candidate in a smaller State or Union Territory is ₹28 lakh; the earlier limit was ₹20 lakh.
64.tq: Use the constituency type and election level together to locate the correct figure.

64.s: The current election expenditure limits were raised through which instrument?
64.x: The limits were raised through the Conduct of Elections (Amendment) Rules, 2022, made under the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961.
64.tq: Identify the subordinate legislation and distinguish it from the parent Act.

64.s:
Consider the following statements regarding election expenditure limits:
1. The limits apply to candidates rather than political parties.
2. The travel expenses of 20 star campaigners are excluded from the candidate's expenditure limit.
3. The limits are fixed under Rule 90 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
64.x: All three statements are correct. The limits concern candidates, exclude the travel expenses of 20 star campaigners, and are fixed under Rule 90.
64.tq: Check the subject of the limit, the exclusion and the precise rule number independently.

64.s: Under Section 77 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, a candidate is required to:
o: File an election petition in the High Court
Disclose criminal antecedents of every proposer
Deposit the election expenditure with the District Election Officer
Maintain an account of election expenses
64.x: Section 77 requires candidates to keep an account of election expenses.
64.tq: Match the section number with its specific compliance obligation.

64.s: Under Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the account of election expenses must be filed within 30 days with the:
64.x: The account must be filed within 30 days with the District Election Officer under Section 78.
64.tq: Identify both the time limit and the correct receiving authority.

64.s: Failure to comply with the prescribed election expenditure account requirements may result in disqualification by the:
64.x: Failure to comply with the expenditure-account requirements can lead to disqualification by the Election Commission of India.
64.tq: Ask which authority has the power to impose the electoral consequence.

64.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Section of the RPA, 1951)
A. Section 8
B. Section 29A
C. Section 33A
D. Section 123

List-II (Subject)
1. Registration of political parties
2. Disclosure of criminal antecedents
3. Disqualification on conviction
4. Corrupt practices

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
64.x: Section 8 concerns disqualification on conviction, Section 29A registration of political parties, Section 33A criminal-antecedent disclosure, and Section 123 corrupt practices.
64.tq: Start with the sure section–subject pairs and eliminate codes containing a misplaced provision.

64.s: Under Section 8 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, conviction resulting in imprisonment of two years or more entails disqualification for:
o: The term of imprisonment and six years after release
The term of imprisonment and two years after release
Six years from the date of conviction only
64.x: The disqualification operates during the term of imprisonment and continues for six years after release.
64.tq: Read the duration as a two-part rule: imprisonment period plus the post-release period.

64.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Section 8(4) of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 is correct?
o: It was expanded by the Lily Thomas judgment of 2013.
It was replaced by Section 29A in 2013.
It continues to protect every convicted sitting legislator from disqualification.
It was struck down by the Lily Thomas judgment of 2013.
64.x: Section 8(4), which provided protection to sitting legislators in specified circumstances, was struck down by the Supreme Court in Lily Thomas v. Union of India in 2013.
64.tq: Use the landmark-case association to distinguish an invalidated provision from a continuing one.

64.s: Section 29A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 deals with:
o: Election petitions in the High Court
Registration of political parties with the Election Commission of India
64.x: Section 29A provides for registration of political parties with the Election Commission of India.
64.tq: Match the section with the institutional process it regulates.

64.s: Section 33 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 primarily concerns:
o: The declaration of an election void
The filing of election expenditure accounts
64.x: Section 33 deals with the presentation of nomination papers.
64.tq: Distinguish nomination-stage provisions from post-election and expenditure provisions.

64.s: The restriction that no person may contest an election from more than two constituencies is contained in:
64.x: Section 33(7), introduced through the 1996 amendment, restricts a person from contesting an election from more than two constituencies.
64.tq: Pair the sub-section number with the numerical restriction it creates.

64.s: Section 33A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 requires a candidate to disclose:
o: The assets of all political parties in the constituency
The number of electors who voted for the candidate
64.x: Section 33A provides for the candidate's disclosure of criminal antecedents.
64.tq: Identify the candidate-specific disclosure obligation rather than a party or constituency record.

64.s: The security deposit for a Lok Sabha election candidate belonging to the general category is ₹25,000. What is the corresponding deposit for an Assembly election candidate of the general category?
64.x: The security deposit is ₹25,000 for a general-category Lok Sabha candidate and ₹10,000 for a general-category Assembly candidate.
64.tq: Compare the deposits by election level before applying the separate SC/ST concession.

64.s: What security deposit is required from an SC/ST candidate contesting a Lok Sabha election?
64.x: The Lok Sabha security deposit is ₹25,000 for general-category candidates, and half of that amount—₹12,500—for SC/ST candidates.
64.tq: Apply the stated half-rate concession to the correct election level.

64.s: Section 81 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 relates to:
o: Corrupt practices during an election campaign
The maintenance of election expenditure accounts
Election petitions presented in the High Court within 45 days of the result
64.x: Section 81 concerns election petitions, which are presented in the High Court within 45 days of the election result.
64.tq: Separate the post-result election-petition provision from campaign and nomination provisions.

64.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the corrupt practices covered by Section 123 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951?
o: Failure to file an election expenditure account within 30 days
Appeal on the grounds of religion or caste
64.x: Section 123 covers corrupt practices such as bribery, undue influence and appeals based on religion or caste. Filing the expenditure account within 30 days is governed by Section 78.
64.tq: Find the provision belonging to a neighbouring compliance area rather than the corrupt-practices list.

64.s: Section 125 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 is associated with:
64.x: Section 125 deals with promoting enmity at elections.
64.tq: Match the section number with the election-related offence it addresses.

64.s: The provision relating to the ban on exit polls is:
64.x: Section 126A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 concerns the ban on exit polls.
64.tq: Distinguish the exit-poll provision from the nearby provision on promoting enmity.

64.s:
Arrange the following provisions of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 in ascending order of their section numbers:
A. Corrupt practices
B. Registration of political parties
C. Election petition
D. Disclosure of criminal antecedents
64.x: The correct sequence is Section 29A (registration), Section 33A (criminal antecedents), Section 81 (election petition), and Section 123 (corrupt practices).
64.tq: Arrange by section number, using the first and last provisions as anchors.

64.s:
Under the electoral disclosure requirements introduced in 2002, a candidate is required to file an affidavit regarding which of the following?
1. Criminal cases
2. Assets and liabilities
3. Educational qualifications
4. Party manifesto expenditure
Which of the statements given above are correct?
64.x: The 2002 disclosure requirement covers criminal cases, assets, liabilities and educational qualifications. It does not require candidates to file an affidavit on party manifesto expenditure.
64.tq: Identify the precise scope of a disclosure requirement and reject the unrelated addition.

64.s: The judgment in Lily Thomas v. Union of India (2013) is associated with which of the following conclusions?
o: Disqualification of legislators was transferred from Parliament to the Election Commission.
Only a sitting legislator can be disqualified after a three-month period.
A convicted legislator remains protected until the disposal of the appeal.
A convicted legislator is disqualified immediately, without protection during the pendency of an appeal.
64.x: The Lily Thomas judgment held that conviction leads to immediate disqualification and that an appeal does not provide protection against that disqualification.
64.tq: Test the holding of a landmark judgment against closely related but reversed legal effects.

64.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Section 8 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951:
1. Conviction resulting in imprisonment of two years or more attracts disqualification.
2. The disqualification rule is contained in a law made by Parliament.
3. Disqualification begins only after the appeal against conviction is finally decided.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
64.x: Section 8 provides disqualification on conviction involving imprisonment of two years or more, and the rule is contained in a parliamentary law. Lily Thomas removed the protection during pendency of an appeal, making statement 3 incorrect.
64.tq: Use the immediate-effect rule to identify the false statement about the appeal period.

64.s: In Public Interest Foundation v. Union of India (2018), the five-judge Bench directed political parties to do which of the following?
o: Refer all criminal cases against candidates to the President.
Disqualify every candidate against whom charges have been framed.
Prevent candidates with pending cases from filing nomination papers.
Publicise the criminal records of selected candidates and the reasons for selecting them.
64.x: The Court ordered publicity of candidates’ criminal records and the reasons for their selection. It did not itself impose disqualification merely on the framing of charges.
64.tq: Separate judicial directions on transparency from the power to impose disqualification.

64.s:
With reference to Public Interest Foundation v. Union of India (2018), consider the following statements:
1. The Court itself imposed disqualification upon the framing of charges in serious offences.
2. The question of disqualification upon framing of charges was left to Parliament.
3. Publicity of criminal records of candidates was ordered.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
64.x: The Court left the issue of disqualification on framing of charges to Parliament but ordered publicity of criminal records. It did not itself impose such disqualification.
64.tq: Distinguish between what a court ordered and what it left to the legislature.

64.s:
The Election Commission’s current requirement concerning candidates with criminal records includes publication of which of the following by political parties?
1. Details of the candidates’ criminal records
2. Reasons for selecting such candidates
3. Mandatory withdrawal of their candidature
Which of the statements given above are correct?
64.x: Political parties must publish the criminal-record details of selected candidates and the reasons for their selection. Mandatory withdrawal of candidature is not part of the stated requirement.
64.tq: Reject the extreme consequence when the actual reform is based on disclosure and justification.

64.s: The Law Commission’s recommendation to bar candidates after framing of charges was specifically related to which category of offences?
o: Only offences under the Tenth Schedule
64.x: The Law Commission recommended barring candidates once charges were framed in serious offences.
64.tq: Focus on the qualifying phrase that limits the scope of a legal recommendation.

64.s: The recommendation to bar candidates upon framing of charges in serious offences was made in which report of the Law Commission?
64.x: The recommendation was made in the Law Commission’s 244th Report of 2014.
64.tq: Match the recommendation with its specific report number and year.

64.s: According to the cited ADR data, what proportion of Members of Parliament and Members of Legislative Assemblies face serious criminal charges, respectively?
64.x: The cited ADR figures are 31% of MPs and 29% of MLAs facing serious criminal charges.
64.tq: Keep the categories in the order asked and distinguish the two percentages.

64.s: The share of Members of Parliament facing serious criminal charges increased from 14% in 2009 to what percentage in 2024?
64.x: The cited data show an increase in the share from 14% in 2009 to 31% in 2024.
64.tq: Track the stated time trend rather than confusing it with the MLA figure.

64.s: Which of the following statements regarding the current judicial and institutional response to criminalisation of politics is correct?
o: A lifetime ban on convicted legislators has already been enacted and no petition is pending.
The Supreme Court has abolished all special courts for MPs and MLAs.
A PIL seeking a lifetime ban on convicted legislators is pending, and 12 special courts exist for MPs and MLAs.
Only one special court exists for all cases involving elected representatives.
64.x: A PIL seeking a lifetime ban on convicted legislators is pending, while 12 special courts have been established for cases involving MPs and MLAs.
64.tq: Distinguish a pending proposal from an already enacted reform.

64.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Case)
A. ADR v. Union of India
B. PUCL v. Union of India
C. Ramesh Dalal v. Union of India
D. Krishnamurthy v. Sivakumar

List-II (Year)
1. 2002
2. 2003
3. 2005
4. 2015

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
64.x: ADR v. Union of India was decided in 2002, PUCL v. Union of India in 2003, Ramesh Dalal in 2005 and Krishnamurthy in 2015.
64.tq: Start with the sure case-year pair and eliminate codes containing a mismatch.

64.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Krishnamurthy v. Sivakumar — Introduction of electoral bonds
ADR v. Union of India — Mandatory disclosure of criminal cases, assets, liabilities and education
PUCL v. Union of India — Disqualification on framing of charges in every criminal offence
