Ramesh Dalal v. Union of India — Abolition of the right to know
64.x: ADR v. Union of India concerned mandatory disclosure of criminal cases, assets, liabilities and educational qualifications. The other cases are incorrectly associated with the stated subjects.
64.tq: Find the one accurate case-holding pair among swapped judicial subjects.

64.s: The decision in PUCL v. Union of India recognised that the voter’s right to know is part of which constitutional right?
64.x: PUCL v. Union of India recognised the voter’s right to know as part of the freedom of speech and expression under Article 19(1)(a).
64.tq: Identify the constitutional article linked to the specific fundamental right.

64.s: What was the principal holding in Ramesh Dalal v. Union of India (2005)?
o: A candidate is disqualified merely when an FIR is registered.
The Election Commission must fund all candidates in kind.
A sitting MP or MLA convicted and sentenced to two years or more is barred from contesting elections.
Political parties must publish their election manifestos in newspapers.
64.x: Ramesh Dalal v. Union of India held that a sitting MP or MLA convicted and sentenced to imprisonment of two years or more is barred from contesting elections.
64.tq: Link the case to the precise conviction threshold instead of the earlier stage of an FIR or charge.

64.s: Non-disclosure of serious criminal cases by a candidate was held to vitiate the nomination in which case?
o: Public Interest Foundation v. Union of India
64.x: Krishnamurthy v. Sivakumar (2015) held that non-disclosure of serious criminal cases vitiates the nomination.
64.tq: Discriminate between cases dealing with disclosure, publicity and nomination validity.

64.s: Which of the following correctly states the direction associated with Public Interest Foundation v. Union of India (2018)?
o: Only the courts may publish criminal records after conviction.
The Election Commission must keep candidates’ criminal records confidential.
Political parties must publicise candidates’ criminal records on websites, in newspapers and on television.
Candidates may be barred solely by the Election Commission after an FIR.
64.x: The judgment directed political parties to publicise candidates’ criminal records through websites, newspapers and television.
64.tq: Use the complete set of prescribed publicity channels to identify the precise option.

64.s: Disqualification under the Tenth Schedule is decided by the Speaker or Chairman, subject to which limitation?
o: Approval by the President in all cases
A referendum among members of the House
Approval by the Election Commission before every decision
64.x: The Speaker or Chairman decides disqualification under the Tenth Schedule, but the decision remains subject to judicial review, as recognised by the Supreme Court in 1992.
64.tq: Ask who exercises the power and then identify the constitutional check on that power.

64.s: State funding of elections was recommended in 1998 by which committee?
64.x: The Indrajit Gupta Committee recommended state funding of elections in 1998.
64.tq: Match the reform proposal with the committee that made it.

64.s: The Indrajit Gupta Committee recommended state funding of elections in which form?
o: Loans from commercial banks to all contestants
Partial funding in kind to recognised parties and candidates
Full funding in cash to every individual candidate
64.x: The committee recommended partial state funding in kind for recognised political parties and candidates.
64.tq: Separate the model, beneficiaries and mode of funding rather than remembering only the committee name.

64.s: Which one of the following is correct regarding the status of the Indrajit Gupta Committee’s recommendation on state funding?
o: It was adopted only for elections to the Rajya Sabha.
It was fully adopted throughout India in 1998.
It was repealed after being implemented for one election cycle.
It has not yet been adopted.
64.x: The recommendation for partial funding in kind has not yet been adopted.
64.tq: Distinguish a recommendation from its actual implementation.

64.s: The Dinesh Goswami Committee and the Second Administrative Reforms Commission are associated with recommendations regarding which reform?
64.x: Both the Dinesh Goswami Committee and the Second Administrative Reforms Commission recommended public funding of elections.
64.tq: Identify the common reform associated with two separate bodies.

64.s: The Law Commission’s 170th Report stated that full state funding of elections would be desirable only if which condition were fulfilled?
o: Only independent candidates received public funds.
Political parties were barred from obtaining funds from other sources.
All candidates were allowed unlimited private donations.
64.x: The Law Commission considered full state funding desirable only if political parties were barred from receiving funds from other sources.
64.tq: Test the conditional nature of a recommendation and reject an unconditional formulation.

64.s:
Consider the following statements about models of state funding of elections:
1. Public funding may be full or partial.
2. Funding may be provided in cash or in kind.
3. Partial funding means that the State bears all legitimate costs and private donations are banned.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
64.x: State funding may be full or partial and may be in cash or in kind. Bearing all legitimate costs while banning private donations describes full funding, not partial funding.
64.tq: Use the definition of partial funding to catch the swapped meaning in statement 3.

64.s: Which of the following best describes partial state funding of elections?
o: The State bears all legitimate costs and private donations are prohibited.
The State provides no assistance but regulates private donations.
The State funds only the election deposits of losing candidates.
The State meets some costs, in cash or in kind, such as free airtime, fuel or rallies.
64.x: Under partial funding, the State meets some election costs, either in cash or in kind. Examples include free airtime, fuel and rallies.
64.tq: Select the option containing both the definition and the relevant examples.

64.s: Which one of the following is NOT cited as a country having public funding of elections?
64.x: Germany, Sweden and Japan are cited as countries with public funding of elections. Brazil is not included in the stated list.
64.tq: Find the country outside the specifically stated group rather than relying on general knowledge.

64.s: Which of the following is an argument in favour of state funding of elections?
o: It does not stop off-book cash spending.
It imposes a heavy fiscal burden on the State.
It can curb black money and quid-pro-quo funding.
It guarantees that private donations will continue without regulation.
64.x: Curbing black money and quid-pro-quo funding is an argument in favour of state funding. Heavy fiscal burden and continued off-book spending are arguments against it.
64.tq: Separate arguments for and against a policy by their direction of effect.

64.s: Which of the following is an argument against state funding of elections?
o: It is linked with the equality principle under Article 14.
It may help create a level field for resource-poor candidates.
It places a heavy fiscal burden on the State.
64.x: The heavy fiscal burden on the State is an argument against public funding. A level field and curbing quid-pro-quo funding are arguments in favour.
64.tq: Identify the negative policy consequence among otherwise favourable effects.

64.s: State funding of elections is associated with the objective of creating a level field for resource-poor candidates, a consideration linked with which constitutional provision?
64.x: The level-playing-field rationale for resource-poor candidates is linked with Article 14, the equality provision.
64.tq: Match the policy rationale with the constitutional article expressly associated with it.

64.s: According to the Supreme Court decision in State of Karnataka v. Prathik Parasrampuria (2026), eliminating black money from elections is primarily whose core responsibility?
64.x: The Supreme Court described elimination of black money from elections as a core responsibility of the Election Commission of India.
64.tq: Ask which constitutional institution has the responsibility, avoiding a swap with an auditing or fiscal body.

64.s:
Which of the following proposals has been suggested as an alternative or supplementary measure for election funding reform?
1. National Election Fund with pooling of corporate donations
2. Democracy vouchers
3. Zero-cash rule
4. CAG audits of political parties
Which of the statements given above are correct?
64.x: The listed reform ideas include a National Election Fund, democracy vouchers, a zero-cash rule and bringing parties under CAG audits. The National Election Fund is envisaged as an IPL-style pooling mechanism linked to vote share.
64.tq: Use an all-inclusive option when every listed reform proposal belongs to the same policy package.

64.s: The proposed National Election Fund has been compared to an IPL-style pooling mechanism in which corporate donations would be shared according to which basis?
64.x: The proposed National Election Fund would pool corporate donations and distribute them according to the vote share of political parties.
64.tq: Identify the allocation criterion in a proposed institutional mechanism.

64.s:
Which of the following combinations is correctly matched with a proposed electoral funding reform?
1. Democracy vouchers — a proposed alternative funding mechanism
2. Zero-cash rule — restriction on cash-based election transactions
3. CAG audits — audit-based oversight of political parties

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
64.x: Democracy vouchers, a zero-cash rule and CAG audits are all among the proposed ideas for electoral funding and governance reform.
64.tq: Confirm whether each reform is correctly paired with its broad purpose.

64.s: Which one of the following was the first reported use of an Electronic Voting Machine (EVM) in India?
64.x: EVMs were first used on a pilot basis at Parur (Paravur) in Kerala in 1982.
64.tq: Use the place-year pair to distinguish the pilot from nationwide implementation.

64.s: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988, brought about which of the following changes?
o: Reduction of the voting age from 21 years to 18 years
Introduction of Electors' Photo Identity Cards
Linking of electoral rolls with Aadhaar
64.x: The 61st Amendment reduced the voting age from 21 to 18 years; the change came into force in 1989.
64.tq: Match the constitutional amendment with its distinctive electoral reform.

64.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Electors' Photo Identity Card (EPIC):
1. EPIC was introduced in 1993.
2. Its number, once issued, remains valid for life even if the elector’s address changes.
3. EPIC was introduced through the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
64.x: EPIC was introduced in 1993, and its number remains valid for life despite a change of address. It was not introduced by the 61st Amendment.
64.tq: Separate the year and legal basis of EPIC from the voting-age amendment.

64.s:
Arrange the following electoral developments in chronological order:
A. Introduction of EPIC
B. EVMs used in all constituencies
C. Introduction of VVPAT and NOTA
D. Reduction of voting age from 21 to 18 years
64.x: The correct sequence is 61st Amendment and voting-age reduction in 1988, EPIC in 1993, nationwide EVM use in 2004, and VVPAT/NOTA in 2013.
64.tq: Fix the earliest constitutional reform first, then place the technology milestones by year.

64.s:
With reference to the Election Laws (Amendment) Act, 2021, consider the following statements:
1. It provided for linking electoral rolls with Aadhaar to check multiple enrolment.
2. It introduced multiple qualifying dates for registration as an elector.
3. It provided for gender-neutral wording in electoral law.
4. It provided for requisition of premises for election-related purposes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
64.x: All four statements describe provisions associated with the Election Laws (Amendment) Act, 2021.
64.tq: Identify the comprehensive option when all listed features belong to the same amendment.

64.s: The remote EVM prototype for domestic migrants was shown to political parties during which period?
64.x: A remote EVM prototype intended for domestic migrants was demonstrated to political parties in 2022–23.
64.tq: Distinguish the prototype period from the dates of earlier EVM and VVPAT milestones.

64.s: Under the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners Act, 2023, the selection panel consists of:
o: The Prime Minister, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and the Union Home Minister
The Prime Minister, a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister and the Leader of the Opposition
The President, the Prime Minister and the Chief Justice of India
The Prime Minister, the Chief Justice of India and the Leader of the Opposition
64.x: The 2023 Act provides for a panel comprising the Prime Minister, a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister, and the Leader of the Opposition. The Chief Justice of India was dropped from the panel.
64.tq: Use the composition trap by identifying the authority omitted from the final arrangement.

64.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: 2013 — Lily Thomas judgment striking down Section 8(4) of the RPA
2002 — Disclosure of criminal record, assets and education
64.x: Electoral bonds were struck down by the Supreme Court in 2024; they were not introduced in that year. The other pairs are correctly matched.
64.tq: Find the reversed action-year pair, particularly where a later year records invalidation rather than introduction.

64.s: The expenditure limit for a Lok Sabha candidate in bigger States was raised to which amount in 2022?
64.x: In 2022, the expenditure ceiling for a Lok Sabha candidate in bigger States was raised to ₹95 lakh.
64.tq: Distinguish the revised ceiling from the corresponding Assembly limit and earlier figures.

64.s: ECINET, described as a single platform integrating more than 40 applications, and 100 per cent webcasting are associated with which year?
64.x: ECINET, 100 per cent webcasting and the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls are identified with 2025.
64.tq: Match the digital-election initiative with its year rather than with the year of the CEC selection law.

64.s: Under Section 33(7) of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, a candidate may contest from a maximum of:
64.x: Since the 1996 amendment, Section 33(7) permits a candidate to contest from at most two constituencies.
64.tq: Recall the statutory numerical cap and avoid the pre-1996 position.
64.sec: Contesting from more than one constituency - Section 33(7)  [other exams, GROUP-II]

64.s: A candidate elected from both constituencies under Section 33(7) must vacate one of them within:
64.x: Under Section 70 of the Representation of the People Act, the candidate must vacate one seat within 14 days after being elected from both constituencies.
64.tq: Separate the two-constituency entitlement under Section 33(7) from the time limit under Section 70.
64.sec: Contesting from more than one constituency - Section 33(7)  [other exams, GROUP-II]

64.s:
Which of the following has been proposed as a reform concerning candidates contesting from more than one constituency?
1. One candidate, one seat
2. Requiring the vacating candidate to bear the cost of the resulting by-election
3. Allowing an unlimited number of constituencies if the candidate deposits additional security
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
64.x: The Law Commission proposed the principle of one candidate, one seat, while the Election Commission proposed that a candidate vacating a seat should bear the cost of the by-election. Unlimited contesting was not proposed.
64.tq: Reject the extreme ‘unlimited’ proposal and retain the two stated reform alternatives.
64.sec: Contesting from more than one constituency - Section 33(7)  [other exams, GROUP-II]

64.s: Which one of the following was a major provision of the Representation of the People (Amendment) Act, 1996?
o: Removal of the limit on constituencies from which a candidate may contest
Reduction of security deposits and proposers for independent candidates
Abolition of by-elections within six months
Capping a candidate’s contest to two constituencies and increasing security deposits
64.x: The 1996 amendment capped contests at two constituencies, increased security deposits, and required more proposers for independents and unrecognised parties.
64.tq: Identify the option that combines the principal nomination-related changes without reversing them.
64.sec: RP (Amendment) Act 1996 - nominations, deposits, poll day  [other exams, GROUP-II]

64.s: Under the amended election law, the poll is countermanded on the death of:
o: A candidate of a recognised political party
A candidate of an unrecognised political party only
64.x: The poll is countermanded only when a candidate of a recognised political party dies.
64.tq: Focus on the qualification ‘recognised party’ rather than treating the rule as applying to every candidate.
64.sec: RP (Amendment) Act 1996 - nominations, deposits, poll day  [other exams, GROUP-II]

64.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Section 135B — Liquor ban for 48 hours before polling
Section 135C — Paid holiday on polling day
Section 70 — Disqualification under the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971
64.x: Section 151A concerns holding a by-election within six months. Section 135B provides for a paid holiday, Section 135C concerns the liquor ban, and Section 70 deals with vacating one of two seats.
64.tq: Match statutory sections with their functions and eliminate the swapped-section pairs.
64.sec: RP (Amendment) Act 1996 - nominations, deposits, poll day  [other exams, GROUP-II]

64.s:
Consider the following statements regarding election-day provisions:
1. A paid holiday is provided on the day of poll.
2. Sale of liquor is prohibited during the 48 hours preceding the poll.
3. A by-election is required to be held within six months in the circumstances specified by law.
4. Disqualification may arise for offences under the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
64.x: All four statements describe provisions associated with election regulation and disqualification under the relevant law.
64.tq: Check each statement independently, including the less prominent disqualification provision.
64.sec: RP (Amendment) Act 1996 - nominations, deposits, poll day  [other exams, GROUP-II]

64.s: Section 77 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, is criticised in the context of party expenditure because it:
o: Prohibits all expenditure on election campaigns
Places a ceiling only on the expenditure of candidates, not on the election expenditure incurred directly by political parties
Places a ceiling only on political parties, not on candidates
Requires all campaign expenditure to be incurred in cash
64.x: The perceived loophole is that Section 77 caps candidate expenditure while not imposing a comparable ceiling on the parties’ own election spending.
64.tq: Ask who bears the statutory ceiling to expose the candidate-party distinction.
64.sec: Money power - party expenditure ceiling debate, cash donation limits  [GROUP-II]

64.s: For a political party to retain tax exemption under the stated provisions, which combination is relevant?
o: No donation above ₹2,000 in any form and no record of larger donations
No cash donation above ₹20,000 and records only of donations above ₹2,000
No cash donation above ₹2,000 and proper records of donations above ₹20,000
Acceptance of unlimited cash donations provided they are reported after the election
64.x: The stated conditions include no cash donation above ₹2,000 and maintenance of records for donations above ₹20,000. These are referred to under Section 12 of the Income Tax Act, 2025, replacing the earlier reference to Section 13A of the 1961 Act.
64.tq: Keep the two monetary thresholds separate instead of reversing their functions.
64.sec: Money power - party expenditure ceiling debate, cash donation limits  [GROUP-II]

64.s: Which of the following is identified as a method of evading the donation-recording threshold?
o: Restricting all campaign publicity to official election broadcasts
Converting all party donations into government grants
Splitting a large gift into several gifts below ₹20,000 and diverting funds through surrogate digital advertisements or paid news
Depositing every donation directly into the Consolidated Fund of India
64.x: Evasion may occur by splitting large gifts into amounts below ₹20,000 and by diverting money through surrogate digital advertisements and paid news.
64.tq: Identify the practical loophole that exploits the threshold and indirect campaign channels.
64.sec: Money power - party expenditure ceiling debate, cash donation limits  [GROUP-II]

64.s: According to the Association for Democratic Reforms’ assessment cited in relation to party funding, what share of party funds during 2004–23 came from undisclosed sources?
64.x: The cited ADR assessment states that 60 per cent of party funds, amounting to ₹19,083 crore, came from undisclosed sources during 2004–23.
64.tq: Test the paired percentage and absolute amount together to prevent partial recall.
64.sec: Money power - party expenditure ceiling debate, cash donation limits  [GROUP-II]

64.s: The Supreme Court struck down the electoral bonds scheme in February 2024 in which case?
o: Tarkunde Committee v Union of India
Lily Thomas v Union of India
64.x: The electoral bonds scheme was struck down by the Supreme Court in Association for Democratic Reforms v Union of India in February 2024.
64.tq: Distinguish the case concerning electoral bonds from the cases concerning NOTA and disqualification.
64.sec: Money power - party expenditure ceiling debate, cash donation limits  [GROUP-II]

64.s: In PUCL v Union of India (2013), the Supreme Court directed that voters should have the option of:
o: Voting twice, once for a candidate and once for a party
Choosing the Chief Election Commissioner directly
Rejecting all candidates through a ‘None of the Above’ option on ballots and EVMs
Requiring a fresh election whenever NOTA receives the highest votes
64.x: PUCL v Union of India led to the provision of a ‘None of the Above’ option on ballot papers and EVMs. It did not mandate re-election when NOTA is highest.
64.tq: Separate the right to express rejection from the unrelated consequence of automatically holding a fresh poll.

64.s: The Supreme Court located the right to reject candidates through NOTA primarily in which constitutional provision?
64.x: The right to reject was linked to freedom of speech and expression under Article 19(1)(a).
64.tq: Match the electoral expression right with the constitutional freedom that supports it.

64.s: NOTA was first used in the 2013 Assembly elections in which set of States and Union Territory?
o: Chhattisgarh, Mizoram, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Delhi
Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Delhi
Chhattisgarh, Mizoram, Haryana, Maharashtra and Delhi
Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Puducherry
64.x: The first use of NOTA was in the 2013 Assembly elections in Chhattisgarh, Mizoram, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Delhi.
64.tq: Use the complete geographical set to distinguish the first Assembly use from later nationwide use.

64.s: NOTA was used for the first time in a Lok Sabha election in:
64.x: NOTA was first used in a Lok Sabha election in 2014, after its initial use in the 2013 Assembly elections.
64.tq: Distinguish the first Assembly-election year from the first Lok Sabha-election year.

64.s: Which State was the first to conduct its entire Assembly election using EVMs?
64.x: Goa conducted the first whole-State Assembly election using EVMs in 1999. Gujarat was not the first State to do so.
64.tq: Separate pilot use from the first whole-State use.
64.sec: EVMs - FIRST use, capacity, manufacturers, NOTA  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

64.s: EVMs were used at every polling station for the first time in which election?
64.x: The first nationwide use of EVMs at every polling station occurred during the Lok Sabha General Election of 2004.
64.tq: Match the scale of use with the correct milestone year.
64.sec: EVMs - FIRST use, capacity, manufacturers, NOTA  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

64.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the manufacture of EVMs:
1. Bharat Electronics Limited manufactures EVMs.
2. Electronics Corporation of India Limited manufactures EVMs.
3. Both the manufacturing public sector undertakings are headquartered in Bengaluru.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
64.x: BEL, Bengaluru, and ECIL, Hyderabad, are the two public sector undertakings that manufacture EVMs. Statement 3 is false because ECIL is based in Hyderabad.
64.tq: Catch the swapped location in a manufacturer-location statement.
64.sec: EVMs - FIRST use, capacity, manufacturers, NOTA  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

64.s: An M3 EVM can record up to how many votes?
64.x: An M3 EVM can record up to 2,000 votes.
64.tq: Identify the machine-generation capacity rather than the candidate capacity.
64.sec: EVMs - FIRST use, capacity, manufacturers, NOTA  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

64.s: With respect to the capacity of EVMs, which one of the following is correct?
o: An M2 system can connect 24 ballot units and accommodate 384 candidates, whereas an M3 system can connect four ballot units and accommodate 64 candidates.
An M3 system can accommodate 2,000 candidates through 24 ballot units.
An M2 system can connect four ballot units and accommodate 64 candidates, whereas an M3 system can connect 24 ballot units and accommodate 384 candidates including NOTA.
Both M2 and M3 systems can accommodate 64 candidates through four ballot units.
64.x: M2 EVMs support four ballot units and 64 candidates; an M3 control unit can take up to 24 ballot units and accommodate 384 candidates including NOTA.
64.tq: Split the comparison into ballot-unit capacity and candidate capacity.
64.sec: EVMs - FIRST use, capacity, manufacturers, NOTA  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

64.s: The NOTA button was introduced in India on which date pursuant to which judicial decision?
o: 1 January 2014, N. Chandrababu Naidu v Union of India
27 September 2013, PUCL v Union of India
64.x: The NOTA button was added on 27 September 2013 following the Supreme Court decision in PUCL v Union of India.
64.tq: Link the date with the correct case instead of a nearby electoral case.
64.sec: EVMs - FIRST use, capacity, manufacturers, NOTA  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

64.s: Which institution designed the NOTA symbol used on the ballot unit?
o: Electronics Corporation of India Limited, Hyderabad
64.x: The NOTA symbol, depicting a ballot paper with a black cross, was designed by the National Institute of Design at Ahmedabad.
64.tq: Distinguish the symbol designer from the EVM manufacturers.
64.sec: EVMs - FIRST use, capacity, manufacturers, NOTA  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

64.s: The first Lok Sabha election in which the NOTA option was available was held in:
64.x: The first Lok Sabha election with the NOTA option was held in 2014.
64.tq: Do not confuse the introduction date of NOTA with the first Lok Sabha election using it.
64.sec: EVMs - FIRST use, capacity, manufacturers, NOTA  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

64.s: In the first Lok Sabha election in which NOTA was available, its vote share was approximately:
64.x: In the 2014 Lok Sabha election, NOTA received approximately 1.1% of the votes, exceeding 60 lakh votes.
64.tq: Retain both the percentage and the absolute vote figure.
64.sec: EVMs - FIRST use, capacity, manufacturers, NOTA  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

64.s: The first use of VVPAT in India took place in which election?
o: The 2013 by-election in 51-Noksen Assembly constituency, Nagaland
64.x: VVPAT was first used in the 2013 by-election to the 51-Noksen Assembly constituency in Nagaland, after the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 were amended.
64.tq: Distinguish the first VVPAT use from the first EVM milestones.
64.sec: VVPAT - FIRST use, versions, court-ordered verification  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

64.s:
Consider the following statements about the voter-verifiable paper audit trail:
1. The voter can see the printed slip for about seven seconds.
2. The slip provides immediate feedback to the voter.
3. The slip is handed over to the voter after verification.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
64.x: The voter sees the slip for about seven seconds and receives immediate feedback. Statement 3 is false because the slip drops into a sealed box rather than being handed to the voter.
64.tq: Find the false statement by checking what happens to the verified slip.
64.sec: VVPAT - FIRST use, versions, court-ordered verification  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

64.s: Which of the following correctly represents the generations of VVPAT machines?
o: M1, M2 and M3, with M3 being the current generation
M2, M3 and M4, with M4 being the current generation
Only M1 and M2, with M2 being the current generation
M1, M2 and M3, with M1 being the current generation
64.x: The VVPAT generations are M1, M2 and M3; M3 is the current generation.
64.tq: Use the sequence of machine generations and identify the current version.
64.sec: VVPAT - FIRST use, versions, court-ordered verification  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

64.s: Which two public sector undertakings manufacture VVPAT machines?
o: ECI and the Election Commission of a State
ECIL and the National Institute of Design
BEL and the Law Commission of India
64.x: VVPATs are manufactured by Bharat Electronics Limited and Electronics Corporation of India Limited.
64.tq: Separate the machine manufacturers from the institutions involved in design or regulation.
64.sec: VVPAT - FIRST use, versions, court-ordered verification  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

64.s: Which case held that VVPAT is necessary for free and fair elections and directed its introduction in phases?
o: State of Karnataka v Prathik Parasrampuria
64.x: In Subramanian Swamy v ECI (2013), the Supreme Court held that VVPAT was needed for free and fair polls and required phased introduction.
64.tq: Match the judicial case with its distinctive electoral reform.
64.sec: VVPAT - FIRST use, versions, court-ordered verification  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

64.s: The decision in N. Chandrababu Naidu v Union of India (2019) changed the random VVPAT-EVM tally from:
o: Two to five polling stations per district
One to five polling stations per Assembly segment
One to ten polling stations per parliamentary constituency
Five to ten polling stations per Assembly segment
64.x: The 2019 decision raised the random VVPAT-EVM tally from one to five polling stations per Assembly segment.
64.tq: Remember both sides of the judicially ordered numerical increase.
64.sec: VVPAT - FIRST use, versions, court-ordered verification  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

64.s:
Consider the following statements regarding ADR v ECI (April 2024):
1. The Supreme Court rejected the demand for 100% VVPAT slip counting.
2. The Court rejected a return to paper ballots.
3. Symbol-loading units were directed to be sealed for 45 days.
4. Runners-up were permitted to seek verification of 5% of EVMs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
64.x: All four statements correctly describe the directions or conclusions associated with ADR v ECI in April 2024.
64.tq: Check each judicial direction separately, especially the figures and time period.
64.sec: VVPAT - FIRST use, versions, court-ordered verification  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

64.s: Under the newer Election Commission rules, VVPAT slips must be counted when:
o: EVM data do not match Form 17C
Postal ballots are counted before the EVMs in every constituency
The number of NOTA votes exceeds the winning margin
A losing candidate demands counting in every polling station
64.x: VVPAT slips must be counted wherever the EVM data do not match Form 17C. The penultimate EVM/VVPAT round is counted only after postal ballots are completed.
64.tq: Apply the rule to the specific trigger condition instead of a general demand for recounting.
64.sec: VVPAT - FIRST use, versions, court-ordered verification  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

64.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Supreme Court's position on EVMs is NOT correct?
o: In ADR v ECI (2024), the Court refused to order a return to paper ballots.
The Supreme Court has repeatedly upheld the use of EVMs.
In ADR v ECI (2024), the Court ordered a return to paper ballots.
The Court has considered safeguards relating to VVPAT verification.
64.x: The Supreme Court refused to order a return to paper ballots in ADR v ECI (2024). The other statements correctly reflect the Court's approach to EVMs and verification safeguards.
64.tq: Identify the reversed judicial conclusion in the NOT question.
64.sec: EVM credibility debate - SC rulings, paper-ballot demand  [GROUP-II]

64.s: The Election Commission has described EVMs as:
o: Still a subject of frequent public questioning
Devices whose use has been prohibited in Assembly elections
Machines that can be replaced only by paper ballots
Machines no longer subject to public scrutiny
64.x: The Election Commission has stated that EVMs are still a subject of frequent public questioning.
64.tq: Recall the precise institutional characterisation rather than an inferred conclusion.
64.sec: EVM credibility debate - SC rulings, paper-ballot demand  [GROUP-II]

64.s: What is the principal purpose of a Remote Voting Machine (RVM) prototype?
o: To permit domestic migrants to vote for up to 72 constituencies from one remote polling station
To count postal ballots together with EVM votes
To enable overseas citizens to vote in all constituencies without registration
To conceal booth-wise voting patterns by pooling control units
64.x: The ECI's RVM prototype is intended to enable domestic migrants to vote for up to 72 constituencies from one remote polling station.
64.tq: Distinguish remote voting from totaliser-based secrecy of booth results.
64.sec: Remote voting machine and totaliser proposals  [GROUP-II]

64.s: The ECI demonstrated its Remote EVM prototype to political parties in:
64.x: The Remote EVM prototype was demonstrated to political parties in January 2023.
64.tq: Use the event date to distinguish the proposal from later court proceedings.
64.sec: Remote voting machine and totaliser proposals  [GROUP-II]

64.s: A totaliser is intended to:
o: Replace all VVPAT slips with postal ballots
Pool the count of several control units so that booth-wise voting patterns remain hidden
Verify the identity of voters through biometric data
Allow one voter to cast votes in several constituencies
64.x: A totaliser pools the counts of several control units, thereby concealing booth-wise voting patterns.
64.tq: Match the device with its core function and distinguish it from an RVM.
64.sec: Remote voting machine and totaliser proposals  [GROUP-II]

64.s: On 1 September 2026, the Supreme Court sought the Centre's response regarding totalisers as a:
64.x: The Supreme Court sought the Centre's response on using totalisers as a “fall-back option.”
64.tq: Recall the exact status of the proposal rather than treating it as an implemented reform.
64.sec: Remote voting machine and totaliser proposals  [GROUP-II]

64.s: Which of the following was an objection raised by the Election Commission to the use of totalisers?
o: The Constitution expressly prohibits pooling of votes.
There is no legal framework in the RPA or the Conduct of Election Rules, and booth-wise checks would become harder.
Totalisers would make it impossible to count votes in urban constituencies.
The Law Commission had withdrawn its recommendation on totalisers.
64.x: The ECI objected that neither the RPA nor the Conduct of Election Rules provides a legal framework, and that pooling would make booth- and machine-wise checks involving EVMs, VVPATs and Form 17C harder.
64.tq: Combine the legal-framework objection with the practical verification objection.
64.sec: Remote voting machine and totaliser proposals  [GROUP-II]

64.s: Which of the following correctly describes the electoral status of Registered Unrecognised Political Parties (RUPPs) mentioned in current discussions?
o: There are about 750 RUPPs, all of which contested the 2024 election.
There are about 280 RUPPs, of which 75 contested the 2024 election.
There are over 2,800 RUPPs, but only about 750 contested the 2024 election.
There are over 2,800 RUPPs, all of which contested the 2024 election.
64.x: The number of RUPPs exceeds 2,800, while only approximately 750 contested the 2024 election.
64.tq: Check both numbers and avoid reversing the larger registered figure with the smaller contested figure.

64.s: Under the current provision referred to in the context of RUPPs, donations are tax-exempt under:
o: Section 12 of the Income Tax Act, 2025
Section 81 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951
Section 29A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951
64.x: The stated provision is Section 12 of the Income Tax Act, 2025, under which the relevant donations are tax-exempt.
64.tq: Distinguish the tax-law provision from nearby election-law provisions.

64.s: Which pair of actions was attributed to the Election Commission in relation to RUPPs?
o: Recognising 808 RUPPs and capping candidates at 1,200 per constituency
Delisting 808 RUPPs and capping electors at 1,200 per polling station
Deregistering 1,200 RUPPs and capping polling stations at 808 per district
Delisting 750 RUPPs and permitting unlimited electors per polling station
64.x: The Election Commission delisted 808 RUPPs and capped the number of electors per polling station at 1,200.
64.tq: Keep the two numerical administrative measures together.

64.s: The 2023 Act relating to the selection panel for the election referee has been criticised because it:
o: Gives the judiciary a majority over the executive
Gives State Election Commissions exclusive control over the panel
Gives the executive a majority and removed the Chief Justice of India from the panel
Removes the Election Commission from the selection process entirely
64.x: The criticism is that the 2023 Act gives the executive a majority on the panel and removes the Chief Justice of India from it.
64.tq: Identify both linked changes instead of selecting only one part of the criticism.

64.s: In State of Karnataka v Prathik Parasrampuria (2026), the Supreme Court treated which matter as a core duty of the Election Commission of India?
64.x: The Supreme Court made curbing electoral black money a core duty of the Election Commission in the 2026 case.
64.tq: Match the case with the specific institutional responsibility identified by it.

64.s: Which limitation of the Election Commission is highlighted in relation to financial non-compliance by political parties?
o: It cannot prepare electoral rolls for Parliament.
It lacks the power to deregister parties for financial non-compliance.
It has no power to scrutinise campaign expenditure.
It cannot conduct elections using EVMs.
64.x: The Election Commission still lacks the power to deregister political parties for financial non-compliance.
64.tq: Distinguish a specific statutory limitation from broader election powers.

64.s:
Which of the following are identified as unfinished areas in electoral reform discussions?
1. State funding of elections
2. Disqualification upon framing of charges
3. A cap on political party expenditure
4. Universal compulsory voting
Which of the statements given above are correct?
64.x: State funding, disqualification on framing of charges and a party spending cap are identified as unfinished agendas. Universal compulsory voting is not included in the stated list.
64.tq: Separate listed reform priorities from an unlisted but plausible electoral reform.

64.s: The expression “bahubali culture” in the context of electoral politics refers primarily to the erosion of trust in legislatures through:
64.x: The expression refers to the use of muscle power and its adverse effect on trust in legislatures.
64.tq: Decode the contextual meaning of a politically significant phrase.

64.s:
Which of the following developments was reported in relation to electoral reforms in February 2026?
1. The Joint Parliamentary Committee was still examining the 129th Amendment Bill.
2. The ECI and State Election Commissions declared that they would share EVMs, electoral rolls and ECINET.
3. The declaration was associated with Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
64.x: All three statements correctly describe the developments reported in February 2026.
64.tq: Verify the date, institutional cooperation and office-holder together.

64.s: Which one of the following correctly matches the institution or issue with the associated electoral reform debate?
o: Totaliser — replacement of the electoral roll
Remote EVM — pooling booth-wise counts to hide patterns
129th Amendment Bill — VVPAT slip design by NID Ahmedabad
64.x: Electoral bonds have been criticised in relation to opaque corporate funding. A totaliser pools counts, an RVM facilitates remote voting, and NID Ahmedabad designed the NOTA symbol rather than the 129th Amendment Bill being related to VVPAT design.
64.tq: Start with the sure conceptual pair and reject cross-linked distractors.

69.s: With reference to the composition of Public Service Commissions, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: The Constitution fixes the strength of both UPSC and SPSC
The strength of both Commissions is decided by Parliament
The strength of UPSC is decided by the President and that of SPSC by the Governor
The strength of UPSC is decided by the Governor and that of SPSC by the President
69.x: The Constitution does not fix the strength of either Commission. The President determines the strength of UPSC, while the Governor determines the strength of an SPSC.
69.tq: Test the authority responsible for composition instead of confusing it with the appointing authority.
69.sec: Appointment and removal of UPSC and SPSC members (Art. 316-317)

69.s: The usual strength of the Union Public Service Commission, including its Chairman, is stated to be approximately
69.x: The strength of UPSC is not constitutionally fixed, but it usually consists of about 9–11 members including the Chairman.
69.tq: Use the numerical range directly and distinguish a usual practice from a constitutionally fixed strength.
69.sec: Appointment and removal of UPSC and SPSC members (Art. 316-317)

69.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the tenure of members of Public Service Commissions:
1. A member of UPSC holds office for six years or until attaining the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
2. A member of an SPSC holds office for six years or until attaining the age of 62 years, whichever is earlier.
3. A member of a Joint State Public Service Commission retires at the age of 65 years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
69.x: UPSC members retire at 65 years and SPSC members at 62 years, subject in both cases to the six-year term. The age limit for a Joint State Public Service Commission is 62 years, not 65.
69.tq: Separate the age limits of UPSC, SPSC and JSPSC before selecting the coded combination.
69.sec: Appointment and removal of UPSC and SPSC members (Art. 316-317)

69.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the resignation arrangement for the three types of Public Service Commissions?
69.x: Members of UPSC and a Joint State Public Service Commission resign to the President. Members of an SPSC resign to the Governor.
69.tq: Start from the sure resignation authority and compare all three bodies.
69.sec: Appointment and removal of UPSC and SPSC members (Art. 316-317)

69.s:
With reference to removal of members of Public Service Commissions, consider the following statements:
1. Insolvency is a ground for removal.
2. Paid employment outside the duties of office is a ground for removal.
3. Infirmity of mind or body is a ground for removal.
4. Misbehaviour can be established by the President without referring the matter to the Supreme Court.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
69.x: Insolvency, outside paid employment and infirmity of mind or body are grounds for removal. In the case of misbehaviour, the President must first refer the matter to the Supreme Court.
69.tq: Find the one wrong procedural statement among otherwise established removal grounds.
69.sec: Appointment and removal of UPSC and SPSC members (Art. 316-317)

69.s: In the case of alleged misbehaviour by a member of a Public Service Commission, which procedure is constitutionally required?
o: The Governor conducts the inquiry and gives the final decision in every case
The Union Cabinet conducts the inquiry and recommends removal to the concerned Commission
The President refers the matter to the Supreme Court, and removal follows only if the Court upholds the charge
Parliament must pass an impeachment resolution by special majority
69.x: For misbehaviour, the President refers the matter to the Supreme Court. The member may be removed only when the Supreme Court upholds the cause, and its advice is binding.
69.tq: Follow the constitutional sequence: reference, judicial examination and binding outcome.
69.sec: Appointment and removal of UPSC and SPSC members (Art. 316-317)

69.s: During an inquiry by the Supreme Court into alleged misbehaviour of a member of an SPSC, who may suspend the member?
o: The Governor of the State בלבד
69.x: The President may suspend a member during the Supreme Court inquiry, including a member of an SPSC.
69.tq: Apply the removal-authority rule rather than the appointment-authority rule.
69.sec: Appointment and removal of UPSC and SPSC members (Art. 316-317)

69.s: Which of the following is included within the meaning of misbehaviour for the purpose of Article 317?
o: Failure to secure unanimous decisions in the Commission
Refusal to accept a temporary appointment
Disagreement with a recommendation of the Commission
Being interested in a government contract or sharing in its profit
69.x: Misbehaviour includes being interested in a government contract or sharing in its profit under Article 317(4).
69.tq: Discriminate the specific statutory example from general administrative disagreements.
69.sec: Appointment and removal of UPSC and SPSC members (Art. 316-317)

69.s: A constitutional requirement relating to the background of members of a Public Service Commission is that
o: all members must have held office under the Union Government
at least one-fourth of the members must have served in Parliament
at least half the members must have held government office for at least ten years
all members must have served in the judiciary for ten years
69.x: At least half of the members must have held office under the Government of India or a State Government for a minimum of ten years.
69.tq: Watch the quantifier and the alternative government levels in a composition requirement.
69.sec: Appointment and removal of UPSC and SPSC members (Art. 316-317)

69.s: When the office of the Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission falls vacant or the Chairman is unable to perform the duties of office, the Acting Chairman is appointed by the
69.x: The President appoints an Acting Chairman during a vacancy in the office of the Chairman or during the Chairman's absence or inability to function.
69.tq: Ask who would perform the constitutional appointment function during a vacancy.
69.sec: Appointment and removal of UPSC and SPSC members (Art. 316-317)

69.s: Under Article 320, the Union Public Service Commission conducts examinations primarily for appointment to
o: only Group B and Group C posts
69.x: UPSC conducts examinations for appointment to All-India services, Central services and Group-A services. Group B and C posts and the highest diplomatic posts are outside the stated purview.
69.tq: Distinguish the principal examination mandate from categories expressly excluded from consultation.
69.sec: Functions of UPSC - consulted and not consulted (Art. 320, 321)

69.s: Which one of the following is NOT ordinarily a matter on which the Union Public Service Commission is consulted?
o: Suitability of candidates for appointment, promotion or transfer
Methods of recruitment to civil services and posts
Manner of reservation for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes
69.x: The manner of reservation for SCs and STs is outside UPSC's consultation function. Recruitment methods, promotion and transfer principles, and candidate suitability are matters for consultation.
69.tq: Find the excluded subject rather than selecting a familiar UPSC function.
69.sec: Functions of UPSC - consulted and not consulted (Art. 320, 321)

69.s:
Consider the following matters:
1. Claims of SCs and STs to services and posts
2. Temporary appointments for less than one year
3. Temporary appointments for more than one year
4. Group B and Group C posts
Which of the above are generally outside the consultation of UPSC?
69.x: Claims of SCs and STs, temporary appointments of less than one year, and Group B and C posts are excluded. Temporary appointments exceeding one year are ordinarily subject to consultation.
69.tq: Split the options using the critical duration distinction of less than or more than one year.
69.sec: Functions of UPSC - consulted and not consulted (Art. 320, 321)

69.s:
Which of the following matters is included among the disciplinary matters on which UPSC may be consulted?
1. Censure
2. Withholding of increments
3. Demotion
4. Removal from service
69.x: The disciplinary consultation of UPSC may cover censure, withholding of increments, demotion and removal, among other disciplinary penalties.
69.tq: Recognize that the list spans penalties from censure to removal rather than stopping at minor penalties.
69.sec: Functions of UPSC - consulted and not consulted (Art. 320, 321)

69.s: UPSC may be consulted regarding claims for
o: political allowances of Ministers and Members of Parliament
pension arising from service injuries and reimbursement of legal expenses incurred in official duties
tax exemptions claimed by government employees
69.x: UPSC is consulted on claims for pension in respect of injuries sustained in government service and claims for reimbursement of legal expenses incurred in defending official actions.
69.tq: Select the precise paired subject instead of broad welfare or financial claims.
69.sec: Functions of UPSC - consulted and not consulted (Art. 320, 321)

69.s: Which one of the following statements best describes the legal effect of advice given by UPSC?
o: The advice can be rejected only by Parliament
The advice is advisory, and action taken without consultation is not invalid merely for that reason
The advice has no relevance in disciplinary matters
The advice is binding and any departure automatically invalidates the appointment
69.x: UPSC advice is advisory rather than binding. A decision taken without consultation does not become invalid solely because consultation was omitted.
69.tq: Apply the directory-versus-mandatory distinction to an administrative decision.
69.sec: Functions of UPSC - consulted and not consulted (Art. 320, 321)

69.s: A Ministry disagrees with the advice of UPSC on a matter requiring consultation. Which statement is correct?
o: The Ministry may reject the advice on its own authority in every case
The advice can be rejected by the Chairman of UPSC
The advice must be accepted by the Supreme Court
The advice can be disregarded only after approval of the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet
69.x: Non-acceptance of UPSC advice requires the approval of the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet; a Ministry cannot reject it alone.
69.tq: Identify the higher authority required when an executive department seeks to depart from advice.
69.sec: Functions of UPSC - consulted and not consulted (Art. 320, 321)

69.s: Under Article 321, the functions of UPSC may be extended by
o: a resolution of the UPSC itself
an executive order of any Ministry
a regulation made by a State Governor alone
69.x: Parliament may extend the functions of UPSC by law, including functions relating to personnel systems of local bodies, corporations or public institutions.
69.tq: Distinguish legislative extension of functions from executive allocation of work.
69.sec: Functions of UPSC - consulted and not consulted (Art. 320, 321)

69.s:
Which of the following may be included in an extension of UPSC functions under Article 321?
1. Personnel system of a local body
2. Personnel system of a corporation
3. Personnel system of a public institution
4. Conduct of elections to Parliament
Select the correct answer using the code below.
69.x: Article 321 permits extension of UPSC functions to personnel systems of local bodies, corporations and public institutions. Conduct of parliamentary elections is not such a personnel function.
69.tq: Separate personnel-related extensions from an unrelated constitutional function.
69.sec: Functions of UPSC - consulted and not consulted (Art. 320, 321)

69.s: The power to exclude posts from consultation with a Public Service Commission may be exercised through regulations by the
o: Parliament for UPSC and Supreme Court for SPSC
President for UPSC and Governor for SPSC
Governor for UPSC and President for SPSC
Chairman of the concerned Commission in both cases
69.x: The President may exclude posts from consultation with UPSC, while the Governor may exclude posts from consultation with the SPSC through regulations.
69.tq: Match the regulatory authority with the corresponding Union or State Commission.
69.sec: Functions of UPSC - consulted and not consulted (Art. 320, 321)

69.s: Regulations excluding posts from consultation with a Public Service Commission must be laid before the concerned legislature for a period of
69.x: Regulations excluding posts from consultation must be laid before Parliament or the concerned State Legislature for fourteen days.
69.tq: Test the specific statutory duration rather than the general legislative laying requirement.
69.sec: Functions of UPSC - consulted and not consulted (Art. 320, 321)

69.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: UPSC—consultation on reservation of posts for SCs and STs
69.x: Reservation of posts for SCs and STs is excluded from UPSC consultation. Recruitment methods, candidate suitability, and extension or re-employment are listed consultation matters.
69.tq: Look for the excluded reservation subject among genuine Article 320 functions.
69.sec: Functions of UPSC - consulted and not consulted (Art. 320, 321)

69.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes UPSC from the Central Vigilance Commission in disciplinary matters?
o: Only UPSC is consulted on disciplinary matters
Only CVC is consulted on disciplinary matters
Both may be consulted on disciplinary matters, with UPSC having the stated edge in this area
Neither body has any role in disciplinary matters
69.x: The disciplinary role is shared by UPSC and the Central Vigilance Commission. CVC was established in 1964 and given statutory status in 2003, while UPSC retains the stated edge in this area.
69.tq: Avoid the exclusive-word trap by recognizing overlapping institutional roles.
69.sec: Functions of UPSC - consulted and not consulted (Art. 320, 321)

69.s: The Central Vigilance Commission was established in 1964 and received statutory status in
69.x: The Central Vigilance Commission was established in 1964 and became a statutory body in 2003.
69.tq: Pair the institution with its two separate milestone years.
69.sec: Functions of UPSC - consulted and not consulted (Art. 320, 321)

69.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the role of a State Public Service Commission in relation to the State Vigilance Commission?
o: The State Vigilance Commission shares the disciplinary role with the State Public Service Commission
The State Public Service Commission has no role in disciplinary matters
The State Vigilance Commission appoints all members of the SPSC
The State Public Service Commission is the sole disciplinary authority
69.x: The disciplinary role of an SPSC is shared with the State Vigilance Commission, just as the UPSC's role is shared with the CVC at the Union level.
69.tq: Compare the corresponding Union and State institutional arrangements.
69.sec: Functions of UPSC - consulted and not consulted (Art. 320, 321)

69.s: The State Public Service Commission is commonly described as the watchdog of the
69.x: The SPSC is described as the watchdog of the merit system in public services.
69.tq: Recall the distinctive institutional description without confusing it with financial or electoral oversight.
69.sec: Functions of UPSC - consulted and not consulted (Art. 320, 321)

69.s: Which one of the following is outside the principal concern of a State Public Service Commission?
o: Classification, pay and training of government employees
Advice on promotion and transfer principles
69.x: An SPSC is not concerned with classification, pay or training. Its principal concerns include recruitment, promotion, transfer and candidate suitability.
69.tq: Identify the administrative personnel subjects expressly placed outside the Commission's concern.
69.sec: Functions of UPSC - consulted and not consulted (Art. 320, 321)

69.s: The Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission came into existence on which date?
69.x: The Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission came into existence on 1 November 1956, with the formation of Andhra Pradesh.
69.tq: Use the precise date rather than the related formation year.
69.sec: APPSC - establishment, headquarters, composition

69.s: The Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission was formed by merging which of the following?
69.x: The APPSC was formed by merging the Andhra Public Service Commission, established in 1953, and the Hyderabad Public Service Commission.
69.tq: Test the exact institutional predecessors of the body.
69.sec: APPSC - establishment, headquarters, composition

69.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission:
1. It continues to serve the residuary State of Andhra Pradesh after the 2014 bifurcation.
2. Telangana obtained the Telangana State Public Service Commission after bifurcation.
3. Its Chairman and members are appointed by the Governor of Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
69.x: All three statements are correct. After bifurcation, APPSC continued for residuary Andhra Pradesh, Telangana constituted TSPSC, and the Governor appoints APPSC members.
69.tq: Check each institutional consequence of bifurcation separately.
69.sec: APPSC - establishment, headquarters, composition

69.s: Which one of the following functions is performed by the Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission in addition to recruitment to State services?
o: Conducting examinations for the lower judicial service
Auditing the accounts of the State Government
Appointing judges of the High Court
69.x: The APPSC conducts recruitment examinations for State services and examinations for the lower judicial service under Article 234.
69.tq: Distinguish a recruitment function from constitutional appointments and auditing.
69.sec: APPSC - establishment, headquarters, composition

69.s: A Joint State Public Service Commission can be established only when which of the following conditions is fulfilled?
o: The Governors of two or more States issue a joint notification.
The Parliament passes an Act on the request of two or more State Legislatures.
The President issues an executive order on his own initiative.
The UPSC recommends its establishment to the Union Cabinet.
69.x: A Joint State Public Service Commission is created by an Act of Parliament following a request from the legislatures of two or more States.
69.tq: Ask which authority performs the job and identify the required initiating condition.
69.sec: Joint State Public Service Commission

69.s: A Joint State Public Service Commission is best described as a:
o: Constitutional body created directly by Article 315
Statutory body created by an Act of Parliament
Temporary committee of the Inter-State Council
Non-statutory advisory body created by the President
69.x: Although Public Service Commissions are constitutionally recognised, a Joint State Public Service Commission is established by a Parliamentary Act and is therefore statutory.
69.tq: Separate the constitutional recognition of PSCs from the statutory character of a Joint Commission.
69.sec: Joint State Public Service Commission

69.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Joint State Public Service Commission — annual report laid before Parliament
Joint State Public Service Commission — annual report laid before each concerned State Legislature by the Governor
Joint State Public Service Commission — annual report laid before the Supreme Court
Joint State Public Service Commission — annual report laid before the UPSC
69.x: The Joint State Public Service Commission submits its report to each concerned Governor, who lays it before the relevant State Legislature.
69.tq: Trace the reporting chain from the Commission to the legislature.
69.sec: Joint State Public Service Commission

69.s:
Consider the following statements about a Joint State Public Service Commission:
1. Its Chairman and members are appointed by the President.
2. Their service conditions and the number of members are fixed by the President.
3. A member submits resignation to the concerned Governor.
4. The normal term is six years or until the age of 62 years, whichever is earlier.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
69.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. A member of a Joint Commission resigns to the President, not to the concerned Governor, making statement 3 incorrect.
69.tq: Use the authority-based trap in the resignation provision.
69.sec: Joint State Public Service Commission

69.s: Punjab and Haryana had a Joint State Public Service Commission for a brief period after:
69.x: Punjab and Haryana had a Joint State Public Service Commission briefly after the reorganisation associated with 1966.
69.tq: Distinguish the specific reorganisation year from nearby constitutional dates.
69.sec: Joint State Public Service Commission

69.s: Which of the following Articles deals with regulations regarding conditions of service of members and staff of a Public Service Commission?
69.x: Article 318 empowers the competent authority to make regulations regarding conditions of service and staff of a Public Service Commission.
69.tq: Discriminate between consecutive constitutional provisions by subject.
69.sec: Articles 315-323 → content

69.s: Which Article of the Constitution imposes a bar on holding office after a person ceases to be a member of a Public Service Commission?
69.x: Article 319 provides the post-office restrictions applicable to the Chairman and members of Public Service Commissions.
69.tq: Match the constitutional article with its exact subject.
69.sec: Articles 315-323 → content

69.s: Under which Article can the functions of a Public Service Commission be extended?
69.x: Article 321 provides for the power to extend the functions of a Public Service Commission.
69.tq: Use the article-number sequence while focusing on the operative verb.
69.sec: Articles 315-323 → content

69.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Article 322 of the Constitution?
o: It deals with expenses of Public Service Commissions being charged on the Consolidated Fund.
It deals with annual reports of Public Service Commissions.
It deals with appointment and term of members.
It deals with removal and suspension of members.
69.x: Article 322 provides that the expenses of Public Service Commissions are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India or the State, as applicable.
69.tq: Identify the provision by its institutional subject rather than by sequence alone.
69.sec: Articles 315-323 → content

69.s:
Arrange the following Articles in ascending order of their constitutional sequence:
A. Functions of Public Service Commissions
B. Reports of Public Service Commissions
C. Extension of functions
D. Expenses of Public Service Commissions
69.x: The correct sequence is Article 320 (functions), Article 321 (extension), Article 322 (expenses), and Article 323 (reports).
69.tq: Anchor the sequence at the consecutive Articles 320 to 323.
69.sec: Articles 315-323 → content

69.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Public Service Commissions form part of Part XIV of the Constitution.
2. The UPSC is directly created by the Constitution.
3. The UPSC is the central recruiting agency for the Union.
4. A member's service conditions may be varied to his or her disadvantage after appointment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
69.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Service conditions cannot be varied to a member's disadvantage after appointment, so statement 4 is false.
69.tq: Find the single statement that reverses an independence safeguard.
69.sec: Articles 315-323 → content

69.s: The normal term of office of a member of a State Public Service Commission ends on completion of:
o: Five years or 60 years of age, whichever is earlier
Six years or 65 years of age, whichever is earlier
Seven years or 62 years of age, whichever is earlier
Six years or 62 years of age, whichever is earlier
69.x: A State Public Service Commission member holds office for six years or until attaining 62 years of age, whichever is earlier.
69.tq: Compare the tenure and age limits of State and Union Commissions.
69.sec: SPSC members - term, age, strength, post-retirement eligibility

69.s: Which of the following statements regarding the strength of a State Public Service Commission is correct?
o: It is fixed by the Parliament for all States uniformly.
It is fixed permanently by the Constitution.
It is left to be determined by the Governor.
It is determined by the Chief Justice of the High Court.
69.x: The strength of a State Public Service Commission is left to the Governor, unlike a constitutionally fixed uniform number.
69.tq: Test who determines the composition rather than who appoints the members.
69.sec: SPSC members - term, age, strength, post-retirement eligibility

69.s: Which one of the following is NOT permissible for a member of a State Public Service Commission after ceasing to hold office?
o: Becoming Chairman of the same or another State Public Service Commission
Accepting any other employment under the Government of India
Becoming a member of the UPSC
69.x: A former SPSC member may become UPSC Chairman or member, or Chairman of the same or another SPSC, but cannot accept any other government employment.
69.tq: Use the post-office bar to eliminate the broadly worded employment option.
69.sec: SPSC members - term, age, strength, post-retirement eligibility

69.s: Which of the following correctly states the post-retirement eligibility of a UPSC member?
o: He or she may serve a second term as a UPSC member.
He or she may become UPSC Chairman or Chairman of an SPSC, but nothing else.
He or she may accept any employment under the Union Government.
He or she may become Governor of any State as a matter of right.
69.x: A UPSC member may become Chairman of the UPSC or Chairman of an SPSC, but cannot take other government employment or serve a second term in the same office.
69.tq: Distinguish the limited permitted offices from the general post-office bar.
69.sec: SPSC members - term, age, strength, post-retirement eligibility

69.s: Which statement correctly compares the age limits for members of the UPSC and State Public Service Commissions?
o: 60 years for UPSC and 62 years for SPSC
62 years for UPSC and 65 years for SPSC
65 years for both UPSC and SPSC
65 years for UPSC and 62 years for SPSC
69.x: The age limit is 65 years for UPSC members and 62 years for SPSC and Joint State Public Service Commission members, subject in each case to the six-year term.
69.tq: Compare the two figures directly instead of transferring the Union limit to the States.
69.sec: SPSC members - term, age, strength, post-retirement eligibility

69.s: The Government of India Act, 1919 provided for the establishment of a:
69.x: The Government of India Act, 1919 provided for a Public Service Commission; the Federal Public Service Commission came later under the Government of India Act, 1935.
69.tq: Separate the generic early provision from the later Federal Commission.
69.sec: UPSC history

69.s: The Lee Commission recommended the establishment of a Public Service Commission in:
69.x: The Lee Commission recommended the establishment of a Public Service Commission in 1924.
69.tq: Distinguish the recommendation year from the year of actual establishment.
69.sec: UPSC history

69.s: The Federal Public Service Commission became the Union Public Service Commission on:
69.x: The Federal Public Service Commission became the UPSC on 26 January 1950, and its members continued under Article 378.
69.tq: Place the constitutional transition at the commencement of the Constitution.
69.sec: UPSC history

69.s: The ICS examinations began to be held simultaneously in India from 1922 in the context of the:
69.x: ICS examinations began to be held simultaneously in India from 1922 in the context of the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms.
69.tq: Link the date with the reform framework rather than the later statutory Act.
69.sec: UPSC history

69.s: The headquarters of the Union Public Service Commission is located at:
69.x: The headquarters of the UPSC is Dholpur House in New Delhi.
69.tq: Test the exact location, not merely the city.
69.sec: UPSC history

69.s:
Which of the following safeguards contributes to the independence of Public Service Commissions?
1. Their salaries, allowances and expenses are charged on the Consolidated Fund.
2. Their service conditions cannot be varied to their disadvantage after appointment.
3. Their members may be removed at the discretion of the appointing authority.
4. A post-office bar restricts subsequent government employment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
69.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are safeguards of independence. Statement 3 is false because removal is governed by constitutional grounds and procedure, not mere discretion of the appointing authority.
69.tq: Identify the statement that weakens, rather than protects, institutional independence.
69.sec: Independence safeguards

69.s:
Assertion (A): The service conditions of a member of a Public Service Commission cannot be varied to his or her disadvantage after appointment.
Reason (R): Protection from disadvantageous alteration of service conditions is intended to preserve the independence of the Commission.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
69.x: Both statements are true, and the protection exists precisely to prevent executive or political pressure on Commission members after appointment.
69.tq: Test whether the constitutional safeguard and its institutional purpose are directly connected.
69.sec: Independence safeguards

69.s: In the case of the UPSC, the memorandum accompanying the annual report relates to:
o: Cases in which the Commission's advice was not accepted
The annual expenditure of every State PSC
The personal assets of Commission members
The number of candidates appearing for examinations
69.x: The UPSC annual report is accompanied by a memorandum explaining cases in which its advice was not accepted.
69.tq: Identify the specific content of the accompanying memorandum.
69.sec: Annual report and non-acceptance of advice

69.s: Which authority must approve every case in which the advice of the UPSC is not accepted?
o: The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet
The Union Public Service Commission itself
69.x: Every case of non-acceptance of UPSC advice must be approved by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet; an individual ministry cannot reject the advice on its own.
69.tq: Ask which authority would perform the specific approval function.
69.sec: Annual report and non-acceptance of advice

69.s:
Consider the following statements regarding annual reports of Public Service Commissions:
1. The UPSC submits its report to the President.
2. The UPSC report is laid before both Houses of Parliament.
3. An SPSC submits its report to the Governor.
4. The Governor lays the SPSC report before the State Legislature.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
69.x: All four statements are correct. The UPSC report follows the President-Parliament route, while an SPSC report follows the Governor-State Legislature route.
69.tq: Trace and compare the two reporting chains.
69.sec: Annual report and non-acceptance of advice

69.s: A ministry rejects the advice of the UPSC without obtaining approval from any other authority. Which statement is correct?
o: The rejection must first be approved by the concerned State Legislature.
The rejection is not procedurally complete because approval of the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet is required.
The rejection is valid if the ministry records reasons in its internal file.
The rejection is valid because UPSC advice is never binding.
69.x: A ministry cannot reject UPSC advice on its own; every such case must be approved by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet and reported through the prescribed memorandum.
69.tq: Apply the approval-chain rule to an administrative situation.
69.sec: Annual report and non-acceptance of advice

69.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Article 316 — Appointment and term of members
Article 317 — Functions of Public Service Commissions
Article 323 — Reports of Public Service Commissions
Article 315 — Public Service Commissions for the Union and States
69.x: Article 317 deals with removal and suspension of members. Functions of Public Service Commissions are dealt with in Article 320.
69.tq: Find the swapped subject among consecutive constitutional Articles.
69.sec: Articles 315-323 → content

Match List-I with List-II regarding committees that reviewed the Civil Services Examination:

List-I (Committee)
a. D.S. Kothari Committee
b. Satish Chandra Committee
c. Y.K. Alagh Committee
d. P.C. Hota Committee

iv. Introduction of the three-stage examination system

69.s:
Consider the following committees:
1. D.S. Kothari Committee
2. Satish Chandra Committee
3. Y.K. Alagh Committee
4. P.C. Hota Committee
5. B.S. Baswan Committee

Which one of the following represents the correct chronological order of their constitution?
69.x: The committees belong respectively to 1974–76, 1989, 2000–01, 2004 and 2016, giving the order D.S. Kothari, Satish Chandra, Y.K. Alagh, P.C. Hota and B.S. Baswan.

69.x: The three-stage examination system recommended by the D.S. Kothari Committee came into effect from 1979.
