69.s: The Satish Chandra Committee is associated with which one of the following recommendations or developments?
o: Civil service reforms relating to administrative restructuring
Review of age limit, number of attempts and examination pattern
Review of the Kothari scheme and introduction of an essay paper
Introduction of the three-stage examination system from 1979
69.x: The Satish Chandra Committee, constituted in 1989, reviewed the Kothari scheme and was associated with the essay paper.
69.tq: Apply the wrong-committee trap by matching each committee with its specific theme.
69.sec: Committees reviewing the civil services examination  [other exams, GROUP-II]

69.s: Which one of the following committees was associated with civil service reforms?
69.x: The P.C. Hota Committee, constituted in 2004, dealt with civil service reforms.
69.tq: Test the committee-theme association rather than relying only on chronological recall.
69.sec: Committees reviewing the civil services examination  [other exams, GROUP-II]

69.s: The B.S. Baswan Committee, constituted in 2016, examined issues relating to:
o: The introduction of the essay paper alone
Age limit, number of attempts and examination pattern
The three-stage examination system introduced in 1979
69.x: The B.S. Baswan Committee examined the age limit, number of attempts and examination pattern for the Civil Services Examination.
69.tq: Beware of the word “only” and identify the option that captures all the stated areas of review.
69.sec: Committees reviewing the civil services examination  [other exams, GROUP-II]

69.s:
With reference to the committees reviewing the Civil Services Examination, consider the following statements:
1. The Y.K. Alagh Committee was constituted during 2000–01.
2. The P.C. Hota Committee was constituted in 2004.
3. The B.S. Baswan Committee was constituted in 2016.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
69.x: All three statements are correct: Y.K. Alagh was associated with 2000–01, P.C. Hota with 2004 and B.S. Baswan with 2016.
69.tq: Check each year independently before selecting the cumulative code.
69.sec: Committees reviewing the civil services examination  [other exams, GROUP-II]

69.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the present concerns associated with State Public Service Commissions:
1. Paper leaks have affected public confidence.
2. Flawed evaluation has led to disputes.
3. Delays and litigation have emerged as significant concerns.
4. Telangana examinations in 2023 and Bihar examinations in 2024 are cited in this context.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
69.x: Paper leaks, flawed evaluation, delays and litigation are identified as major concerns, with the Telangana 2023 and Bihar 2024 examinations cited as examples.
69.tq: Treat the examples in the final statement as factual anchors and verify the broader concerns around them.
69.sec: Universal angles

69.s: The Supreme Court stressed the importance of Public Service Commission independence in which of the following cases?
69.x: In T.N. PSC v. A. Balasubramaniam (1994), the Supreme Court stressed that PSC independence is essential for fair administration.
69.tq: Discriminate carefully among the case name, year and institution instead of accepting a familiar-looking combination.
69.sec: Universal angles

69.s:
Assertion (A): Independence of Public Service Commissions is essential for fair administration.
Reason (R): Public Service Commissions are intended to safeguard merit in public recruitment and administration.

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
69.x: Both statements are true, and the merit-protection role of Public Service Commissions explains why their institutional independence is essential for fair administration.
69.tq: Test whether the Reason explains the institutional purpose stated in the Assertion.
69.sec: Universal angles

69.s: Who was the first Indian to clear the Indian Civil Service examination?
69.x: Satyendranath Tagore was the first Indian to clear the Indian Civil Service examination, in 1864.
69.tq: Use the first-person-in-history cue and avoid confusing it with later examination reform committees.
69.sec: Universal angles

69.s: The simultaneous conduct of the Indian Civil Service examinations in India began in 1922 at:
69.x: From 1922, the Indian Civil Service examinations were conducted simultaneously in India at Allahabad.
69.tq: Separate the starting year from the examination venue and identify the precise location.
69.sec: Universal angles

70.x: The award period of the 13th Finance Commission was 2010–15.

70.x: The 14th Finance Commission covered 2015–20.

70.s:
With reference to the Finance Commission, consider the following statements:
1. It is constituted under Article 280 of the Constitution.
2. It is a quasi-judicial constitutional body.
3. It is constituted by the President every fifth year or earlier.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
70.x: All three statements are correct. Article 280 provides for a quasi-judicial Finance Commission constituted by the President every fifth year or earlier.
70.tq: Verify the constitutional article, institutional character and periodicity together.

70.s: The Finance Commission consists of:
o: A Chairman and four members appointed by the President
A Chairman and three members appointed by Parliament
A Chairman and four members appointed by the Prime Minister
70.x: The Finance Commission comprises a Chairman and four other members appointed by the President.
70.tq: Test composition and appointing authority in the same question.

70.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the members of the Finance Commission:
1. Their term is specified by the President.
2. They are eligible for reappointment.
3. Their term is fixed permanently by the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
70.x: The President specifies the term, and members are eligible for reappointment. The Constitution does not permanently prescribe one fixed term.
70.tq: Identify the true provisions and reject the absolute claim about a permanently fixed term.

70.s: The qualifications of the Chairman and members of the Finance Commission are prescribed by Parliament under the:
70.x: Parliament prescribed the qualifications through the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951, also referred to in abbreviated form as the Finance Commission Act, 1951.
70.tq: Distinguish the exact statutory title from plausible but nonexistent titles.

70.s: Which of the following is the prescribed qualification for the Chairman of the Finance Commission?
o: Service as a Governor of a State
Experience exclusively as a High Court Chief Justice
Membership of Parliament for ten years
70.x: The Chairman must have experience in public affairs.
70.tq: Match the office with its exact statutory qualification rather than a prestigious but unstated qualification.

70.s: Which one of the following is NOT among the specified fields from which the four members of the Finance Commission are drawn?
o: A person with special knowledge of international diplomacy
A High Court judge or a person qualified to be one
A person with wide experience in financial administration
An expert in government finance and accounts
70.x: The specified fields include judicial qualification, government finance and accounts, financial administration, and economics. International diplomacy is not one of them.
70.tq: Find the one field outside the statutory list of member qualifications.

70.s: Which of the following correctly states the nature of the recommendations of the Finance Commission?
o: They have the force of constitutional amendments.
They are binding on the Union Government in all circumstances.
They are advisory and are not binding.
They are binding only on State Governments.
70.x: The recommendations of the Finance Commission are advisory and not binding.
70.tq: Discriminate between advisory and binding constitutional recommendations.

70.s: P.V. Rajamannar observed that the recommendations of the Finance Commission:
o: Can be modified only by the Supreme Court
May be rejected without assigning any reason
Are automatically enforceable as judicial decrees
Should not be rejected without very compelling reasons
70.x: P.V. Rajamannar stated that the recommendations should not be rejected without very compelling reasons.
70.tq: Recall the precise qualification attached to the advisory nature of recommendations.

70.s: Under Article 281, the President is required to place before each House of Parliament:
o: Only the report of the Comptroller and Auditor General
The recommendations along with an explanatory memorandum on the action taken
The recommendations after approval by the Supreme Court
70.x: Article 281 requires the President to lay the Finance Commission’s recommendations together with an explanatory memorandum on the action taken before each House of Parliament.
70.tq: Test the constitutional procedure and watch for the omission of the explanatory memorandum.

70.s: Which Article provides for the Finance Commission, while Article 290 deals with pensions?
70.x: Article 280 provides for the Finance Commission, whereas Article 290 deals with pensions. Article 281 concerns laying the recommendations before Parliament.
70.tq: Separate the look-alike constitutional article numbers by their subjects.

70.s: Which of the following correctly shows the States’ share of central taxes recommended by the 10th to 13th Finance Commissions?
70.x: The respective shares were 29% under the 10th, 29.5% under the 11th, 30.5% under the 12th and 32% under the 13th Finance Commission.

70.x: The 80th Amendment, 2000 implemented the 10th Finance Commission’s sharing of all central taxes with effect from 1 April 1996.
70.tq: Separate the amendment year from its effective date.
70.sec: Share of central taxes recommended (10th onward)  [APPSC]

Consider the following sequence of States’ share of central taxes:
1. 42%
2. 41%
3. 41%

The introduction of the GDP criterion
Jammu and Kashmir becoming a Union Territory

70.x: The 14th Finance Commission was constituted on 2 January 2013.
70.tq: Distinguish the constitution date from the date of acceptance and implementation.

70.s: Which major change was associated with the 14th Finance Commission?
o: A shift towards tax devolution as the main route, along with ignoring the Plan/non-Plan distinction
A shift from tax devolution to exclusive grants
Introduction of the GDP criterion for the first time

70.sec: Finance Commission number → award period and key recommendations  [APPSC]

70.s: Under the 14th Finance Commission’s allocation formula for local-body grants, the weights assigned to the 2011 population and area were respectively:

70.x: The 15th Finance Commission retained the 41% share and added demographic performance and tax effort as considerations.
70.tq: Identify the new criteria rather than a feature associated with an earlier commission.
70.sec: Finance Commission number → award period and key recommendations  [APPSC]

70.x: The 15th Finance Commission used the 2011 population base.

o: Revenue-deficit grants, sector-specific grants and State-specific grants
All grants to rural local bodies

70.sec: Finance Commission number → award period and key recommendations  [APPSC]

70.s: In the context of Finance Commission devolution, the term ‘vertical distribution’ refers to:
o: Allocation of the States’ share among different States
Distribution of the divisible pool between the Union and the States
Distribution of grants among Panchayats and Municipalities
Allocation of State taxes between rural and urban local bodies
70.x: Vertical distribution refers to the share of the divisible pool transferred to the States from the Union. Horizontal distribution refers to allocation of that States’ share among individual States.
70.tq: Discriminate between two closely related terms by identifying the level at which distribution takes place.
70.sec: Vertical vs horizontal distribution; 15th FC weights  [APPSC]

70.s: With reference to the divisible pool of central taxes, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: It excludes the proceeds of all shareable taxes under Article 270.
It consists only of State taxes collected by the Union.
It includes all gross tax revenue, including cesses and surcharges.
It was approximately 81% of gross tax revenue in 2025–26.
70.x: The divisible pool comprises shareable taxes under Article 270, excluding cesses and surcharges. In 2025–26, it was approximately 81% of gross tax revenue.
70.tq: Separate the divisible pool from gross tax revenue by checking the stated proportion and exclusions.
70.sec: Vertical vs horizontal distribution; 15th FC weights  [APPSC]

70.s: Which of the following best describes ‘horizontal distribution’ by the Finance Commission?
o: Division of the divisible pool between the Union and the States
Division of a State’s revenue between the State Government and local bodies
Allocation of the States’ share among the States according to a formula
Distribution of the Consolidated Fund of India between the two Houses of Parliament
70.x: Horizontal distribution is the allocation among States of the share assigned to the States through a prescribed formula.
70.tq: Test the distinction between vertical and horizontal distribution by focusing on the recipients of the allocation.
70.sec: Vertical vs horizontal distribution; 15th FC weights  [APPSC]

70.s:
Consider the following pairs relating to the criteria used by the Fourteenth and Fifteenth Finance Commissions:
a. Income distance — 50% under the 14th FC; 45% under the 15th FC
b. Population 1971 — 17.5% under the 14th FC
c. Population 2011 — 10% under the 14th FC; 15% under the 15th FC
d. Area — 15% under both the 14th and 15th FCs
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
70.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. The 14th FC gave weight to both 1971 and 2011 population, while the 15th FC used 2011 population and retained the 15% weight for area.
70.tq: Start from the sure numerical pair and verify whether the remaining criteria preserve their stated weights.
70.sec: Vertical vs horizontal distribution; 15th FC weights  [APPSC]

70.s:
With reference to the Sixteenth Finance Commission for 2026–31, consider the following statements:
1. Income distance has a weight of 42.5%.
2. Population 2011 has a weight of 17.5%.
3. Contribution to GDP has been introduced with a weight of 10%.
4. Tax and fiscal effort has been retained with a weight of 2.5%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
70.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false: the Sixteenth Finance Commission dropped the 2.5% criterion for tax and fiscal effort.
70.tq: Find the dropped criterion before selecting the coded combination of retained weights.
70.sec: Vertical vs horizontal distribution; 15th FC weights  [APPSC]

70.s: Under the Sixteenth Finance Commission, income distance is measured from:
o: The average of the top five States by population
The income of the poorest State alone
The average of the top three large States
The average income of all States
70.x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission measures income distance from the average of the top three large States.
70.tq: Test the exact reference point used for a comparative fiscal criterion.
70.sec: Vertical vs horizontal distribution; 15th FC weights  [APPSC]

70.s: The demographic performance criterion under the Sixteenth Finance Commission is based on:
o: The share of working-age population in 2026
70.x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission bases demographic performance on population growth between 1971 and 2011, replacing the total fertility rate measure.
70.tq: Discriminate between the earlier fertility-rate measure and the later population-growth measure.
70.sec: Vertical vs horizontal distribution; 15th FC weights  [APPSC]

70.s: Which of the following changes in the treatment of forests is associated with the Sixteenth Finance Commission?
o: Open forest and the increase in forest area between 2015 and 2023 are included.
Only reserved forests are counted, excluding open forests.
Forest cover has been removed as a criterion altogether.
Only forest revenue collected by a State is considered.
70.x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission includes open forest and the increase in forest area during 2015–2023 in its treatment of the forest criterion.
70.tq: Identify the precise expansion of a criterion rather than accepting an absolute or exclusive formulation.
70.sec: Vertical vs horizontal distribution; 15th FC weights  [APPSC]

70.s: What was Andhra Pradesh’s share of the States’ divisible pool under the Fifteenth Finance Commission?
70.x: Andhra Pradesh’s share was 4.05% under the Fifteenth Finance Commission. Its share was 4.305% under the Fourteenth and 4.217% under the Sixteenth Finance Commission.
70.tq: Distinguish closely spaced percentages by associating each figure with the correct Finance Commission period.

70.s: Which of the following correctly states the allocations for Andhra Pradesh under the Sixteenth Finance Commission for 2026–31?
o: Rural local bodies: ₹16,627 crore; urban local bodies: ₹12,158 crore; disaster: ₹6,125 crore
Rural local bodies: ₹12,158 crore; urban local bodies: ₹16,627 crore; disaster: ₹5,000 crore
Rural local bodies: ₹16,627 crore; urban local bodies: ₹6,125 crore; disaster: ₹12,158 crore
Rural local bodies: ₹5,000 crore; urban local bodies: ₹12,158 crore; disaster: ₹6,627 crore
70.x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission allocation for Andhra Pradesh is ₹16,627 crore for rural local bodies, ₹12,158 crore for urban local bodies and ₹6,125 crore for disaster-related grants.
70.tq: Match each financial figure with its correct recipient category rather than relying on the size of the number alone.

70.s:
Consider the following statements regarding special urban grants under the Sixteenth Finance Commission:
1. Vijayawada is eligible for a special urban grant.
2. Visakhapatnam is eligible for a special urban grant.
3. Each of the two cities can receive up to ₹5,000 crore for wastewater systems.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
70.x: Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam are both eligible for special urban grants, with each eligible to receive up to ₹5,000 crore for wastewater systems.
70.tq: Check whether the same eligibility condition applies to both named cities and whether the ceiling is correctly stated.

70.s: The discontinuation of revenue-deficit grants to Andhra Pradesh under the Sixteenth Finance Commission is associated with which stated fiscal position?
o: The State reduced its revenue deficit to 1.1% in Budget 2026–27.
The State’s fiscal deficit became equal to zero in Budget 2026–27.
The State increased its revenue deficit to 4.22% in Budget 2026–27.
The State eliminated all public debt by Budget 2026–27.
70.x: Revenue-deficit grants were stopped after Andhra Pradesh reduced its revenue deficit to 1.1% in Budget 2026–27.
70.tq: Link a fiscal outcome to the policy consequence without substituting a different deficit measure.

70.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: It was rejected in Parliament in 2014 and replaced by a constitutional tax devolution formula.
It was included in the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act and implemented by the 14th Finance Commission.
It was promised in Parliament in 2014 but was not included in the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act.
It was granted by the 15th Finance Commission through a separate constitutional amendment.
70.x: Special Category Status was promised in Parliament in 2014, but it was not included in the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act. The 14th Finance Commission made no distinction between special and general category States, and the Centre offered special assistance instead.
70.tq: Separate a parliamentary assurance from statutory inclusion and subsequent Finance Commission treatment.

70.x: The descending order is Uttar Pradesh (17.619%), Bihar (9.948%), Andhra Pradesh (4.217%) and Kerala (2.382%).

70.s: Which of the following statements about the southern States under the Sixteenth Finance Commission is correct?
o: All five southern States received exactly the same percentage share.
Only Andhra Pradesh and Telangana gained, while the other southern States lost.
Karnataka and Tamil Nadu were excluded from the horizontal distribution formula.
All five southern States gained in their shares of the States’ pool.

70.s: Which Article requires the President to lay the report of the Finance Commission before each House of Parliament along with an explanatory memorandum on the action taken?
70.x: Article 281 requires the President to lay the Finance Commission’s report before each House of Parliament together with an explanatory memorandum on the action taken.
70.tq: Distinguish the Article dealing with presentation of the report from the Article establishing the Commission and its functions.

70.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Finance Commission:

2. Its recommendations cover cesses and surcharges as part of the divisible pool.
3. It may deal with matters referred to it by the President.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
70.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is false: cesses and surcharges are excluded from the divisible pool covered by the Finance Commission’s tax-sharing recommendations.
70.tq: Locate the exception in the scope of tax devolution and separate it from the Commission’s advisory character.

70.s: The State Finance Commission is constituted:
o: Only once after the formation of a State under Article 356
Every third year under Articles 280 and 281
Every fifth year under Articles 243-I and 243-Y

70.s: The Finance Commission’s function of recommending measures to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State for supplementing the resources of Panchayats and Municipalities was added through the:
70.x: The relevant function was added by the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments, 1992, relating respectively to Panchayats and Municipalities.

increases the divisible pool available for tax devolution

71.s: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India functions under the legal framework of the
o: CAG (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971
71.x: The CAG’s duties, powers and conditions of service are governed by the Comptroller and Auditor General’s Act of 1971, made under Articles 148 and 149.
71.tq: Identify the correct statute by matching the institution with its specific enabling Act.
71.sec: CAG duties - Art. 149, 1971 Act; what he does not control

71.s: Which of the following is a function performed by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India in addition to auditing government accounts?
o: Prescribing the Union Budget without executive approval
Compiling the accounts of the States
Appointing members of the Public Accounts Committee
Approving every withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund of India
71.x: The CAG also compiles State accounts. He does not approve every withdrawal, appoint PAC members or prescribe the Union Budget.
71.tq: Distinguish an actual accounting function from powers belonging to the executive or legislature.
71.sec: CAG duties - Art. 149, 1971 Act; what he does not control

71.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the audit jurisdiction of the Comptroller and Auditor General:
1. He audits the Consolidated Fund of India.
2. He audits the Consolidated Funds of States and Union Territories having legislatures.
3. He audits the Contingency Funds and Public Accounts.
4. He audits only expenditure and not receipts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
71.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the CAG audits both receipts and expenditure.
71.tq: Reject the exclusive claim that narrows a broad constitutional audit jurisdiction.
71.sec: CAG duties - Art. 149, 1971 Act; what he does not control

71.s: The Comptroller and Auditor General may audit the accounts of which of the following?
o: Only private companies receiving no government assistance
Bodies substantially financed by the government and government companies
Only constitutional bodies and never government companies
Only departments of the Union Government
71.x: The CAG audits bodies substantially financed by the government and government companies, in addition to the other accounts specified by law.
71.tq: Select the option that combines two related categories within the audit mandate.
71.sec: CAG duties - Art. 149, 1971 Act; what he does not control

71.s: Which of the following accounts falls within the audit scope of the Comptroller and Auditor General?
o: Personal accounts of all elected representatives
Trading and manufacturing accounts of government departments
Accounts of every private household receiving a subsidy
Accounts of political parties without any government financing
71.x: The CAG audits trading, manufacturing and profit-and-loss accounts of government departments where applicable.
71.tq: Apply the audit-scope rule to distinguish government departmental accounts from unrelated private accounts.
71.sec: CAG duties - Art. 149, 1971 Act; what he does not control

71.s: The audit of local bodies by the Comptroller and Auditor General is undertaken
o: only on the direction of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
only after approval by the Public Accounts Committee
on the request of the President or the Governor, as applicable
automatically in every case without any request
71.x: Local bodies may be audited by the CAG on the request of the President or the Governor, as applicable.
71.tq: Identify the authority competent to trigger an audit instead of assuming an automatic power.
71.sec: CAG duties - Art. 149, 1971 Act; what he does not control

71.s: Why is the Comptroller and Auditor General of India described as only an Auditor-General and not a true Comptroller?
o: He cannot audit the accounts of State Governments.
He cannot audit receipts of the Consolidated Fund.
He cannot submit reports to the President.
He has no control over the issue or release of money from the Consolidated Fund.
71.x: The CAG audits public finances but does not control the issue or release of money from the Consolidated Fund. This control exists for the Comptroller and Auditor General in Britain.
71.tq: Discriminate between the auditing function and the comptrolling function by focusing on control over release of funds.
71.sec: CAG duties - Art. 149, 1971 Act; what he does not control

71.s: The Comptroller and Auditor General cannot audit secret service expenditure because he must
o: refer it to the Supreme Court for approval
obtain prior approval of the Public Accounts Committee
accept the certificate of the competent authority
submit it directly to the Governor
71.x: In the case of secret service expenditure, the CAG must accept the certificate of the competent authority and cannot audit the expenditure in the ordinary manner.
71.tq: Test the statutory exception to the general power of audit.
71.sec: CAG duties - Art. 149, 1971 Act; what he does not control

71.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the types of audit conducted by the Comptroller and Auditor General?
o: Propriety audit is obligatory, whereas legal audit is discretionary.
Legal and regulatory audit is obligatory, whereas propriety audit is discretionary.
All forms of audit are performed only at the request of Parliament.
Performance audit alone is obligatory and financial audit is prohibited.
71.x: Legal and regulatory audit is obligatory. Propriety audit, which examines wisdom and economy of expenditure, is discretionary.
71.tq: Compare obligatory and discretionary audits instead of treating every audit category identically.
71.sec: CAG duties - Art. 149, 1971 Act; what he does not control

71.s: A propriety audit by the Comptroller and Auditor General primarily examines the
o: wisdom and economy of public expenditure
71.x: Propriety audit examines whether expenditure was characterised by wisdom, economy and proper use of public resources.
71.tq: Apply the meaning of propriety audit to a practical question about public expenditure.
71.sec: CAG duties - Art. 149, 1971 Act; what he does not control

71.s: Under Article 150, the form of accounts of the Union and the States is prescribed by the President on the advice of the
71.x: Article 150 provides that the form of accounts of the Union and the States is prescribed by the President on the advice of the CAG.
71.tq: Identify the constitutional adviser rather than the body that later scrutinises the accounts.
71.sec: Articles 148-151 → content

71.s: Which Article of the Constitution specifically deals with the audit reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General?
71.x: Article 151 deals with the submission and laying of the CAG’s audit reports before the appropriate legislature.
71.tq: Distinguish the reporting provision from the neighbouring Articles on appointment, powers and accounts.
71.sec: Audit reports - Art. 151 and the PAC

71.s: The audit reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General relating to a State are submitted to the
o: Speaker of the Lok Sabha, who refers them to the PAC
Chief Minister, who lays them before the Legislative Assembly
Governor, who lays them before the State Legislature
President, who lays them before Parliament
71.x: Under Article 151(2), State audit reports are submitted to the Governor, who causes them to be laid before the State Legislature.
71.tq: Follow the Union–State distinction and assign the report to the correct constitutional recipient.
71.sec: Audit reports - Art. 151 and the PAC

71.s: Which of the following is the correct sequence for Union audit reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General?
o: CAG → President → both Houses of Parliament → Public Accounts Committee
CAG → Public Accounts Committee → President → both Houses of Parliament
CAG → Speaker → President → Public Accounts Committee
CAG → Parliament Secretariat → Governor → Public Accounts Committee
71.x: Union reports are submitted by the CAG to the President, laid before both Houses, and then examined by the Public Accounts Committee.
71.tq: Arrange the institutional stages in sequence, beginning with the report-making authority.
71.sec: Audit reports - Art. 151 and the PAC

71.s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the three principal Union reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General mentioned in this context?
o: Report on the delimitation of constituencies
71.x: The three Union reports are the Appropriation Accounts Report, Finance Accounts Report and Report on Public Undertakings. Delimitation of constituencies is unrelated to CAG reporting.
71.tq: Identify the unrelated institutional subject among three closely associated CAG reports.
71.sec: Audit reports - Art. 151 and the PAC

71.s: Reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General relating to public sector undertakings are examined by the
71.x: Reports relating to public sector undertakings are referred to the Committee on Public Undertakings, while the PAC examines the other relevant CAG reports.
71.tq: Separate the two parliamentary committees by the subject of the report they examine.
71.sec: Audit reports - Art. 151 and the PAC

71.s: The Comptroller and Auditor General is described as the Public Accounts Committee’s
71.x: The CAG acts as the PAC’s friend, philosopher and guide by assisting it in examining audit findings.
71.tq: Recall the distinctive institutional relationship without confusing advisory assistance with membership.
71.sec: Audit reports - Art. 151 and the PAC

71.s:
Which of the following correctly describes the audit types mentioned for the Comptroller and Auditor General?
1. Compliance audit is obligatory.
2. Financial attest audit is obligatory.
3. Performance audit is discretionary.
4. Performance audit is constitutionally prohibited.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
71.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: compliance and financial attest audits are obligatory, while performance audit is discretionary. Statement 4 is false because performance audit is permitted as a discretionary audit.
71.tq: Separate obligatory audit categories from discretionary performance audit and reject the prohibition trap.
71.sec: Audit reports - Art. 151 and the PAC

71.s: Which statement best reflects Dr. B. R. Ambedkar’s description of the Comptroller and Auditor General?
o: The principal law officer of the Union
The chief electoral authority of India
The least independent officer under the Constitution
The most important officer under the Constitution
71.x: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar described the CAG as the most important officer under the Constitution.
71.tq: Match the quoted assessment with the correct constitutional office.
71.sec: CAG duties - Art. 149, 1971 Act; what he does not control

71.s: Which one of the following correctly describes a legal and regulatory, or compliance, audit conducted by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India?
o: It examines whether money was legally available and spent according to rules
It measures the economy, efficiency and effectiveness of schemes
It examines only the wisdom and economy of expenditure
It certifies that accounts conform to a prescribed reporting framework
71.x: A legal and regulatory audit is obligatory and examines whether money was legally available and spent in accordance with applicable rules.
71.tq: Match the audit type with its distinctive test.
71.sec: Types of audit

71.s: The primary purpose of a financial attest audit is to determine whether:
o: Accounts are true and conform to the applicable reporting framework
All expenditure was approved by the Public Accounts Committee
Schemes achieved their intended social outcomes
71.x: Financial attest audit is an obligatory audit concerned with the truthfulness of accounts and their conformity with the reporting framework.
71.tq: Use the function-based distinction between similar audit types.
71.sec: Types of audit

71.s:
Consider the following statements regarding types of audit:
1. Propriety audit examines wisdom, faithfulness and economy in expenditure.
2. Performance audit examines the economy, efficiency and effectiveness of schemes.
3. Both propriety audit and performance audit are obligatory audits.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
71.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because propriety and performance audits are discretionary, whereas legal-regulatory and financial-attest audits are obligatory.
71.tq: Separate the nature of an audit from the subject it tests.
71.sec: Types of audit

71.s: A discretionary audit intended to flag extravagance in public expenditure is known as:
71.x: Propriety audit is discretionary and examines wisdom, faithfulness and economy, including possible extravagance in expenditure.
71.tq: Identify the audit from its characteristic purpose.
71.sec: Types of audit

71.s: Social audits conducted under MGNREGA are relevant to the Comptroller and Auditor-General's performance audits because they:
o: Determine the CAG's term of office
Are conducted exclusively by the CAG
Replace the statutory audit of MGNREGA accounts
71.x: Social audits can provide inputs to CAG performance audits. The MGNREGA social audit standards mentioned are from 2016 and are associated with the CDI.
71.tq: Apply the relationship between participatory audit and performance audit.
71.sec: Types of audit

71.s: The separation of accounts from audit at the Union level took place in:
71.x: Accounts were separated from audit at the Centre in 1976. The 1976 amendment relieved the CAG of compiling Union Government accounts through departmentalisation.
71.tq: Distinguish the enactment year from the year of departmentalisation.
71.sec: CAG and accounts - separation, state audits, charged expenditure

71.s: With reference to the accounts of States, which one of the following is correct?
o: The CAG continues to keep most State accounts
The CAG keeps no State accounts after 1976
State accounts are kept by the Public Accounts Committee
All State accounts are kept exclusively by the Union Finance Ministry
71.x: Although Union accounts were separated from audit in 1976, the CAG continues to keep most State accounts.
71.tq: Use the Centre-State contrast to avoid overgeneralisation.
71.sec: CAG and accounts - separation, state audits, charged expenditure

71.s: Reports of the CAG relating to the accounts of Andhra Pradesh are submitted to the:
o: Speaker of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly
71.x: Reports relating to the accounts of Andhra Pradesh are submitted to the Governor of Andhra Pradesh under Article 151(2).
71.tq: Identify the constitutional recipient rather than the implementing authority.
71.sec: CAG and accounts - separation, state audits, charged expenditure

71.s: Which one of the following expenditures is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India rather than voted by Parliament?
o: The salary and office expenses of the CAG
All expenditure recommended by the PAC
Every expenditure incurred by a public sector undertaking
The entire expenditure of State Governments
71.x: The salary and office expenses of the CAG are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India and are not subject to vote.
71.tq: Identify the constitutional office whose expenditure is charged, not voted.
71.sec: CAG and accounts - separation, state audits, charged expenditure

71.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with regard to audit of public sector entities?
1. DVC — Audited directly by the CAG
2. ONGC — Audited directly by the CAG
3. Central Warehousing Corporation — Private auditors appointed on the CAG's advice, with supplementary audit by the CAG
4. RBI — Supplementary audit by the CAG after appointment of private auditors on its advice
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
71.x: DVC and ONGC are directly audited by the CAG. Central Warehousing Corporation follows the private-auditor and supplementary-audit arrangement; RBI is wholly privately audited, so statement 4 is false.
71.tq: Classify entities by the mode of CAG involvement.
71.sec: CAG's audit of PSUs, local bodies - limits

71.s: Which one of the following is correctly classified as a wholly privately audited entity?
71.x: LIC and RBI are cited as examples of entities subject to wholly private audit. DVC and ONGC are directly audited by the CAG.
71.tq: Use the three-way classification of public-sector audits.
71.sec: CAG's audit of PSUs, local bodies - limits

71.s: In the case of which category of entities are private auditors appointed on the CAG's advice and the CAG conducts a supplementary audit?
71.x: Central Warehousing Corporation and IFCI are examples where private auditors are appointed on the CAG's advice and the CAG carries out a supplementary audit.
71.tq: Start with the sure pair in the audit-classification table.
71.sec: CAG's audit of PSUs, local bodies - limits

71.s: Local bodies may be audited by the CAG when such audit is requested by the:
71.x: The CAG may audit local bodies when requested by the President or the Governor. Sixth Schedule councils are also covered.
71.tq: Identify who can trigger the audit rather than who conducts it.
71.sec: CAG's audit of PSUs, local bodies - limits

71.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Sixth Schedule councils may also come within the scope of CAG audit of local bodies.
2. The CAG can audit secret service expenditure in the same manner as ordinary expenditure.
3. In relation to secret service expenditure, the CAG accepts a certificate from the competent authority.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
71.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is false because the CAG cannot audit secret service expenditure and instead accepts a certificate from the competent authority.
71.tq: Find the exception to the general audit power.
71.sec: CAG's audit of PSUs, local bodies - limits

71.s: The presumptive loss figure associated with the CAG's 2G spectrum report of 2010 was approximately:
71.x: The 2010 2G spectrum report, prepared during Vinod Rai's tenure, referred to a presumptive loss of ₹1.76 lakh crore.
71.tq: Separate the closely resembling 2G and coal-block figures.
71.sec: Criticisms and landmark reports

71.s: The CAG report on coal block allocation in 2012 referred to a figure of approximately:
71.x: The coal block allocation report of 2012 referred to a presumptive loss of ₹1.86 lakh crore.
71.tq: Discriminate between the two similar lakh-crore estimates.
71.sec: Criticisms and landmark reports

71.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the CAG's landmark reports is NOT correctly matched?
71.x: The 2G spectrum report is associated with 2010. Coal block allocation is associated with 2012, and the Rafale report with 2019.
71.tq: Use the date-event pairing to eliminate the swapped-year option.
71.sec: Criticisms and landmark reports

71.s: The CAG's 2019 Rafale report was notable for containing:
o: A recommendation to abolish the PAC
A complete ban on defence procurement
A finding on coal block allocation
71.x: The 2019 Rafale report contained redacted pricing information. It was distinct from the 2G and coal block allocation reports.
71.tq: Match the report with its distinctive feature.
71.sec: Criticisms and landmark reports

71.s:
Which of the following is a criticism or debate associated with the functioning of the CAG?
1. Use of the presumptive-loss method
2. Auditing policy choices rather than merely execution
3. Delay in submission of reports
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
71.x: All three are identified as debates concerning CAG auditing: the presumptive-loss method, the boundary between policy and execution, and delayed reports.
71.tq: Recognise a set of related criticisms without treating one as an unrelated audit function.
71.sec: Criticisms and landmark reports

71.s: Who authored the book titled “When Audit Matters”?
71.x: Former CAG Vinod Rai authored “When Audit Matters.”
71.tq: Match the publication with its author rather than with a current office-holder.
71.sec: Criticisms and landmark reports

71.s: Which one of the following constitutional posts has a term of five years, unlike the CAG, CEC and a UPSC member?
o: Member of the Union Public Service Commission
71.x: The President has a five-year term, whereas the CAG, CEC and UPSC member have a term of six years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier.
71.tq: Split the options into the six-year-or-65 group and the five-year group.
71.sec: Term compared with other constitutional posts

71.s:
Consider the following statements regarding terms of constitutional posts:
1. The President and Vice-President have five-year terms.
2. A Lok Sabha member ordinarily has a five-year term unless the House is dissolved earlier.
3. The CAG, CEC and a UPSC member have the same stated term structure.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
71.x: All three statements are correct. The CAG, CEC and UPSC member have a term of six years or until 65, while the President, Vice-President and ordinarily a Lok Sabha member have five-year terms.
71.tq: Compare term structures rather than relying only on the number of years.
71.sec: Term compared with other constitutional posts

71.s: Among the following, whose normal constitutional term is the longest in duration?
71.x: The CAG's term is six years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier; the other listed posts ordinarily have five-year terms.
71.tq: Compare the numerical term lengths before considering qualifications such as dissolution.
71.sec: Term compared with other constitutional posts

71.s: The official constitutional name of the office is:
71.x: The official name is Comptroller and Auditor-General of India. “Controller” and “Attorney” are not substitutes for the constitutional terms.
71.tq: Discriminate between similar-looking official titles.
71.sec: Official full name

71.s: The CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 provides, among other things, for:
o: Appointment of all State Finance Ministers
Preparation of the Union Budget by the CAG
Conduct of elections to local bodies
Compilation of State accounts and their submission to the President, Governors or Administrators
71.x: The Act provides for compilation of State accounts and their submission to the President, Governors or Administrators. It does not make the CAG the budget-making or election authority.
71.tq: Identify the statutory function without confusing it with executive functions.
71.sec: CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971

71.s: Which consequence followed the 1976 amendment relating to the CAG?
o: The CAG was relieved of compiling Union Government accounts
The CAG's term was reduced to five years
The CAG was given power to audit secret service expenditure directly
71.x: The 1976 amendment separated accounts from audit and relieved the CAG of compiling Union Government accounts through departmentalisation.
71.tq: Link the amendment to its institutional consequence.
71.sec: CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971

71.s: V. Narahari Rao served as the first CAG of India in:
71.x: V. Narahari Rao was the first CAG, in 1948.
71.tq: Use the founding-period chronology to identify the precise year.
71.sec: CAGs by number - FIRST and present

71.s: CAG Report No. 31 of 2026 found bio-toilets deficient or non-functional at how many of the railway stations examined?
71.x: The report found bio-toilets deficient or non-functional at 491 out of 512 railway stations examined.
71.tq: Preserve the numerator-denominator order in a quantitative finding.
71.sec: Universal angles

71.s: The Public Accounts Committee that pulled up the Railways in relation to CAG Report No. 31 of 2026 was chaired by:
71.x: The PAC was under K.C. Venugopal when it pulled up the Railways over the bio-toilet findings.
71.tq: Match the parliamentary response with its committee chairperson.
71.sec: Universal angles

71.s: The Green India Mission audit mentioned a shortfall of:
71.x: The reported shortfall in the Green India Mission was 91.87 percent.
71.tq: Check the placement of digits in a closely similar percentage figure.
71.sec: Universal angles

71.s: Which one of the following correctly describes a current audit initiative associated with the CAG?
o: Auditing 512 cities exclusively for railway sanitation
Auditing all private companies without statutory limits
Auditing only one city for urban mobility
Auditing 101 cities for ease of living
71.x: The CAG was auditing 101 cities for ease of living, including urban-mobility concerns.
71.tq: Identify the precise scale and subject of the audit initiative.
71.sec: Universal angles

71.s: India hosted the 5th BRICS SAI Leaders' Summit in 2026 with the theme associated with:
o: Ease of living and urban mobility
71.x: The 5th BRICS SAI Leaders' Summit hosted by India in 2026 was associated with the theme of ease of living and urban mobility.
71.tq: Match the international institutional meeting with its theme.
71.sec: Universal angles

71.s: Which technological approach is being used by the CAG to detect fraud in welfare schemes?
o: Only manual inspection of paper vouchers
Artificial intelligence and machine learning-based audits
71.x: The CAG is using AI/ML-based audits to detect fraud in welfare schemes and is expanding remote audits.
71.tq: Match the technology with the governance problem it addresses.
71.sec: Universal angles

71.s: The principal institutional significance of CAG reports is that they facilitate:
o: Replacement of legislative scrutiny by private auditors
Direct administration of State Governments by the CAG
Judicial appointment by the Supreme Court
71.x: CAG reports are a principal mechanism through which executive accountability to Parliament operates.
71.tq: Identify the constitutional accountability chain rather than an operational audit task.
71.sec: Universal angles

71.s:
Consider the following statements regarding recent issues relating to the Public Accounts Committee:
1. PAC recommendations are binding on the executive.
2. There is a reported backlog of Action Taken Notes.
3. CAG reports provide the principal basis for parliamentary examination of executive financial accountability.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
71.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is false because PAC recommendations are not binding on the executive.
71.tq: Test the difference between parliamentary scrutiny and binding executive orders.
71.sec: Universal angles

72.s:
With reference to the qualifications prescribed for appointment as the Attorney General for India, consider the following statements:
1. The person must be a citizen of India.
2. The person must have been a Judge of a High Court for at least five years, or an advocate of a High Court for at least ten years.
3. An eminent jurist may also be appointed if the President considers the person suitable.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
72.x: All three statements are correct. Article 76 requires the Attorney General to satisfy the qualifications for appointment as a Supreme Court Judge, including the stated judicial, advocacy or eminent-jurist qualifications.
72.tq: Combine the constitutional qualification routes and check whether the broader category of eminent jurist is included.
72.sec: Attorney General - Article 76, appointment, qualification, term, removal

72.s: In relation to the resignation of the Attorney General for India, which one of the following is correct?
o: The resignation is addressed to the President
The resignation is addressed to the Union Law Minister
The resignation is addressed to the Chief Justice of India
The resignation is addressed to the Prime Minister
72.x: The Attorney General resigns by addressing the resignation to the President.
72.tq: Use the appointing authority and the resignation authority as a paired constitutional relationship.
72.sec: Attorney General - Article 76, appointment, qualification, term, removal

72.s: Which of the following statements regarding the removal of the Attorney General for India is correct?
o: Removal can be ordered only by the Supreme Court
Removal requires impeachment by both Houses of Parliament
The Constitution specifies detailed grounds and a special removal procedure
The Constitution does not specify grounds or a separate removal procedure; the office is held during the President's pleasure
72.x: The Constitution does not prescribe specific grounds or a special procedure for removal of the Attorney General. The office is held during the pleasure of the President.
72.tq: Distinguish an office held during pleasure from constitutional offices having a prescribed removal procedure.
72.sec: Attorney General - Article 76, appointment, qualification, term, removal

72.s: The convention that the Attorney General resigns when the Council of Ministers resigns or is replaced is primarily related to the fact that the Attorney General is appointed on the advice of the:
72.x: The Attorney General is appointed by the President on the advice of the Council of Ministers. By convention, the Attorney General resigns when that Council resigns or is replaced.
72.tq: Link the convention to the political advice underlying the appointment rather than to the formal appointing authority alone.
72.sec: Attorney General - Article 76, appointment, qualification, term, removal

72.s: Who determines the remuneration of the Attorney General for India?
72.x: The remuneration of the Attorney General is determined by the President.
72.tq: Apply the authority-power test: identify which constitutional authority is assigned the remuneration decision.
72.sec: Attorney General - Article 76, appointment, qualification, term, removal

72.s: The Attorney General is consulted through the Ministry of Law primarily on:
o: All administrative matters of the Union Government
72.x: References to the Attorney General are made through the Ministry of Law, and consultation is confined to legal matters of real importance.
72.tq: Watch for the overbroad word 'all' and identify the carefully limited scope of consultation.
72.sec: Highest law officer of India

72.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Attorney General — Statutory office; Solicitor General — Constitutional office
Attorney General — Constitutional office under Article 76; Solicitor General — Statutory office
Attorney General — Judicial office under Article 124; Solicitor General — Constitutional office under Article 165
Attorney General — Parliamentary office; Solicitor General — Judicial office
72.x: The Attorney General is a constitutional authority under Article 76, whereas the Solicitor General is a statutory office.
72.tq: Separate constitutional and statutory offices before comparing their functions.
72.sec: Highest law officer of India

72.s: Which one of the following statements best distinguishes the Solicitor General from the Attorney General?
o: The Solicitor General advises State Governments while the Attorney General advises only courts
The Solicitor General assists the Attorney General and is confined to appearing in courts for the Union
The Solicitor General is the first law officer and the Attorney General is the second law officer
The Solicitor General is the head of the judiciary and the Attorney General assists him
72.x: The Solicitor General is the second law officer, assists the Attorney General and is confined to appearing in courts for the Union; the Attorney General is the chief legal adviser to the Government of India.
72.tq: Compare the offices by rank, advisory role and court-related function rather than by title alone.
72.sec: Highest law officer of India

72.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Chief Justice of India is the head of the judiciary.
2. The Attorney General is a government law officer and the chief legal adviser to the Government of India.
3. The Solicitor General is the second law officer of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
72.x: All three statements are correct. The Chief Justice of India heads the judiciary, while the Attorney General and Solicitor General occupy the first and second positions among Union law officers respectively.
72.tq: Keep the head of the judiciary distinct from the hierarchy of government law officers.
72.sec: Highest law officer of India

72.s: The order of precedence assigned to the Attorney General, Solicitor General, and Advocates General is, respectively:
72.x: The Attorney General is placed at 11, the Solicitor General at 23, and the Additional Solicitors General and Advocates General at 25 in the stated order of precedence.
72.tq: Read the numerical sequence as an order-of-precedence comparison and avoid reversing the office hierarchy.
72.sec: Highest law officer of India

72.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Solicitor General — Second law officer of India
Chief Justice of India — Government's first law officer
Attorney General — Constitutional office under Article 76
Attorney General — Chief legal adviser to the Government of India
72.x: The Chief Justice of India is the head of the judiciary, not the government's first law officer. The Attorney General is the chief legal adviser and first law officer of India.
72.tq: Find the swapped institutional role among closely related constitutional and legal offices.
72.sec: Highest law officer of India

72.s:
With reference to the Advocate General of a State, consider the following statements:
1. The Advocate General is appointed by the Governor.
2. The Advocate General holds office during the pleasure of the Governor.
3. The remuneration of the Advocate General is determined by the Governor.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
72.x: All three statements are correct under the constitutional arrangement governing the Advocate General of a State.
72.tq: Use the State-level parallel of the Attorney General arrangement while retaining the Governor as the relevant authority.
72.sec: Advocate General - appointment, duties, Art. 177, remuneration

72.s: Under Article 177, the Advocate General of a State may:
o: Speak and take part in the proceedings of either House of the State Legislature and its committees, but not vote
Vote in the State Legislature but not speak in its committees
Dissolve the State Legislature when legal advice is sought
Participate only in the Legislative Assembly and vote in both Houses
72.x: Article 177 permits the Advocate General to speak and take part in either House of the State Legislature and its committees, but does not confer a right to vote.
72.tq: Separate the right to participate from the right to vote, a standard constitutional distinction.
72.sec: Advocate General - appointment, duties, Art. 177, remuneration

72.s: Which Article provides that the Advocate General enjoys the privileges of a member of the State Legislature?
72.x: Article 194(4) extends legislative privileges to the Advocate General in the State Legislature. Article 105(4) performs the corresponding function for the Attorney General at the Union level.
72.tq: Distinguish the participation article from the legislative-privileges article and separate Union from State provisions.
72.sec: Advocate General - appointment, duties, Art. 177, remuneration

72.s: The right of audience of the Advocate General extends to:
o: Only the High Court of the State
72.x: The Advocate General has the right of audience in any court within the State. The Attorney General has the corresponding right of audience in all courts in India.
72.tq: Use the territorial scope of the office to distinguish the State law officer from the Union law officer.
72.sec: Advocate General - appointment, duties, Art. 177, remuneration

72.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

a. Attorney General — Article 76
b. Advocate General — Article 165
c. Attorney General's parliamentary rights — Article 88
d. Advocate General's State Legislature rights — Article 177
72.x: The correct matching is Attorney General—Article 76, Advocate General—Article 165, Attorney General's parliamentary rights—Article 88, and Advocate General's State Legislature rights—Article 177.
72.tq: Start with the sure Article-office pairs and then verify the corresponding legislative-rights provisions.
72.sec: State-level counterpart of the Attorney General

72.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Attorney General and the Advocate General:
1. The Attorney General is qualified to be a Supreme Court Judge, whereas the Advocate General is qualified to be a High Court Judge.
2. The Attorney General holds office during the pleasure of the President, whereas the Advocate General holds office during the pleasure of the Governor.
3. The remuneration of both offices is determined by the President.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
72.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false: the Attorney General's remuneration is determined by the President, while the Advocate General's remuneration is determined by the Governor.
72.tq: Compare corresponding entries row by row and detect the reversed authority in the remuneration row.
72.sec: State-level counterpart of the Attorney General

72.s:
Arrange the following Attorneys General of India in chronological order of holding office, beginning with the earliest:
A. K.K. Venugopal
B. M.C. Setalvad
C. Mukul Rohatgi
D. R. Venkataramani
72.x: M.C. Setalvad was the first, followed by Mukul Rohatgi, K.K. Venugopal and R. Venkataramani in the sequence represented here.
72.tq: Fix the first office-holder and then place the later Attorneys General in sequence.
72.sec: Attorneys General of India → FIRST and current

72.s: K.K. Venugopal served as the Attorney General of India during which period?
72.x: K.K. Venugopal served as Attorney General of India from 2017 to 2022.
72.tq: Treat the paired years as a tenure range and distinguish it from the tenures of neighbouring office-holders.
72.sec: Attorneys General of India → FIRST and current

72.s: Who is the Attorney General of India as stated for September 2026?
72.x: R. Venkataramani is the current Attorney General of India as stated for September 2026. He was first appointed in 2022 and was reappointed for a two-year term in 2025.
72.tq: Apply the current-affairs date carefully and distinguish the present office-holder from earlier Attorneys General.
72.sec: Attorneys General of India → FIRST and current

72.s: R. Venkataramani was first appointed as Attorney General of India in:
72.x: R. Venkataramani was first appointed Attorney General of India in 2022 and was subsequently reappointed for a two-year term in 2025.
72.tq: Separate the first appointment year from the later reappointment year.
72.sec: Attorneys General of India → FIRST and current

72.s: Under Article 88, the Attorney General may take part in:
o: Only the Lok Sabha and its committees
Either House of Parliament, a joint sitting and committees of which he is named a member
Only the Rajya Sabha and joint sittings
Parliamentary proceedings only after becoming a nominated member
72.x: Article 88 permits the Attorney General to speak and take part in either House, joint sittings and committees of which he is named a member. This right does not make him a member of Parliament.
72.tq: Read the full scope of participation and avoid converting a right to attend into membership.
72.sec: Rights of AG in Parliament - Art. 88; right of audience

72.s: Which one of the following rights is NOT available to the Attorney General under Article 88?
o: The right to vote in parliamentary proceedings
The right to take part in a joint sitting of Parliament
The right to speak in either House of Parliament
The right to take part in a committee of which he is named a member
72.x: Article 88 permits participation and speaking but does not confer a right to vote. The Attorney General is not a voting member of Parliament by virtue of that Article.
72.tq: Find the one power expressly excluded from a broad participation provision.
72.sec: Rights of AG in Parliament - Art. 88; right of audience

72.s: The parliamentary privileges of the Attorney General are derived from:
72.x: Article 105(4) provides the parliamentary privileges applicable to the Attorney General. Article 88 deals with the right to speak and participate without a right to vote.
72.tq: Distinguish the Article granting participation from the Article extending parliamentary privileges.
72.sec: Rights of AG in Parliament - Art. 88; right of audience

72.s: Which Article, among the following, specifically deals with the Attorney General's right to speak and participate in Parliament without voting rights?
72.x: Article 88 confers the Attorney General's right to speak and take part in parliamentary proceedings without the right to vote. Article 78 concerns the duties of the Prime Minister in relation to the President.
72.tq: Reject the look-alike Article number and identify the precise constitutional provision.
72.sec: Rights of AG in Parliament - Art. 88; right of audience

72.s: Additional Advocates General are appointed primarily to:
o: Replace the Governor in legal matters
Assist the office of the Advocate General
Exercise the voting rights of the Advocate General in the Legislature
Serve as members of the Supreme Court
72.x: Additional Advocates General assist the office of the Advocate General in discharging its legal responsibilities.
72.tq: Match the supporting office with its assistance function and avoid assigning it the principal office's constitutional powers.
72.sec: Advocate General - appointment, duties, Art. 177, remuneration

72.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the constitutional status of the Solicitor General of India?
o: He is a constitutional authority appointed by the President under Article 165
He is a statutory law officer governed by the Law Officers (Terms and Conditions) Rules, 1987
He is created under Article 76 of the Constitution
He is an ex officio member of the Union Cabinet
72.x: The Solicitor General is not mentioned in the Constitution. The post is statutory and is governed by the Law Officers (Terms and Conditions) Rules, 1987.
72.tq: Distinguish the constitutional Attorney General from the statutory Solicitor General.
72.sec: Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General

72.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Solicitor General of India:
1. He is the second law officer of India.
2. He is appointed by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet.
3. His normal term is three years.
4. He is a member of the Union Cabinet.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
72.x: The Solicitor General is the second law officer, is appointed through the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet, and has a three-year term. He is not a member of the Union Cabinet.
72.tq: Use the membership trap to separate a senior law officer from a Cabinet Minister.
72.sec: Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General

72.s: The Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General primarily perform which of the following functions?
o: They conduct elections to Parliament and State Legislatures
They advise the government and appear for the Government of India in courts
They audit the accounts of the Union Government
They preside over joint sittings of Parliament
72.x: The Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General advise the government and represent the Government of India before courts.
72.tq: Identify the core function from the office’s legal responsibilities.
72.sec: Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General

72.s:
With reference to the law officers of India, consider the following statements:
1. References concerning the Attorney General are made through the Ministry of Law.
2. Law officers conventionally resign when a new government assumes office.
3. The Attorney General alone among these offices is created by the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
72.x: References concerning the Attorney General go through the Ministry of Law; law officers conventionally resign after a change of government; and only the Attorney General is constitutionally created, under Article 76.
72.tq: Combine institutional procedure, convention and constitutional classification.
72.sec: Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General

72.s: Tushar Mehta was reappointed as the Solicitor General of India for a period of three years with effect from:
72.x: Tushar Mehta was reappointed as Solicitor General for three years with effect from 1 July 2026.
72.tq: Discriminate between closely spaced dates in a current-affairs appointment.
72.sec: Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General

72.s: Which of the following persons was NOT included among the five Additional Solicitors General reappointed for the Supreme Court?
72.x: The five reappointed Additional Solicitors General were Vikramjit Banerjee, K.M. Nataraj, S.V. Raju, N. Venkataraman and Aishwarya Bhati. R. Venkataramani is the Attorney General, not one of those five ASGs.
72.tq: Find the odd name by checking membership of a specifically stated list.
72.sec: Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General

72.s: The Attorney General of India and the Solicitor General of India are ex officio members of the:
72.x: Under the Advocates Act, 1961, the Attorney General and Solicitor General are ex officio members of the Bar Council of India.
72.tq: Recall the statutory body associated with the two principal Union law officers.
72.sec: Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General

72.s: Which of the following is NOT a permissible activity for the Attorney General of India without the required government permission or contrary to his professional restrictions?
o: Advising the Government of India on legal matters
Engaging in private practice subject to applicable restrictions
Appearing for the Government of India in courts
Defending an accused person in a criminal prosecution
72.x: The Attorney General must not defend accused persons in criminal prosecutions. He is not a full-time counsel and is not debarred from private practice, but he must comply with restrictions on conflicts and government permission.
72.tq: Use the exception-based method to separate permitted private practice from prohibited criminal defence.
72.sec: Limitations on Attorney General

72.s:
The Attorney General of India must not do which of the following?
1. Advise against the Government of India.
2. Hold a brief against the Government of India.
3. Advise in a case in which he has already advised the Government of India.
4. Become a company director without government permission.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
72.x: All four are restrictions applicable to the Attorney General. He must avoid conflicts with the Government of India and cannot become a company director without government permission.
72.tq: Check each restriction separately, especially the conflict-of-interest and permission clauses.
72.sec: Limitations on Attorney General

72.s:
Consider the following statements about the Attorney General of India:
1. He is a full-time counsel of the Union Government.
2. He is a government servant.
3. He is not debarred from private practice merely by holding the office.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
72.x: The Attorney General is neither a full-time counsel nor a government servant. Consequently, he is not debarred from private practice, subject to the restrictions governing the office.
72.tq: Reject absolute status claims and identify the precise legal position.
72.sec: Limitations on Attorney General

72.s: The privileges and immunities available to the Attorney General of India in relation to parliamentary participation are those of:
o: A Union Cabinet Minister under Article 77
A Judge of the Supreme Court under Article 124
A member of a State Legislature under Article 194
A Member of Parliament under Article 105(4)
72.x: Article 105(4) extends parliamentary privileges and immunities to a person who has the right to speak or otherwise take part in parliamentary proceedings without being a member.
72.tq: Match the constitutional privilege with the correct article and institutional status.
72.sec: Limitations on Attorney General

72.s: A private client asks the Attorney General of India to advise against the Government of India in a matter unrelated to his official duties. Which course is consistent with the limitations on the office?
o: He may do so after obtaining permission from the Chief Justice of India
He may do so because private practice is always unrestricted
He may do so only if the matter is heard outside India
He must decline because he cannot advise or hold a brief against the Government of India
72.x: Although the Attorney General is not debarred from private practice, he must not advise or hold a brief against the Government of India.
72.tq: Apply the conflict-of-interest restriction to a practical professional situation.
72.sec: Limitations on Attorney General

72.s:
With reference to the Advocate General of Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. The office is provided under Article 165 of the Constitution.
2. The Advocate General is appointed by the Governor of Andhra Pradesh.
3. The Advocate General holds office during the pleasure of the Governor.
4. The office necessarily continues unchanged when the State Government changes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
72.x: The Advocate General is a constitutional office under Article 165, appointed by the Governor and holding office at the Governor’s pleasure. By convention, the officeholder may change with the State Government.
72.tq: Separate constitutional provisions from conventions and test the effect of a change of government.
72.sec: Advocates General of AP → current holder

72.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the right of audience of the Attorney General and the Advocate General?
o: The Advocate General has it in all courts in India, while the Attorney General has it only in the State courts
The Attorney General has it in all courts in India, while the Advocate General has it in all courts in the State
Both have it only in the Supreme Court of India
Neither has a right of audience in courts
72.x: The Attorney General has the right of audience in all courts in India, whereas the Advocate General has the right of audience in all courts within the State.
72.tq: Split the comparison by territorial scope rather than by rank alone.
72.sec: Limitations on Attorney General

72.s: Who was the first Solicitor General of India?
72.x: C.K. Daphtary was the first Solicitor General of India.
72.tq: Apply the FIRST/LAST approach to closely related law-officer posts.
72.sec: Universal angles

72.s:
Arrange the following offices in descending order according to their position in the precedence table, where the smaller item number indicates higher precedence:
A. Solicitor General
B. Advocate Generals of States
C. Attorney General
D. Additional Solicitors General
Select the correct sequence.
72.x: The Attorney General is at item 11, the Solicitor General at item 23, and the Advocate Generals of States and Additional Solicitors General are at item 25. Thus the order is Attorney General, Solicitor General, Advocate Generals of States, Additional Solicitors General.
72.tq: Convert precedence numbers into an ordered sequence and check the tied item number.
72.sec: Universal angles

72.s: Which one of the following statements best reflects the criticism of the convention concerning the resignation of law officers when a new government assumes office?
o: It is criticised for linking the offices too closely with the ruling party
It prevents the Attorney General from appearing in constitutional cases
It makes law officers directly elected representatives of the ruling party
It converts statutory law officers into constitutional authorities
72.x: The convention is criticised because the resignation of all law officers after a change of government can make the offices appear tied to the ruling party rather than being institutionally independent.
72.tq: Identify the institutional consequence of a convention rather than a formal constitutional rule.
72.sec: Universal angles

72.s: In September 2026, the Supreme Court asked Attorney General R. Venkataramani to relay directions to all Advocates General concerning:
o: Reorganisation of the Bar Council of India
72.x: The Supreme Court asked Attorney General R. Venkataramani to communicate directions to all Advocates General concerning facilities for senior citizens.
72.tq: Use the subject of a current judicial direction to identify the correct issue.
72.sec: Universal angles

72.s: Which of the following current officeholder–tenure pairs is correctly matched?
o: R. Venkataramani—reappointed Attorney General for two years
C.K. Daphtary—reappointed Additional Solicitor General for three years
M.C. Setalvad—reappointed Solicitor General for three years from July 2026
Tushar Mehta—reappointed Attorney General for two years
72.x: R. Venkataramani was reappointed as Attorney General for two years. Tushar Mehta was reappointed as Solicitor General for three years from 1 July 2026.
72.tq: Match the current officeholder with the correct office and tenure before evaluating the distractors.
72.sec: Universal angles

73.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Body — Article

1. National Commission for Scheduled Castes — Article 338
2. National Commission for Scheduled Tribes — Article 338A
3. National Commission for Backward Classes — Article 338B
73.x: The NCSC, NCST and NCBC are provided for under Articles 338, 338A and 338B respectively.
73.tq: Start with the sure Article–body pairs and eliminate codes containing a swapped constitutional provision.

73.s: The National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, as a combined commission, was created by the
73.x: The 65th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1990 created the combined National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes under Article 338.
73.tq: Use the amendment-number trap by distinguishing the original provision from the later bifurcation.

73.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The 65th Constitutional Amendment replaced the original Special Officer for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
2. The 65th Constitutional Amendment also replaced the commission established by the 1987 Resolution.
3. The 65th Constitutional Amendment created the separate National Commission for Scheduled Tribes under Article 338A.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Separate constitutional provision for the NCST under Article 338A came through the 89th Amendment, not the 65th Amendment.
73.tq: Check the amendment sequence carefully; the false statement swaps the combined commission with the later bifurcation.

73.s: The bifurcation of the combined National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes into separate NCSC and NCST was effected by the
73.x: The 89th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 bifurcated the combined commission, creating separate constitutional commissions for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
73.tq: Discriminate between closely related amendment numbers by matching the amendment with its precise institutional change.

73.s: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes was set up on
73.x: The NCST was set up on 19 February 2004 pursuant to the 89th Constitutional Amendment, 2003.
73.tq: Treat the exact establishment date as distinct from the year of the constitutional amendment.

73.s: Which of the following correctly describes the constitutional position of the National Commission for Backward Classes before the 102nd Constitutional Amendment?
o: It was a constitutional body under Article 338B from 1993.
It was a body created by the 89th Constitutional Amendment.
It was a statutory body under the NCBC Act, 1993.
It was a constitutional body under Article 350B.
73.x: Before receiving constitutional status through the 102nd Amendment, the NCBC functioned as a statutory body under the NCBC Act, 1993.
73.tq: Separate statutory status before an amendment from constitutional status after the amendment.

73.s: The separate Ministry of Tribal Affairs, established in 1999, was significant because it
o: created the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
paved the way for a separate National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
abolished the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
transferred Article 338A to the State List
73.x: The establishment of the separate Ministry of Tribal Affairs in 1999 paved the way for the creation of a separate NCST.
73.tq: Link the institutional cause with its stated administrative consequence rather than confusing it with formal constitutional creation.

73.s: Which one of the following is NOT a function of the National Commissions for the protected communities?
o: Inquiring into specific complaints of deprivation of rights
Investigating and monitoring constitutional and legal safeguards
Adjudicating criminal cases and awarding punishment to offenders
Advising on socio-economic planning and evaluating progress
73.x: The Commissions investigate safeguards, inquire into complaints and advise on development; they do not function as criminal courts or award criminal punishment.
73.tq: Find the institutionally impossible power by asking which function belongs to a court rather than a commission.
