73.s: In respect of reports of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes, which one of the following is correct?
o: The Commission submits its reports directly to the Supreme Court for approval.
The Commission submits its reports annually to the Prime Minister, who lays them before Parliament.
The Commission submits its reports to the President, who lays them before Parliament with a memorandum of action taken.
The Commission submits its reports only to the concerned State Governor.
73.x: The Commission submits annual or other appropriate reports to the President. The President lays them before Parliament along with a memorandum of action taken; State-related reports are sent to the Governor.
73.tq: Use the authority trap: distinguish the President, who receives and lays the report, from the Prime Minister or Governor.

73.s:
With reference to the reports of the National Commissions, consider the following statements:
1. A report may be submitted annually or whenever the Commission considers it necessary.
2. Reports relating to State matters are sent to the Governor.
3. The President lays the reports before Parliament with a memorandum of action taken.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: All three statements are correct. The reporting arrangement includes annual or need-based reports, transmission of State-related reports to the Governor and laying before Parliament with an action-taken memorandum.
73.tq: Test the full reporting chain rather than focusing only on the authority to whom the report is submitted.

73.s:
While investigating a matter, the National Commission may exercise the powers of a civil court in respect of which of the following?
1. Summoning and examining a person on oath
2. Requiring the discovery and production of documents
3. Receiving evidence on affidavits
4. Requisitioning public records from a court or office
5. Issuing commissions for the examination of witnesses
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
73.x: All the listed powers are available to the Commission while inquiring into matters, including summoning persons, requiring documents, receiving affidavit evidence, requisitioning records and issuing witness commissions.
73.tq: When several procedural powers are listed, verify whether the entire set belongs to the civil-court power rather than excluding the final item.

73.s: The Union Government and every State Government are required to consult the Commission on
o: only matters relating to elections to local bodies
all major policy matters affecting the concerned protected community
every item of financial legislation before introduction
all appointments to the higher judiciary
73.x: Article 338(9) and Article 338A(9) require consultation with the concerned Commission on all major policy matters affecting Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes, as applicable.
73.tq: Avoid the scope trap: the consultation requirement concerns major policy matters affecting the community, not every governmental decision.

73.s: Who was the first Chairperson of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes constituted separately in 2004?
73.x: Suraj Bhan was the first Chairperson of the separately constituted National Commission for Scheduled Castes in 2004.
73.tq: Discriminate among chairpersons by linking each name to the correct commission and period.

73.s: Who was the first Chairperson of the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes constituted separately in 2004?
73.x: Kunwar Singh was the first Chairperson of the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes constituted separately in 2004.
73.tq: Use the commission–chairperson association instead of relying only on the common year of constitution.

73.s: The first Chairperson of the constitutionally established National Commission for Backward Classes in 2019 was
73.x: Bhagwan Lal Sahni was the first Chairperson of the constitutionally established NCBC in 2019.
73.tq: Distinguish the first chairperson of the constitutional NCBC from chairpersons of other commissions.

73.s: Who was serving as Chairperson of the National Commission for Backward Classes in the current reference period?
73.x: Niranjan Jyoti is identified as the current Chairperson of the National Commission for Backward Classes in the stated reference period.
73.tq: Separate a current office-holder from the first office-holder of the same commission.

73.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is correct?
o: The officer is appointed by the President and reports to the President.
The officer is appointed by the Chief Minister and reports to the Governor.
The officer is appointed by the Parliament and reports to the Prime Minister.
The officer is appointed by the Governor and reports to the State Legislature.
73.x: Under Article 350B, the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is appointed by the President and submits reports to the President.
73.tq: Apply the authority trap by matching appointment and reporting powers with the President.
73.sec: Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities and Art. 350A

73.s: The headquarters of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities is located at
73.x: The office styled as the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities has its headquarters at Prayagraj, formerly Allahabad.
73.tq: Test the exact headquarters rather than the more obvious national-capital location.
73.sec: Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities and Art. 350A

73.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Articles 350A and 350B were inserted by the 7th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956.
2. The amendment was associated with the reorganisation of States.
3. The office under Article 350B is styled as the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: All three statements are correct. The 7th Amendment of 1956, connected with the States Reorganisation process, inserted Articles 350A and 350B and provided for the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities.
73.tq: Combine amendment, context and official designation; all three details refer to the same constitutional arrangement.
73.sec: Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities and Art. 350A

73.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Article — Subject

a. Article 347 — Recognition of a language spoken by a substantial section of a State
b. Article 350 — Representation for the redress of grievances in any language used in the Union or a State
c. Article 350A — Mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
73.x: Article 347 concerns recognition of a language spoken by a substantial section of a State; Article 350 concerns representation in any language used in the Union or a State; and Article 350A concerns mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage.
73.tq: Use the article-number sequence to distinguish the closely related linguistic safeguards.
73.sec: Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities and Art. 350A

73.s: Which one of the following statements about linguistic minorities is correct?
o: They are notified under the National Commission for Minorities Act, and Article 350B has no role concerning them.
They are covered exclusively by Article 338B.
They are treated only as religious minorities for purposes of constitutional safeguards.
They are not notified under the National Commission for Minorities Act and are covered by the officer under Article 350B.
73.x: Linguistic minorities are not notified under the National Commission for Minorities Act; safeguards for them are covered through the officer provided under Article 350B.
73.tq: Separate linguistic-minority coverage under Article 350B from the statutory framework of the National Commission for Minorities.
73.sec: Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities and Art. 350A

73.s: The Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities launched a programme consisting of
o: a twelve-point programme for tribal development
a ten-point programme to preserve language and culture
a five-point programme to promote official-language use
a seven-point programme for State reorganisation
73.x: The Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities launched a 10-point programme aimed at preserving the language and culture of linguistic minorities.
73.tq: Treat the numerical feature as decisive and avoid substituting the nearby States Reorganisation or tribal-development figures.
73.sec: Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities and Art. 350A

73.s: Which statement correctly describes the constitutional basis of State Commissions for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes?
o: State Commissions are created by the Supreme Court under Article 32.
State Commissions are created only by the President through an executive order under Article 350B.
State Commissions are created by State law; Articles 338(9) and 338A(9) concern consultation on major policy matters.
Every State Commission is automatically created directly by Article 338(9).
73.x: State Commissions are created through State legislation. Articles 338(9) and 338A(9) deal with consultation on major policy matters and do not empower the President to create State Commissions.
73.tq: Reject the wrong-authority trap by distinguishing a State legislative creation from a constitutional consultation clause.
73.sec: AP State Commission for SCs and STs

73.s: Which one of the following persons was identified as the Chairman of the Andhra Pradesh State Commission for Scheduled Castes during the review of welfare schemes in SPSR Nellore?
73.x: K.S. Jawahar was identified as the Chairman of the Andhra Pradesh State Commission for Scheduled Castes while reviewing SC/ST welfare schemes in SPSR Nellore.
73.tq: Keep State-level office-holders separate from chairpersons of the corresponding national commissions.
73.sec: AP State Commission for SCs and STs

73.s:
With reference to the National Commission for Women, consider the following statements:
1. It is a statutory body.
2. It was created under the National Commission for Women Act, 1990.
3. It was constituted in 1992.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: All three statements are correct. The NCW is statutory, derives its authority from the 1990 Act and was constituted in 1992.
73.tq: Check whether the question distinguishes the year of the Act from the year of constitution.

73.s: The First Backward Classes Commission was appointed in which year, and its report was submitted in which year?
73.x: The First Backward Classes Commission was appointed in 1953 and submitted its report in 1955. It was headed by Kaka Kalelkar.
73.tq: Separate the appointment year from the report year instead of treating them as the same date.
73.sec: Backward Classes Commissions → chairman, year, government

73.s: The recommendation of 27 per cent reservation for Other Backward Classes was implemented by which government in 1990?
73.x: The Mandal Commission recommended 27 per cent reservation for OBCs, and the recommendation was implemented by the V.P. Singh government in 1990.
73.tq: Distinguish the government that appointed a commission from the government that implemented its recommendation.
73.sec: Backward Classes Commissions → chairman, year, government

73.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the composition of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes and the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes:
1. Each Commission consists of a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and three members.
2. All members are appointed by the President by warrant.
3. Their service conditions and tenure are fixed by the President.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: All three statements are correct. Each Commission has five members in all, appointed by the President by warrant, with service conditions and tenure fixed by the President.
73.tq: Verify composition, appointing authority and service conditions independently before selecting the coded option.

73.s: Under the applicable rules, the tenure of the Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and members of the NCSC and NCST is:
73.x: The term of office of the Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and members is three years under the applicable rules.
73.tq: Focus on the precise numerical term rather than confusing it with the term of another constitutional office.

73.s: Which of the following correctly describes the rank associated with offices in the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes?
o: Chairperson—Union Cabinet Minister; Vice-Chairperson—Minister of State; members—Secretary rank
Chairperson—Minister of State; Vice-Chairperson—Secretary rank; members—Cabinet Minister rank
Chairperson—Secretary rank; Vice-Chairperson—Cabinet Minister; members—Minister of State rank
Chairperson—Chief Minister; Vice-Chairperson—Cabinet Secretary; members—Joint Secretary rank
73.x: The Chairperson of the NCST has the rank of a Union Cabinet Minister, the Vice-Chairperson has the rank of a Minister of State, and the members have Secretary rank.
73.tq: Match each office with its designated rank, taking care not to reverse the hierarchy.

73.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the National Commission for Backward Classes is correct?
o: Its constitutional composition consists of a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and three members.
It continues to have only the five-member composition of the 1993 statutory body.
It is headed by a retired Supreme Court or High Court judge as a constitutional requirement.
Its members are appointed by the Central Government without presidential involvement.
73.x: The constitutional NCBC consists of a Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and three members appointed by the President. The earlier statutory NCBC had five members and was headed by a retired Supreme Court or High Court judge.
73.tq: Separate the present constitutional NCBC from the earlier five-member statutory NCBC.

73.s:
Arrange the following developments relating to the National Commissions in chronological order:
A. Creation of non-statutory commissions by government resolutions
B. Replacement of the Special Officer by a multi-member constitutional commission
C. Bifurcation into the NCSC and NCST
D. Creation of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs
73.x: The correct order is A (1978 and 1987), B (1990), D (1999), and C (2003, followed by implementation in 2004).
73.tq: Anchor the sequence with the dated constitutional amendments and place the 1999 ministry between them.

73.s: The 65th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1990 is associated with which development?
o: Replacement of the Special Officer for SCs and STs by a multi-member National Commission
Bifurcation of the NCSC into the NCSC and NCST
Restoration of the States’ power to prepare SEBC lists
Creation of the constitutional NCBC under Article 338B
73.x: The 65th Amendment, 1990 replaced the Special Officer for SCs and STs with a multi-member constitutional National Commission. The NCBC was constitutionalised by the 102nd Amendment, while bifurcation occurred through the 89th Amendment.
73.tq: Match the amendment with its precise institutional change rather than a later development.

73.s: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes became operational with effect from:
73.x: The NCST was set up with effect from 19 February 2004 following the bifurcation authorised by the 89th Constitutional Amendment.
73.tq: Test the exact operational date separately from the year of the constitutional amendment.

73.s: Which development provided the contextual basis for creating a separate commission for Scheduled Tribes?
o: Creation of the Ministry of Social Justice in 1990
The Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
The National Commission for Women Act, 1990
Creation of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs in 1999
73.x: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs was created in 1999, a development that preceded and supported the establishment of a separate commission for Scheduled Tribes.
73.tq: Link the institutional development with the ministry specifically concerned with tribal affairs.

73.s: In Indra Sawhney v. Union of India, decided on 16 November 1992, the Supreme Court, among other things, upheld:
o: 27 per cent reservation for OBCs and the concept of the creamy layer
50 per cent reservation exclusively for economically weaker sections
The abolition of all reservation in public employment
The exclusive power of States to notify all SEBCs without constitutional limitation
73.x: The judgment upheld 27 per cent reservation for OBCs, introduced the creamy-layer principle and directed the creation of a permanent body concerning inclusion and exclusion from the OBC list.
73.tq: Combine the date with the judgment’s distinct holdings instead of confusing it with later amendments.
73.sec: Indra Sawhney and creamy layer link to NCBC

73.s: The income ceiling associated with the creamy layer, as notified in 2017, is:
73.x: The creamy-layer income ceiling mentioned in the relevant notification is ₹8 lakh per year. Andhra Pradesh aligned its definitions with the central thresholds.
73.tq: Compare the closely spaced monetary figures and select the notified threshold.
73.sec: Indra Sawhney and creamy layer link to NCBC

73.s: Which one of the following correctly states the effect of the 102nd and 105th Constitutional Amendments in relation to SEBCs?
o: The 102nd Amendment created the creamy layer, while the 105th Amendment abolished it.
The 102nd Amendment gave the President power to notify SEBCs, while the 105th Amendment restored the States’ power to prepare their own lists.
The 102nd Amendment restored State lists, while the 105th Amendment gave the President the first power to notify SEBCs.
Both amendments abolished the power of the President to notify SEBCs.
73.x: The 102nd Amendment enabled the President to notify SEBCs. The 105th Amendment, 2021 restored the States’ power to prepare their own SEBC lists.
73.tq: Compare the two amendments by assigning one distinct constitutional effect to each.
73.sec: Indra Sawhney and creamy layer link to NCBC

73.s:
Consider the following statements about the statutory National Commission for Backward Classes:
1. It was established under the NCBC Act, 1993.
2. The Act came into force on 2 April 1993.
3. It had five members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: All three statements are correct. The statutory NCBC was established under the 1993 Act, which came into force on 2 April 1993, and it had five members.
73.tq: Check the Act, commencement date and composition as separate components of the earlier statutory body.
73.sec: Indra Sawhney and creamy layer link to NCBC

73.s: The direction in Indra Sawhney concerning a permanent body for inclusion and exclusion from the OBC list led to the establishment of the:
o: National Commission for Scheduled Tribes under the 89th Amendment
National Commission for Women under the 1990 Act
Statutory National Commission for Backward Classes under the 1993 Act
National Commission for Minorities under the 1992 Act
73.x: The direction in Indra Sawhney led to the NCBC Act, 1993 and the establishment of the statutory NCBC. It was intended to advise on inclusion and exclusion from the OBC list.
73.tq: Trace the judicial direction to the institution created to perform the specified function.
73.sec: Indra Sawhney and creamy layer link to NCBC

73.s: Which one of the following was a consequence of the 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2018?
o: Bifurcation of the NCSC and NCST
Insertion of Article 338B and constitutional status for the NCBC
Insertion of Article 350B and creation of the Linguistic Minorities Officer
Creation of the first statutory NCBC
73.x: The 102nd Amendment inserted Article 338B and gave constitutional status to the NCBC. The other developments belong to different constitutional provisions or earlier enactments.
73.tq: Match the amendment with its article and institutional result, avoiding chronology traps.
73.sec: Indra Sawhney and creamy layer link to NCBC

73.s: The 102nd Constitutional Amendment also had the effect of:
o: Transferring all SEBC-list powers to State Governors
Removing Scheduled Tribes from the purview of the NCST
Removing backward classes from the purview of the NCSC
73.x: The 102nd Amendment removed backward classes from the purview of the NCSC while constitutionalising the NCBC under Article 338B.
73.tq: Look for the precise change in jurisdiction rather than a general statement about reservation.
73.sec: Indra Sawhney and creamy layer link to NCBC

73.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Commission for Minorities:
1. It is a statutory body under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992.
2. The first statutory National Commission for Minorities was constituted in 1993.
3. The Chairperson and members are appointed by the President of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false: the Chairperson and members of the NCM are appointed by the Central Government, not by the President.
73.tq: Apply the ‘who appoints?’ trap, especially where a constitutional President may be confused with the Central Government.

73.s: Which of the following correctly describes the composition of the National Commission for Minorities after the 1995 amendment?
o: A Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and five members
A Chairperson and three members only
A Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and three members
A Chairperson, two Vice-Chairpersons and four members
73.x: The 1995 amendment added a Vice-Chairperson, resulting in a total of seven members: a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and five members.
73.tq: Calculate the total composition after identifying the amendment’s specific addition.

73.s: Under Section 3(2) of the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992, at least how many members including the Chairperson must belong to minority communities?
73.x: Five members, including the Chairperson, must be from minority communities under Section 3(2) of the Act.
73.tq: Read the qualifying phrase ‘including the Chairperson’ carefully before selecting the number.

73.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the National Commission for Minorities is correct?
o: It has a five-year term and exercises criminal court powers in all matters.
It has a one-year term and no inquiry powers resembling those of a civil court.
It has a six-year term and is constituted by a constitutional amendment.
It has a three-year term and exercises civil court powers during inquiries.
73.x: The NCM has a three-year term and exercises civil court powers during inquiries. It is a statutory body under the 1992 Act, not a constitutional body.
73.tq: Separate the duration of tenure from the nature of inquiry powers and the body’s legal status.

73.s: Which of the following was the precursor to the statutory National Commission for Minorities?
o: The 1993 Protection of Human Rights Act
The 1990 National Commission for Women Act
A 1978 resolution of the Ministry of Home Affairs
A 1987 resolution of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs
73.x: The Minorities Commission created by a 1978 Ministry of Home Affairs resolution was the precursor to the statutory NCM established under the 1992 Act.
73.tq: Distinguish the precursor executive resolution from the later statutory enactment.

73.s: Which of the following pairs of communities is NOT included among the notified minority communities?
73.x: The notified minority communities are Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis and Jains. Jews are not included in this listed group.
73.tq: Find the outsider in a recognised statutory list rather than choosing a community from memory alone.

73.s: Who was appointed Chairperson of the National Commission for Minorities for a three-year term in 2026?
73.x: Harjit Singh Grewal was appointed Chairperson of the National Commission for Minorities for a three-year term in 2026.
73.tq: Match the current appointee with the correct statutory commission and tenure.

73.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis:
1. It was created by the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis Act, 1993.
2. The Act lapsed in 2004.
3. The Commission continues as a non-statutory body with its tenure extended by resolution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: All three statements are correct. The NCSK was created under the 1993 Act; after the Act lapsed in 2004, it continued as a non-statutory body through tenure extensions by resolution.
73.tq: Track the transition from statutory creation to present non-statutory continuation.

73.s: Who headed the National Commission for Backward Classes in 2026?
o: The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
73.x: Niranjan Jyoti headed the National Commission for Backward Classes in 2026.
73.tq: Use the office-holder distinction to separate the NCBC from the National Commission for Minorities and the AP State SC Commission.

73.s: Who was reported as the Chairperson of the National Commission for Minorities in July 2026?
73.x: Harjit Singh Grewal headed the National Commission for Minorities in July 2026.
73.tq: Discriminate between closely related constitutional and statutory commission office-holders.

73.s:
With reference to Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. Andhra Pradesh has a State Minorities Commission.
2. Andhra Pradesh has a State Scheduled Castes Commission.
3. Andhra Pradesh has no State-level commission dealing with minorities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Andhra Pradesh has both a State Minorities Commission and a State Scheduled Castes Commission. Statement 3 is false because it contradicts the existence of the State Minorities Commission.
73.tq: Find the internally contradictory statement and distinguish the two State-level commissions.

73.s: Who was identified as the Chairman of the Andhra Pradesh State Scheduled Castes Commission in August 2026?
o: The Chairperson of the State Minorities Commission
73.x: K.S. Jawahar was identified as the Chairman of the Andhra Pradesh State Scheduled Castes Commission in August 2026.
73.tq: Match the person with the correct State commission rather than a similarly named national commission.

73.s: Which one of the following correctly describes a criticism associated with the functioning of commissions such as the National Commission for Minorities?
o: Their recommendations are enforceable only through the National Commission for Backward Classes.
Their recommendations are advisory only, and long vacancies have been noted in the National Commission for Minorities.
Their recommendations are binding on every authority, and vacancies are constitutionally prohibited.
Their recommendations are advisory only, but long vacancies have never been reported in the National Commission for Minorities.
73.x: The criticism identified is that recommendations are advisory only and that the National Commission for Minorities has experienced long vacancies, a matter noted by the Delhi High Court in 2026.
73.tq: Reject absolute claims such as 'every' and 'never' while retaining both parts of the precise criticism.

74.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. National Commission for Women — NCW Act, 1990
2. National Commission for Minorities — NCM Act, 1992
3. National Human Rights Commission — Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
4. National Commission for Protection of Child Rights — Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005
74.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. The respective governing Acts were enacted in 1990, 1992, 1993 and 2005.
74.tq: Start from the sure Act-year pairs and eliminate codes that omit a correct pair.
74.sec: Statutory body → Act and year (NHRC, NCW, NCM, NCPCR, NCSK)

74.s:
The National Commission for Women was constituted in:

a. January 1990
b. January 1992
c. January 1993
d. January 1995
74.x: The National Commission for Women was constituted in January 1992 under the National Commission for Women Act, 1990.
74.tq: Distinguish the year of the parent Act from the year in which the body was set up.
74.sec: NCW - NCW Act 1990, composition, functions (Section 10), first chairperson, Jan Sunwai

74.s:
The first statutory National Commission for Minorities was set up in:

a. 1978
b. 1990
c. 1992
d. 1993
74.x: The first statutory National Commission for Minorities was set up in 1993 under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992. A non-statutory Minorities Commission had earlier been created by a Ministry of Home Affairs resolution in 1978.
74.tq: Separate the earlier non-statutory body from the later statutory commission.
74.sec: Statutory body → Act and year (NHRC, NCW, NCM, NCPCR, NCSK)

74.s:
The National Human Rights Commission was established on:

a. 28 September 1993
b. 12 October 1993
c. 26 November 1993
d. 10 December 1993
74.x: The NHRC was established on 12 October 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. The Ordinance relating to it had been promulgated on 28 September 1993.
74.tq: Discriminate between the date of the Ordinance and the date of establishment.
74.sec: Statutory body → Act and year (NHRC, NCW, NCM, NCPCR, NCSK)

74.s:
Which one of the following bodies was set up in 2007 under a law enacted in 2005?

a. National Commission for Women
b. National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
c. National Commission for Minorities
d. National Commission for Safai Karamcharis
o: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
74.x: The NCPCR was set up in 2007 under the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005.
74.tq: Use the distinctive Act-year and establishment-year combination to identify the body.
74.sec: Statutory body → Act and year (NHRC, NCW, NCM, NCPCR, NCSK)

74.s:
Consider the following statements:

1. The NCSC is provided for under Article 338.
2. The NCST is provided for under Article 338A.
3. The NCBC is provided for under Article 338B.
4. The National Commission for Women is provided for under Article 338C.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
74.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The NCW is a statutory body under the NCW Act, 1990 and is not established under Article 338C.
74.tq: Check the constitutional Article attached to each commission and reject the invented Article.
74.sec: Statutory body → Act and year (NHRC, NCW, NCM, NCPCR, NCSK)

74.s:
Which of the following statements regarding commissions for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes is correct?

a. The 65th Constitutional Amendment of 1990 created separate commissions for the SCs and STs.
b. The 89th Constitutional Amendment of 2003 bifurcated the combined commission into the NCSC and NCST.
c. The separate commissions began functioning in 1990.
d. The NCST is established under Article 338B.
o: The 65th Constitutional Amendment of 1990 created separate commissions for the SCs and STs.
The separate commissions began functioning in 1990.
The NCST is established under Article 338B.
The 89th Constitutional Amendment of 2003 bifurcated the combined commission into the NCSC and NCST.
74.x: The 65th Amendment created a combined SC/ST Commission. The 89th Amendment in 2003 bifurcated it, and separate bodies functioned from 2004; the NCST is under Article 338A.
74.tq: Watch for swapped amendment numbers, Articles and dates in constitutional-body questions.
74.sec: Statutory body → Act and year (NHRC, NCW, NCM, NCPCR, NCSK)

74.s:
Which one of the following is NOT a statutory body under the Ministry of Women and Child Development?

a. National Commission for Women
b. National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
c. Central Adoption Resource Authority
d. National Commission for Safai Karamcharis
o: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
74.x: NCW, NCPCR and CARA are the three statutory bodies under the Ministry of Women and Child Development. The NCSK is under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and is non-statutory since 2004.
74.tq: Find the body belonging to the neighbouring ministry and different legal category.
74.sec: Statutory body → Act and year (NHRC, NCW, NCM, NCPCR, NCSK)

74.s:
Which one of the following statements regarding linguistic minorities is correct?

a. Linguistic minorities are dealt with by the National Commission for Minorities under the NCM Act, 1992.
b. Linguistic minorities are dealt with by the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities under Article 350B.
c. Linguistic minorities are dealt with by the NCBC under Article 338B.
d. Linguistic minorities are dealt with by the National Commission for Women.
o: Linguistic minorities are dealt with by the National Commission for Women.
Linguistic minorities are dealt with by the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities under Article 350B.
Linguistic minorities are dealt with by the National Commission for Minorities under the NCM Act, 1992.
Linguistic minorities are dealt with by the NCBC under Article 338B.
74.x: Linguistic minorities do not fall under the National Commission for Minorities. They fall under the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities provided under Article 350B.
74.tq: Separate religious-minority institutions from the constitutional protection for linguistic minorities.
74.sec: Statutory body → Act and year (NHRC, NCW, NCM, NCPCR, NCSK)

74.s:
The National Commission for Women consists of:

a. A Chairperson, three Members and a Member-Secretary
b. A Chairperson, five Members and a Member-Secretary
c. A Chairperson, seven Members and a Secretary-General
d. Five Members and a Secretary appointed by Parliament
o: A Chairperson, seven Members and a Secretary-General
A Chairperson, three Members and a Member-Secretary
Five Members and a Secretary appointed by Parliament
A Chairperson, five Members and a Member-Secretary
74.x: The NCW comprises one Chairperson, five Members and one Member-Secretary. All are nominated by the Central Government.
74.tq: Use the exact composition and do not confuse nomination with election or parliamentary appointment.
74.sec: NCW - NCW Act 1990, composition, functions (Section 10), first chairperson, Jan Sunwai

74.s:
Who nominates the Chairperson, Members and Member-Secretary of the National Commission for Women?

a. The President of India
b. The Parliament
c. The Central Government
d. The Supreme Court of India
74.x: The Chairperson, five Members and Member-Secretary of the NCW are nominated by the Central Government.
74.tq: Apply the “who would do this job?” method to distinguish nomination from constitutional appointment.
74.sec: NCW - NCW Act 1990, composition, functions (Section 10), first chairperson, Jan Sunwai

74.s:
Who was the first Chairperson of the National Commission for Women?

a. Jayanti Patnaik
b. Vijaya Rahatkar
c. Mohini Giri
d. Girija Vyas
74.x: Jayanti Patnaik was the first Chairperson of the National Commission for Women.
74.tq: Distinguish the first office-holder from later chairpersons and other prominent office-holders.
74.sec: NCW - NCW Act 1990, composition, functions (Section 10), first chairperson, Jan Sunwai

74.s:
Which one of the following is NOT a function of the National Commission for Women?

a. Suggesting amendments to laws affecting women
b. Taking suo motu notice where women’s rights are denied
c. Commissioning special studies on discrimination and atrocities against women
d. Enforcing criminal sentences imposed by courts
o: Suggesting amendments to laws affecting women
Taking suo motu notice where women’s rights are denied
Commissioning special studies on discrimination and atrocities against women
Enforcing criminal sentences imposed by courts
74.x: The NCW may review laws, suggest amendments, take suo motu notice and commission special studies. It does not enforce criminal sentences imposed by courts.
74.tq: Reject the option that converts a recommendatory statutory function into a coercive judicial power.
74.sec: NCW - NCW Act 1990, composition, functions (Section 10), first chairperson, Jan Sunwai

74.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Commission for Women:

1. The Central Government must consult it on all major policy matters affecting women.
2. It may appoint committees for particular purposes.
3. It may co-opt persons from outside the Commission.
4. It has no power to regulate its own procedure.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
74.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The NCW may regulate its own procedure, so statement 4 is false.
74.tq: Spot the negative statement that reverses an expressly stated procedural power.
74.sec: NCW - NCW Act 1990, composition, functions (Section 10), first chairperson, Jan Sunwai

74.s:
In the context of women’s rights, a ‘Jan Sunwai’ refers to:

a. A closed-door meeting of judges
b. A public hearing of women’s grievances
c. An annual financial audit of women’s commissions
d. A legislative session on gender budgeting
o: A public hearing of women’s grievances
A legislative session on gender budgeting
An annual financial audit of women’s commissions
74.x: Jan Sunwai refers to public hearings conducted to hear and address women’s grievances.
74.tq: Test the exact meaning of a programme term rather than its broad policy context.
74.sec: NCW - NCW Act 1990, composition, functions (Section 10), first chairperson, Jan Sunwai

74.s:
The five-day Jan Sunwai conducted by the Andhra Pradesh Mahila Commission in March 2026 was held during:

a. 1–5 March 2026
b. 9–13 March 2026
c. 15–19 March 2026
d. 20–24 March 2026
74.x: The five-day Jan Sunwai was held from 9 to 13 March 2026 in five zones, including Nellore, Guntur, Vijayawada and Rajamahendravaram, on directions from the NCW.
74.tq: Use the exact date range and distinguish it from nearby five-day alternatives.
74.sec: NCW - NCW Act 1990, composition, functions (Section 10), first chairperson, Jan Sunwai

74.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis?

a. Act lapsed — 1998
b. Change to non-statutory status — 2004
c. Ministry — Women and Child Development
d. Governing Act currently in force — NCSK Act, 1993
o: Governing Act currently in force — NCSK Act, 1993
74.x: The NCSK Act, 1993 lapsed in 2004, after which the NCSK continued as a non-statutory body under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. The Act is not currently in force as its governing basis.
74.tq: Separate the original statutory status from the present non-statutory status.
74.sec: National Commission for Safai Karamcharis - legal status, tenure extensions

74.s:
The National Commission for Safai Karamcharis is presently continued primarily through:

a. Constitutional provision under Article 338D
b. Periodic tenure extensions by government resolution
c. Annual elections conducted by sanitation workers
d. Orders of the Supreme Court alone
o: Orders of the Supreme Court alone
Periodic tenure extensions by government resolution
Annual elections conducted by sanitation workers
74.x: After the NCSK Act lapsed in 2004, the Commission continued as a non-statutory body through periodic tenure extensions by government resolution.
74.tq: Apply the legal-status distinction to determine the present institutional basis.
74.sec: National Commission for Safai Karamcharis - legal status, tenure extensions

74.s:
In January 2022, the Union Cabinet extended the tenure of the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis for:

a. One year beyond 31 March 2022
b. Two years beyond 31 March 2022
c. Three years beyond 31 March 2022
d. Five years beyond 31 March 2022
74.x: In January 2022, the Union Cabinet extended the NCSK for three years beyond 31 March 2022, taking the tenure up to 31 March 2025.
74.tq: Match the extension period with its terminal date rather than relying on the Act’s original year.
74.sec: National Commission for Safai Karamcharis - legal status, tenure extensions

74.s:
The tenure of the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis was subsequently extended up to:

a. 31 March 2026
b. 31 March 2027
c. 31 March 2028
d. 31 December 2028
74.x: After the extension up to 31 March 2025, the NCSK received a further three-year extension up to 31 March 2028.
74.tq: Track successive tenure extensions chronologically and identify the final date.
74.sec: National Commission for Safai Karamcharis - legal status, tenure extensions

74.s:
Which of the following functions is associated with the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis?

a. Monitoring the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers Act, 2013 and reporting to the Government
b. Conducting the census of all urban households
c. Appointing municipal commissioners in every State
d. Issuing constitutional amendments concerning sanitation
o: Appointing municipal commissioners in every State
Conducting the census of all urban households
Monitoring the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers Act, 2013 and reporting to the Government
74.x: The NCSK monitors implementation of the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers Act, 2013 and reports to the Government.
74.tq: Identify the option that states a monitoring and reporting responsibility rather than an unrelated executive power.
74.sec: National Commission for Safai Karamcharis - legal status, tenure extensions

74.s:
The missed-call grievance line for sanitation workers was launched on the foundation day of the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis, observed on:

a. 15 August
b. 23 August
c. 2 October
d. 26 November
74.x: The missed-call grievance line was launched on the NCSK’s foundation day, 23 August 2026.
74.tq: Use the distinctive institutional date instead of confusing it with national observance days.
74.sec: National Commission for Safai Karamcharis - legal status, tenure extensions

74.s:
Who among the following was the Vice-Chairperson of the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis as reported in 2026?

a. Hardeep Singh Gill
b. Jayanti Patnaik
c. Vijaya Rahatkar
d. Santosh Hegde
74.x: Hardeep Singh Gill was the Vice-Chairperson of the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis as reported in 2026.
74.tq: Match the office-holder with the correct statutory body and avoid swapping names across commissions.
74.sec: National Commission for Safai Karamcharis - legal status, tenure extensions

74.s:
Which one of the following is correctly matched?

a. NAMASTE — 2022; associated with NSKFDC
b. Jan Sunwai — appointment of NCSK Vice-Chairperson
c. NCSK Act — constitutional provision under Article 338A
d. Article 350B — National Commission for Safai Karamcharis
o: Jan Sunwai — appointment of NCSK Vice-Chairperson
NCSK Act — constitutional provision under Article 338A
Article 350B — National Commission for Safai Karamcharis
74.x: NAMASTE is associated with the NSKFDC and dates from 2022. Jan Sunwai concerns public hearings of women’s grievances, Article 338A concerns the NCST, and Article 350B concerns linguistic minorities.
74.tq: Use nearby institutional facts to catch swapped bodies, Articles and programmes.
74.sec: National Commission for Safai Karamcharis - legal status, tenure extensions

74.s: The National Human Rights Commission was established under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 on
74.x: The NHRC was established on 12 October 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. The Ordinance preceding the Act was promulgated on 28 September 1993.

2. They may summon and enforce the attendance of persons and examine them on oath.
3. They may requisition public records from any office or organization.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
74.x: All three statements are correct. The NCSC, NCST and NCBC exercise civil-court powers during investigations and inquiries, including summoning persons, examining them on oath, calling for documents and requisitioning public records.
74.tq: Combine several related powers and verify each statement rather than relying on one familiar power.
74.sec: Powers of commissions - civil court powers, investigation, reports to whom (NCSC, NCST, NCBC)

74.s: The civil-court powers of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes, while investigating or inquiring into matters, are derived from which Article of the Constitution?
74.x: Article 338 provides the constitutional basis for the powers of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes. Article 338A relates to the NCST and Article 338B to the NCBC.
74.tq: Use the article-number distinction among closely related constitutional commissions.
74.sec: Powers of commissions - civil court powers, investigation, reports to whom (NCSC, NCST, NCBC)

74.s: Article 338B of the Constitution deals with the National Commission for:
74.x: Article 338B provides for the National Commission for Backward Classes. The NCST is dealt with under Article 338A.
74.tq: Test the exact constitutional article through a closely confusable commission name.
74.sec: Powers of commissions - civil court powers, investigation, reports to whom (NCSC, NCST, NCBC)

74.s: The annual and special reports of the National Commissions for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Backward Classes are submitted to the:
74.x: The annual and special reports of these constitutional commissions are submitted to the President. The President lays them before Parliament along with an action-taken memorandum.
74.tq: Apply the ‘who receives the report?’ method to distinguish the reporting authority from the laying authority.
74.sec: Powers of commissions - civil court powers, investigation, reports to whom (NCSC, NCST, NCBC)

74.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the reports of the NCSC, NCST and NCBC:
1. The President lays the reports before Parliament.
2. An action-taken memorandum accompanies the reports.
3. Portions concerning a particular State are sent to the Governor of that State.
4. The Union and every State are required to consult these commissions on major policy matters affecting their subjects.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
74.x: All four statements are correct. The reports are submitted to the President, laid before Parliament with an action-taken memorandum, and State-related portions go to the concerned Governor; major policy matters require consultation with the commissions.
74.tq: Separate submission, laying, State transmission and consultation duties instead of treating them as one procedure.
74.sec: Powers of commissions - civil court powers, investigation, reports to whom (NCSC, NCST, NCBC)

74.s: Which one of the following is specifically associated with the functions of the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes?
o: Appointment of State Human Rights Commissioners
Protection of minor forest produce ownership and tribal mineral and water rights
74.x: The NCST deals, among other matters, with ownership of minor forest produce, mineral and water rights, and rehabilitation of displaced tribal communities.
74.tq: Identify the commission from a distinctive cluster of subject-specific responsibilities.
74.sec: Powers of commissions - civil court powers, investigation, reports to whom (NCSC, NCST, NCBC)

74.s: Before a proposal for de-reservation of posts is implemented, it must first be examined by the concerned:
o: NCSC, NCST or NCBC, as applicable
74.x: Proposals for de-reservation of posts must first be examined by the relevant NCSC, NCST or NCBC, depending on the category concerned.
74.tq: Ask which authority would perform the specialised constitutional safeguard in a practical administrative situation.
74.sec: Powers of commissions - civil court powers, investigation, reports to whom (NCSC, NCST, NCBC)

74.s: In 2026, which commission began a full review of proposals relating to de-reservation of posts?
o: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
74.x: In August 2026, the National Commission for Scheduled Castes began a full review of proposals relating to de-reservation of posts.
74.tq: Use the current-affairs date and the specific institutional action as the deciding clues.
74.sec: Universal angles

74.s:
With reference to the powers of statutory commissions in inquiries, consider the following statements:
1. The NHRC has civil-court powers.
2. The National Commission for Minorities has powers under its Act that enable it to exercise civil-court powers in inquiries.
3. The National Commission for Minorities has no automatic civil-court powers independent of its statutory framework.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
74.x: All three statements are correct. The NHRC has civil-court powers in inquiries, while the NCM’s inquiry powers arise from its statutory framework and should not be described as automatic or unrestricted constitutional powers.
74.tq: Distinguish statutory powers from automatic or constitutional powers when similar commissions are compared.
74.sec: Powers of commissions - civil court powers, investigation, reports to whom (NCSC, NCST, NCBC)

74.s: The NHRC sought reports from the Andhra Pradesh Director General of Police, the Chief Secretary and the Andhra Pradesh State Human Rights Commission in connection with the alleged custodial death of:
74.x: The NHRC sought reports in connection with the alleged custodial death of Gade Sai Krishna. The matter was considered in the context of Article 21.
74.tq: Match the reported institutional action with the specific person involved, avoiding name substitution.
74.sec: Universal angles

74.s: The NHRC’s reference to Article 21 in the alleged custodial-death matter primarily relates to protection of the:
o: Right to life and personal liberty
74.x: Article 21 guarantees protection of life and personal liberty. Alleged custodial death directly raises concerns relating to this constitutional guarantee.
74.tq: Translate a current administrative action into the constitutional right it invokes.
74.sec: Universal angles

74.s:
Which of the following developments was associated with criticism concerning the National Commission for Minorities and the NHRC in 2026?
1. The post of NCM Chairperson remained vacant for 15 months.
2. An adviser resigned from the NHRC LGBTQI+ core group over the Transgender Persons Amendment Bill, 2026.
3. The NHRC was dissolved following the resignation.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
74.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. A long vacancy affected the NCM, and an adviser resigned from the NHRC LGBTQI+ core group over the Transgender Persons Amendment Bill, 2026; the NHRC was not dissolved.
74.tq: Find the false institutional consequence in a set containing two current-affairs facts and one exaggerated claim.
74.sec: Universal angles

74.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the constitutional status of the commissions listed below?
o: All commissions listed are constitutional bodies with identical powers
NCSC, NCST and NCBC are constitutional bodies; the other commissions depend on parliamentary Acts
NHRC, NCM and NCW are constitutional bodies; NCSC is statutory
Only NHRC and NCM are constitutional bodies
74.x: The NCSC, NCST and NCBC are constitutional commissions. Bodies such as the NHRC, NCM and NCW derive their existence from parliamentary Acts, which Parliament may amend or allow to lapse.
74.tq: Separate constitutional bodies from statutory bodies before comparing their legal status.
74.sec: Universal angles

74.s: Which one of the following is an example of a commission whose existence depends on a parliamentary statute rather than directly on a constitutional provision?
74.x: The National Commission for Safai Karamcharis is a statutory commission. The NCSC, NCST and NCBC are constitutional bodies.
74.tq: Identify the odd body by separating the three constitutional commissions from the statutory example.
74.sec: Universal angles

74.s: Jains were notified as a minority community at the national level in:
74.x: Jains were the latest community to be notified as a national minority, in 2014.
74.tq: Use the first/latest distinction and select the precise year rather than a nearby milestone year.
74.sec: Universal angles

74.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Jains notified as a national minority
B. Harjit Singh Grewal became Chairperson of the National Commission for Minorities
C. National Commission for Scheduled Castes began a full review of de-reservation proposals
D. Adviser resigned from the NHRC LGBTQI+ core group over the Transgender Persons Amendment Bill, 2026
74.x: Jains were notified as a minority in 2014, the adviser’s resignation occurred in March 2026, Harjit Singh Grewal became NCM Chairperson in July 2026, and the NCSC review began in August 2026.
74.tq: Fix the earliest dated event first and then order the 2026 developments by month.
74.sec: Universal angles

75.s: The idea of an Ombudsman originated in which country in 1809?
75.x: The Ombudsman institution originated in Sweden in 1809.
75.tq: Directly identify the country associated with the origin of an institution.
75.sec: Lokpal Bill history - first introduction, attempts, year passed, Anna Hazare movement

75.s: Who coined the term ‘Lokpal’?
75.x: The word ‘Lokpal’ was coined by Dr. L.M. Singhvi.
75.tq: Test the person associated with the exact origin of a term.
75.sec: Lokpal Bill history - first introduction, attempts, year passed, Anna Hazare movement

75.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the history of the Lokpal Bill:
1. The First Lokpal Bill was passed by the Lok Sabha in 1969.
2. The Bill lapsed when the concerned Lok Sabha was dissolved.
3. The Bill was first introduced in the Rajya Sabha in 1968.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
75.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the First Lokpal Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha, not the Rajya Sabha.
75.tq: Separate the House of introduction from the House of passage and identify the wrong House.
75.sec: Lokpal Bill history - first introduction, attempts, year passed, Anna Hazare movement

75.s: Which one of the following years was NOT among the years in which the Lokpal Bill was re-introduced after 1969?
75.x: The Bill was re-introduced in 1971, 1977, 1985, 1989, 1996, 1998, 2001, 2005 and 2008. The year 1992 was not among these years.
75.tq: Find the year that does not belong to a stated sequence of legislative attempts.
75.sec: Lokpal Bill history - first introduction, attempts, year passed, Anna Hazare movement

75.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Lokpal Bill passed by the Lok Sabha in 1969
B. Re-introduction of the Bill in 2008
C. Introduction of the First Lokpal Bill
D. Parliament passed the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Bill in December 2013
75.x: The correct order is introduction in 1968, passage by the Lok Sabha in 1969, re-introduction in 2008, and passage by Parliament in December 2013.
75.tq: Use the first and last events, then place the intermediate legislative attempt.
75.sec: Lokpal Bill history - first introduction, attempts, year passed, Anna Hazare movement

75.s:
With reference to the Lokpal Bill, 2011, consider the following statements:
1. It was introduced in the Lok Sabha in August 2011.
2. It was examined by a Standing Committee chaired by Abhishek Manu Singhvi in late 2011.
3. The new Bill was passed by the Lok Sabha on 27 December 2011.
4. The Rajya Sabha debate on the Bill was completed in December 2011 without reference to a Select Committee.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
75.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the Rajya Sabha debate remained unfinished and the Bill was sent to a Rajya Sabha Select Committee.
75.tq: Spot the false statement by checking the legislative procedure and its completion status.
75.sec: Lokpal Bill history - first introduction, attempts, year passed, Anna Hazare movement

75.s: Which of the following correctly represents the sequence of parliamentary passage of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013?
o: Lok Sabha on 17 December 2013 and Rajya Sabha on 18 December 2013
Rajya Sabha on 17 December 2013 and Lok Sabha on 18 December 2013
Lok Sabha on 27 December 2011 and Rajya Sabha on 16 January 2014
75.x: The Rajya Sabha passed the Bill with amendments on 17 December 2013, and the Lok Sabha passed it on 18 December 2013.
75.tq: Read the two House dates carefully and avoid reversing the order of passage.
75.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

75.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the dates associated with the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013?
o: Assent was given on 1 January 2014 and the Act came into force on 16 January 2014.
Assent was given on 16 January 2014 and the Act came into force on 1 January 2014.
Both assent and commencement took place on 1 January 2014.
Both assent and commencement took place on 16 January 2014.
75.x: The President gave assent on 1 January 2014, while the Act came into force on 16 January 2014.
75.tq: Discriminate between two closely related dates by matching each date with its legal event.
75.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

75.s: The Lokpal actually began functioning on:
75.x: Although the Act came into force in 2014, the Lokpal began functioning on 27 March 2019 after its Chairperson and members were appointed.
75.tq: Distinguish commencement of an Act from the date on which an institution began functioning.
75.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

75.s:
Consider the following statements about the Lokpal:
1. It is a statutory body.
2. It is a constitutional body created directly by the Constitution.
3. Its composition may include a Chairperson and up to eight members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
75.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The Lokpal is established by statute and is not a constitutional body.
75.tq: Use the statutory-versus-constitutional distinction and test the numerical composition separately.
75.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

75.s: Which of the following is a correct feature of the composition of the Lokpal?
o: At least 75 per cent of the members must be elected MPs.
All members must be serving judges of the Supreme Court.
At least 50 per cent of the members must belong to SCs, STs, OBCs, minorities or be women.
The Chairperson and every member must be a serving MLA.
75.x: The Lokpal must have not less than 50 per cent representation from SCs, STs, OBCs, minorities and women. Its members need not all be serving judges or legislators.
75.tq: Test a composition requirement through the exact minimum-percentage qualification.
75.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

75.s: Who among the following can be appointed as Chairperson of the Lokpal?
o: Only the serving Speaker of the Lok Sabha
Only a retired Chief Minister of a State
A former Chief Justice of India, a sitting or former Supreme Court judge, or an eminent person
Only a sitting Chief Justice of India
75.x: The Chairperson may be a former Chief Justice of India, a sitting or former Supreme Court judge, or an eminent person.
75.tq: Identify the alternatives in an eligibility list without treating one category as exclusive.
75.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

75.s: Which of the following persons is NOT a member of the Selection Committee for appointment of the Lokpal?
o: Chief Justice of India or a Supreme Court judge nominated by the Chief Justice of India
75.x: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is not a member of the Lokpal Selection Committee. The committee includes the Prime Minister, Lok Sabha Speaker, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, the CJI or nominee, and an eminent jurist.
75.tq: Use the membership trap involving the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha and the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
75.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

75.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Selection Committee of the Lokpal:
1. The Prime Minister is its Chairperson.
2. The Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha is a member.
3. One eminent jurist is nominated by the President on the recommendation of the other members.
4. The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is its ex officio member.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
75.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is not a member of the Selection Committee.
75.tq: Identify the incorrect member by comparing the two presiding officers of Parliament.
75.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

75.s:
With reference to the Search Committee constituted for the Lokpal, consider the following statements:
1. It is set up by the Selection Committee.
2. It prepares a panel for consideration.
3. It must have at least seven persons.
4. At least half of its members must be from SCs, STs, OBCs, minorities and women.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
75.x: All four statements are correct. The Search Committee is constituted by the Selection Committee, prepares a panel, has at least seven persons and must satisfy the specified representation requirement.
75.tq: Check each component of a statutory committee’s constitution and functions.
75.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

75.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the jurisdiction of the Lokpal?
o: Central officials of Groups A, B, C and D — Group C and D complaints are referred to the CVC
Members of Parliament — all speeches and votes in Parliament are subject to inquiry
NGOs — covered only when they receive foreign contribution below ₹10 lakh
Indian public servants abroad — excluded because jurisdiction ends outside India
75.x: The Lokpal’s jurisdiction covers central officials of Groups A, B, C and D, while complaints against Group C and D officials are sent to the CVC, which reports back to the Lokpal. Parliamentary speeches and votes are excluded, NGOs are covered above the stated threshold, and public servants outside India are included.
75.tq: Separate closely related jurisdictional exceptions and administrative routes.
75.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

75.s: Which of the following categories of organisations comes within the Lokpal’s jurisdiction when the stated condition is fulfilled?
o: Only organisations receiving domestic donations above ₹10 lakh
Only constitutional bodies receiving no government funding
Every private company, irrespective of funding
NGOs, trusts and societies receiving foreign contributions above ₹10 lakh
75.x: NGOs, trusts and societies receiving foreign contributions above ₹10 lakh come within the stated jurisdiction of the Lokpal.
75.tq: Focus on both the organisation category and the exact monetary threshold.
75.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

75.s:
The jurisdiction of the Lokpal over the Prime Minister is subject to which of the following exclusions?
1. International relations
2. Security
3. Public order
4. Atomic energy and space
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
75.x: The Prime Minister’s excluded areas include international relations, external and internal security, public order, atomic energy and space. Therefore, all four listed categories are covered by the exclusions.
75.tq: Group several statutory exceptions together and check whether any listed category falls outside them.
75.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

75.s: An allegation against the Prime Minister relates to a matter not covered by the statutory exclusions. Which condition is required for an inquiry by the Lokpal?
o: Approval by the Union Cabinet through an open hearing
Prior approval of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha alone
Approval by the full Bench with at least a two-thirds majority, with the proceedings held in camera
Approval by a simple majority of any two members, in public proceedings
75.x: An inquiry against the Prime Minister requires approval of the full Bench by at least a two-thirds majority, and the inquiry is held in camera.
75.tq: Apply the special procedural safeguards to a concrete jurisdictional situation.
75.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

75.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the jurisdiction of the Lokpal:
1. It extends to Union Ministers and Members of Parliament.
2. It covers anything said or any vote given by an MP in Parliament.
3. It applies to Indian public servants both within and outside India.
4. It covers bodies established by an Act of Parliament or funded by the government.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
75.x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is false because anything said or any vote given by an MP in Parliament is outside the Lokpal’s jurisdiction.
75.tq: Use the parliamentary speech-and-vote exception to reject an otherwise broad jurisdiction statement.
75.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

75.s: A complaint is filed before the Lokpal against a Central Government employee belonging to Group D. What is the prescribed route mentioned in the Act’s working arrangement?
o: The complaint is transferred to the State Lokayukta.
The complaint goes to the Central Vigilance Commission, which reports back to the Lokpal.
The complaint is sent to the Election Commission of India.
The complaint is automatically dismissed for lack of jurisdiction.
75.x: Complaints against central officials in Groups C and D go to the Central Vigilance Commission, which reports back to the Lokpal.
75.tq: Identify the correct authority by following the special referral arrangement for lower groups of officials.
75.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

75.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Lokpal is correct?
o: The Lokpal may inquire into a complaint filed at any time after the alleged offence.
A Chairperson or member of the Lokpal may simultaneously be an MP or MLA.
The Act applies only to public servants posted within India.
A Chairperson or member of the Lokpal cannot be an MP or MLA.
75.x: A Chairperson or member of the Lokpal cannot be a Member of Parliament or a Member of a Legislative Assembly. The Act also covers public servants outside India and bars complaints filed after seven years from the alleged offence.
75.tq: Reject the option that reverses an eligibility restriction while checking related jurisdictional limits.
75.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

75.s: A complaint is made seven years after the alleged offence. Under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, the Lokpal:
o: can inquire only if the complaint concerns a Union Minister
cannot inquire into it after the statutory seven-year period
can inquire only after approval of the Rajya Sabha Chairman
must inquire into it because there is no limitation period
75.x: The Lokpal cannot inquire into a complaint made after seven years from the alleged offence.
75.tq: Apply the statutory time limit to a filing scenario.
75.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

75.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: 2016 amendment — creation of the Lokpal Selection Committee
DSPE Act amendment — abolition of the Directorate of Prosecution
2013 Act — exclusion of all Group C and D officials from every vigilance process
75.x: The 2016 amendment to the Lokpal law dealt with asset declarations. The Act also amended the DSPE Act in relation to the CBI Director’s committee and a Directorate of Prosecution.
75.tq: Match a specific amendment with its subject while rejecting broader invented consequences.
75.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

75.s: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act required every State to establish a Lokayukta within:
o: Six months of the Act’s assent
Two years of the first Lokpal appointment
One year of the commencement of the Act
Five years of the establishment of the Central Vigilance Commission
75.x: Every State was required to set up a Lokayukta within one year of the commencement of the Act.
75.tq: Test the exact time limit and its starting point.
75.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

75.s: The Lokayukta in a State is generally appointed by the
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
75.x: The Lokayukta is appointed by the Governor under the respective State's Lokayukta Act.
75.tq: Identify the authority legally associated with the appointment.
75.sec: Lokayukta - first state, appointing authority, tenure changes, CM within ambit

75.s:
While appointing a Lokayukta, the Governor generally consults which of the following?
1. Chief Justice of the High Court
2. Leader of the Opposition
3. Chief Election Commissioner
Which of the statements given above are correct?
75.x: The Governor generally consults the Chief Justice of the High Court and the Leader of the Opposition. The Chief Election Commissioner is not part of this consultation process.
75.tq: Separate the prescribed consultation authorities from an unrelated constitutional authority.
75.sec: Lokayukta - first state, appointing authority, tenure changes, CM within ambit

75.s: The annual consolidated report of a State Lokayukta is submitted to the
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
75.x: The Lokayukta submits an annual consolidated report to the Governor.
75.tq: Test the reporting relationship by identifying the constitutional recipient.
75.sec: Lokayukta - first state, appointing authority, tenure changes, CM within ambit

75.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the working of Lokayuktas:
1. A Lokayukta generally relies on State investigating agencies for inquiries.
2. Recommendations of Lokayuktas are advisory in many States.
3. Recommendations are binding in every State.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
75.x: Lokayuktas generally rely on State investigating agencies, and their recommendations are advisory in many States. They are not binding in every State, though they are binding in some States.
75.tq: Find the statement using an absolute word and distinguish general practice from an exception.
75.sec: Lokayukta - first state, appointing authority, tenure changes, CM within ambit

75.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Structure — States
o: Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta — Rajasthan, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra
Officials designated as Lokpal — Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Himachal Pradesh
Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta — Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Himachal Pradesh
75.x: Rajasthan, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra have both a Lokayukta and a Upa-Lokayukta. Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Himachal Pradesh have only a Lokayukta, while Punjab and Odisha designate officials as Lokpal.
75.tq: Start from the sure structure–State combination and eliminate swapped groups.
75.sec: Lokayukta - first state, appointing authority, tenure changes, CM within ambit

75.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I (State)

a. Bihar
b. Uttar Pradesh
c. Punjab
 d. Maharashtra

List-II (Institutional arrangement)
 i. Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta
 ii. Lokayukta only
 iii. Officials designated as Lokpal
75.x: Bihar and Uttar Pradesh have only a Lokayukta; Punjab has officials designated as Lokpal; Maharashtra has a Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta.
75.tq: Use the repeated institutional pattern to match each State without relying on chronology.
75.sec: Lokayukta - first state, appointing authority, tenure changes, CM within ambit

75.s: Which one of the following States does NOT require a judicial qualification for appointment as Lokayukta, according to the listed State-wise pattern?
75.x: Judicial qualification is required in Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Assam. It is not required in Maharashtra, Bihar or Rajasthan under the listed pattern.
75.tq: Find the exception by comparing the judicial-qualification groups.
75.sec: Lokayukta - first state, appointing authority, tenure changes, CM within ambit

75.s:
Which of the following States is included among those requiring a judicial qualification for the Lokayukta?
1. Uttar Pradesh
2. Himachal Pradesh
3. Rajasthan
4. Gujarat
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
75.x: Judicial qualification is required in Uttar Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh and Gujarat. Rajasthan is among the States where it is not required.
75.tq: Classify the States into judicial-qualification and non-qualification groups.
75.sec: Lokayukta - first state, appointing authority, tenure changes, CM within ambit

75.s: The term of the newly appointed Lokayukta in Andhra Pradesh is
75.x: The new Lokayukta of Andhra Pradesh has a five-year term.
75.tq: Distinguish the State-specific tenure from other tenure figures.
75.sec: Lokayukta - first state, appointing authority, tenure changes, CM within ambit

75.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the uniformity of Lokayukta institutions in India?
o: All States follow an identical Act and identical jurisdiction.
The Chief Justice of India determines the jurisdiction of every Lokayukta.
Each State establishes the institution under its own Lokayukta Act, resulting in differences in jurisdiction and coverage.
The Union Government appoints all Lokayuktas under one central law.
75.x: Lokayuktas are established under the respective State Acts, and there is no uniformity among States regarding jurisdiction, coverage of the Chief Minister or judicial qualifications.
75.tq: Reject the absolute uniformity claim and apply the federal institutional arrangement.
75.sec: Lokayukta - first state, appointing authority, tenure changes, CM within ambit

75.s: Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose, the first Lokpal of India, left office on
75.x: Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose left office on 27 May 2022.
75.tq: Discriminate between the dates of appointment, functioning, departure and later events.
75.sec: Lokpal working - first Lokpal, chairpersons, complaints, prosecution wing

75.s: Who has been the second Chairperson of the Lokpal since 10 March 2024?
75.x: Justice Ajay Manikrao Khanwilkar, a retired Supreme Court judge, became the second Chairperson of the Lokpal on 10 March 2024.
75.tq: Distinguish the Chairperson from the judicial members of the bench.
75.sec: Lokpal working - first Lokpal, chairpersons, complaints, prosecution wing

75.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the composition of the Lokpal:
1. The Chairperson may be a former Chief Justice of India or a former Supreme Court judge.
2. An eminent person with 25 years' experience in specified fields may be eligible to be Chairperson.
3. The Chairperson must necessarily be a serving judge of the Supreme Court.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
75.x: A former Chief Justice of India, former Supreme Court judge, or an eminent person with 25 years' relevant experience may qualify. The Chairperson need not be a serving Supreme Court judge.
75.tq: Identify the false restrictive qualification created by the word 'necessarily'.
75.sec: Lokpal working - first Lokpal, chairpersons, complaints, prosecution wing

75.s: Under the Lokpal framework, which combination correctly states the two representation requirements for members?
o: At least 50% judicial members and at least 50% representation from SC, ST, OBC, minorities and women
At least 50% judicial members and at least 25% representation from specified social groups and women
