83.s: Under the proviso to Article 164(1), a Minister in charge of tribal welfare must be appointed in which group of States?
o: Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha
Jharkhand, Odisha, Telangana and West Bengal
Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan
83.x: The States specified are Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha. The Minister may also be placed in charge of SC and BC welfare.
83.tq: Use a State-list question with a historically changed State as the trap.
83.sec: Article 164(1) proviso - tribal welfare minister

83.s: Which constitutional amendment removed Bihar and added Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh from the States requiring a tribal welfare Minister under Article 164(1)?
83.x: The 94th Amendment Act, 2006 removed Bihar and added Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh to the relevant provision.
83.tq: Match the constitutional change with its exact amendment year and number.
83.sec: Article 164(1) proviso - tribal welfare minister

83.s: Who notifies the Scheduled Tribes for a State or Union Territory under Article 342?
o: The Union Council of Ministers by executive order
The Parliament after consultation with the Governor
The President after consultation with the Governor
The Governor after consultation with the President
83.x: The President specifies the Scheduled Tribes for a State or Union Territory after consultation with the Governor of the concerned State, through the Constitutional Scheduled Tribes Order, 1950.
83.tq: Ask who performs the constitutional notification function and who is consulted.
83.sec: Article 342 - notification of STs; religion

83.s: After the initial notification under Article 342, inclusion in or exclusion from the list of Scheduled Tribes can be made only by:
o: The President through a fresh notification
The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes by recommendation
83.x: Subsequent inclusion or exclusion of communities from the Scheduled Tribe list requires a law made by Parliament.
83.tq: Distinguish the original notifying authority from the authority competent to alter the list later.
83.sec: Article 342 - notification of STs; religion

83.s: Article 366(25) defines Scheduled Tribes with reference to communities deemed to be Scheduled Tribes under which Article?
83.x: Article 366(25) refers to communities deemed to be Scheduled Tribes under Article 342.
83.tq: Separate the definitional provision from the provisions dealing with reservation and commissions.
83.sec: Article 342 - notification of STs; religion

83.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes Scheduled Tribe status from Scheduled Caste status?
o: Scheduled Tribe status is religion-neutral, whereas Scheduled Caste status is restricted to Hindus, Sikhs and Buddhists.
Scheduled Tribe status is restricted to Hindus, while Scheduled Caste status is religion-neutral.
Both statuses are restricted exclusively to persons professing Hinduism.
Both statuses are determined solely by the religion of the individual.
83.x: Scheduled Tribe status is religion-neutral. Scheduled Caste status is restricted to persons belonging to Hindu, Sikh or Buddhist communities under the relevant constitutional orders.
83.tq: Test a frequently confused distinction by reversing the qualifying conditions in the distractors.
83.sec: Article 342 - notification of STs; religion

83.s: The Kalelkar Commission noted that tribal communities may belong to:
83.x: The Kalelkar Commission observed that tribes may belong to any religion, supporting the religion-neutral character of Scheduled Tribe status.
83.tq: Use the exact scope of a commission’s observation instead of a familiar SC-related limitation.
83.sec: Article 342 - notification of STs; religion

83.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the identification traits associated with the Lokur Committee, 1965?
83.x: The traits include primitive traits, distinctive culture, geographical isolation, shyness of contact and backwardness. Advanced urbanisation is not one of them.
83.tq: Find the odd characteristic among a recognised list of identification traits.
83.sec: Article 342 - notification of STs; religion

83.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Scheduled Tribes of India:
1. There are 705 notified ethnic groups.
2. Scheduled Tribes constitute 8.6 per cent of the population.
3. They reside on 15 per cent of the geographical area.
4. Madhya Pradesh has the largest tribal population.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
83.x: The stated figures are 705 notified ethnic groups, 10.45 crore persons, 8.6 per cent of the population and residence over 15 per cent of the area; Madhya Pradesh has the largest tribal population.
83.tq: Combine demographic figures and the leading State in one coded statement question.
83.sec: Article 342 - notification of STs; religion

83.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
83.x: Bhil is the largest tribe. Madhya Pradesh has the largest tribal population, 705 ethnic groups are notified, and Scheduled Tribes constitute 8.6 per cent of the population.
83.tq: Use a correctly matched pair question to separate similar demographic figures and rankings.
83.sec: Article 342 - notification of STs; religion

83.s: Scheduled Tribes have not been notified in which of the following groups of States and Union Territories?
o: Delhi, Punjab, Haryana, Puducherry and Chandigarh
Punjab, Gujarat, Haryana, Goa and Chandigarh
Delhi, Punjab, Himachal Pradesh, Puducherry and Chandigarh
Delhi, Rajasthan, Haryana, Puducherry and Chandigarh
83.x: No Scheduled Tribe has been notified in Delhi, Punjab, Haryana, Puducherry or Chandigarh.
83.tq: Test an exact exclusion list and trap it with neighbouring regions having tribal populations.
83.sec: Article 342 - notification of STs; religion

83.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Article — Subject
o: Article 46 — Educational and economic interests of SCs and STs
Article 342 — National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
83.x: Article 46 concerns the educational and economic interests of SCs and STs. Article 342 concerns notification of STs, Article 338A establishes the NCST, and Article 275(1) concerns grants-in-aid.
83.tq: Start with the sure Article–subject pair and eliminate swapped constitutional provisions.
83.sec: Articles number game for STs

83.s:
Which of the following combinations is correctly matched?

1. Article 15(4) and Article 16(4) — Special provisions and reservation in posts
2. Article 244(1) — Fifth Schedule administration
3. Article 244(2) — Sixth Schedule administration
4. Article 244A — Autonomous State within Assam
83.x: All four pairings are correct. Article 244A provides for an Autonomous State within Assam and was inserted by the 22nd Amendment in 1969.
83.tq: Test a sequence of closely numbered Articles by matching each with its subject.
83.sec: Articles number game for STs

83.s: The provision for grants-in-aid for ST welfare and for raising the level of administration of Scheduled Areas is contained in:
83.x: Article 275(1) provides grants-in-aid for ST welfare and for raising the level of administration of Scheduled Areas, including funds associated with the Tribal Sub-Plan.
83.tq: Identify the exact Article associated with a financial and administrative support function.
83.sec: Articles number game for STs

83.s: Articles 330 and 332 respectively relate to reservation of seats for Scheduled Tribes in the:
o: Rajya Sabha and State Legislative Councils
State Legislative Assemblies and Lok Sabha
Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies
83.x: Article 330 concerns reservation of seats for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha, while Article 332 concerns such reservation in State Legislative Assemblies.
83.tq: Discriminate between two neighbouring reservation Articles by comparing their institutions.
83.sec: Articles number game for STs

83.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Article 338A — National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
Article 339 — President’s Commission on Scheduled Areas and Union directions on ST schemes
83.x: Article 244A provides for an Autonomous State within Assam. Grants-in-aid for ST welfare are provided under Article 275(1).
83.tq: Locate the swapped Article–subject pair among closely related tribal provisions.
83.sec: Articles number game for STs

83.s: Which of the following is NOT an area of special focus associated with the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes?
o: Regulation of inter-State trade in agricultural commodities
83.x: The Commission focuses on minor forest produce, mineral and water rights, and rehabilitation of displaced tribals. Regulation of inter-State agricultural trade is not listed as this special focus.
83.tq: Identify the unrelated function among several functions linked to tribal safeguards.
83.sec: Article 338A - National Commission for Scheduled Tribes

83.s: In relation to implementation of the Forest Rights Act, the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes invoked its powers to requisition reports from:
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
83.x: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes requisitioned reports on Forest Rights Act implementation from the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
83.tq: Identify the concerned ministry from the subject matter of the statutory implementation report.
83.sec: Article 338A - National Commission for Scheduled Tribes

83.s: The 30th anniversary of the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996, was marked by which event hosted in Andhra Pradesh?
83.x: The 30th anniversary of PESA was marked by the PESA Mahotsav hosted in Visakhapatnam.
83.tq: Use the event-location association to distinguish closely related tribal-governance programmes.
83.sec: Universal angles

83.s:
Which of the following initiatives has been associated with the Ministry of Panchayati Raj in connection with the implementation of PESA?
1. Setting up of a PESA Cell
2. Training of more than one lakh representatives
3. Launch of the PESA-GPDP portal
4. Creation of autonomous district councils in all Fifth Schedule States
Which of the statements given above are correct?
83.x: The Ministry of Panchayati Raj set up a PESA Cell, trained more than one lakh representatives and launched the PESA-GPDP portal. Creation of autonomous district councils in all Fifth Schedule States is not part of these initiatives.
83.tq: Find the statement that wrongly transfers a Sixth Schedule institution to Fifth Schedule areas.
83.sec: Universal angles

83.s: With reference to PESA, which one of the following correctly describes its institutional approach to tribal self-rule?
o: The autonomous district council is the mandatory institution in every PESA area.
The Tribal Advisory Council replaces every Gram Sabha in Scheduled Areas.
The Governor is the sole nucleus of self-rule in Scheduled Areas.
The Gram Sabha is the nucleus of self-rule, rather than the Panchayat as an institution alone.
83.x: PESA places the Gram Sabha at the centre of self-rule in Scheduled Areas. Autonomous district councils are associated with the Sixth Schedule and are not mandatory in every PESA area.
83.tq: Discriminate between the Gram Sabha-centred PESA model and the council-centred Sixth Schedule model.
83.sec: Universal angles

83.s: The Scheduled Tribe population covered by PESA is approximately what proportion of India's population?
83.x: PESA covers Scheduled Tribe populations constituting approximately 8.6 percent of India's population.
83.tq: Identify the precise percentage rather than relying on approximate scale comparisons.
83.sec: Universal angles

83.s: In the Rampachodavaram agency area of Andhra Pradesh, the PESA Committee is associated with approval of which of the following?
o: The list of middlemen permitted to trade annatto seeds
The list of autonomous district councils permitted to collect forest revenue
The list of political parties permitted to contest Panchayat elections
The list of contractors permitted to mine minor minerals
83.x: In the Rampachodavaram agency area, the PESA Committee approves which middlemen may trade annatto seeds.
83.tq: Apply the institutional role to a concrete local-governance scenario.
83.sec: Universal angles

83.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the implementation of PESA:
1. The criticism that consultation is not consent questions whether consultation alone adequately protects tribal decision-making.
2. Provisions relating to minor minerals and minor forest produce are among the least implemented.
3. Gram Sabha consent is always obtained before land acquisition in PESA areas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
83.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because Gram Sabha consent has been reported as being ignored in land acquisition in some PESA areas.
83.tq: Spot the absolute word in a statement that contradicts a documented implementation criticism.
83.sec: Universal angles

83.s: Which of the following is identified as a criticism of the functioning of the Fifth Schedule framework?
o: Fifth Schedule States are required to establish Sixth Schedule autonomous councils.
Tribal Advisory Councils rarely meet and Governors rarely use their Fifth Schedule powers.
Governors have no role whatsoever under the Fifth Schedule.
Tribal Advisory Councils are constitutionally prohibited from meeting in Scheduled Areas.
83.x: The functioning of the Fifth Schedule has been criticised because Tribal Advisory Councils rarely meet and Governors rarely exercise their Fifth Schedule powers.
83.tq: Reject statements that convert limited or infrequent exercise of a power into complete constitutional absence.
83.sec: Universal angles

83.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the Fifth Schedule from the Sixth Schedule?
o: The Fifth Schedule provides autonomous district councils in all States, whereas the Sixth Schedule deals only with PESA.
The Fifth Schedule involves the Governor, Tribal Advisory Councils and PESA, whereas the Sixth Schedule provides for autonomous district councils in specified north-eastern States.
The Sixth Schedule applies to Andhra Pradesh's agency areas, whereas the Fifth Schedule applies only to Ladakh.
Both Schedules establish identical systems of tribal self-governance throughout India.
83.x: The Fifth Schedule framework involves the Governor, Tribal Advisory Councils and PESA, while the Sixth Schedule provides autonomous district councils in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.
83.tq: Compare the governing institution and territorial application before choosing the correct pair.
83.sec: Universal angles

83.s: The Sixth Schedule demands from Ladakh represent a demand for which type of constitutional arrangement?
o: Transfer of all Scheduled Area powers to Parliament
Abolition of all Tribal Advisory Councils in Fifth Schedule States
A framework of autonomous tribal self-governance comparable to the Sixth Schedule
Extension of PESA exclusively to urban municipalities
83.x: The demand from Ladakh is for a Sixth Schedule-type arrangement providing stronger autonomous tribal self-governance.
83.tq: Infer the institutional demand from the constitutional model named in the issue.
83.sec: Universal angles

83.s: An interim proposal concerning Assam suggested which of the following classifications for Scheduled Tribes?
o: ST Plains, ST Hills and new ST Valley
ST Hills, ST Valleys and ST Autonomous Councils
ST Plains, ST Forests and ST Islands
ST Valley, ST Coast and ST Frontier
83.x: The proposed three-tier classification was ST Plains, ST Hills and new ST Valley.
83.tq: Recall the exact three-part classification and avoid substituting familiar geographical categories.
83.sec: Universal angles

83.s: The CPI(M)'s opposition in Andhra Pradesh was directed against the Centre's approval of mining surveys in Agency areas without which of the following?
o: PESA Gram Sabha consent and Tribal Advisory Council consultation
Approval of the Election Commission and Finance Commission
Sixth Schedule approval and Lok Sabha consent
Municipal council permission and Governor's ordinance
83.x: The objection was that mining surveys in AP's Agency areas were approved without PESA Gram Sabha consent and consultation with the Tribal Advisory Council.
83.tq: Identify the two omitted tribal-governance safeguards rather than unrelated constitutional approvals.
83.sec: Universal angles

83.s: Parasnath Hills, also known as Marang Buru, has been associated with competing claims under the Fifth Schedule by which communities?
o: Todas and Todas of the Nilgiris
83.x: The issue concerning Parasnath Hills or Marang Buru involves competing Jain and Santhal claims under the Fifth Schedule context.
83.tq: Discriminate between communities linked to the same contested tribal-cultural site.
83.sec: Universal angles

83.s:
Which of the following statements about Andhra Pradesh and the Fifth Schedule is correct?
1. Andhra Pradesh's Scheduled Areas are the old Agency tracts.
2. Andhra Pradesh is one of the ten Fifth Schedule States.
3. Araku is an Andhra Pradesh Scheduled Tribe Lok Sabha constituency.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
83.x: All three statements are correct. AP's Scheduled Areas correspond to the old Agency tracts, AP is among the ten Fifth Schedule States, and Araku is an ST Lok Sabha seat.
83.tq: Check the State-specific territorial, numerical and electoral facts together.
83.sec: Universal angles

83.s: Which of the following best reflects the post-Maoism policy concern regarding PESA?
o: A decision to suspend Gram Sabha functioning in Agency areas
A proposal to replace PESA with the Sixth Schedule throughout India
A policy to remove all tribal representation from local bodies
A push to implement PESA in earnest in affected areas
83.x: A post-Maoism policy discussion has emphasised the need to implement PESA in earnest rather than abandon its Gram Sabha-centred framework.
83.tq: Choose the policy response that follows the stated governance concern, not an extreme institutional replacement.
83.sec: Universal angles

84.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Urban Local Bodies in Andhra Pradesh according to the APSES 2025–26 figures:
1. There are 17 Municipal Corporations.
2. There are 76 Municipalities.
3. There are 30 Nagar Panchayats.
4. The total number of Urban Local Bodies is 123.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
84.x: All four statements are correct: 17 Corporations, 76 Municipalities and 30 Nagar Panchayats make a total of 123 Urban Local Bodies.
84.tq: Check each numerical statement against the table before selecting the complete combination.
84.sec: Urban local bodies in AP - numbers and upgradations

84.s: The APSES 2024–25 figures recorded which of the following combinations for Urban Local Bodies in Andhra Pradesh?
84.x: The APSES 2024–25 figures recorded 17 Municipal Corporations and 79 Municipalities within the total of 123 Urban Local Bodies.
84.tq: Compare the year attached to the figures instead of treating changing counts as permanent facts.
84.sec: Urban local bodies in AP - numbers and upgradations

84.s:
With reference to Urban Local Bodies in Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. Elections are due in 100 of the 123 Urban Local Bodies.
2. The remaining 23 Urban Local Bodies are involved in court cases.
3. The proposed merger of 23 Municipalities is to be taken up before the elections.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
84.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The proposed merger of 23 Municipalities has been deferred until after the elections, so statement 3 is false.
84.tq: Watch for the time-sequence trap in the phrase ‘before the elections’.
84.sec: Urban local bodies in AP - numbers and upgradations

84.s: The proposed merger of 23 Municipalities in Andhra Pradesh has been deferred until:
o: the completion of the delimitation process
the constitution of a new State Election Commission
the publication of the next Census
84.x: The proposed merger has been deferred until after the elections.
84.tq: Identify the exact stage at which the administrative action is scheduled to occur.
84.sec: Urban local bodies in AP - numbers and upgradations

84.s: The State Election Commission of Andhra Pradesh has notified electoral rolls for how many Urban Local Bodies?
84.x: Electoral rolls have been notified for 41 Urban Local Bodies.
84.tq: Separate the number of bodies with notified rolls from the total number of Urban Local Bodies.
84.sec: Urban local bodies in AP - numbers and upgradations

84.s: The 41 Urban Local Bodies for which electoral rolls were notified comprise:
84.x: The notified rolls cover 12 Corporations and 29 Municipalities or Nagar Panchayats, together making 41 Urban Local Bodies.
84.tq: Split the total into its two stated components before choosing the combination.
84.sec: Urban local bodies in AP - numbers and upgradations

84.s: The electoral rolls notified for 41 Urban Local Bodies in Andhra Pradesh are due on:
84.x: The electoral rolls are due on 22 September 2026.
84.tq: Distinguish the publication or reporting date from the date on which the rolls are due.
84.sec: Urban local bodies in AP - numbers and upgradations

84.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
84.x: Proddatur is included among the Municipalities or Nagar Panchayats for which rolls were notified; it is not listed as a named Municipal Corporation in this context. Greater Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Tirupati are named Corporations.
84.tq: Find the location or classification mismatch among closely related urban bodies.
84.sec: Urban local bodies in AP - numbers and upgradations

84.s: The nodal agency for all 123 Urban Local Bodies in Andhra Pradesh is the:
o: Municipal Administration and Urban Development Department
84.x: The Municipal Administration and Urban Development Department is the nodal agency for all 123 Urban Local Bodies.
84.tq: Apply the ‘which department handles this subject?’ method to identify the nodal authority.
84.sec: Urban local bodies in AP - numbers and upgradations

84.s: Which of the following places is NOT included among the named Municipal Corporations in recent reports?
84.x: Nandyal is mentioned among the Municipalities or Nagar Panchayats, whereas Kurnool, Guntur and Vijayawada are named Municipal Corporations.
84.tq: Classify each place by its urban-body category rather than by name recognition alone.
84.sec: Urban local bodies in AP - numbers and upgradations

84.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the Sarpanch from the Panchayat Secretary in Andhra Pradesh?
o: The Sarpanch is the elected political head, while the Panchayat Secretary is the executive functionary.
The Sarpanch is the executive functionary, while the Secretary is the elected political head.
Both are appointed executive functionaries of the State Government.
Both are directly elected by the Gram Sabha.
84.x: The Sarpanch is the elected political head of the Gram Panchayat, whereas the Panchayat Secretary is the executive functionary responsible for administration.
84.tq: Separate political leadership from administrative execution in local government.
84.sec: Gram Panchayat working - meetings, execution, functions, Marriage Officer

84.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the Sarpanch of a Gram Panchayat is:
o: elected indirectly by the Panchayat Secretary
84.x: The Sarpanch is directly elected by the voters in Andhra Pradesh.
84.tq: Identify the mode of election of the village-level chairperson, which is left to State legislation.
84.sec: Gram Panchayat working - meetings, execution, functions, Marriage Officer

84.s: Which of the following is an obligatory function of a Gram Panchayat?
84.x: Sanitation, drinking water, drains, street lighting, village roads and burial grounds are obligatory functions. Tree planting, libraries and markets are examples of discretionary functions.
84.tq: Classify the function according to whether the law makes it compulsory or dependent on available funds.
84.sec: Gram Panchayat working - meetings, execution, functions, Marriage Officer

84.s: Which one of the following is a discretionary function of a Gram Panchayat?
84.x: Tree planting is a discretionary function dependent on available funds. Village roads, street lighting and drains are obligatory functions.
84.tq: Find the function that depends on funds rather than being compulsory under the Act.
84.sec: Gram Panchayat working - meetings, execution, functions, Marriage Officer

84.s: The Gram Sabha consists of:
o: the Sarpanch and Panchayat Secretary alone
all elected members of the Gram Panchayat only
all government employees posted in the village
all registered voters of the Panchayat area
84.x: The Gram Sabha consists of all persons registered as voters in the area of the Panchayat.
84.tq: Distinguish the general body of registered voters from the elected Panchayat body.
84.sec: Gram Panchayat working - meetings, execution, functions, Marriage Officer

84.s:
With reference to the Gram Sabha, consider the following statements:
1. Article 243A recognises the Gram Sabha.
2. The powers and functions of the Gram Sabha are fixed by State law.
3. The Gram Sabha consists only of elected Panchayat representatives.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
84.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the Gram Sabha consists of all registered voters of the Panchayat area, not merely elected representatives.
84.tq: Reject the composition trap that substitutes elected representatives for all registered voters.
84.sec: Gram Panchayat working - meetings, execution, functions, Marriage Officer

84.s: Under Article 243C, the mode of election of the chairperson at the village level is left to the:
84.x: Article 243C leaves the mode of election of the village-level chairperson to the State Legislature. Chairpersons at the intermediate and district levels are elected indirectly.
84.tq: Identify which constitutional authority is empowered to determine the election method.
84.sec: Gram Panchayat working - meetings, execution, functions, Marriage Officer

84.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 243K — State Election Commission for local-body elections
Article 243A — Constitution of the State Election Commission
84.x: Article 243K provides the constitutional basis for the State Election Commission in relation to Panchayat elections; Article 243ZA relates to municipal elections.
84.tq: Match the constitutional article with its precise local-government subject.
84.sec: AP State Election Commission

84.s: The constitutional basis for the State Election Commission in relation to Municipal elections is provided by:
84.x: Article 243ZA provides the constitutional basis for the State Election Commission’s role in Municipal elections.
84.tq: Discriminate between the closely related constitutional provisions for Panchayats and Municipalities.
84.sec: AP State Election Commission

84.s: Which one of the following is NOT a function of the State Election Commission under Articles 243K and 243ZA?
o: Direction and control of electoral rolls
Appointment of all Sarpanches after elections
84.x: The State Election Commission supervises, directs and controls electoral rolls and local-body elections, including republication of Gram Panchayat rolls. It does not appoint Sarpanches after elections.
84.tq: Find the option that assigns an electoral authority a post-election appointment power.
84.sec: AP State Election Commission

84.s:
The functions of the Andhra Pradesh State Election Commission include:
1. Superintendence, direction and control of electoral rolls.
2. Conduct of elections to local bodies.
3. Rearrangement and republication of Gram Panchayat rolls.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
84.x: All three are functions of the State Election Commission under Articles 243K and 243ZA.
84.tq: Look for the complete set when every statement describes an electoral-roll or election-control function.
84.sec: AP State Election Commission

84.s: As provided in the stated reservation framework, the reservation for Backward Classes is:
o: 34% in rural local bodies and 33⅓% in Urban Local Bodies
33⅓% in rural local bodies and 34% in Urban Local Bodies
34% in both rural and Urban Local Bodies
50% in rural local bodies and 34% in Urban Local Bodies
84.x: The BC quota is 34% in rural bodies and 33⅓% in Urban Local Bodies. The SC/ST quotas remain unchanged.
84.tq: Compare the percentages by institutional setting and avoid reversing the two figures.
84.sec: AP State Election Commission

84.s: Which of the following statements regarding reservation in local bodies is correct?
o: Women’s reservation is fixed at exactly 50% in every State.
SC/ST seats are allotted without reference to population.
SC/ST seats are allotted in proportion to population and by rotation.
84.x: SC/ST reservation is provided in proportion to population, with seats allotted by rotation. Constitutional provision requires not less than one-third reservation for women, while many States have raised it to 50%.
84.tq: Separate the constitutional minimum for women from the population-based and rotational rule for SC/ST seats.
84.sec: AP State Election Commission

84.s: The Andhra Pradesh Municipalities Act, 1965 primarily governs which of the following?
84.x: The Andhra Pradesh Municipalities Act, 1965 governs Municipalities and Nagar Panchayats.
84.tq: Match the statute with the exact category of local bodies governed by it.
84.sec: AP municipal laws - Acts, Amendment Bills, Mayor election mode  [APPSC]

84.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the 33.33 per cent reservation for Backward Classes in Andhra Pradesh urban local bodies:
1. It is implemented under the Andhra Pradesh Municipal Corporations Act, 1994.
2. It is also implemented under the Andhra Pradesh Municipalities Act, 1965.
3. It is provided exclusively under the Panchayat Raj Act, 1994.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
84.x: The 33.33 per cent BC quota is implemented under the Andhra Pradesh Municipal Corporations Act, 1994 and the Andhra Pradesh Municipalities Act, 1965. It is not stated to be exclusively under the Panchayat Raj Act.
84.tq: Identify the correctly associated laws and reject the exclusive claim in statement 3.
84.sec: AP municipal laws - Acts, Amendment Bills, Mayor election mode  [APPSC]

84.s: Who introduced the Andhra Pradesh Municipal Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024?
o: The Chairperson of the Zilla Parishad
84.x: The Andhra Pradesh Municipal Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024 was introduced by Municipal Minister P. Narayana.
84.tq: Use the person–legislation association; APPSC commonly tests the minister responsible for introducing a Bill.
84.sec: AP municipal laws - Acts, Amendment Bills, Mayor election mode  [APPSC]

84.s:
Consider the following statements about the Andhra Pradesh Municipal Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024:
1. It was passed without debate in the Assembly.
2. It reversed an earlier amendment.
3. It restored the two-child restriction for municipal election candidates.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
84.x: The Bill was passed without debate and reversed an earlier amendment. It removed, rather than restored, the two-child restriction.
84.tq: Find the false statement by checking the direction of the legal change.
84.sec: AP municipal laws - Acts, Amendment Bills, Mayor election mode  [APPSC]

84.s: The principal purpose of the 2024 amendment relating to municipal elections in Andhra Pradesh was to:
o: Transfer municipal elections to the Union Election Commission
Remove the two-child norm for contesting municipal elections
Introduce direct election of all councillors
Create a new intermediate rural tier
84.x: The amendment removed the restriction that barred persons with more than two children from contesting municipal elections.
84.tq: Apply the stated legal purpose to identify the precise consequence of the amendment.
84.sec: AP municipal laws - Acts, Amendment Bills, Mayor election mode  [APPSC]

84.s: Which of the following correctly describes the companion legislative change relating to rural local bodies in Andhra Pradesh?
o: A companion Bill removed the two-child bar for panchayat elections in November 2024.
The Panchayat Raj Act was repealed in November 2024.
A companion Bill introduced a two-child bar for panchayat elections in November 2024.
The Bill transferred panchayat elections to municipalities.
84.x: A companion Bill removed the two-child bar on contesting panchayat elections in November 2024.
84.tq: Discriminate between removal and introduction of a qualification restriction.
84.sec: AP municipal laws - Acts, Amendment Bills, Mayor election mode  [APPSC]

84.s: The Andhra Pradesh Municipal Laws (Third Amendment) Bill, 2026 provides for:
o: A Uniform Mutation Fee on title transfers in municipal records
Direct election of Mandal Parishad Presidents
