84.x: The Amaravati Capital Region Development Authority was established under the APCRDA Act, 2014.
84.tq: Match the authority with its founding statute and year.
84.sec: Urban development authorities - APCRDA, VMRDA and others

84.s: The VMRDA is associated with the development of the:
84.x: VMRDA is the major Urban Development Authority associated with Visakhapatnam.
84.tq: Test the territorial association of an acronym-based authority.
84.sec: Urban development authorities - APCRDA, VMRDA and others

84.s: A uniform three-level mechanism for building checks and Occupancy Certificates in Andhra Pradesh covers:
o: Nagar Panchayats, municipalities, corporations and Urban Development Authorities
Only corporations and Urban Development Authorities
Only Gram Panchayats and Mandal Praja Parishads
84.x: The three-level uniform mechanism extends across Nagar Panchayats, municipalities, corporations and Urban Development Authorities.
84.tq: Test the complete coverage of a common regulatory mechanism.
84.sec: Urban development authorities - APCRDA, VMRDA and others

84.s: The incomplete devolution of which three elements is identified as a reason for Panchayati Raj Institutions continuing mainly as implementing agencies?
84.x: Incomplete devolution of the three Fs—Funds, Functions and Functionaries—limits Panchayati Raj Institutions and leaves them mainly as implementing agencies.
84.tq: Test the exact expansion of a commonly used three-term formulation.
84.sec: Universal angles

84.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with an Andhra Pradesh Panchayat and its 2026 award-related achievement?
o: Bokkasam Palem — first for women-friendly panchayats
84.x: Bokkasam Palem in Srikalahasti mandal of Tirupati stood first in the women-friendly panchayat category, while Sringavaram topped governance.
84.tq: Separate similar place names by matching each to its specific achievement.
84.sec: Universal angles

84.s: Sringavaram, in Andhra Pradesh, topped the category of:
84.x: Sringavaram in Visakhapatnam topped the governance category in the Deendayal Upadhyay Panchayat Satat Vikas awards.
84.tq: Test the category associated with a named award recipient.
84.sec: Universal angles

84.s: Under the Atmanirbhar Panchayat Program, the minimum own-source revenue requirement for Block Panchayats is:
84.x: The minimum own-source revenue requirement is Rs 1 crore for Block Panchayats, compared with Rs 50 lakh for Gram Panchayats.
84.tq: Compare threshold figures for two levels of Panchayati Raj institutions.
84.sec: Universal angles

84.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the 74th Constitutional Amendment is correct?
1. It relates to urban local government.
2. It inserted Part IX-A.
3. It contains Articles 243P to 243ZG.
4. It is associated with 18 subjects in the Twelfth Schedule.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
84.x: The 74th Amendment constitutionalised urban local government through Part IX-A, Articles 243P–243ZG and 18 Twelfth Schedule subjects.
84.tq: Link an amendment with its Part, Article range and Schedule content.
84.sec: Universal angles

84.s: The AIIB-aided Andhra Pradesh Urban Water Supply Project has an estimated cost of:
84.x: The AIIB-aided Andhra Pradesh Urban Water Supply Project has an estimated cost of Rs 300 crore.
84.tq: Test the exact project outlay against nearby rounded figures.
84.sec: Universal angles

84.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the coverage of the AIIB-aided Andhra Pradesh Urban Water Supply Project?
o: 2.048 million people in 50 Urban Local Bodies
3.3 million people in 123 Urban Local Bodies
5 million people in 123 Urban Local Bodies
3.3 million people in 50 Urban Local Bodies
84.x: The project is intended to benefit 3.3 million people across 50 Urban Local Bodies.
84.tq: Match two quantitative dimensions of a project rather than its cost.
84.sec: Universal angles

84.s: According to the stated urban water-supply figures, the quantity supplied across 123 Urban Local Bodies is:
84.x: The reported supply across 123 Urban Local Bodies is 2,048 million litres per day (MLD).
84.tq: Test a capacity figure while avoiding confusion with the project’s population coverage.
84.sec: Universal angles

84.s:
Arrange the following municipal corporations in chronological order of establishment:
A. Calcutta
B. Madras
C. Bombay
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
84.x: Madras was established in 1688, followed by Bombay and Calcutta in 1726. Thus the order is B, C, A.
84.tq: Fix the earliest date first and then resolve institutions sharing the later year.
84.sec: Universal angles

85.s: Who defined public policy as “whatever governments choose to do or not to do”?
85.x: Thomas Dye defined public policy as whatever governments choose to do or not to do, thereby treating governmental inaction also as policy.
85.tq: Use direct thinker-definition matching.

85.s: The definition of public policy as the “authoritative allocation of values for the whole society” is associated with:
85.x: David Easton described public policy as the authoritative allocation of values for the whole society.
85.tq: Discriminate between closely related thinker-definition pairs.

85.s: Who described public policy as a projected programme of goals, values and practices and is regarded as the founder of policy sciences?
85.x: Harold Lasswell described policy as a projected programme of goals, values and practices and is associated with the founding of policy sciences.
85.tq: Match the distinctive description with its proponent.

85.s: James Anderson defined public policy as:
o: A purposive course of action followed by an actor or set of actors in dealing with a problem
Whatever governments choose to do or not to do
A projected programme of goals, values and practices
An authoritative allocation of values for the whole society
85.x: James Anderson defined public policy as a purposive course of action followed by an actor or set of actors in dealing with a problem.
85.tq: Test exact wording in a definition-based question.

85.s: Which one of the following best represents the working definition of public policy?
o: A systematic course of action adopted by the state to address public issues, achieve development goals and regulate behaviour
A judicial determination applicable only to an individual dispute
A temporary administrative order issued only during emergencies
A set of private decisions taken by market participants without state intervention
85.x: Public policy is a systematic state course of action addressing public issues, pursuing development goals and regulating behaviour; it bridges political intent and administrative action.
85.tq: Choose the precise comprehensive definition over narrower alternatives.

85.s:
Which of the following constitute important Indian bases of public policy?
1. The Preamble and Directive Principles of State Policy
2. Judicial interpretation, including the Right to Food under Article 21
3. International commitments such as the SDGs and Paris Agreement
4. NITI Aayog agendas, the Budget and the Economic Survey
Which of the statements given above are correct?
85.x: All four are identified as bases of Indian public policy: constitutional principles, judicial interpretation, international commitments, and policy and fiscal documents.
85.tq: Treat a comprehensive list as an all-inclusive statement question.

85.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Distributive policy — Benefits spread to specific groups while costs are borne by all
2. Redistributive policy — Transfer of resources from one group to another
3. Regulatory policy — Creation or reorganisation of institutions
4. Constitutive policy — Limitation of individual or firm behaviour
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
85.x: Distributive and redistributive are correctly matched. Regulatory policy limits behaviour, while constitutive policy creates or reorganises institutions; pairs 3 and 4 are interchanged.
85.tq: Find the swapped meanings in a classification table.

85.s: Farm input subsidies and PM-KISAN are examples of which type of policy under Lowi’s classification?
85.x: Distributive policies spread benefits to specific groups while their costs are generally borne by the wider public; farm input subsidies and PM-KISAN illustrate this type.
85.tq: Link the Indian example to the correct classification.

85.s: Land reforms and progressive income tax are generally classified as:
85.x: Redistributive policies transfer resources from one group to another, as in land reforms and progressive income taxation.
85.tq: Use the direction of resource transfer to identify the policy type.

85.s: Licensing and environmental and food-safety standards are examples of:
85.x: Regulatory policies limit or control the behaviour of individuals and firms through measures such as licensing and standards.
85.tq: Identify the policy type from its controlling function.

85.s: Setting up NITI Aayog and delimitation are examples of which type of policy?
85.x: Constitutive policies create or reorganise institutions and rules; setting up NITI Aayog and delimitation illustrate this category.
85.tq: Match institutional restructuring with the constitutive category.

85.s: Which one of the following is the correct sequence of the principal stages in the public policy cycle?
85.x: The principal sequence is agenda-setting, formulation, adoption, implementation and evaluation.
85.tq: Fix the first and last stages before ordering the intermediate stages.

85.s: At which stage of the policy cycle are research, stakeholder consultation, cost-benefit analysis and impact assessment of options undertaken?
85.x: These activities are characteristic of policy formulation, when alternative courses of action are developed and assessed.
85.tq: Match the activity cluster with its stage.

85.s: Which stage involves legislative or executive debate, amendment and formal acceptance of a policy?
85.x: Adoption is the stage at which the legislature or executive debates, amends and formally adopts the policy.
85.tq: Identify the formal decision point in the cycle.

85.s: Planning, resource allocation, coordination and the possible creation of new regulations are characteristic of:
85.x: Implementation translates an adopted policy into action through planning, allocation of resources, coordination and, where necessary, new regulations or programmes.
85.tq: Connect operational activities with implementation.

85.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Agenda setting involves identifying a problem and bringing it onto the policy agenda.
2. Media, advocacy and expert analysis can help place an issue on the agenda.
3. Monitoring and evaluation generate data and feedback that may lead to policy adjustment.
4. Communication and transparency are confined to the evaluation stage.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
85.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Communication and transparency run through every stage of the cycle, not only evaluation.
85.tq: Reject the restrictive word that confines a cross-cutting function to one stage.

85.s: A policy that is ineffective may be ended or revised, with lessons from the process feeding back into agenda setting. This describes:
85.x: Termination or revision deals with ineffective policies and allows policy learning to feed back into agenda setting.
85.tq: Apply the feedback-loop concept to a policy scenario.

85.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the policy cycle is NOT correct?
o: Formulation may involve stakeholder consultation and impact assessment.
Evaluation uses data and metrics to assess whether goals are met.
Implementation is limited to formal adoption by the legislature or executive.
Agenda setting identifies a problem and brings it to official attention.
85.x: Implementation is not formal adoption; it involves planning, resource allocation, coordination and execution of the policy.
85.tq: Find the stage-description mismatch by separating adoption from implementation.

85.s: The Draft National Policy for Women, 2016, was based on the recommendations of which committee?
85.x: The Draft National Policy for Women, 2016, was based on the Pam Rajput Committee.
85.tq: Test the policy-document and committee association directly.

85.s: Which model of public policy is associated with Herbert Simon and the idea of bounded rationality and “satisficing”?
85.x: Herbert Simon is associated with the rational-comprehensive model and its critique based on bounded rationality and satisficing.
85.tq: Match the distinctive concept with the model proponent.

85.s: “The science of muddling through” and incrementalism are associated with:
85.x: Charles Lindblom developed incrementalism, famously described as the “science of muddling through,” in 1959.
85.tq: Use a famous phrase to identify the correct proponent.

85.s: Mixed scanning as a policy model was propounded by:
85.x: Amitai Etzioni is the proponent of the mixed-scanning model.
85.tq: Direct model-proponent discrimination.

85.s:
Which of the following pairs are correctly matched?
1. Elite theory — C. Wright Mills; Dye and Zeigler
2. Group theory — Arthur Bentley and David Truman
3. Systems model — David Easton
4. Optimal model — Yehezkel Dror
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
85.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Elite theory is associated with C. Wright Mills, Dye and Zeigler; group theory with Bentley and Truman; systems theory with Easton; and the optimal model with Dror.
85.tq: Verify several model-proponent pairs before selecting the comprehensive code.

85.s: In the systems model of public policy, which sequence best represents the relationship among its elements?
85.x: David Easton’s systems model represents policy-making through inputs, conversion, outputs and feedback.
85.tq: Arrange the functional stages from demand to feedback.

85.s: Which one of the following is an example of regulation as a policy instrument?
o: Proactive disclosure under Section 4 of the RTI Act
85.x: Regulation uses licensing, standards and mandates to guide or restrict behaviour. The other options represent direct provision, information and subsidy instruments.
85.tq: Classify an instrument by the mechanism through which it influences behaviour.

85.s: Under the Delhi EV policy illustration, which of the following registration requirements is correctly stated?
o: All electric vehicles may be registered from 1 January 2027, irrespective of category.
Only e-three-wheelers and N1 trucks may be registered from 1 January 2027, and e-two-wheelers from 1 April 2028.
Only e-three-wheelers may be registered from 1 April 2028.
Only e-two-wheelers may be registered from 1 January 2027.
85.x: The stated regulatory illustration permits registration of only e-three-wheelers and N1 trucks from 1 January 2027 and e-two-wheelers from 1 April 2028.
85.tq: Track both dates and vehicle categories in a regulatory provision.

85.s:
Which of the following are examples of taxes and subsidies as policy instruments?
1. Tax rates
2. DBT-based subsidy reform
3. Production-linked incentive incentives
4. Public borrowing
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
85.x: Tax rates, subsidies, DBT-based subsidy reform, PLI incentives and public borrowing are listed as fiscal policy instruments under this category.
85.tq: Recognise the complete set of fiscal instruments rather than treating subsidies narrowly.

85.s: Government schools and primary health centres directly operated by the government illustrate which policy instrument?
85.x: Direct provision occurs when the government itself delivers a service, such as through schools and primary health centres.
85.tq: Identify the instrument from who directly delivers the service.

85.s: Proactive disclosure under Section 4 of the Right to Information Act and public campaigns are examples of:
85.x: Information instruments influence public action through disclosure, communication and campaigns; proactive disclosure under Section 4 of the RTI Act is an example.
85.tq: Distinguish information-based action from coercive and fiscal instruments.

85.s: The concept of nudges in public policy is associated with:
85.x: Behavioural nudges and their use in policy design are associated with Richard Thaler and Cass Sunstein.
85.tq: Match the behavioural policy concept with its proponents.

85.s: In Hood’s NATO classification of policy tools, the letter ‘T’ stands for:
85.x: Hood’s NATO tools are Nodality, Authority, Treasure and Organisation; therefore, T stands for Treasure.
85.tq: Expand the acronym from the exact set of neighbouring terms.

85.s: Which one of the following correctly gives Hood’s NATO policy tools?
85.x: Hood’s NATO framework consists of Nodality, Authority, Treasure and Organisation.
85.tq: Reject look-alike expansions of a well-known policy acronym.

85.s: Which statement best distinguishes top-down and bottom-up approaches to policy implementation?
o: Top-down implementation is set at the centre and carried out faithfully, whereas bottom-up implementation recognises the role of front-line officials in shaping outcomes.
Top-down implementation applies only to fiscal policy, whereas bottom-up implementation applies only to social policy.
Top-down implementation is shaped mainly by front-line officials, whereas bottom-up implementation is fixed at the centre.
Both approaches require that front-line discretion be eliminated.
85.x: The top-down approach emphasises central direction and faithful execution, while the bottom-up approach recognises that front-line officials shape actual outcomes.
85.tq: Compare the location of authority and discretion in the two approaches.

85.s: Pressman and Wildavsky’s work titled “Implementation” was published in:
85.x: Pressman and Wildavsky’s “Implementation,” published in 1973, showed how chains of clearances can derail programmes.
85.tq: Use the year attached to a classic implementation study.

85.s: The concept of “street-level bureaucracy” is associated with:
85.x: Michael Lipsky developed the concept of street-level bureaucracy in 1980, referring to front-line officials who shape policy outcomes.
85.tq: Separate the proponents of related implementation concepts.

85.s: “Backward mapping” in policy implementation is associated with:
85.x: Richard Elmore is associated with the bottom-up implementation concept of backward mapping.
85.tq: Discriminate between the two bottom-up implementation scholars.

85.s:
Which of the following statements about the Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office is correct?
1. DMEO is the apex monitoring and evaluation office under NITI Aayog.
2. It evaluates Central schemes suo motu or at the request of a ministry.
3. It advises States and supports evidence-based policy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
85.x: DMEO is the apex M&E office under NITI Aayog; it evaluates Central schemes on its own initiative or at a ministry’s request, advises States and supports evidence-based policy.
85.tq: Select the comprehensive description of an institutional mandate.

85.s: Gender budgeting in India and the Outcome Budget both began in:
85.x: Gender budgeting was adopted in 2005-06, and the Outcome Budget also began in 2005-06.
85.tq: Identify the common year attached to two budgetary initiatives.

85.s: The Draft National Health Research Policy 2026 evaluates research partly on the basis of its contribution to public policy and practice by using which scale?
o: ICMR Impact of Research and Innovation Scale
85.x: The Draft National Health Research Policy 2026 uses the ICMR Impact of Research and Innovation Scale to assess research contributions to public policy and practice.
85.tq: Match the policy document with its named evaluation framework.

85.s: Which of the following is NOT a recognised cause of policy failure or an implementation gap?
85.x: Weak coordination, resource shortfalls and poor targeting are causes of policy failure. Real-time public outcome tracking is a remedy.
85.tq: Find the option that represents a remedy rather than a cause.

85.s: Which one of the following is associated with the bypassing of citizens in policy implementation?
85.x: The bypassing of citizens by parastatals and Special Purpose Vehicles is identified as a cause of implementation gaps.
85.tq: Identify the institutional arrangement linked to the stated implementation problem.

85.s: Which of the following measures is most appropriate for reducing an implementation gap?
o: Phased roll-out with milestones and real-time monitoring
85.x: Phased implementation with milestones, real-time monitoring and public outcome tracking is prescribed as a remedy for implementation gaps.
85.tq: Apply the remedy-oriented features to the implementation scenario.

85.s: Swarna Andhra Vision 2047 is associated with which of the following implementation features?
o: Replacement of all departments by parastatals
Multi-phase execution and a performance-evaluation framework
85.x: Swarna Andhra Vision 2047 is cited as an example of multi-phase execution combined with performance evaluation.
85.tq: Match the named policy initiative with its distinctive implementation feature.

85.s: The Action Taken Reports of Andhra Pradesh referred to in the context of policy implementation relate to how many sector white papers?
85.x: The Action Taken Reports were issued against seven sector white papers.
85.tq: Recall the exact number associated with the implementation review.

85.s: Social welfare services are primarily targeted at which of the following groups?
o: Disabled persons, destitute children and widows
Only persons employed in organised industries
85.x: Social welfare services target vulnerable groups such as disabled persons, destitute children and widows.
85.tq: Identify the vulnerable-group focus of welfare services.
85.sec: Social welfare services and social development programmes - Social Policy/Justice/Defence/Welfare

85.s: Which one of the following is NOT generally regarded as a social welfare service in the stated classification?
85.x: General health services for all are not classified as targeted social welfare services, whereas the other three serve vulnerable groups.
85.tq: Separate targeted welfare services from universal public services.
85.sec: Social welfare services and social development programmes - Social Policy/Justice/Defence/Welfare

85.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding social-sector concepts.

List-I
(a) Social policy
(b) Social justice
(c) Social welfare
(d) Social defence

List-II
(i) Rehabilitation in deviant or vulnerable situations
(ii) Services for weaker and vulnerable sections
(iii) State's overall framework for social well-being
(iv) Removal of social and economic inequalities

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
85.x: Social policy is the overall framework for social well-being; social justice removes inequalities; social welfare serves vulnerable sections; and social defence involves rehabilitation in deviant or vulnerable situations.
85.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes with mismatched definitions.
85.sec: Social welfare services and social development programmes - Social Policy/Justice/Defence/Welfare

85.s: Articles 38 and 46 are particularly associated with which social-policy objective?
o: Removal of social and economic inequalities and advancement of weaker sections
85.x: Article 38 concerns social order and reduction of inequalities, while Article 46 concerns the interests of SCs, STs and weaker sections.
85.tq: Link the constitutional provisions with their shared social-justice objective.
85.sec: Social welfare services and social development programmes - Social Policy/Justice/Defence/Welfare

85.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Social welfare is generally short-term and consumption-oriented.
2. Social development is generally long-term and production-oriented.
3. Social welfare and social development are identical in their time orientation and economic orientation.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
85.x: Social welfare is described as short-term and consumption-oriented, whereas development is long-term and production-oriented. Therefore, statement 3 is false.
85.tq: Contrast the two concepts and reject the statement that erases their distinction.
85.sec: Social welfare services and social development programmes - Social Policy/Justice/Defence/Welfare

85.s: The principal aim of social legislation is to:
o: Protect vulnerable persons and establish minimum conditions for a dignified life
Promote unrestricted freedom of contract in every circumstance
Restrict public assistance to private organisations
85.x: Social legislation protects vulnerable groups and establishes minimum floors for a dignified life. It represents a movement from freedom of contract towards fairness in contract.
85.tq: Identify the broad aim rather than a narrow legal instrument.

85.s: The evolution of social legislation from ‘freedom of contract’ to ‘fairness in contract’ signifies:
o: Replacement of legislation by customary law
Greater concern for substantive protection of vulnerable parties
Complete withdrawal of the State from labour relations
A ban on all private contracts
85.x: The shift signifies State intervention to protect vulnerable parties and ensure minimum standards of fairness.
85.tq: Interpret the legal phrase through its underlying social objective.

85.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding types of social legislation.

List-I
(a) Protective legislation
(b) Regulatory legislation
(c) Enabling legislation

List-II
(i) Creates entitlements
(ii) Protects against exploitation
(iii) Regulates conduct and relations

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
85.x: Protective legislation prevents exploitation, regulatory legislation governs conduct and relations, and enabling legislation creates entitlements.
85.tq: Use the purpose of each legislative type to establish the matching code.

85.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Right to Information Act, 2005 — Enabling legislation
85.x: The Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 is an example of regulatory legislation. The other pairs are correctly matched.
85.tq: Check whether the example fits the purpose of the legislative category.

85.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
85.x: The Bonded Labour Act, 1976 is protective legislation. Child Labour legislation is protective, while NREGA and RTE are enabling legislation.
85.tq: Use the category-purpose distinction to detect swapped examples.

85.s: What was the major organisational change during 1985–86 in the history of welfare administration?
o: The Ministry of Welfare was abolished and all functions transferred to the Ministry of Home Affairs
The Ministry of Welfare was split into the Department of Women and Child Development and the Department of Welfare
The Ministry of Tribal Affairs was merged with the Ministry of Welfare
The Ministry of Minority Affairs became the sole welfare ministry
85.x: During 1985–86, the Ministry of Welfare was split into the Department of Women and Child Development and the Department of Welfare. SC, Tribal and Minority divisions also moved in from the Ministry of Home Affairs.
85.tq: Recall the institutional change associated with the specified period.
85.sec: Welfare ministries → renaming and bifurcation history

85.s: During the 1985–86 reorganisation, which divisions moved into the welfare administrative structure from the Ministry of Home Affairs?
o: Defence, Finance and External Affairs divisions
85.x: The SC, Tribal and Minority divisions moved from the Ministry of Home Affairs into the reorganised welfare structure.
85.tq: Identify the divisions transferred in the administrative reorganisation.
85.sec: Welfare ministries → renaming and bifurcation history

85.s: In which year was the Ministry of Welfare renamed the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment?
85.x: The Ministry of Welfare was renamed the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment in 1998.
85.tq: Recall the precise year of renaming among closely related administrative dates.
85.sec: Welfare ministries → renaming and bifurcation history

85.s: Which statement correctly describes the 2006–07 change in welfare ministries?
o: The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment was renamed the Ministry of Home Affairs.
The Ministry of Tribal Affairs was dissolved and merged with the Ministry of Welfare.
The Ministry of Minority Affairs and the Ministry of Women and Child Development became separate ministries.
The Department of Welfare became part of the Ministry of Defence.
85.x: The Ministry of Minority Affairs and the Ministry of Women and Child Development became separate ministries during 2006–07. The ministry was created in January 2006, while the transfer is dated to 2007 in the cited chronology.
85.tq: Read the institutional change carefully and distinguish creation from transfer dates.
85.sec: Welfare ministries → renaming and bifurcation history

85.s: Which of the following is included among the present departments of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment?
o: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (Divyangjan)
85.x: The present departments include Social Justice and Empowerment and Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (Divyangjan).
85.tq: Identify the department belonging to the ministry rather than a neighbouring governmental sector.
85.sec: Welfare ministries → renaming and bifurcation history

85.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Directive Principles of State Policy:
1. They are contained in Part IV of the Constitution.
2. They extend from Article 36 to Article 51.
3. They are enforceable in a court of law in the same manner as Fundamental Rights.
4. They are fundamental in the governance of the country.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
85.x: The DPSPs are in Part IV, Articles 36–51, and are fundamental in governance. They cannot be enforced by courts, so statement 3 is false.
85.tq: Use the constitutional distinction between governance principles and enforceable rights.
85.sec: Welfare state - concept, aims, DPSP mandate

85.s: The Directive Principles of State Policy were inspired by the Constitution of:
85.x: The Directive Principles of State Policy were inspired by the Irish Constitution.
85.tq: Recall the constitutional source associated with the DPSPs.
85.sec: Welfare state - concept, aims, DPSP mandate

85.s:
Match the following Articles of the Constitution with their principal welfare-related mandates.

List-I
(a) Article 41
(b) Article 42
(c) Article 43
(d) Article 47

List-II
(i) Living wage
(ii) Nutrition, public health and prohibition
(iii) Work, education and public assistance
(iv) Humane conditions of work and maternity relief

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
85.x: Article 41 covers work, education and public assistance; Article 42 humane work conditions and maternity relief; Article 43 living wage; and Article 47 nutrition, public health and prohibition.
85.tq: Match each Article with its distinctive welfare mandate.
85.sec: Welfare state - concept, aims, DPSP mandate

85.s: Which Article of the Constitution directs the State to secure a social order informed by justice and to minimise inequalities?
85.x: Article 38 deals with social order based on justice and reduction of inequalities.
85.tq: Separate closely related DPSP provisions by their specific mandate.
85.sec: Welfare state - concept, aims, DPSP mandate

85.s: Article 46 specifically concerns the promotion of the interests of:
85.x: Article 46 directs the State to promote the educational and economic interests of SCs, STs and other weaker sections.
85.tq: Identify the protected social groups linked to the Article.
85.sec: Welfare state - concept, aims, DPSP mandate

85.s:
Arrange the following phases of India's welfare approach in chronological order:
A. Rights-based laws
B. State-led planned development and welfare
C. Empowerment approach
D. Welfare-to-development approach for women
85.x: State-led planned development characterised the 1950s–70s, welfare shifted towards development in the Sixth Plan, empowerment marked the Eighth–Ninth Plans, and rights-based laws emerged in the 2000s.
85.tq: Anchor the sequence using the dated plans and the 2000s transition.
85.sec: Evolution of welfare approach - Five Year Plan phases

85.s: The Central Social Welfare Board was established in:
85.x: The Central Social Welfare Board was established in 1953 during the state-led planned development and welfare phase.
85.tq: Recall the specific institutional milestone within the early welfare phase.
85.sec: Evolution of welfare approach - Five Year Plan phases

85.s: The Sixth Five Year Plan (1980–85) marked which shift in welfare policy?
o: From welfare towards development, particularly concerning women
From rights-based laws towards centralised charity
From empowerment towards universal military service
85.x: The Sixth Plan marked a shift from welfare towards development, particularly in relation to women.
85.tq: Link the Plan period with the policy-direction change.
85.sec: Evolution of welfare approach - Five Year Plan phases

85.s: The Eighth and Ninth Five Year Plans are associated with an approach centred on:
85.x: The Eighth and Ninth Plans emphasised empowerment.
85.tq: Identify the defining policy emphasis of the plan phase.
85.sec: Evolution of welfare approach - Five Year Plan phases

85.s: Which development is associated with the 2000s phase of welfare policy?
o: Exclusive reliance on the Central Social Welfare Board
85.x: The 2000s witnessed the development of rights-based laws as a major welfare approach.
85.tq: Match the decade with its characteristic policy approach.
85.sec: Evolution of welfare approach - Five Year Plan phases

85.s: The term ‘New welfarism’ refers to an approach based primarily on:
o: Targeted, technology-driven DBT benefits rather than legal rights
85.x: New welfarism is described as targeted and technology-driven, relying on DBT benefits rather than primarily on legal rights.
85.tq: Distinguish technology-driven targeted benefits from rights-based welfare.
85.sec: Evolution of welfare approach - Five Year Plan phases

85.s: The Right to Information Act guarantees access to information ordinarily within:
85.x: The Right to Information framework provides information within 30 days in the stated entitlement summary.
85.tq: Recall the exact statutory response period.
85.sec: Rights-based entitlements - RTI, NREGA, NFSA, RTE

85.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: NREGA — 2013 — 5 kg grain per person per month
85.x: The RTI Act dates to 2005 and guarantees information within 30 days. The other pairs interchange the years or entitlements of different laws.
85.tq: Use both the year and the guaranteed entitlement to eliminate swapped pairs.
85.sec: Rights-based entitlements - RTI, NREGA, NFSA, RTE

85.s: Under the original NREGA entitlement stated here, the guarantee was for:
85.x: NREGA provided a guarantee of 100 days of work. The entitlement was noted as 125 days under the VB-G RAM G Bill, 2025.
85.tq: Distinguish the original entitlement from the later proposed or stated figure.
85.sec: Rights-based entitlements - RTI, NREGA, NFSA, RTE

85.s: The Right to Education Act, 2009 relates to free schooling for children in which age group?
85.x: The RTE Act, 2009 provides free schooling for children aged 6–14 years under Article 21A.
85.tq: Recall the age band and distinguish it from adjacent child-development categories.
85.sec: Rights-based entitlements - RTI, NREGA, NFSA, RTE

85.s: Which of the following correctly describes the National Food Security Act, 2013?
o: It guarantees 100 days of work to every rural household.
It covers 50% of the rural population and 75% of the urban population, with 10 kg per household per month.
It covers 75% of the rural population and 50% of the urban population, with 5 kg of grain per person per month.
85.x: The NFSA coverage is 75% in rural areas and 50% in urban areas, with an entitlement of 5 kg of grain per person per month.
85.tq: Check both coverage percentages and the unit of the food entitlement.
85.sec: Rights-based entitlements - RTI, NREGA, NFSA, RTE

85.s: Which institution or social force is credited with helping to secure rights-based entitlements such as RTI, NREGA, NFSA and RTE?
85.x: Civil society played an important role in helping to win these rights-based entitlements.
85.tq: Identify the non-state social force associated with rights mobilisation.
85.sec: Rights-based entitlements - RTI, NREGA, NFSA, RTE

85.s: The subsequent shift in welfare emphasis described in relation to rights-based entitlements has been towards:
85.x: The emphasis has subsequently shifted towards cash transfers.
85.tq: Identify the later policy trend contrasted with legal entitlements.
85.sec: Rights-based entitlements - RTI, NREGA, NFSA, RTE

85.s: Direct Benefit Transfer was introduced from:
85.x: Direct Benefit Transfer began from 1 January 2013.
85.tq: Recall the exact launch date of the delivery reform.
85.sec: Delivery reforms - DBT, JAM trinity, social audit (AP model)

85.s: JAM is an abbreviation for:
85.x: JAM stands for Jan Dhan, Aadhaar and Mobile.
85.tq: Expand the acronym using its three delivery components.
85.sec: Delivery reforms - DBT, JAM trinity, social audit (AP model)

85.s: The JAM trinity was discussed in the Economic Survey of:
85.x: The JAM framework was associated with the Economic Survey 2014–15.
85.tq: Distinguish the Economic Survey year from the DBT launch year.
85.sec: Delivery reforms - DBT, JAM trinity, social audit (AP model)

85.s: Which of the following is a recognised gain of DBT and JAM-based delivery?
o: Exclusion of all beneficiaries without exception
Reduction in ghost beneficiaries and elimination of middlemen
Removal of the need for beneficiary identification
85.x: DBT and JAM can reduce ghost beneficiaries and remove middlemen from benefit delivery.
85.tq: Identify the intended administrative gains of digital benefit delivery.
85.sec: Delivery reforms - DBT, JAM trinity, social audit (AP model)

85.s: A major drawback of technology-driven DBT is that it may:
o: Guarantee access to every person automatically
Prevent any direct transfer to beneficiaries
85.x: People lacking digital access may be excluded from technology-driven benefit delivery.
85.tq: Apply the inclusion-exclusion consequence to a digitally inaccessible beneficiary.
85.sec: Delivery reforms - DBT, JAM trinity, social audit (AP model)

85.s: Under Section 17 of MGNREGA, a social audit is conducted by the:
85.x: Section 17 of MGNREGA provides for social audit by the Gram Sabha.
85.tq: Ask which participatory institution performs the statutory function.
85.sec: Delivery reforms - DBT, JAM trinity, social audit (AP model)

85.s: Which statement correctly describes Andhra Pradesh's model of NREGS social audits?
o: Andhra Pradesh pioneered statewide NREGS social audits in 2006 through the independent SSAAT established in 2009.
Andhra Pradesh began social audits only after 2014 through a Union ministry department.
The audits were conducted exclusively by private contractors without an independent institution.
SSAAT was created before the statewide social audits in 2001.
85.x: Andhra Pradesh pioneered statewide NREGS social audits in 2006, and the independent Society for Social Audit, Accountability and Transparency was established in 2009.
85.tq: Check the sequence of the pioneering initiative and the later institutionalisation.
85.sec: Delivery reforms - DBT, JAM trinity, social audit (AP model)

85.s: In Andhra Pradesh, fast-tracked DBT was used for:
85.x: Andhra Pradesh used fast-tracked DBT for minority post-matric scholarships.
85.tq: Match the delivery reform with the specific beneficiary programme.
85.sec: Delivery reforms - DBT, JAM trinity, social audit (AP model)

85.s: Which institution, in association with WRI India, launched the second India Electric Mobility Index?
85.x: NITI Aayog, with WRI India, launched the second India Electric Mobility Index.
85.tq: Use the institutional-identity approach and distinguish the policy think tank from an evaluation body.

85.s: The second India Electric Mobility Index assigns weights to its three major dimensions in which of the following proportions?
85.x: The index gives weights of 50:30:20 to transport electrification, charging and research and development, respectively.
85.tq: Read the three-part numerical sequence in the same order as the listed dimensions.

85.s: The India Electric Mobility Index is intended primarily to reinforce which approach to policymaking?
85.x: The index is intended to reinforce evidence-based policymaking by providing an analytical basis for decisions on electric mobility.
85.tq: Match the policy instrument with its stated governance purpose rather than with a broad ideological label.

85.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the proposed new retail excise policy in Andhra Pradesh:
1. A Group of Ministers is framing the policy.
2. Kollu Ravindra is the Minister under whose charge the Group of Ministers is functioning.
3. The existing 2024–26 policy expires on 30 September 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
85.x: All three statements are correct: the Group of Ministers is framing the policy under Excise Minister Kollu Ravindra, and the 2024–26 policy expires on 30 September 2026.
85.tq: Check the office-holder, institutional arrangement and expiry date separately before selecting the coded combination.

85.s: The existing retail excise policy in Andhra Pradesh, for which a new policy is being framed, is scheduled to expire on:
85.x: The existing 2024–26 retail excise policy expires on 30 September 2026.
85.tq: Use exact-date recall and distinguish the month-end expiry from nearby administrative dates.

85.s: The framing of the new retail excise policy in Andhra Pradesh is cited as an example of policy formulation involving:
85.x: The policy-framing process is described as a live example of formulation with stakeholder feedback.
85.tq: Identify the policy-cycle stage from the action described and connect consultation with formulation.

85.s: The shift from announcement-based governance to outcome-based governance is associated with which of the following mechanisms?
85.x: The shift toward outcome-based governance is linked with Action Taken Reports (ATRs) and evaluations by the Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office (DMEO).
85.tq: Link the governance objective to the monitoring and evaluation mechanisms named with it.

85.s:
Consider the following statements about outcome-based governance:
1. It gives importance to assessing results rather than merely recording announcements.
2. Action Taken Reports are associated with this shift.
3. DMEO evaluations are relevant to this shift.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
85.x: All three statements are correct. Outcome-based governance focuses on results and uses ATRs and DMEO evaluations as monitoring and evaluation mechanisms.
85.tq: Separate the defining feature from the two supporting mechanisms and test the complete combination.

85.s: Andhra Pradesh spent approximately what amount in two years, according to the expenditure figure cited?
85.x: The cited expenditure by Andhra Pradesh over two years was ₹2.83 lakh crore.
85.tq: Distinguish the overall expenditure figure from the welfare subcomponent mentioned alongside it.

85.s: Of the ₹2.83 lakh crore spent by Andhra Pradesh in two years, approximately how much was spent on welfare?
85.x: ₹1.49 lakh crore of the total expenditure of ₹2.83 lakh crore was spent on welfare.
85.tq: Split the total and component figures instead of treating the larger total as the welfare expenditure.

85.s: How much fee reimbursement was provided to SC students in the expenditure period referred to?
85.x: Fee reimbursement amounting to ₹1,543.17 crore was provided to SC students.
85.tq: Use precise-figure discrimination when two expenditure amounts belong to different categories.

85.s: The fee reimbursement of ₹1,543.17 crore in Andhra Pradesh benefited approximately how many SC students?
85.x: The fee reimbursement benefited 5.40 lakh SC students.
85.tq: Match the exact beneficiary count with the corresponding scheme expenditure figure.

85.s: Which one of the following best represents the criticism associated with the idea of “new welfarism”?
o: It eliminates all social protection expenditure
It transfers welfare functions exclusively to local bodies
It strengthens rights-based entitlements in every case
85.x: The criticism is that “new welfarism” weakens rights. The cited social protection spending is 4.0% of GDP.
85.tq: Identify the precise criticism and reject absolute extensions not supported by the stated position.

85.s: Social protection spending, as cited in the discussion of new welfarism, is approximately what percentage of GDP?
85.x: Social protection spending is cited as only 4.0% of GDP.
85.tq: Focus on the percentage attached to the criticism rather than the separate population-coverage figures.

85.s: According to the cited estimate, social protection currently covers approximately what share of the population?
85.x: Social protection covers approximately 64.3% of the population.
85.tq: Distinguish the current coverage figure from the earlier benchmark of 22%.

85.s: Social protection coverage increased from which level in 2016 to 64.3% of the population?
85.x: The coverage level increased from 22% in 2016 to 64.3% of the population.
85.tq: Read the direction and endpoints of the comparison carefully before selecting the earlier value.

85.s: Andhra Pradesh has set which of the following objectives for the year 2047?
o: To become a completely industrialised state
To replace all central welfare schemes
85.x: Andhra Pradesh aims to become a welfare state by 2047.
85.tq: Match the stated long-term target with its exact policy objective and year.

86.s: Which of the following is recognised as a driver of media agenda-setting?
86.x: Public awareness and media coverage are identified as important drivers through which issues are pushed onto the policy agenda.
86.tq: Identify the two direct drivers instead of confusing agenda-setting with implementation.
86.sec: Media - agenda setting, public opinion, image-building, free press and new media  [APPSC]

86.s: Media organisations are generally regarded as stakeholders of governance under which category?
86.x: Media organisations are counted among civil society stakeholders involved in governance.
86.tq: Test institutional classification through a nearby-category distinction.
86.sec: Media - agenda setting, public opinion, image-building, free press and new media  [APPSC]

86.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the image-building role of mass media:
1. Mass media shape the image and identity of political personalities.
2. The ideology of a media outlet can influence its treatment of news.
3. Media treatment has no bearing on the public image of political personalities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
86.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because media treatment helps explain the image formed about political personalities.
86.tq: Reject the absolute negative statement and combine the two related true statements.
86.sec: Media - agenda setting, public opinion, image-building, free press and new media  [APPSC]

86.s: Which institution is associated with press briefings, accreditation and social-media communication on behalf of the Government of India?
86.x: Government communication runs through the Press Information Bureau, including press briefings, accreditation and social-media communication.
86.tq: Match the communication function with the responsible institution.
86.sec: Media - agenda setting, public opinion, image-building, free press and new media  [APPSC]

86.s: The PM's Communication Wing is primarily associated with which of the following functions?
o: Publicity for the PMO and Cabinet and daily newspaper feedback
Conducting judicial inquiries into media reports
86.x: The PM's Communication Wing handles publicity for the PMO and Cabinet and provides daily newspaper feedback.
86.tq: Use the institutional-function method to distinguish communication work from policy and recruitment functions.
86.sec: Media - agenda setting, public opinion, image-building, free press and new media  [APPSC]

86.s: Which of the following correctly describes the new information risk associated with AI-driven foreign information manipulation?
o: It operates exclusively through printed newspapers.
It exploits social fault lines through synthetic media and algorithmic polarisation.
It is limited to parliamentary committee reports.
It eliminates political polarisation through uniform information flows.
86.x: AI-driven foreign information manipulation can exploit social fault lines by using synthetic media and algorithmic polarisation.
86.tq: Identify the causal mechanism in a contemporary information-security scenario.
86.sec: Media - agenda setting, public opinion, image-building, free press and new media  [APPSC]

86.s: Political parties seeking to court Gen Z, identified in the age group of 14–29 years, mainly use which platform?
86.x: Political parties are described as courting Gen Z, aged 14–29 years, mainly through digital platforms.
86.tq: Link the stated age range with the specific communication platform.
86.sec: Media - agenda setting, public opinion, image-building, free press and new media  [APPSC]

86.s: Which one of the following best describes the relationship among Parliament, the Cabinet and the bureaucracy in the legislative process?
o: The bureaucracy decides the substance and Parliament merely publishes bills.
The Cabinet has no role in determining the timing of bills.
Private members' bills constitute the principal source of legislation.
Parliament is the chief law-making body, the Cabinet decides the substance and timing, and the bureaucracy drafts bills.
86.x: Parliament is the chief law-making body, but the Cabinet determines the substance and timing of bills, while the bureaucracy generally drafts them. Private members' bills rarely pass.
86.tq: Separate formal law-making authority from political decision-making and administrative drafting.
86.sec: Legislature - law-making, committees, options against a Supreme Court decision  [APPSC]

86.s: Which of the following is regarded as the most effective parliamentary control over the executive among the listed devices?
86.x: Question Hour is identified as the most effective among the listed parliamentary controls over the executive.
86.tq: Recall the relative effectiveness of a parliamentary control device.
86.sec: Legislature - law-making, committees, options against a Supreme Court decision  [APPSC]

86.s:
Consider the following as instruments of parliamentary control over the executive:
1. Zero Hour
2. Half-an-hour discussions
3. Adjournment motions
4. Financial control
5. Ratification of laws
Which of the statements given above are correct?
86.x: All five listed devices are identified as means by which the legislature controls or scrutinises the executive.
86.tq: Recognise the complete list rather than selecting only the familiar parliamentary devices.
86.sec: Legislature - law-making, committees, options against a Supreme Court decision  [APPSC]

86.s: What is a likely consequence when a government does not have a majority in the Rajya Sabha?
o: It can pass every bill without negotiation.
The Lok Sabha automatically becomes dissolved.
It must concede or negotiate on legislative proposals.
The Supreme Court assumes legislative power.
86.x: Without a Rajya Sabha majority, a government may have to concede or negotiate, as illustrated by the rejection of the Prevention of Terrorism Bill, 2002, in the Rajya Sabha.
86.tq: Apply the effect of an upper-house majority to a legislative situation.
86.sec: Legislature - law-making, committees, options against a Supreme Court decision  [APPSC]

86.s: The percentage of bills referred to committees declined from approximately what level in the 15th Lok Sabha to what level in the 17th Lok Sabha?
86.x: Committee referral of bills fell from 71% in the 15th Lok Sabha to 16% in the 17th Lok Sabha.
86.tq: Compare both ends of the numerical trend rather than recalling only one percentage.
86.sec: Legislature - law-making, committees, options against a Supreme Court decision  [APPSC]

86.s:
With reference to options available against a decision of the Supreme Court, consider the following:
1. Parliament may amend the law to remove the basis of a judgment, but cannot simply overrule the verdict.
2. A constitutional amendment under Article 368 must respect the basic structure.
3. A review or curative petition by the Government is considered before the same Court.
4. A Presidential reference under Article 143 produces a binding judgment on the dispute.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
86.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. A Presidential reference under Article 143 results in an advisory opinion, not a binding judgment on the dispute.
86.tq: Find the one reversed legal effect among several correctly stated remedies.
86.sec: Legislature - law-making, committees, options against a Supreme Court decision  [APPSC]

86.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Article 143 — Power of the President to overrule a Supreme Court verdict
86.x: Article 143 enables a Presidential reference for an advisory opinion; it does not empower the President to overrule a Supreme Court verdict.
86.tq: Find the option that converts an advisory power into an overriding power.
86.sec: Legislature - law-making, committees, options against a Supreme Court decision  [APPSC]

86.s: Which of the following is a criticism associated with Cabinet and Cabinet Committees?
o: They are limited exclusively to judicial appointments.
They function without any relationship to the executive.
They may involve delays, bureaucratic sway, overlapping mandates, political considerations and secrecy.
They are constitutionally prohibited from taking key decisions.
86.x: The noted criticisms include delays, bureaucratic influence, overlapping mandates, political considerations and secrecy, even though the Cabinet and Cabinet Committees take key decisions.
86.tq: Select the comprehensive criticism list without treating it as a constitutional prohibition.
86.sec: Executive - Cabinet, PMO, Cabinet Secretariat, NITI Aayog

86.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Cabinet Secretariat from the PMO?
o: The PMO is responsible only for recruitment to State PSCs.
The Cabinet Secretariat, headed by the Cabinet Secretary, works directly under the PM and runs the Transaction of Business Rules; the PMO is the PM's policy office.
The Cabinet Secretariat is the PM's policy office, whereas the PMO runs the Transaction of Business Rules.
Both institutions are headed by the Chief Justice of India.
86.x: The Cabinet Secretariat is headed by the Cabinet Secretary, works directly under the Prime Minister and administers the Transaction of Business Rules. The PMO functions as the Prime Minister's policy office.
86.tq: Separate the two closely related executive offices by their distinctive functions.
86.sec: Executive - Cabinet, PMO, Cabinet Secretariat, NITI Aayog

86.s: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission in which year?
86.x: NITI Aayog was established in 2015, replacing the Planning Commission, which had been established in 1950.
86.tq: Distinguish the replacement year from the year of establishment of the earlier body.
86.sec: Executive - Cabinet, PMO, Cabinet Secretariat, NITI Aayog

86.s:
Consider the following statements about NITI Aayog:
1. It is a non-constitutional and non-statutory body.
2. It is the apex public policy think tank.
3. It is chaired by the Prime Minister.
4. It works on cooperative federalism.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
86.x: All four statements correctly describe NITI Aayog.
86.tq: Use the complete institutional profile when all listed attributes are mutually consistent.
86.sec: Executive - Cabinet, PMO, Cabinet Secretariat, NITI Aayog

86.s: A two-month review cycle for ₹50,999 crore worth of Amaravati contracts was ordered by the Chief Minister of which State?
86.x: The Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh ordered a two-month review cycle for ₹50,999 crore of Amaravati contracts, drawing on the Centre's PRAGATI model.
86.tq: Combine the amount, review period and location to identify the policy-monitoring example.
86.sec: Executive - Cabinet, PMO, Cabinet Secretariat, NITI Aayog

86.s: The Public Interest Litigation movement in India began in 1979 with a case filed on behalf of whom?
86.x: PIL began in 1979 with a case filed on behalf of prisoners, rather than by the prisoners themselves.
86.tq: Test the distinctive beneficiary-versus-petitioner feature of the origin of PIL.
86.sec: Judiciary - activism, PIL, court guidelines acting as law

86.s: Which of the following have been used as vehicles for courts to take up matters in the development of PIL?
86.x: Courts acted on newspaper reports and postcards in the development of PIL.
86.tq: Recall the unusual access routes associated with the early PIL process.
86.sec: Judiciary - activism, PIL, court guidelines acting as law

86.s: The constitutional basis associated with Public Interest Litigation and the Supreme Court's power to do complete justice includes which combination?
86.x: The identified basis comprises Articles 32, 226 and 142, with Article 142 providing the power to do complete justice.
86.tq: Match the constitutional provisions with the judicial mechanism they support.
86.sec: Judiciary - activism, PIL, court guidelines acting as law

86.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Case)
a. Vishaka
b. Prakash Singh
c. T.S.R. Subramanian

List-II (Guideline subject)
i. Civil Services Boards and written instructions
 ii. Workplace sexual harassment
 iii. Police reforms

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
86.x: Vishaka dealt with workplace sexual harassment, Prakash Singh with police reforms, and T.S.R. Subramanian with civil-services safeguards.
86.tq: Start from the sure Vishaka pair and complete the remaining case-to-guideline matches.
86.sec: Judiciary - activism, PIL, court guidelines acting as law

86.s: The Vishaka guidelines continued to operate in a legislative vacuum until the enactment of which law?
o: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955
86.x: The Vishaka guidelines on workplace sexual harassment operated until the POSH Act was enacted in 2013.
86.tq: Link the judicial guideline with the later legislation that occupied the legislative field.
86.sec: Judiciary - activism, PIL, court guidelines acting as law

86.s: Which of the following was NOT among the police reforms associated with the Prakash Singh judgment?
o: Abolition of the Police Establishment Board
Fixed tenure for the Director General of Police
86.x: The Prakash Singh reforms included a Police Establishment Board; its abolition was not one of the guidelines. They also included a State Security Commission, fixed DGP tenure and a Police Complaints Authority.
86.tq: Find the option that reverses an included institutional reform.
86.sec: Judiciary - activism, PIL, court guidelines acting as law

86.s: Which combination correctly represents the safeguards associated with the T.S.R. Subramanian judgment?
o: Civil Services Boards, fixed tenure for civil servants and written instructions from political executives
State Security Commission, Police Complaints Authority and separation of investigation from law and order
Workplace harassment guidelines and the POSH Act
86.x: T.S.R. Subramanian was associated with Civil Services Boards, fixed tenure for civil servants and written instructions from political executives.
86.tq: Distinguish civil-service safeguards from the police reforms of Prakash Singh.
86.sec: Judiciary - activism, PIL, court guidelines acting as law

86.s: Which one of the following is NOT included in Upendra Baxi's typology of fears concerning judicial activism?
86.x: Upendra Baxi's typology includes ideological, epistemic, management, legitimation and democratic fears. Electoral fear is not included in the listed typology.
86.tq: Use the complete named classification to identify the outsider.
86.sec: Judiciary - activism, PIL, court guidelines acting as law

86.s: The fact that police-reform orders are ignored is cited as evidence of which risk of judicial activism?
86.x: Ignoring police-reform orders illustrates the legitimation risk identified in the criticism of judicial activism.
86.tq: Apply the criticism category to the institutional example supplied.
86.sec: Judiciary - activism, PIL, court guidelines acting as law

86.s: Which of the following is identified as a consequence of excessive judicial overreach?
o: Expansion of the Rajya Sabha majority
Automatic passage of private members' bills
86.x: Excessive judicial overreach is associated with policy paralysis and backlog.
86.tq: Match the criticism of overreach with its stated administrative consequences.
86.sec: Judiciary - activism, PIL, court guidelines acting as law

86.s: An MP described the Supreme Court's orders concerning an NCERT Class 8 chapter on which subject as an instance of judicial overreach?
86.x: The orders concerning an NCERT Class 8 chapter on “corruption in judiciary” were described by an MP as judicial overreach.
86.tq: Recall the specific contemporary example rather than the general criticism.
86.sec: Judiciary - activism, PIL, court guidelines acting as law

86.s: Which principle was affirmed by the Supreme Court in the contemporary constitutionalism-related development mentioned?
o: Judicial guidelines automatically require constitutional amendment.
Parliament cannot make any law affecting rights.
Majoritarianism may override constitutionalism in all cases.
86.x: The Supreme Court held that majoritarianism cannot override constitutionalism.
86.tq: Reject the reversed constitutional principle and select the precise judicial proposition.
86.sec: Judiciary - activism, PIL, court guidelines acting as law

86.s: Which of the following correctly describes the permanent executive?
o: It is composed exclusively of private members of Parliament.
It consists only of Union ministers elected to Parliament.
It includes All-India Services, State services, local staff and PSU staff, and helps ministers formulate and implement policies.
It is limited to judges appointed under Article 124.
86.x: The permanent executive includes personnel from All-India Services, State services, local bodies and public sector undertakings, assisting ministers in policy formulation and implementation.
86.tq: Use the composition-and-function test to distinguish the permanent executive from the political executive.
86.sec: Bureaucracy - advice, drafting, implementation discretion

86.s: Which one of the following statements regarding bureaucracy is correct?
o: Bureaucracy can disregard legislative policy while implementing a scheme.
Bureaucracy alone determines the constitutional validity of laws.
Bureaucracy is bound by policies approved by the legislature.
Bureaucracy is not involved in policy formulation.
86.x: Although bureaucracy assists ministers in formulating and implementing policies, it remains bound by policy approved by the legislature.
86.tq: Distinguish administrative assistance and discretion from authority to override legislative policy.
86.sec: Bureaucracy - advice, drafting, implementation discretion

86.s: Recruitment to the principal civil services is conducted by which bodies?
o: The Supreme Court and High Courts
The Election Commission and Finance Commission
The UPSC and State Public Service Commissions
86.x: Recruitment is conducted by the Union Public Service Commission and the State Public Service Commissions.
86.tq: Match the recruitment function with the constitutionally recognised recruiting bodies.
86.sec: Bureaucracy - advice, drafting, implementation discretion

86.s: The members of the UPSC and State Public Service Commissions are removable only after an inquiry by which institution?
86.x: Members of the UPSC and State Public Service Commissions are removable only after an inquiry by the Supreme Court.
86.tq: Identify the authority associated with the special removal safeguard.
86.sec: Bureaucracy - advice, drafting, implementation discretion

86.s:
Which of the following are identified as concerns relating to bureaucracy?
1. Insensitivity to citizens
2. Political interference
3. Discretion at the front line
4. Complete absence of implementation discretion
Which of the statements given above are correct?
86.x: Insensitivity to citizens, political interference and frontline discretion are identified concerns. Statement 4 is false because implementation discretion is itself a concern.
86.tq: Reject the absolute reversal of a stated concern and retain the three applicable concerns.
86.sec: Bureaucracy - advice, drafting, implementation discretion

86.s: Which of the following is NOT an accountability tool mentioned in relation to bureaucracy?
86.x: Vigilance, conduct rules, the CAG, CVC and Lokpal are accountability tools for bureaucracy. A Presidential reference under Article 143 is a constitutional judicial-advisory mechanism, not a bureaucratic accountability tool.
86.tq: Separate administrative accountability mechanisms from a judicial-constitutional procedure.
86.sec: Bureaucracy - advice, drafting, implementation discretion

86.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding campaigns and laws:

List-I (Campaign)
a. MKSS right-to-information movement
b. Right to Work/NAC advocacy
c. Right to Food campaign

List-II (Law)
i. National Food Security Act, 2013
ii. RTI Act, 2005
iii. MGNREGA, 2005

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
86.x: The MKSS movement led to the RTI Act, 2005; Right to Work/NAC advocacy was associated with MGNREGA, 2005; and the Right to Food campaign contributed to the National Food Security Act, 2013.
86.tq: Start from the sure campaign-law pair and eliminate codes containing a wrong association.
86.sec: Civil society and pressure groups - campaigns that produced laws

86.s:
With reference to the stakeholders of governance, consider the following statements:
1. The State includes the legislature, judiciary, executive and bureaucracy.
2. The Market is one of the three broad stakeholder groups.
3. Civil society includes NGOs, voluntary organisations, media, trade unions, religious groups and pressure groups.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
86.x: All three statements are correct. Governance stakeholders include the State, the Market and Civil Society, with the listed institutions and organisations falling within these categories.

1. The year 2026 was declared the Technology-Driven Decision Making Year.
2. Artificial Intelligence is proposed for grievance redress.
3. Mana Mitra is described as WhatsApp Governance.
4. Sanjeevani is a digital health programme associated with ABHA IDs from August 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
88.x: All four statements are correct. The initiatives cover technology-driven decision-making, AI-based grievance redress, Mana Mitra WhatsApp Governance and the Sanjeevani digital health programme with ABHA IDs.
88.tq: Check several current-affairs facts by separating the year, technology, platform and health initiative.
88.sec: Universal angles

88.s: A Singapore delegation reviewed which system in Andhra Pradesh?
88.x: A Singapore delegation reviewed RTGS in Andhra Pradesh.
88.tq: Distinguish the reviewed financial system from other digital governance networks.
88.sec: Universal angles

88.s: At the Raisina Dialogue, the Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister spoke on which subject?
88.x: The subject of the speech was ‘Technology, governance and the future’.
88.tq: Recall the precise theme rather than substituting a related governance topic.
88.sec: Universal angles

88.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a significance of e-governance?
88.x: E-governance is associated with citizen engagement, better service delivery, fewer face-to-face contacts and audit trails. It does not remove audit trails; digital systems can strengthen them.
88.tq: Find the option that reverses a governance outcome while retaining the same vocabulary.
88.sec: Universal angles

89.s: The Citizens' Charter concept originated in which country and under which government?
o: India under the United Progressive Alliance Government in 1997
Australia under the Howard Government in 1996
The United Kingdom under the John Major Government in 1991
The United States under the Clinton Government in 1993
89.x: The Citizens' Charter originated in the United Kingdom in 1991 during the government of John Major.
89.tq: Use the origin-country and government pair to distinguish the concept from its later Indian adoption.
89.sec: Citizens' Charter - origin, purpose, elements, adoption in India

89.s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the six principles of the Citizens' Charter introduced in the United Kingdom?
89.x: The six principles were quality, choice, standards, value, accountability and transparency. Participation was not included in that list.
89.tq: Find the option outside the exact six-item list rather than relying on general governance terminology.
89.sec: Citizens' Charter - origin, purpose, elements, adoption in India

89.s: The six principles associated with the original Citizens' Charter are correctly represented by which of the following?
o: Choice, competition, secrecy, value, neutrality and standards
Equality, liberty, justice, participation, efficiency and transparency
Quality, choice, standards, value, accountability and transparency
Quality, consultation, legality, economy, participation and accountability
89.x: The original six principles were quality, choice, standards, value, accountability and transparency.
89.tq: Test the complete named list and reject options containing substituted governance terms.
89.sec: Citizens' Charter - origin, purpose, elements, adoption in India

89.s: Which of the following best describes the nature of a Citizens' Charter?
o: A constitutional guarantee enforceable directly in every court
An internal financial audit of government departments
A written commitment regarding service standards, time-bound delivery and grievance redress
A statutory code that automatically penalises every service delay
89.x: A Citizens' Charter records commitments on service standards, time-bound service delivery and grievance redress. It is not by itself a constitutionally or legally enforceable right.
89.tq: Choose the precise functional description while rejecting an overstatement of legal enforceability.
89.sec: Citizens' Charter - origin, purpose, elements, adoption in India

89.s:
Consider the following as basic elements of a Citizens' Charter:
1. Clear service standards
2. Information about services
3. A grievance redress mechanism
4. Contact details of responsible officers
Which of the statements given above are correct?
89.x: All four are basic elements: service standards, service information, grievance redress arrangements and details of responsible officers.
89.tq: Check each component against the complete-elements list before selecting the combined option.
89.sec: Citizens' Charter - origin, purpose, elements, adoption in India

89.s:
With reference to Citizens' Charters in India, consider the following statements:
1. They are legally enforceable rights in their present form.
2. They are generally non-justiciable.
3. The Second Administrative Reforms Commission recommended statutory status for them.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
89.x: Indian Citizens' Charters are generally non-justiciable and are not presently legally enforceable rights. The Second Administrative Reforms Commission recommended statutory status for them.
89.tq: Use the legal-status distinction to identify the false statement containing an absolute present claim.
89.sec: Citizens' Charter - origin, purpose, elements, adoption in India

89.s: India adopted the Citizens' Charter in:
89.x: India adopted the Citizens' Charter in 1997.
89.tq: Separate the original 1991 UK date from India's 1997 adoption date.
89.sec: Citizens' Charter - origin, purpose, elements, adoption in India

89.s: Which institution coordinates the formulation of Citizens' Charters in India?
o: Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances
89.x: The Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances, or DARPG, coordinates the formulation of Citizens' Charters.
89.tq: Identify the administrative department associated with governance reform rather than a constitutional body.
89.sec: Citizens' Charter - origin, purpose, elements, adoption in India

89.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched in relation to Citizens' Charters in India?
o: Coordinating body — Election Commission of India
Responsible officers — not named in ministries
89.x: The website associated with Citizens' Charters is goicharters.nic.in. DARPG coordinates their formulation and nodal officers are named in every ministry.
89.tq: Start with the sure website pair and eliminate options that reverse institutional responsibilities.
89.sec: Citizens' Charter - origin, purpose, elements, adoption in India

89.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Citizens Charter Bill, 2011:
1. It dealt with time-bound delivery of services and grievance redress.
2. It became law in 2014.
3. It lapsed with the dissolution of the Lok Sabha in 2014.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
89.x: The Bill concerned time-bound service delivery and grievance redress, but it did not become law. It lapsed when the Lok Sabha was dissolved in 2014.
89.tq: Spot the false legal-status statement while retaining the correct subject and lapse event.
89.sec: Citizens' Charter - origin, purpose, elements, adoption in India

89.s: Which one of the following Andhra Pradesh initiatives provided web-based online receipt, reply and monitoring of grievances at District Collectorates?
89.x: Prajavani was an earlier Andhra Pradesh initiative for online receipt, reply and monitoring of grievances at District Collectorates.
89.tq: Match the distinctive operational function with the correct platform rather than the later statewide portals.
89.sec: AP grievance platforms - period/government and purpose

89.s: Meekosam, meaning “For You”, was associated with which of the following?
89.x: Meekosam was introduced in 2015 during the TDP Government. It functioned as a single-window portal for grievances and suggestions, with status tracking and data analytics.
89.tq: Pair the platform with its period and government, avoiding confusion with Spandana.
89.sec: AP grievance platforms - period/government and purpose

89.s: Which of the following correctly describes Meekosam?
o: A pensioners-only grievance portal of the Union Government
A portal exclusively for social audits of MGNREGA works
A certification system for service-delivery capability
A single-window portal to lodge grievances and suggestions and track their status
89.x: Meekosam enabled citizens to lodge grievances and suggestions through a single window and track their status. Data analytics was also added to the platform.
89.tq: Use the portal's service function to distinguish it from audit, pension and certification systems.
89.sec: AP grievance platforms - period/government and purpose

89.s: Spandana was launched in Andhra Pradesh in 2019 during the government of:
89.x: Spandana was associated with the YSRCP Government in 2019 and served as a one-stop public grievance redressal platform.
89.tq: Discriminate between the two major AP grievance platforms by matching year and government.
89.sec: AP grievance platforms - period/government and purpose

89.s: Social audit is regarded as which of the following in relation to MGNREGA?
o: A replacement for the Gram Sabha
A method of calculating minimum wages
A process limited to departmental financial accounts
89.x: Social audit functions as an accountability tool under MGNREGA and enables community scrutiny of works and implementation.
89.tq: Choose the broad governance function rather than a narrow financial or administrative description.
89.sec: Social audit - MGNREGA, first law, AP society

89.s: Which State passed the first law making social audit of government programmes mandatory?
89.x: Meghalaya passed the first state law making social audit of government programmes mandatory in 2017.
89.tq: Distinguish the first state law from Andhra Pradesh's pioneering implementation institution.
89.sec: Social audit - MGNREGA, first law, AP society

89.s: The AP Society for Social Audit, Accountability and Transparency (SSAAT) was set up in:
89.x: SSAAT was established in Andhra Pradesh in 2009 as an independent society.
89.tq: Separate the establishment year of the AP institution from the MGNREGA and Meghalaya dates.
89.sec: Social audit - MGNREGA, first law, AP society

89.s:
Which of the following statements about SSAAT is correct?
1. It is an independent society.
2. It is associated with social audit, accountability and transparency.
3. Andhra Pradesh pioneered state-wide social audits of MGNREGA.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
89.x: SSAAT is an independent society concerned with social audit, accountability and transparency, and Andhra Pradesh pioneered state-wide MGNREGA social audits.
89.tq: Verify the institutional character, full name and state-level achievement together.
89.sec: Social audit - MGNREGA, first law, AP society

89.s: The concept of Right to Services Acts developed principally from which earlier idea?
89.x: The Right to Services concept grew out of the Citizens' Charter idea that public services should be delivered according to declared standards and timelines.
89.tq: Trace the conceptual relationship between service guarantees and Citizens' Charters.
89.sec: Right to Services Acts - origin, order of enactment, first state

89.s: Which State enacted the first Right to Services law in India?
89.x: The first such law was the Madhya Pradesh Lok Sewa Guarantee Act, 2010. Bihar followed in 2011.
89.tq: Distinguish the first state law from the later state sequence beginning with Punjab.
89.sec: Right to Services Acts - origin, order of enactment, first state

89.s:
Arrange the following States in the order associated with the enactment of Right to Services laws:
A. Gujarat
B. Punjab
C. Maharashtra
D. Assam
89.x: The order is Punjab, Assam, Gujarat and Maharashtra.
89.tq: Fix the first and last entries and then place Assam and Gujarat in the correct middle order.
89.sec: Right to Services Acts - origin, order of enactment, first state

89.s: Which of the following is NOT a normal feature of Right to Services legislation?
o: Automatic abolition of all departmental grievance mechanisms
A penalty on the responsible official
A right of appeal in case of delay
Notification of services to be delivered within a fixed time
89.x: Right to Services laws provide notified services within fixed time limits, appeals against delay and penalties for responsible officials. They do not automatically abolish all other grievance mechanisms.
89.tq: Identify the option that goes beyond the stated legal features and uses an absolute institutional claim.
89.sec: Right to Services Acts - origin, order of enactment, first state

89.s:
With reference to Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
