129.s: A complaint under the POSH Act is ordinarily required to be made within how many months from the date of the incident?
129.x: A complaint is ordinarily to be made within three months; this period may be extended by a further three months in appropriate circumstances.
129.tq: Recall the basic limitation period and distinguish it from the extension period.
129.sec: POSH Act 2013 - what it addresses, Vishaka, Internal and Local Committees, time limits

129.s: Which of the following correctly states the time limits under the POSH Act?
o: Complaint within 6 months, inquiry within 60 days and employer action within 90 days
Complaint within 3 months, inquiry within 90 days and employer action within 60 days
Complaint within 90 days, inquiry within 3 months and employer action within 6 months
Complaint within 3 months, inquiry within 60 days and employer action within 30 days
129.x: The complaint is ordinarily filed within three months, the inquiry is to be completed within 90 days, and the employer is to act within 60 days.
129.tq: Keep the three separate statutory periods distinct instead of swapping their order.
129.sec: POSH Act 2013 - what it addresses, Vishaka, Internal and Local Committees, time limits

129.s: Which of the following is NOT a stated duty of an employer under the POSH Act?
o: Displaying the policy relating to prevention of sexual harassment
Transferring every complainant to another workplace
129.x: Employer duties include constituting the Internal Committee, displaying the policy, conducting awareness programmes and acting on reports. Mandatory transfer of every complainant is not stated as a general duty.
129.tq: Find the option that imposes an absolute duty not included among the listed employer responsibilities.
129.sec: POSH Act 2013 - what it addresses, Vishaka, Internal and Local Committees, time limits

129.s: The penalty for failure to comply with the employer duties under the POSH framework may extend up to:
129.x: The penalty for failure to comply with the specified duties may extend up to ₹50,000.
129.tq: Test the exact monetary ceiling rather than the general nature of the penalty.
129.sec: POSH Act 2013 - what it addresses, Vishaka, Internal and Local Committees, time limits

129.s: SHe-Box 2.0, under Mission Shakti, is best described as:
o: A fund exclusively providing maternity benefits
An employment exchange for women in rural areas
A single-window online system for complaint and tracking of Internal and Local Committees
A criminal investigation portal for dowry deaths
129.x: SHe-Box 2.0 is a single-window online complaint and tracking system for Internal and Local Committees under Mission Shakti.
129.tq: Match the digital platform with its operational function rather than its broad women-welfare context.
129.sec: POSH Act 2013 - what it addresses, Vishaka, Internal and Local Committees, time limits

129.s:
With reference to SHe-Box 2.0, consider the following statements:
1. It is associated with the Ministry of Women and Child Development.
2. It covers public, private, organised and unorganised sectors.
3. The SHINE app was launched by the Railways for its staff.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: All three statements are correct. SHe-Box 2.0 is associated with the Ministry of Women and Child Development under Mission Shakti, while Railways launched the SHINE app for its staff.
129.tq: Combine institutional ownership, coverage and the related-app distinction without confusing the two platforms.
129.sec: POSH Act 2013 - what it addresses, Vishaka, Internal and Local Committees, time limits

129.s: According to the reported Andhra Pradesh implementation figures for 2025-26, which of the following is correct regarding POSH committees and cases?
o: 88 Local Committees, 86 Internal Committees and 10,437 cases resolved
26 Local Committees, 10,437 Internal Committees and all 88 cases pending
10 Local Committees, 26,437 Internal Committees and 88 of 86 cases resolved
26 Local Committees, 10,437 Internal Committees and 86 of 88 cases resolved
129.x: The reported figures were 26 Local Committees, 10,437 Internal Committees and 86 cases resolved out of 88.
129.tq: Read the three figures together and reject reversed counts and altered outcomes.
129.sec: POSH Act 2013 - what it addresses, Vishaka, Internal and Local Committees, time limits

129.s: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 is primarily classified as a:
129.x: The Act is a civil law protecting women from domestic violence, although other criminal provisions may also apply to related conduct.
129.tq: Discriminate between the civil character of the Act and criminal provisions dealing with particular offences.
129.sec: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005 - commencement, definition, Protection Officers, reliefs

129.s: Which of the following combinations correctly represents the forms of domestic violence covered under Section 3 of the Domestic Violence Act?
o: Physical, sexual, verbal or emotional, and economic abuse
129.x: Section 3 covers physical, sexual, verbal or emotional, and economic abuse.
129.tq: Recall the complete statutory classification rather than selecting a partial list.
129.sec: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005 - commencement, definition, Protection Officers, reliefs

129.s:
Consider the following statements about the scope of the Domestic Violence Act:
1. It protects a woman irrespective of the nature of her relationship with the respondent.
2. It applies only when the relationship has been formally registered.
3. Protection Officers and registered Service Providers assist the aggrieved woman.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is false because protection is not restricted to formally registered relationships.
129.tq: Spot the formal-registration limitation, which improperly narrows the Act's relationship-based protection.
129.sec: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005 - commencement, definition, Protection Officers, reliefs

129.s: Protection Officers under the Domestic Violence Act are appointed by the:
129.x: Protection Officers are appointed by the State Government. Registered Service Providers also assist the aggrieved woman.
129.tq: Ask which level of government holds the appointing authority.
129.sec: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005 - commencement, definition, Protection Officers, reliefs

129.s:
Match the relief under the Domestic Violence Act with its section:

List-I (Relief)
 a. Protection order
 b. Residence order
 c. Monetary relief
 d. Compensation order

List-II (Section)
 i. Section 20
 ii. Section 22
 iii. Section 18
 iv. Section 19

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
129.x: Protection orders are under Section 18, residence orders under Section 19, monetary relief under Section 20 and compensation orders under Section 22.
129.tq: Start with the familiar protection-order provision and verify the sequential relief sections.
129.sec: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005 - commencement, definition, Protection Officers, reliefs

129.s: Which of the following statements regarding reliefs under the Domestic Violence Act is correct?
o: Several forms of relief may be sought in one case and the matter is to be disposed of within 60 days.
Relief is limited to compensation and does not include residence rights.
Only one form of relief can be sought in a case.
Temporary custody cannot be granted under the Act.
129.x: Multiple reliefs may be sought in one case, including residence, protection, monetary relief, temporary custody and compensation; disposal is contemplated within 60 days.
129.tq: Reject absolute restrictions by applying the Act's cumulative-relief structure and time limit.
129.sec: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005 - commencement, definition, Protection Officers, reliefs

129.s: In Andhra Pradesh, which of the following have been identified as Protection Officers for implementation of the Domestic Violence Act?
o: DWCDA Project Directors and Revenue Divisional Officers
Police Superintendents and Village Secretaries only
District Collectors and Municipal Commissioners only
Judicial Magistrates and Members of Parliament
129.x: In Andhra Pradesh, DWCDA Project Directors and Revenue Divisional Officers are identified as Protection Officers.
129.tq: Identify the specific state-level implementation authorities rather than generic administrative officers.
129.sec: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005 - commencement, definition, Protection Officers, reliefs

129.s: Which of the following correctly reflects the reported Andhra Pradesh implementation figures for 2024-25 under the Domestic Violence Act?
o: 55 NGOs as Service Providers, 47,734 petitions, 23,644 Domestic Incident Reports and 7,307 final orders
47,734 NGOs, 55 petitions, 7,307 reports and 23,644 final orders
55 NGOs as Protection Officers, 47,734 petitions, 23,644 final orders and 7,307 reports
23,644 NGOs, 7,307 petitions, 55 reports and 47,734 final orders
129.x: The reported figures were 55 NGOs as Service Providers, 47,734 petitions, 23,644 Domestic Incident Reports and 7,307 final orders.
129.tq: Keep the institutional count and three case figures in their correct categories.
129.sec: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005 - commencement, definition, Protection Officers, reliefs

129.s: According to the reported Andhra Pradesh figures for 2025-26, which statement is correct?
o: 2,207 cases were addressed and ₹51,581 crore was paid.
51,581 cases were addressed and ₹9 crore relief was paid to 2,207 victims.
9 crore cases were addressed and 51,581 victims received relief.
129.x: The reported figures were 51,581 cases addressed, ₹9 crore relief paid and 2,207 victims assisted through the relief payment.
129.tq: Match each number with its unit—cases, money or victims—before selecting the option.
129.sec: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005 - commencement, definition, Protection Officers, reliefs

129.s: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, voyeurism is dealt with under Section:
129.x: Voyeurism is dealt with under Section 77 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, corresponding to Section 354C of the IPC.
129.tq: Recall the exact BNS section and distinguish neighbouring sexual-offence provisions.
129.sec: Criminal provisions under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 - cruelty, dowry death, stalking, voyeurism

129.s: Stalking under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is associated with Section:
129.x: Stalking is covered by Section 78 of the BNS, corresponding to Section 354D of the IPC.
129.tq: Use the adjacent-section comparison to distinguish stalking from voyeurism and cruelty.
129.sec: Criminal provisions under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 - cruelty, dowry death, stalking, voyeurism

129.s: Dowry death under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is provided under Section 80. Its corresponding provision under the Indian Penal Code was:
129.x: BNS Section 80 deals with dowry death, corresponding to IPC Section 304B.
129.tq: Link the new BNS provision with its corresponding old IPC provision without swapping it with cruelty.
129.sec: Criminal provisions under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 - cruelty, dowry death, stalking, voyeurism

129.s: Cruelty by a husband or his relatives is covered under which provision of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
129.x: Cruelty by a husband or relatives is covered under BNS Sections 85-86, corresponding to IPC Section 498A.
129.tq: Distinguish the cruelty provision from the nearby dowry-death provision by section number.
129.sec: Criminal provisions under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 - cruelty, dowry death, stalking, voyeurism

129.s: For the purpose of the dowry-death provision, the relevant death is one occurring within how many years of marriage?
129.x: The dowry-death provision refers to a death occurring within seven years of marriage.
129.tq: Recall the statutory time threshold and avoid substituting common alternative periods.
129.sec: Criminal provisions under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 - cruelty, dowry death, stalking, voyeurism

129.s:
Match the offence with the corresponding BNS provision:

List-I (Offence)
 a. Rape
 b. Trafficking of persons
 c. Selling or buying minors for prostitution
 d. Acid attack

List-II (BNS provision)
 i. Sections 98-99
 ii. Sections 63-64
 iii. Section 124
 iv. Section 143

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
129.x: Rape is covered by Sections 63-64, trafficking by Section 143, selling or buying minors for prostitution by Sections 98-99, and acid attack by Section 124.
129.tq: Begin with the sure rape pair and use elimination to place the remaining BNS provisions.
129.sec: Criminal provisions under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 - cruelty, dowry death, stalking, voyeurism

129.s:
Consider the following statements regarding selected provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023:
1. Sections 74 and 75 deal respectively with outraging the modesty of a woman and sexual harassment.
2. Section 67 concerns intercourse with a separated wife and prescribes imprisonment of two to seven years.
3. Section 124 concerns trafficking of persons.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because Section 124 concerns acid attack; trafficking of persons is covered under Section 143.
129.tq: Catch the swapped-offence trap between the acid-attack and trafficking provisions.
129.sec: Criminal provisions under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 - cruelty, dowry death, stalking, voyeurism

129.s: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, rape is dealt with under Sections 63-64, corresponding to which IPC provisions?
129.x: BNS Sections 63-64 correspond to IPC Sections 375-376. The stated exception excludes a wife aged 18 years or above from the rape provision.
129.tq: Match the new section pair with the correct old-code pair rather than a neighbouring offence pair.
129.sec: Criminal provisions under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 - cruelty, dowry death, stalking, voyeurism

129.s: Under BNSS Section 144, maintenance of wives is available:
o: Only to wives belonging to a specified religion
Only when domestic violence has been proved
Only when the marriage is less than seven years old
129.x: BNSS Section 144 provides for maintenance of wives regardless of religion; it corresponds to old CrPC Section 125.
129.tq: Reject the religion-based limitation and apply the express universal qualification.
129.sec: Criminal provisions under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 - cruelty, dowry death, stalking, voyeurism

129.s: The Supreme Court is examining the marital rape exception in relation to which of the following provisions?
o: The domestic-violence relief provisions under Sections 17-22
The rape provisions under BNS Sections 63-64
The maintenance provision under BNSS Section 144
The trafficking provision under BNS Section 143
129.x: The Supreme Court is examining the marital rape exception associated with the rape provisions under BNS Sections 63-64.
129.tq: Connect the constitutional-legal issue with the relevant offence provision rather than a related women-protection law.
129.sec: Criminal provisions under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 - cruelty, dowry death, stalking, voyeurism

129.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the services provided by One Stop Centres (Sakhi)?
o: Medical, legal, counselling and shelter services under one roof
Only emergency police assistance and prosecution
Vocational training and permanent employment exclusively
Only temporary shelter and financial assistance
129.x: One Stop Centres, also known as Sakhi centres, provide medical, legal, counselling and shelter services under one roof to women affected by violence.
129.tq: Identify the option that combines the complete service package rather than a single function.
129.sec: Legal aid and support institutions - One Stop Centres, Women Helpline, fast track courts

129.s:
Consider the following statements regarding legal aid and support institutions in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Women Helpline 181 provides emergency help and counselling.
2. ERSS 112 is a single emergency number supported through the Nirbhaya Fund.
3. Women Help Desks function in police stations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: All three statements are correct. Women Helpline 181 provides emergency help and counselling, ERSS 112 is the single emergency number, and Women Help Desks operate in police stations.
129.tq: Check each institution against its specific function before selecting the combined code.
129.sec: Legal aid and support institutions - One Stop Centres, Women Helpline, fast track courts

129.s: As per the Andhra Pradesh figures cited for the relevant period, which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: One Stop Centres — 3 lakh plus calls
129.x: The cited Andhra Pradesh figures record 3,590 women helped through One Stop Centres and more than three lakh calls to Women Helpline 181.
129.tq: Match each numerical figure with the institution to which it specifically relates.
129.sec: Legal aid and support institutions - One Stop Centres, Women Helpline, fast track courts

129.s:
With reference to Fast Track Special Courts, consider the following statements:
1. There were 743 functional courts.
2. Of these, 394 were exclusive POCSO courts.
3. They had disposed of 3,39,644 cases as on 31 July 2025.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: All three statements are correct: 743 Fast Track Special Courts were functional, including 394 exclusive POCSO courts, and 3,39,644 cases had been disposed of by 31 July 2025.
129.tq: Treat the court total, the exclusive POCSO subset and the disposal figure as separate numerical facts.
129.sec: Legal aid and support institutions - One Stop Centres, Women Helpline, fast track courts

129.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with Shakti Sadans in Andhra Pradesh?
129.x: The Andhra Pradesh figures mention 26 Shakti Sadans sheltering 950 trafficked women.
129.tq: Use the institution-specific numerical pair and reject figures belonging to other support mechanisms.
129.sec: Legal aid and support institutions - One Stop Centres, Women Helpline, fast track courts

129.s: Free legal aid for women and other eligible persons is provided through which institutional mechanism?
129.x: Free legal aid is provided through the Legal Services Authorities. Courts and police desks may support access to justice but are not the institution identified for providing free legal aid.
129.tq: Distinguish the institution providing legal aid from institutions providing emergency, police or judicial support.
129.sec: Legal aid and support institutions - One Stop Centres, Women Helpline, fast track courts

129.s: According to UNODC trafficking findings, which one of the following countries is identified as both a high origin country and a high destination country?
129.x: Bangladesh, India, Nepal and Pakistan are identified as high origin countries, while India and Pakistan are also identified as high destination countries.
129.tq: Separate the overlapping origin-and-destination category from countries listed only as origins.
129.sec: Trafficking - UNODC GLOTIP findings, US TIP tiers, forms

129.s: The GLOTIP 2016 finding that traffickers and victims often share the same national or ethnic background relates to which aspect of trafficking?
o: The compulsory involvement of only foreign nationals
The classification of countries into US TIP tiers
The social and demographic relationship between traffickers and victims
The exclusive role of state agencies in trafficking
129.x: GLOTIP 2016 highlighted that traffickers and victims often come from the same national or ethnic background. This is a finding about the relationship between perpetrators and victims, not about TIP classification.
129.tq: Identify the precise subject of the finding instead of confusing it with country ranking or tier classification.
129.sec: Trafficking - UNODC GLOTIP findings, US TIP tiers, forms

129.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the US Trafficking in Persons Report tiers:

List-I
 a. Tier 1
 b. Tier 2
 c. Tier 2 Watch List
 d. Tier 3

List-II
 i. Does not fully meet minimum standards but is making significant efforts
 ii. Not making significant efforts
 iii. Fully meets the minimum standards
 iv. Special watch-list category associated with Tier 2

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
129.x: Tier 1 fully meets the minimum standards; Tier 2 does not fully meet them but is making significant efforts; Tier 2 Watch List is the watch-list category; and Tier 3 represents countries not making significant efforts.
129.tq: Start with the sure pair Tier 1–fully meets standards and eliminate codes that disturb it.
129.sec: Trafficking - UNODC GLOTIP findings, US TIP tiers, forms

129.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the forms of trafficking covered by the CLA 2013 definition?
129.x: The listed forms include sex trafficking, forced or bonded labour, child trafficking, slavery and servitude, and organ removal. Voluntary migration without exploitation is not one of these forms.
129.tq: Find the option that falls outside the stated list and does not involve exploitation.
129.sec: Trafficking - UNODC GLOTIP findings, US TIP tiers, forms

129.s: The CLA 2013 definition covers the listed forms of trafficking irrespective of which factor?
129.x: The CLA 2013 definition covers the specified forms of trafficking irrespective of consent.
129.tq: Focus on the qualifying phrase that applies across all listed forms.
129.sec: Trafficking - UNODC GLOTIP findings, US TIP tiers, forms

129.s: Which one of the following statements regarding India’s international obligations is correct?
o: India has ratified only the US Trafficking in Persons Report.
India has rejected all protocols concerning transnational organised crime.
India has ratified the UN Convention against Transnational Organized Crime and its protocols.
India has ratified only conventions relating to domestic labour and not transnational crime.
129.x: India has ratified the UN Convention against Transnational Organized Crime and its protocols.
129.tq: Distinguish a binding international convention and its protocols from an assessment report or domestic law.
129.sec: Trafficking - UNODC GLOTIP findings, US TIP tiers, forms

129.s: The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956 was originally known as the:
o: Protection of Women from Traffic Act
129.x: The law originally started as the Suppression of Immoral Traffic Act, commonly abbreviated as SITA, and was later renamed the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act.
129.tq: Test the original title directly, a common law-name confusion point.
129.sec: Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act 1956 and the Trafficking in Persons Bill

129.s: The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956 gives effect to which international instrument?
o: The 1948 Universal Declaration of Human Rights alone
The 1992 UN Framework Convention on Climate Change
129.x: The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act gives effect to the 1950 UN Convention relating to trafficking and exploitation.
129.tq: Match the domestic law with the specific international instrument it implements.
129.sec: Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act 1956 and the Trafficking in Persons Bill

129.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the scope of the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956?
o: It penalises activities such as brothel-keeping, living on the earnings of prostitution, soliciting, detaining persons and clients, but does not criminalise prostitution itself.
It regulates only the registration of protective homes and does not prescribe offences.
It deals exclusively with child trafficking and has no application to brothel-keeping.
It criminalises prostitution itself in every circumstance.
129.x: The Act does not criminalise prostitution itself. It penalises specified activities including brothel-keeping, living on prostitution earnings, soliciting, detaining people and clients.
129.tq: Separate the underlying activity from the exploitative or facilitating activities made punishable by the law.
129.sec: Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act 1956 and the Trafficking in Persons Bill

129.s: Under the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, protective homes are run by:
129.x: The Act provides for protective homes run by the States.
129.tq: Ask which authority operates the protective institution rather than which authority frames the law.
129.sec: Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act 1956 and the Trafficking in Persons Bill

129.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Trafficking in Persons (Prevention, Protection and Rehabilitation) Bill, 2018:
1. It was passed by the Lok Sabha.
2. It lapsed.
3. A draft dealing with the subject followed in 2021.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: The 2018 Bill was passed by the Lok Sabha but later lapsed, and a 2021 draft followed it.
129.tq: Track the legislative sequence: passage, lapse and subsequent draft.
129.sec: Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act 1956 and the Trafficking in Persons Bill

129.s: The Victim Protection Plan is intended to provide which of the following through a common protocol?
o: Legal aid, education, skills and livelihood support for rescued victims
129.x: The Victim Protection Plan provides a common protocol for legal aid, education, skills and livelihood support to rescued victims.
129.tq: Select the option containing the complete rehabilitation-support package.
129.sec: Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act 1956 and the Trafficking in Persons Bill

129.s: Ujjawala, launched in 2007, covered which combination of activities?
o: Only prosecution and conviction of traffickers
Prevention, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of trafficking victims
129.x: Ujjawala covered prevention, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of trafficking victims.
129.tq: Recall the four-part programme design instead of reducing the scheme to rescue alone.
129.sec: Prevention, rescue and rehabilitation - Ujjawala, AHTUs

129.s: Ujjawala is now part of which institutional framework under Mission Shakti?
o: Legal Services Authorities, through Women Helpline 181
129.x: Ujjawala is now part of Shakti Sadan under the Samarthya component of Mission Shakti, providing integrated relief homes for trafficked and destitute women.
129.tq: Distinguish the rehabilitation framework from emergency response, judicial and legal-aid mechanisms.
129.sec: Prevention, rescue and rehabilitation - Ujjawala, AHTUs

129.s: Which information system shares real-time alerts on trafficking across States?
129.x: Cri-MAC is the Ministry of Home Affairs information technology initiative that shares real-time crime and trafficking alerts across States and supports inter-State coordination.
129.tq: Use the function-based distinction between an alert-sharing system, an emergency number and a global report.
129.sec: Prevention, rescue and rehabilitation - Ujjawala, AHTUs

129.s: The protection under Article 23(1) is available to:
o: Citizens and non-citizens, and operates against the State as well as private persons
Citizens only, unless Parliament extends it to private persons
Citizens only and operates only against the State
Non-citizens only and operates only against private persons
129.x: Article 23 is available to both citizens and non-citizens and can be enforced against the State as well as private persons.
129.tq: Check both dimensions separately: beneficiaries of the right and entities against whom it operates.
129.sec: Constitutional article on traffic in human beings and forced labour

129.s: Which one of the following correctly states the scope of Article 23(2)?
o: It applies only to foreign nationals performing public service.
It permits compulsory service only for persons belonging to a particular caste.
It permits compulsory service for public purposes without discrimination on religion, race, caste or class.
It prohibits every form of compulsory service, including service for public purposes.
129.x: Article 23(2) permits the State to impose compulsory service for public purposes, but it cannot discriminate on grounds of religion, race, caste or class.
129.tq: Distinguish the prohibition in Article 23(1) from the qualified constitutional permission in Article 23(2).
129.sec: Constitutional article on traffic in human beings and forced labour

129.s: Which of the following pairs of enabling laws is correctly associated with Article 23?
o: ITPA 1956 and Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act 1976
Maternity Benefit Act and RPwD Act alone
Forest Rights Act 2006 and Arms Act 1959
129.x: The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956 and the Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976 are enabling laws associated with Article 23.
129.tq: Match the constitutional right with laws directly addressing trafficking and bonded labour.
129.sec: Constitutional article on traffic in human beings and forced labour

129.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 24 prohibits the employment of a child below 14 years in factories, mines or hazardous work.
2. Article 21, understood as the right to life with dignity, forms the basis of mandatory victim rehabilitation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
129.x: Both statements are correct. Article 24 protects children below 14 from employment in factories, mines or hazardous work, while Article 21’s life-with-dignity principle supports mandatory victim rehabilitation.
129.tq: Test the distinction between the child-labour prohibition in Article 24 and the dignity-based rehabilitation principle under Article 21.
129.sec: Constitutional article on traffic in human beings and forced labour

129.s:
Under the directions associated with Laxmi v. Union of India, acid may be sold over the counter only when:
1. The purchaser produces a photo identity document.
2. The sale is recorded in a sales register.
3. The purchaser is not below 18 years of age.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: The Laxmi case directions require photo identification, entry in a sales register and prohibition of sale to anyone below 18 years.
129.tq: Verify each safeguard separately before accepting the complete regulatory combination.
129.sec: Acid attacks - Laxmi case, sale regulation, compensation

129.s: What minimum compensation was directed for victims of acid attacks in Laxmi v. Union of India?
129.x: Victims of acid attacks were directed to receive compensation of at least ₹3 lakh.
129.tq: Use the statutory minimum rather than confusing it with a higher discretionary amount.
129.sec: Acid attacks - Laxmi case, sale regulation, compensation

129.s: Apart from compensation, victims of acid attacks are entitled to:
o: Automatic government employment in every case
129.x: The directions associated with Laxmi v. Union of India provide free treatment for acid-attack victims in addition to compensation.
129.tq: Identify the immediate medical remedy linked with the compensation direction.
129.sec: Acid attacks - Laxmi case, sale regulation, compensation

129.s: Which one of the following correctly states the legal provisions and punishment relating to acid attacks as given in the relevant framework?
o: Sections 326A and 326B of the IPC, now BNS 124; minimum punishment is 10 years, extendable to life imprisonment.
Sections 302 and 304 of the IPC, now BNS 124; minimum punishment is five years.
Sections 354A and 354B of the IPC, now BNS 181; punishment is fine only.
Sections 124A and 124B of the IPC, now BNS 326; maximum punishment is two years.
129.x: Acid-attack offences were covered by Sections 326A and 326B of the IPC and are now identified as BNS 124 in the cited framework. The punishment is a minimum of 10 years, extendable to life imprisonment.
129.tq: Keep the section numbers, new code reference and punishment range together to avoid statute-number swaps.
129.sec: Acid attacks - Laxmi case, sale regulation, compensation

129.s: The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 treats acid-attack injuries as:
o: A form of temporary unemployment only
A disability eligible for disability benefits
129.x: The RPwD Act, 2016 lists acid-attack injuries as a disability, thereby enabling victims to receive disability benefits.
129.tq: Distinguish the disability-law consequence from the criminal-law punishment for the same harm.
129.sec: Acid attacks - Laxmi case, sale regulation, compensation

129.s: According to the current assessment cited, approximately how many dowry deaths occur in India per day?
129.x: The assessment places the incidence at approximately 20 dowry deaths per day.
129.tq: Use the precise numerical figure rather than an approximate distractor.
129.sec: Universal angles

129.s: The annual number of dowry deaths referred to in the current assessment is best represented by which of the following?
129.x: The assessment refers to more than 6,000 dowry deaths annually.
129.tq: Distinguish the annual magnitude from the daily estimate.
129.sec: Universal angles

129.s: Which of the following States are identified as leading in the incidence of dowry deaths?
o: Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh
Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan
Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand
129.x: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan are identified as the leading States in the cited assessment.
129.tq: Test the exact membership of a named group rather than a single State.
129.sec: Universal angles

129.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the implementation of the POSH framework in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Twenty-six Local Committees have been formed.
2. Ten thousand four hundred and thirty-seven Internal Committees have been formed.
3. Eighty-six out of eighty-eight POSH cases have been resolved.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: All three statements are correct: Andhra Pradesh has 26 Local Committees, 10,437 Internal Committees, and 86 of 88 POSH cases were resolved.
129.tq: Retain the exact committee counts and the resolved-case ratio before selecting the combined option.
129.sec: Universal angles

129.s: With reference to the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act in Andhra Pradesh, which one of the following combinations is correct?
o: 51,581 cases and relief of Rs 9 crore
26 cases and relief of Rs 10,437 crore
88 cases and relief of Rs 86 crore
6,000 cases and relief of Rs 20 crore
129.x: The Andhra Pradesh data refer to 51,581 cases under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act and relief amounting to Rs 9 crore.
129.tq: Match the numerical case figure with its corresponding relief amount.
129.sec: Universal angles

129.s: Which one of the following best describes the legal character of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act as highlighted in the current debate?
o: It is a law applicable only to workplace harassment.
It is exclusively a criminal law and provides no civil remedies.
It is exclusively a constitutional remedy.
It is only civil in nature.
129.x: The criticism highlighted is that the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act is only civil in nature.
129.tq: Discriminate between civil domestic-violence remedies and criminal-law provisions.
129.sec: Universal angles

129.s: The rape conviction rate in 2023, as referred to in the current assessment, was approximately:
129.x: The rape conviction rate in 2023 was cited as 22.7%.
129.tq: Separate the latest figure from the earlier-period range used as a distractor.
129.sec: Universal angles

129.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the trend in the rape conviction rate:
1. The rate in 2023 was 22.7%.
2. It was lower than the rate recorded during 2018–2022.
3. The rate during 2018–2022 was in the range of 27–28%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: All three statements are correct. The 2023 conviction rate was 22.7%, compared with approximately 27–28% during 2018–2022.
129.tq: Compare the latest percentage with the earlier range and identify the direction of change.
129.sec: Universal angles

129.s: A film chamber makes submission of an Internal Complaints Committee report compulsory before granting publicity clearance to a film. This measure is most directly associated with which legislation?
o: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
129.x: The compulsory Internal Complaints Committee report is linked to compliance under the POSH Act, 2013.
129.tq: Identify the governing law from the institutional mechanism involved.
129.sec: Universal angles

129.s: Which of the following has been identified as a reason for the continuing ineffectiveness of anti-dowry laws?
o: Poor enforcement, faulty FIRs and disguising cases as accidents or suicides
Excessive conviction rates and compulsory mediation in every case
Absence of any statutory prohibition of dowry
129.x: Poor enforcement, faulty First Information Reports, and presenting dowry-death cases as accidents or suicides are identified as major reasons for ineffectiveness.
129.tq: Select the option containing the complete cause-effect chain rather than an absolute claim.
129.sec: Universal angles

129.s: A special court in which place awarded life imprisonment in a dowry-death case dating from 2020?
129.x: A special court in Guntur awarded life imprisonment in a dowry-death case from 2020.
129.tq: Test the precise location associated with the judicial action.
129.sec: Universal angles

129.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Dowry Prohibition Act — mandatory film publicity clearance report
Section 498A — claims of misuse and heavy under-reporting
129.x: Mandatory film publicity clearance based on an Internal Complaints Committee report is associated with POSH compliance, not the Dowry Prohibition Act. The other pairs reflect the issues highlighted in the debate.
129.tq: Find the mismatched law-mechanism pair by separating subject areas.
129.sec: Universal angles

129.s:
Consider the following statements about the debates surrounding laws concerning women:
1. The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act involves an overlap between prostitution and trafficking concerns.
2. Section 498A has been associated with both claims of misuse and heavy under-reporting.
3. The debate on Section 498A is limited exclusively to the question of conviction rates.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the debate includes misuse claims as well as heavy under-reporting, not only conviction rates.
129.tq: Reject the extreme word 'exclusively' when the issue has two stated dimensions.
129.sec: Universal angles

129.s: Which of the following sets of data sources and subjects is correctly associated with the Andhra Pradesh angle?
o: APSES and CDI AP SES — PWDVA, POSH committees and Shakti Sadans
LENS and TH — parliamentary constituencies and river basins
ITPA and Section 498A — Internal Complaints Committees and Shakti Sadans
POSH Act and Maternity Benefit Act — dowry-death conviction rates only
129.x: The Andhra Pradesh angle refers to APSES and CDI AP SES data concerning PWDVA, POSH committees and Shakti Sadans.
129.tq: Match the named data sources with the subjects covered by the State-level data.
129.sec: Universal angles

130.s: The Disha Bill of Andhra Pradesh was introduced primarily as a response to:
130.x: The Disha Bill was Andhra Pradesh’s legislative response to the 2019 Hyderabad veterinarian rape-murder case.
130.tq: Match the legislation with the immediate triggering event.
130.sec: AP initiatives - Disha Bill/Act, Disha police stations and Disha app

130.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Disha Act of Andhra Pradesh:
1. It provides for investigation of rape cases within seven days.
2. It provides for completion of trial within fourteen days.
3. It mandates a special court in every district.
4. It makes forensic evidence mandatory.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: The Disha Act provides for a seven-day investigation, a fourteen-day trial, mandatory special courts in every district and mandatory forensic evidence.
130.tq: Check each provision separately before selecting the coded combination.
130.sec: AP initiatives - Disha Bill/Act, Disha police stations and Disha app

130.s: Under the Disha Act, the prescribed time structure for investigation and trial of rape cases is:
o: Investigation in 14 days and trial in 7 days
Investigation in 14 days and trial in 21 days
Investigation in 7 days and trial in 14 days
Investigation in 21 days and trial in 14 days
130.x: The Disha Act specifies seven days for investigation and fourteen days for trial, making a total of twenty-one days.
130.tq: Separate the two components of the total time limit.
130.sec: AP initiatives - Disha Bill/Act, Disha police stations and Disha app

130.s: Which one of the following is NOT associated with the provisions of the Disha Act?
o: Mandatory forensic evidence in relevant cases
Death sentence for rape and gang rape
Penalties for cyber-stalking and deepfake misuse
A special court only at the State capital
130.x: The Disha Act provides for a special court in every district, not merely one special court at the State capital.
130.tq: Find the option that reverses the scope of a stated institutional provision.
130.sec: AP initiatives - Disha Bill/Act, Disha police stations and Disha app

130.s: Why does the Disha Act require the assent of the President of India?
o: It seeks to amend the Constitution.
It deals with subjects exclusively placed in the Union List.
It creates a new High Court in Andhra Pradesh.
Criminal law is included in the Concurrent List.
130.x: The Disha Act requires Presidential assent because criminal law falls in the Concurrent List. It has not come into force as passed.
130.tq: Ask which constitutional distribution of legislative power explains the requirement.
130.sec: AP initiatives - Disha Bill/Act, Disha police stations and Disha app

130.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Disha App — SOS alerts for women in distress or danger
2. Abhayam — Chittoor police awareness campaign for the safety of women and children
3. Abhay pilot — Free pick-up and drop for women stranded between 9 p.m. and 5 a.m.
4. Mahila Samrakshana Karyadarsi — Women-protection functionaries in village and ward secretariats
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
130.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Abhayam was associated with Chittoor, while the Abhay pilot was implemented by Prakasam police at Ongole.
130.tq: Verify the purpose and location attached to each similarly named initiative.
130.sec: AP initiatives - Disha Bill/Act, Disha police stations and Disha app

130.s: The Abhay pilot, associated with Prakasam police, provided:
o: An online portal for reporting cybercrime
Free pick-up and drop for women stranded between 9 p.m. and 5 a.m.
Free legal aid in every district court
130.x: The Abhay pilot provided free pick-up and drop facilities for women stranded between 9 p.m. and 5 a.m.
130.tq: Distinguish the operational service from awareness and technology initiatives.
130.sec: AP initiatives - Disha Bill/Act, Disha police stations and Disha app

130.s: Which of the following statements about recent Andhra Pradesh measures is correct?
o: Shakti Teams are used along with Sexual Offender Sheets of repeat offenders.
Sexual Offender Sheets are maintained only for first-time offenders.
Shakti Teams are special courts under the Disha Act.
Trishul committees deal exclusively with cybercrime.
130.x: Shakti Teams are used along with Sexual Offender Sheets for repeat offenders. Trishul committees have a broader three-part zero-tolerance mandate.
130.tq: Use the institutional-function distinction to reject swapped roles.
130.sec: AP initiatives - Disha Bill/Act, Disha police stations and Disha app

130.s:
The Trishul committees in Andhra Pradesh are associated with which of the following objectives?
1. Zero drugs
2. Zero tolerance to atrocities against women
3. Zero road accidents
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
130.x: Trishul committees are described as state and district panels pursuing zero drugs, zero tolerance to atrocities against women and zero road accidents.
130.tq: Treat a three-part slogan as three separate testable components.
130.sec: AP initiatives - Disha Bill/Act, Disha police stations and Disha app

130.s: According to the reported APPCA figure of March 2026, crimes against women in Andhra Pradesh fell by:
130.x: The reported decline in crimes against women was 4.4 percent, with Shakti Teams and Sexual Offender Sheets being associated with the measure.
130.tq: Read percentage options carefully and avoid reversing the reported trend.
130.sec: AP initiatives - Disha Bill/Act, Disha police stations and Disha app

130.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) ITSSO
(b) NDSO
(c) CCTNS
(d) Cri-MAC

List-II
(i) Links police stations
(ii) National database of convicted sexual offenders
(iii) Tracks time-bound investigation of sexual offences
(iv) Real-time sharing of information on significant crimes

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
130.x: ITSSO tracks investigation timelines; NDSO is the database of convicted sexual offenders; CCTNS links police stations; Cri-MAC enables real-time crime information sharing.
130.tq: Start with the distinctive purpose of each database and then eliminate codes.
130.sec: Crime databases and safety IT initiatives → purpose

130.s: The National Database on Sexual Offenders (NDSO) is best described as:
o: A police-only database of convicted sexual offenders
A public database of all persons accused of any offence
A database linking all State police stations
A database of missing children maintained by courts
130.x: NDSO, established by the NCRB in 2018, is a police-only national database of convicted sexual offenders.
130.tq: Distinguish convicted offenders from accused persons and identify the user group.
130.sec: Crime databases and safety IT initiatives → purpose

130.s: Which one of the following initiatives is maintained by the National Crime Records Bureau and links police stations?
130.x: CCTNS links police stations under the National e-Governance Plan and is maintained by the NCRB.
130.tq: Identify the correct body-function combination.
130.sec: Crime databases and safety IT initiatives → purpose

130.s: Cri-MAC primarily facilitates:
o: Online payment of compensation to victims
Real-time sharing of information on significant crimes and inter-State coordination
Registration of convicted offenders in a public database
130.x: Cri-MAC, or Crime Multi-Agency Centre, facilitates real-time sharing of information on significant crimes, including human trafficking, and supports inter-State coordination.
130.tq: Use the expansion of the acronym and its coordination function together.
130.sec: Crime databases and safety IT initiatives → purpose

130.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. ITSSO tracks the time-bound investigation of sexual-offence cases.
2. The Cyber Crime Reporting Portal facilitates online complaints, particularly relating to crimes against women and children.
3. The helpline associated with cybercrime reporting is 1930.
4. ERSS provides the single emergency number 112.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: All four statements are correct. ITSSO tracks sexual-offence investigations, the cybercrime portal accepts online complaints, 1930 is the cybercrime helpline and ERSS uses 112.
130.tq: Group related digital safety services but test their distinct functions and numbers.
130.sec: Crime databases and safety IT initiatives → purpose

130.s: Safe City Projects and ERSS-112 are funded from the:
130.x: Safe City Projects and ERSS-112 receive funding from the Nirbhaya Fund, which is dedicated to women’s-safety projects.
130.tq: Match the safety initiative with its dedicated funding source.
130.sec: Crime databases and safety IT initiatives → purpose

130.s: Safe City Projects include:
o: A national database of convicted sexual offenders
Free transport for women stranded at night in rural areas
CCTV and AI-based public safety measures for women in eight major cities
Only the construction of women’s prisons in every district
130.x: Safe City Projects use CCTV and artificial intelligence-based public-safety measures for women in eight major cities.
130.tq: Distinguish an urban technology project from databases, courts and transport schemes.
130.sec: Crime databases and safety IT initiatives → purpose

130.s: The AI4AP pilot is based on CCTNS and covers which Andhra Pradesh districts?
130.x: The AI4AP pilot is based on CCTNS and covers Chittoor, Guntur and Annamayya districts.
130.tq: Retain the exact three-location combination rather than a broad regional guess.
130.sec: Crime databases and safety IT initiatives → purpose

130.s: The Fast Track Special Courts (FTSC) scheme is a centrally sponsored scheme funded from the Nirbhaya Fund and primarily deals with:
o: Only cases under the Dowry Prohibition Act
130.x: The FTSC scheme is a centrally sponsored scheme funded from the Nirbhaya Fund for cases involving rape and offences under POCSO.
130.tq: Combine the scheme’s funding source with its subject-matter jurisdiction.
130.sec: Fast track courts and special courts - Nirbhaya Fund scheme, States' new courts

130.s: The FTSC scheme, which followed the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018, was extended up to:
130.x: The FTSC scheme was extended up to March 2026 and covered 790 courts under the stated extension.
130.tq: Separate the scheme’s extension date from later reported court-functioning figures.
130.sec: Fast track courts and special courts - Nirbhaya Fund scheme, States' new courts

130.s: As on 31 July 2025, the number of functional FTSCs, including exclusive POCSO courts, was:
130.x: As on 31 July 2025, 743 FTSCs were functional, including 394 exclusive POCSO courts, across 29 States and Union Territories.
130.tq: Keep the total and the included sub-category in their correct order.
130.sec: Fast track courts and special courts - Nirbhaya Fund scheme, States' new courts

130.s: Under the POCSO Act, a special court may be designated by:
o: A Sessions Court in each district
A Magistrate’s Court in each village
A High Court only for the entire State
The Union Cabinet for every Union Territory
130.x: The POCSO Act permits a Sessions Court to be designated as a special court in each district. Pendency remains a major challenge.
130.tq: Identify the judicial level and territorial unit specified in the provision.
130.sec: Fast track courts and special courts - Nirbhaya Fund scheme, States' new courts

130.s: The Nirbhaya Fund was established in:
130.x: The Nirbhaya Fund was established in 2013 as a dedicated corpus for projects related to women’s safety.
130.tq: Link the fund’s establishment year with its purpose, not with a later scheme.
130.sec: Fast track courts and special courts - Nirbhaya Fund scheme, States' new courts

130.s: The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 provided for:
o: The designation of every Sessions Court as a POCSO court
The establishment of Safe City Projects in eight cities
130.x: The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 provided for fast-track courts. The FTSC scheme was subsequently launched in 2019.
130.tq: Distinguish a statutory provision from later administrative schemes and databases.
130.sec: Fast track courts and special courts - Nirbhaya Fund scheme, States' new courts

130.s: In 2025, FTSCs disposed of 87,754 POCSO cases against 80,320 registered cases. This represented a disposal rate of approximately:
130.x: The disposal rate was reported as 109 percent because the number of cases disposed of exceeded the number registered during the stated period.
130.tq: Compare disposed and registered cases rather than assuming a rate cannot exceed 100 percent.
130.sec: Fast track courts and special courts - Nirbhaya Fund scheme, States' new courts

130.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. Establishment of the Nirbhaya Fund
B. Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013
C. FTSC scheme
D. Andhra Pradesh Disha Bill
130.x: The Nirbhaya Fund and the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act belong to 2013, followed by the FTSC scheme in 2019 and the Disha Bill in December 2019. In the ordering used here, the fund is placed before the Act as the dedicated corpus preceded the legislative provision.
130.tq: Place the broad funding and legislative framework before the later schemes and State initiative.
130.sec: Fast track courts and special courts - Nirbhaya Fund scheme, States' new courts

130.s: The Palermo Protocol, adopted in 2000, is formally known as the:
o: UN Protocol on the Rights of Migrant Workers
UN Protocol on Transnational Organised Crime Investigations
UN Convention on the Elimination of Violence against Women
UN Protocol to Prevent, Suppress and Punish Trafficking in Persons, Especially Women and Children
130.x: The Palermo Protocol is the UN Protocol to Prevent, Suppress and Punish Trafficking in Persons, Especially Women and Children.
130.tq: Identify the exact official title rather than a similar human-rights instrument.
130.sec: Trafficking - UNODC report, Palermo Protocol, ITPA, Trafficking of Persons Bill 2018/2021  [APPSC]

130.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Palermo Protocol:
1. It supplements the United Nations Convention against Transnational Organized Crime.
2. India has ratified it.
3. It deals specifically with trafficking in persons, especially women and children.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: All three statements are correct. The Palermo Protocol supplements the UNTOC and addresses trafficking in persons, particularly women and children; India has ratified it.
130.tq: Check each statement against the instrument’s purpose, legal relationship and ratification status.
130.sec: Trafficking - UNODC report, Palermo Protocol, ITPA, Trafficking of Persons Bill 2018/2021  [APPSC]

130.s: Under the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956, which of the following is correct?
o: Prostitution itself is treated as a crime in every circumstance.
Only trafficking of children is punishable.
Brothel-keeping, pimping, soliciting and living on the earnings of prostitution are punishable acts.
The Act abolishes protective homes maintained by State Governments.
130.x: The ITPA does not treat prostitution per se as a crime, but penalises activities such as brothel-keeping, pimping, soliciting and living on prostitution earnings.
130.tq: Use the distinction between the activity itself and associated exploitative activities.
130.sec: Trafficking - UNODC report, Palermo Protocol, ITPA, Trafficking of Persons Bill 2018/2021  [APPSC]

130.s: Which one of the following is associated with the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956?
o: Protective homes maintained by the States
National Investigation Agency as the sole investigating agency
Abolition of all State rehabilitation institutions
130.x: The ITPA provides for protective homes maintained by the States. The other alternatives are not features stated in relation to the Act.
130.tq: Match the statute with its institutional feature and reject unrelated enforcement measures.
130.sec: Trafficking - UNODC report, Palermo Protocol, ITPA, Trafficking of Persons Bill 2018/2021  [APPSC]

130.s: Under Section 143 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, which principle applies to trafficking?
o: Consent is relevant only if the trafficking is inter-State.
The victim’s consent is always a complete defence.
Consent matters only when the victim is an adult male.
130.x: Section 143 of the BNS treats the victim’s consent as immaterial in determining the offence of trafficking.
130.tq: Discriminate between consent as a defence and the statutory rule that consent is immaterial.
130.sec: Trafficking - UNODC report, Palermo Protocol, ITPA, Trafficking of Persons Bill 2018/2021  [APPSC]

130.s: Which of the following was a feature of the Trafficking of Persons Bill, 2018?
o: It limited shelters to private institutions only.
It was enacted by both Houses without lapse.
It removed all provisions relating to rehabilitation.
It proposed aggravated trafficking and aiding trafficking as new offences.
130.x: The 2018 Bill proposed new offences including aggravated trafficking and aiding trafficking, and also provided for shelters and rehabilitation. It was passed by the Lok Sabha but later lapsed.
130.tq: Test the bill’s substantive provisions separately from its legislative status.
130.sec: Trafficking - UNODC report, Palermo Protocol, ITPA, Trafficking of Persons Bill 2018/2021  [APPSC]

130.s:
With reference to the Trafficking of Persons Bill, 2018, consider the following statements:
1. It was passed by the Lok Sabha.
2. It subsequently lapsed.
3. It proposed the National Investigation Agency as the national investigating agency.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: The 2018 Bill was passed by the Lok Sabha and later lapsed. The proposal to designate the NIA as the national investigating agency belonged to the 2021 draft Bill.
130.tq: Separate closely related legislative proposals by year and avoid transferring a feature from one draft to another.
130.sec: Trafficking - UNODC report, Palermo Protocol, ITPA, Trafficking of Persons Bill 2018/2021  [APPSC]

130.s: The 2021 draft Bill relating to trafficking proposed which agency as the national investigating agency?
130.x: The 2021 draft Bill proposed the National Investigation Agency (NIA) as the national investigating agency for trafficking-related matters.
130.tq: Use the agency-name trap among bodies with overlapping law-enforcement roles.
130.sec: Trafficking - UNODC report, Palermo Protocol, ITPA, Trafficking of Persons Bill 2018/2021  [APPSC]

130.s: The UNODC Global Report on Trafficking in Persons, 2016, observed that victims and traffickers often:
o: have no prior social relationship of any kind
belong to entirely different regions and social backgrounds
belong only to organised international networks
130.x: The 2016 UNODC report noted that victims and traffickers often share the same background.
130.tq: Recall the precise relationship highlighted in the report without substituting a stronger generalisation.
130.sec: Trafficking - UNODC report, Palermo Protocol, ITPA, Trafficking of Persons Bill 2018/2021  [APPSC]

130.s: According to the data cited for trafficking cases, which of the following is correctly matched?
o: NCRB 2024 — approximately 2,183 cases in Telangana only
130.x: The cited NCRB 2023 figure is approximately 2,183 trafficking cases. The note separately identifies Telangana as having the most trafficking cases in the NCRB 2024 data.
130.tq: Separate approximate figures, years and geographical conclusions instead of merging them.
130.sec: Trafficking - UNODC report, Palermo Protocol, ITPA, Trafficking of Persons Bill 2018/2021  [APPSC]

130.s: Which State was reported to have the most trafficking cases in the NCRB 2024 data cited?
130.x: Telangana was reported as having the most trafficking cases in the cited NCRB 2024 data.
130.tq: Test the location-specific conclusion rather than the total case figure.
130.sec: Trafficking - UNODC report, Palermo Protocol, ITPA, Trafficking of Persons Bill 2018/2021  [APPSC]

130.s: The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 was enacted in the immediate aftermath of the:
130.x: The 2013 amendment followed the December 2012 Delhi gang rape, commonly referred to as the Nirbhaya case.
130.tq: Use the event-year association and distinguish the context of the 2013 and 2018 amendments.
130.sec: Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 2013 - committee, new offences

130.s:
The Justice J.S. Verma Committee report led to amendments to which of the following laws in 2013?
1. Indian Penal Code
2. Code of Criminal Procedure
3. Indian Evidence Act
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 amended the IPC, CrPC and Indian Evidence Act following the Justice J.S. Verma Committee report.
130.tq: Check the full legislative set instead of stopping at the most familiar statute.
130.sec: Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 2013 - committee, new offences

130.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched under the 2013 criminal law amendments?
130.x: Disrobing was provided under Section 354B IPC, not Section 354E. Sections 354A, 354C and 354D relate respectively to sexual harassment, voyeurism and stalking.
130.tq: Find the wrong statutory pairing among closely numbered provisions.
130.sec: Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 2013 - committee, new offences

130.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (IPC provision)
a. Section 326A
b. Section 326B
c. Section 354C
d. Section 376E

List-II (offence or punishment)
i. Voyeurism
ii. Death for repeat rapists
iii. Acid attack
iv. Attempt to acid attack

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
130.x: Section 326A concerns acid attack, Section 326B attempt to acid attack, Section 354C voyeurism and Section 376E death for repeat rapists.
130.tq: Start with the sure statutory pairs and eliminate codes containing a swapped offence.
130.sec: Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 2013 - committee, new offences

130.s: Which of the following was introduced by the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013?
o: Removal of punishment for repeat rapists
Abolition of the offence of voyeurism
Reduction of the age of consent to 16 years
130.x: The 2013 Act introduced stalking as a specific offence under Section 354D IPC. It also introduced voyeurism, while the age of consent was raised to 18 years.
130.tq: Identify the genuine new offence while rejecting reversals of the amendment’s provisions.
130.sec: Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 2013 - committee, new offences

130.s: Under the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013, the age of consent was raised to:
130.x: The 2013 amendment raised the age of consent to 18 years.
130.tq: Use the exact age figure and distinguish it from the recommendation of the Verma Committee.
130.sec: Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 2013 - committee, new offences

130.s: Which one of the following statements regarding rape under the 2013 amendment is correct?
o: Rape was confined to penile-vaginal penetration.
Penetration by objects or body parts and oral acts were included, and the minimum punishment was raised to seven years.
The minimum punishment was reduced to five years.
Only consensual acts involving adults were covered.
130.x: The 2013 amendment widened the definition of rape to include penetration by objects or body parts and oral acts, and raised the minimum punishment to seven years.
130.tq: Test the expanded definition together with the associated minimum punishment.
130.sec: Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 2013 - committee, new offences

130.s: The Supreme Court struck down the two-finger test in which case?
o: Lata Singh v State of Uttar Pradesh
Shakti Vahini v Union of India
130.x: The Supreme Court struck down the two-finger test in Lillu v State in 2013.
130.tq: Match the judicial directive with the correct case name.
130.sec: Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 2013 - committee, new offences

130.s:
Which of the following was recommended by the Justice J.S. Verma Committee but not adopted in the same form by Parliament?
1. Criminalisation of marital rape
2. No death penalty for rape
3. Keeping the age of consent at 16 years
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: The Verma Committee recommended criminalising marital rape, opposed the death penalty for rape and recommended retaining the age of consent at 16. Parliament raised the age of consent to 18 years.
130.tq: Separate committee recommendations from the final legislative choices.
130.sec: Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 2013 - committee, new offences

130.s: Who among the following was NOT a member of the Justice J.S. Verma Committee as listed?
130.x: The listed members were Justice J.S. Verma, Justice Leila Seth and Gopal Subramanium. Justice Ranjana Desai was not among them.
130.tq: Use the committee-membership trap by identifying the outsider in a closely related judicial group.
130.sec: Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 2013 - committee, new offences

130.s: The report of the Justice J.S. Verma Committee was submitted in:
130.x: The Justice J.S. Verma Committee submitted its report in January 2013.
130.tq: Distinguish the date of the triggering incident from the date of the committee report.

Consider the following statements about crimes against women in India:

130.s: Which one of the following is a major criticism of the death penalty in cases involving sexual offences?
o: It makes rape laws completely gender-neutral.
It may discourage victims from reporting offences.
It necessarily eliminates delays in criminal trials.
It prevents all cases from reaching fast-track courts.
130.x: A stated criticism is that the death penalty may discourage reporting by victims or affected families. It does not automatically eliminate trial delays or make rape law gender-neutral.
130.tq: Identify the policy criticism rather than assuming that a severe punishment solves every procedural problem.
130.sec: Universal angles

130.s: With reference to debates on rape law in India, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Rape law has been criticised for not being gender-neutral.
Gender neutrality has eliminated all criticism of rape law.
The debate concerns only the speed of investigation and not the scope of the law.
Rape law is universally regarded as gender-neutral.
130.x: The notes identify the non-gender-neutral character of rape law as a criticism. The debate is not confined only to investigation speed.
130.tq: Avoid the absolute-word trap in statements claiming that a legal debate has been completely settled.
130.sec: Universal angles

130.s:

130.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because fast-track courts do not guarantee a 100% conviction rate.
