o: Article 16(4) formed part of the original Constitution, whereas Article 15(4) was added by the First Amendment in 1951.
Article 15(4) formed part of the original Constitution, whereas Article 16(4) was added by the First Amendment in 1951.
Both Articles 15(4) and 16(4) were inserted by the 42nd Amendment.
Both Articles 15(4) and 16(4) were inserted by the 1st Amendment.
133.x: Article 16(4) was present in the original Constitution. Article 15(4) was the first reservation clause added by constitutional amendment, through the First Amendment Act, 1951.
133.tq: Discriminate between the original provision and the later amendment-created provision.
133.sec: Universal angles

133.s: The Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955 is significant because it was:
o: The first law providing reservation in the Lok Sabha
The first law using the expression Scheduled Tribes
The first law creating the National Commission for Scheduled Castes
133.x: The Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955 was the first law enacted to enforce Article 17. The Government of India Act, 1935 had earlier used the term Scheduled Castes.
133.tq: Distinguish the first enforcement law from the earlier statutory use of the term Scheduled Castes.
133.sec: Universal angles

133.s: The poem *Gabbilam*, associated with sensitising public opinion against untouchability, was composed by:
133.x: *Gabbilam* was composed by Gurram Jashuva and is associated with creating awareness against untouchability.
133.tq: Match the literary work with its author using the Andhra social-reform context.
133.sec: Universal angles

133.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
133.x: Karamchedu occurred in 1985. Tsundur occurred in 1991, the Siddhantam temple entry was in 1933, and the Davinder Singh judgment was in 2024.
133.tq: Use the year–event pairing and reject the deliberately shifted dates.
133.sec: Universal angles

133.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the status of converts in relation to Scheduled Caste recognition is correct?
o: The judgment concerned only the nomination of Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha.
The judgment abolished all reservation for Scheduled Castes in Andhra Pradesh.
The Supreme Court in Chinthada Anand v. State of Andhra Pradesh held that Christian converts cannot claim Scheduled Caste status.
The Supreme Court held that every religious convert automatically retains Scheduled Caste status.
133.x: In Chinthada Anand v. State of Andhra Pradesh, the Supreme Court held that Christian converts cannot claim Scheduled Caste status. The case did not concern Anglo-Indian nomination or abolition of reservations.
133.tq: Identify the precise holding instead of accepting broad or absolute claims about conversion and reservation.
133.sec: Universal angles

133.s: The K.G. Balakrishnan Commission concerning the Scheduled Caste status of Dalit Christians and Muslims was extended up to:
133.x: The tenure of the K.G. Balakrishnan Commission was extended up to 10 June 2026.
133.tq: Distinguish the exact extension date from nearby years.
133.sec: Universal angles

133.s: Which one of the following statements best reflects the criticism concerning the constitutional treatment of untouchability?
o: Because Article 17 is a directive principle, it cannot support penal legislation.
Because Article 17 applies only to public employment, private discrimination is fully excluded from debate.
Because Article 17 defines every possible form exhaustively, no new form can escape penalty.
Because untouchability is left undefined, new indirect forms may escape penal consequences.
133.x: A major criticism is that untouchability is not constitutionally defined, allowing newer indirect forms to potentially escape effective penal consequences.
133.tq: Apply the legal criticism to a situation involving newer indirect forms rather than relying on an absolute statement.
133.sec: Universal angles

133.s: Which statement correctly describes the Centre's position on an income-based creamy layer in SC/ST reservations in August 2026?
o: It transferred the decision exclusively to State SC Commissions.
It opposed an income-based creamy layer and stated that any change requires a holistic empirical review.
It declared that creamy-layer rules already apply identically to all SC and ST quotas.
It supported immediate introduction of an income-based creamy layer without further study.
133.x: The Centre's affidavit opposed an income-based creamy layer in SC/ST quotas and stated that any change would require a holistic empirical review.
133.tq: Identify the authority's stated position and reject the extreme alternatives of immediate or automatic application.
133.sec: Universal angles

133.s:
The 131st Constitutional Amendment Bill referred to in April 2026 sought to:
1. Amend Articles 330, 332 and 334A.
2. Enlarge the Lok Sabha to 850 members.
3. Create separate State Commissions for Scheduled Castes through Article 338(9).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
133.x: The Bill sought to amend Articles 330, 332 and 334A and enlarge the Lok Sabha to 850 members. It did not create State SC Commissions through Article 338(9), and the Bill had not been passed.
133.tq: Reject the statement that assigns a State-law function to the wrong constitutional provision.
133.sec: Universal angles

133.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the recent Andhra Pradesh-related developments?
o: K.S. Jawahar — review of SC/ST schemes in SPSR Nellore
B.V. Nagarathna — Chairman of the State SC Commission in Nellore
K.G. Balakrishnan — organiser of the Madiga Dandora movement
133.x: K.S. Jawahar, Chairman of the State SC Commission, reviewed SC/ST schemes in SPSR Nellore. B.V. Nagarathna is a Supreme Court judge, Chinthada Anand is a case name, and K.G. Balakrishnan headed the commission on the status of converts.
133.tq: Match the person with the correct institutional or legal role and reject swapped identities.
133.sec: Universal angles

133.s: In the Sabarimala reference, Justice B.V. Nagarathna observed that Article 17 cannot be applied:
o: After the commencement of the Constitution
Only during the annual pilgrimage season
133.x: Justice B.V. Nagarathna stated that Article 17 cannot apply “for three days a month” in the Sabarimala reference.
133.tq: Recall the precise time-related phrase rather than replacing it with a broader limitation.
133.sec: Universal angles

133.s: The petition by 32 Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe Congress MPs concerning the Haldwani “shuddhikaran” row was submitted to the:
133.x: The 32 SC/ST Congress MPs petitioned the President of India concerning the Haldwani “shuddhikaran” row.
133.tq: Identify the constitutional authority approached in the reported development.
133.sec: Universal angles

133.s: Which one of the following statements correctly reflects the recent action of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes?
o: It amended Article 338 through executive order after an alleged remark by a Chief Minister.
It dissolved the State SC Commission of Andhra Pradesh under Article 338(9).
It took suo motu cognisance of an alleged remark by a Chief Minister under Article 338.
It transferred all complaints to the NCBC under Article 342A.
133.x: The NCSC took suo motu cognisance of an alleged remark by a Chief Minister under Article 338. It cannot amend the Constitution or dissolve a State commission through the powers described.
133.tq: Match the constitutional body with its investigative action while rejecting powers assigned to the wrong authority.
133.sec: Universal angles

134.s: Which of the following cases is associated with the Supreme Court directions that were perceived as diluting the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989?
o: Prithvi Raj Chauhan v. Union of India
Subhash Kashinath Mahajan v. State of Maharashtra
Indra Sawhney v. Union of India
134.x: In Subhash Kashinath Mahajan v. State of Maharashtra, decided on 20 March 2018, the Supreme Court issued directions concerning preliminary enquiry, anticipatory bail and prior approval for arrest.
134.tq: Use the case-name and outcome association to distinguish closely related judgments.
134.sec: Atrocities Act - dilution case, 2018 amendment, Prithvi Raj Chauhan  [APPSC]

134.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the directions issued in Subhash Kashinath Mahajan v. State of Maharashtra:
1. A preliminary enquiry was contemplated before registration of an FIR.
2. Anticipatory bail could be granted where no prima facie case existed.
3. Prior approval of the appointing authority was required before arresting a public servant.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
134.x: All three statements correctly describe the directions issued in the Mahajan case, which were viewed as curbing possible misuse of the Atrocities Act.
134.tq: Verify each procedural safeguard separately before selecting the coded combination.
134.sec: Atrocities Act - dilution case, 2018 amendment, Prithvi Raj Chauhan  [APPSC]

134.s: The Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Act, 2018 inserted which provision?
134.x: The 2018 Amendment Act inserted Section 18A. The reference to Section 4A is incorrect.
134.tq: Discriminate between the exact statutory section number and a look-alike number.
134.sec: Atrocities Act - dilution case, 2018 amendment, Prithvi Raj Chauhan  [APPSC]

134.s: The Supreme Court recalled the directions issued in Subhash Kashinath Mahajan v. State of Maharashtra on review in:
134.x: The Supreme Court recalled the Mahajan directions on review in October 2019.
134.tq: Separate the dates of the original directions, recall, later judgment and recent case.
134.sec: Atrocities Act - dilution case, 2018 amendment, Prithvi Raj Chauhan  [APPSC]

134.s:
With reference to Prithvi Raj Chauhan v. Union of India, consider the following statements:
1. The Supreme Court upheld the constitutional validity of the 2018 amendment.
2. Courts may grant anticipatory bail where no prima facie case exists.
3. Courts may quash proceedings where a prima facie case exists, without examining the allegations further.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
134.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The power to grant relief or quash proceedings is available where no prima facie case exists; statement 3 reverses this condition.
134.tq: Find the reversed condition in a legally qualified statement.
134.sec: Atrocities Act - dilution case, 2018 amendment, Prithvi Raj Chauhan  [APPSC]

134.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Decision in Prithvi Raj Chauhan v. Union of India
B. Judgment in Subhash Kashinath Mahajan v. State of Maharashtra
C. Recall of the Mahajan directions on review
D. Decision in Kiran v. Rajkumar Jivaraj Jain
134.x: The correct sequence is Mahajan judgment in March 2018, recall in October 2019, Prithvi Raj Chauhan in February 2020 and Kiran in 2025.
134.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two intervening developments.
134.sec: Atrocities Act - dilution case, 2018 amendment, Prithvi Raj Chauhan  [APPSC]

134.s: In Kiran v. Rajkumar Jivaraj Jain (2025), the Supreme Court:
o: Declared Section 18 of the Atrocities Act unconstitutional.
Directed that a preliminary enquiry must precede every arrest.
Cancelled an anticipatory bail granted by a High Court and held that no mini-trial should be conducted at the bail stage.
Upheld anticipatory bail despite the existence of a prima facie case.
134.x: The Supreme Court cancelled the High Court's anticipatory bail, held that Section 18 applies where a prima facie case exists and stated that a mini-trial is impermissible at the bail stage.
134.tq: Match the latest case with its precise procedural holding, not with the earlier Mahajan directions.
134.sec: Atrocities Act - dilution case, 2018 amendment, Prithvi Raj Chauhan  [APPSC]

134.s: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 derives its constitutional basis primarily from:
134.x: The Act was enacted to give effect to Article 17 of the Constitution, which abolishes untouchability.
134.tq: Match the legislation with its specific constitutional provision.

134.s: Which of the following is correctly matched under the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955?
o: Section 3 — Religious disabilities relating to entry into public places of worship
Section 6 — Collective fine on inhabitants of an area
Section 15A — Refusal to sell goods or render services
134.x: Section 3 deals with religious disabilities, including barring entry to or worship in public places of worship. Section 6 concerns refusal to sell goods or render services, Section 10A concerns collective fines and Section 15A concerns State duties.
134.tq: Start with the sure section–subject pair and eliminate the shifted provisions.

134.s: Under the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955, refusal to sell goods or render services on the ground of untouchability is covered under:
134.x: Section 6 deals with refusal to sell goods or render services on the ground of untouchability.
134.tq: Discriminate between adjacent sections dealing with access, admission and service-related disabilities.

134.s: Which one of the following is NOT a duty of the State under Section 15A of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955?
o: Providing legal aid to affected persons
Conducting surveys of areas prone to untouchability
Making appointments to the Supreme Court
134.x: Section 15A provides for State duties such as legal aid, special courts, surveys of untouchability-prone areas, awareness measures and related implementation duties. Appointment of Supreme Court judges is unrelated to the Act.
134.tq: Identify the one option outside the statutory subject by grouping the implementation duties.

134.s: The first-offence punishment under the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 is generally stated as:
o: Imprisonment from one to six months and fine from ₹100 to ₹500
Imprisonment up to three years without fine
Imprisonment from six months to one year and fine from ₹500 to ₹1,000
134.x: For a first offence, the stated punishment is imprisonment of one to six months and a fine of ₹100 to ₹500. The older wording is also expressed as imprisonment up to six months or fine up to ₹500 or both.
134.tq: Read the range carefully and avoid replacing a statutory range with a single figure.

134.s: A person convicted under the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 is also subject to which electoral consequence mentioned in the law?
o: Permanent disqualification from voting in all elections
Disqualification from holding any private office
Disqualification from contesting elections to Parliament and State Legislatures
134.x: A person convicted under the Act is disqualified from contesting elections to Parliament or a State Legislature.
134.tq: Distinguish the specified electoral consequence from broader penalties not attached to the provision.

134.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the expression 'untouchability' is correct?
1. It is expressly defined in the Constitution.
2. It is expressly defined in the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955.
3. The Mysore High Court interpreted it as a historically developed caste practice.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
134.x: The expression is not defined in either the Constitution or the Act. The Mysore High Court interpreted it as the historically developed caste practice.
134.tq: Watch for the common trap that an important constitutional expression must have a statutory definition.

134.s: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 is implemented primarily by:
o: State Governments and Union Territory administrations
The Supreme Court through its registry
The Election Commission of India alone
134.x: Implementation of the Act is carried out by State Governments and Union Territory administrations.
134.tq: Identify the implementing authority rather than the central nodal ministry.

134.s: At the Union level, which Ministry is the nodal ministry for implementation of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955, with the Ministry of Home Affairs also associated with implementation?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
134.x: The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment is the nodal ministry, with the Ministry of Home Affairs also associated with implementation.
134.tq: Use the nodal-ministry distinction to avoid selecting a neighbouring social-sector ministry.

134.s: The rules framed under the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 are known as the:
134.x: The rules made for carrying out the purposes of the Act are known as the Protection of Civil Rights Rules, 1977, commonly called the PCR Rules, 1977.
134.tq: Distinguish the year and short title of the rules from the years of the Act and its amendment.

134.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Section 3 — Religious disabilities
2. Section 4 — Social disabilities
3. Section 6 — Refusal to sell goods or render services
4. Section 15A — State duties
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
134.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Sections 3 and 4 concern religious and social disabilities, Section 6 concerns sale or services, and Section 15A lays down State duties.
134.tq: Confirm the section sequence from disabilities to services and then to implementation duties.

134.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989:
1. Section 3 deals with atrocities committed by persons who are not members of a Scheduled Caste or a Scheduled Tribe.
2. The Act creates certain offences which are not covered by the Protection of Civil Rights Act or the Indian Penal Code.
3. The Act applies only when the accused and the victim belong to the same Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
134.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the Act principally covers offences by non-SC/ST persons against SC/ST persons.
134.tq: Split the options by checking the scope of the accused and victim rather than accepting a broad statement about applicability.

134.s: Wilful neglect of duty by a public servant under the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 is dealt with under:
134.x: Section 4 provides punishment for wilful neglect of duty by a public servant.
134.tq: Match the official duty-related offence with its precise statutory section.

134.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the special judicial structure under the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989?
o: Special Courts are established only by the Supreme Court without consultation with the State judiciary.
Special Courts are established in every district with the concurrence of the Chief Justice of the High Court.
Exclusive Special Courts existed in the original 1989 Act and were not affected by later amendments.
Trials under the Act can be conducted only by ordinary Magistrates.
134.x: Special Courts are set up in each district with the concurrence of the Chief Justice of the concerned High Court. Exclusive Special Courts were added by the 2015 amendment.
134.tq: Use the ‘who establishes or concurs’ method to avoid confusing the State Government, High Court and Supreme Court.

134.s: Which of the following statements regarding Section 19 of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 is correct?
o: It provides for probation in all cases involving first-time offenders.
It bars probation for persons convicted under the Act.
It provides for an appeal to the High Court within 90 days.
It deals with the definition of economic boycott.
134.x: Section 19 provides that the benefit of probation is not available to persons convicted under the Act.
134.tq: Distinguish the sentencing restriction in Section 19 from appeal and definition provisions in nearby sections.

134.s: The rule-making power under the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 is vested in:
o: The National Commission for Scheduled Castes
134.x: Section 23 vests the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act in the Central Government.
134.tq: Ask ‘who would make rules?’ and distinguish the rule-making authority from implementing authorities.

134.s:
Consider the following statements about the scope and operation of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989:
1. It applies to offences committed by non-SC/ST persons against members of SCs or STs.
2. The offences under the Act are cognizable.
3. Arrest without warrant is permissible for such offences.
4. The Act has applied to Jammu and Kashmir since 2019.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
134.x: All four statements are correct. The Act covers specified offences by non-SC/ST persons against SC/ST persons, treats them as cognizable, permits arrest without warrant, and has applied to Jammu and Kashmir since 2019.
134.tq: Check scope, procedural character and territorial application separately before choosing the coded combination.

134.s: Which of the following is NOT a provision associated with the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989?
o: Grant of arms licences to members of SCs and STs
Enhanced punishment for public servants in specified circumstances
Cancellation of arms licences in atrocity-prone areas
Automatic dissolution of every local authority located in an atrocity-prone area
134.x: The Act provides for cancellation of arms licences of potential offenders in atrocity-prone areas, licences for SC/ST persons and enhanced punishment for public servants. It does not provide for automatic dissolution of local authorities.
134.tq: Find the option that introduces an institutional consequence not connected with the Act’s stated safeguards.

134.s: An offence under the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act committed on or after 1 July 2024 is to be read with references to the:
134.x: Since 1 July 2024, references to the IPC and CrPC in the Act are read as references to the corresponding provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita.
134.tq: Use the one-to-one replacement pair: IPC becomes BNS and CrPC becomes BNSS.

134.s: Which one of the following is the correct combination regarding investigation under the Protection of Civil Rights and Atrocities Rules, 1995?
o: Investigation by an officer not below DSP rank; charge-sheet within 60 days
Investigation by an officer not below Inspector rank; charge-sheet within 30 days
Investigation by an officer not below Superintendent of Police rank; charge-sheet within 90 days
Investigation by an Executive Magistrate; charge-sheet within 60 days
134.x: Investigation is to be conducted by a police officer not below the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police, and the investigation and filing of the charge-sheet are to be completed within 60 days.
134.tq: Start from the sure pair of investigating rank and then verify the prescribed time limit.
134.sec: PoA Rules 1995 - investigation, annual report, relief

134.s: Under the PoA Rules, 1995, the annual report on implementation of the Act is prepared by:
o: The Central Government on the basis of reports received from the States and submitted to Parliament
The concerned State Government and submitted to the district administration
The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes and submitted to the Supreme Court
The Special Public Prosecutor and submitted to the High Court
134.x: The Centre prepares the annual report on implementation using reports received from the States and places it before Parliament.
134.tq: Trace the reporting chain from State reports to the Central Government and finally Parliament.
134.sec: PoA Rules 1995 - investigation, annual report, relief

134.s: The monetary relief and rehabilitation provided under the PoA Rules, 1995 ranges from:
134.x: The relief and rehabilitation amount, fixed in 2016, ranges from ₹85,000 to ₹8.25 lakh.
134.tq: Retain both endpoints of the range and avoid replacing the lower or upper figure with a rounded amount.
134.sec: PoA Rules 1995 - investigation, annual report, relief

134.s: The relief paid to victims under the centrally sponsored scheme for implementation of the Protection of Civil Rights and Atrocities provisions is shared between the Centre and the States in the ratio of:
134.x: The relief is paid under a centrally sponsored scheme on a 50:50 Centre-State basis.
134.tq: Use the exact Centre-State sharing ratio rather than confusing it with ratios used in other schemes.
134.sec: PoA Rules 1995 - investigation, annual report, relief

134.s:
Consider the following statements regarding monitoring under the PoA Rules, 1995:
1. Monitoring takes place at the district level.
2. Monitoring takes place at the State level.
3. Monitoring takes place at the national level.
4. The Rules provide only for judicial monitoring and not administrative monitoring.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
134.x: Monitoring is undertaken at district, State and national levels. Statement 4 is false because the framework is not limited to judicial monitoring.
134.tq: Identify the complete three-level structure and reject the restrictive ‘only’ statement.
134.sec: PoA Rules 1995 - investigation, annual report, relief

134.s: The Protection of Civil Rights Rules were notified in:
134.x: The Protection of Civil Rights Rules were notified in 1977.
134.tq: Distinguish the year of the Rules from the years of the parent Acts and the PoA Rules.
134.sec: PoA Rules 1995 - investigation, annual report, relief

134.s: At the Central level, implementation of the Protection of Civil Rights Rules involves the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. Which of the following ministries is NOT identified with that implementation?
o: The ministries identified for implementation at the Centre
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
134.x: The Ministry of Minority Affairs is not the ministry identified for implementation in the stated Central-level arrangement.
134.tq: Use the ministry-swapping trap and identify the neighbouring but incorrect department.
134.sec: PoA Rules 1995 - investigation, annual report, relief

134.s: The Centre’s scheme for implementation of the Protection of Civil Rights and Atrocities provisions proposed relief for approximately how many atrocity victims?
134.x: The scheme proposed relief for approximately 87,426 atrocity victims.
134.tq: Test the exact estimate by distinguishing the nearby numerical distractors.
134.sec: PoA Rules 1995 - investigation, annual report, relief

134.s: The Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Act, 2015 came into force in:
134.x: The 2015 Amendment Act was enforced from 2016.
134.tq: Separate the year of the amendment from the year in which it was brought into force.

134.s: Which of the following was introduced or specifically recognised as a new atrocity by the 2015 amendment to the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act?
o: Failure to pay a civil debt
Refusal to provide a commercial loan to any person
Disagreement with a local authority’s tax assessment
134.x: Garlanding an SC/ST person with footwear was included among the new or rephrased atrocities under the 2015 amendment.
134.tq: Identify the precise act included in the amended offence list rather than a general civil dispute.

134.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched with a new atrocity recognised under the 2015 amendment?
o: Forcing a person to carry or dispose of a carcass — new atrocity
Dedicating an SC/ST woman as a devadasi — new atrocity
Issuing a general public notice for a government recruitment examination — new atrocity
134.x: Tonsuring, forcing a person to carry or dispose of a carcass and dedicating an SC/ST woman as a devadasi are recognised acts under the amended framework. Issuing a general recruitment notice is not such an atrocity.
134.tq: Find the unrelated administrative act among a cluster of specific amended offences.

134.s:
Consider the following statements regarding offences added or rephrased by the 2015 amendment:
1. Denying access to irrigation facilities may constitute an atrocity.
2. Forcing a person to perform manual scavenging may constitute an atrocity.
3. Preventing SC/ST candidates from contesting an election may constitute an atrocity.
4. Calling a woman a witch is included among the specified atrocities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
134.x: All four statements describe acts included among the new or rephrased atrocities under the 2015 amendment.
134.tq: Use complete-list recognition: verify each concrete act before selecting the coded combination.

134.s: The 2015 amendment specifically recognised which of the following as an atrocity?
o: A civil disagreement over inheritance between persons of the same community
Refusal by a voter to support a particular candidate
Failure of a private employer to grant promotion on seniority
Social or economic boycott of an SC/ST person
134.x: Social or economic boycott was added as an atrocity, and “economic boycott” was separately defined in the amended Act.
134.tq: Distinguish a legally defined boycott from ordinary private disputes or political disagreement.

134.s: Under the 2015 amendment, the trial in an Exclusive Special Court is intended to be completed within:
o: 60 days of filing of the charge-sheet
90 days of arrest of the accused
30 days of registration of the FIR
134.x: The amendment envisages completion of trial within two months, that is, 60 days, from the filing of the charge-sheet.
134.tq: Convert the stated period of two months into the precise numerical option and note the starting point.

134.s: Which of the following was a major institutional change introduced by the 2015 amendment?
o: Transfer of all trials to ordinary civil courts
Creation of Exclusive Special Courts and Exclusive Special Public Prosecutors
Removal of the power of Special Courts to take direct cognizance
134.x: The amendment added Exclusive Special Courts and Exclusive Special Public Prosecutors. It also permitted Special Courts to take direct cognizance.
134.tq: Reject the reversed institutional changes and identify the paired additions made by the amendment.

134.s: The 2015 amendment introduced a new chapter dealing with:
134.x: A new chapter on the rights of victims and witnesses was introduced by the 2015 amendment.
134.tq: Match the amendment with its distinctive new chapter rather than with unrelated social legislation.

134.s: Which one of the following correctly reflects the power of Special Courts after the 2015 amendment?
o: They have no power to take cognizance and can only record evidence.
They may take cognizance only after prior approval of the Central Government.
They may take direct cognizance of offences under the Act.
They may take cognizance only after a civil court’s decree.
134.x: The 2015 amendment enabled Special Courts to take direct cognizance of offences under the Act.
134.tq: Ask which authority can act directly and reject added approval requirements not found in the provision.

134.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Enactment of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act
B. Commencement of the Act
C. Enactment of the 2015 Amendment Act
D. Insertion of Section 18A
E. Extension of the Act to Jammu and Kashmir
134.x: The Act was enacted in 1989, commenced in 1990, amended in 2015, Section 18A was inserted in 2018, and its application extended to Jammu and Kashmir in 2019.
134.tq: Fix the first two dates, then place the 2015 amendment, 2018 insertion and 2019 territorial extension.

134.s: A police officer receives a complaint involving an offence under the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. Which course is consistent with the statutory framework?
o: The investigation may be conducted by any constable and the charge-sheet may be filed whenever convenient.
The matter must be transferred to a civil court for preliminary adjudication.
The investigation should be conducted by an officer not below DSP rank and completed with charge-sheet filing within 60 days.
The case must first undergo a preliminary enquiry and receive approval before arrest in every instance.
134.x: The PoA Rules require investigation by an officer not below the rank of DSP and completion with charge-sheet filing in the Special Court within 60 days. Section 18A removes the requirement of preliminary enquiry or approval before arrest.
134.tq: Combine the rank, time-limit and arrest-procedure rules in a practical fact pattern.
134.sec: PoA Rules 1995 - investigation, annual report, relief

134.s: According to Crime in India 2024, released in May 2026, how many cases of crimes against Scheduled Castes were recorded in India?
134.x: Crime in India 2024 recorded 55,698 cases of crimes against Scheduled Castes. The corresponding figure for 2023 was 57,789.
134.tq: Use the exact figure and distinguish it from the immediately preceding year’s comparison figure.

134.s: The number of crimes against Scheduled Castes in 2024 represented what change over the 2023 figure?
134.x: The 55,698 cases recorded in 2024 were 3.6% lower than the 57,789 cases recorded in 2023.
134.tq: Separate the percentage relating to Scheduled Castes from the different percentage reported for Scheduled Tribes.

134.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the NCRB data for 2024:
1. Crimes against Scheduled Tribes declined by 23.1%.
2. Crimes against Scheduled Castes declined by 3.6%.
3. Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Bihar were among the States reporting the highest number of crimes against Scheduled Castes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
134.x: All three statements are correct. Crimes against Scheduled Tribes declined by 23.1%, crimes against Scheduled Castes by 3.6%, and Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Bihar were the leading States mentioned for crimes against Scheduled Castes.
134.tq: Check each percentage and the State grouping independently before selecting the combined code.

134.s: In NCRB data for 2023, how many cases were recorded in which Scheduled Castes were denied access to public spaces under the Prevention of Atrocities Act?
134.x: NCRB recorded 180 such cases nationally in 2023. Uttar Pradesh accounted for 173 of these cases.
134.tq: Distinguish the national total from the State-wise figure given alongside it.

134.s: Which State accounted for 173 of the 180 cases involving denial of access to public spaces to Scheduled Castes recorded by the NCRB in 2023?
134.x: Uttar Pradesh accounted for 173 of the 180 cases recorded nationally in 2023.
134.tq: Match the State-specific figure with the corresponding national total.

134.s: A probe under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) framework was reported to have continued for 26 months, despite the prescribed limit of 60 days. This primarily illustrates which problem?
o: Excessive pendency and delay in investigation
Absence of a Special Court framework
Replacement of criminal investigation by departmental inquiry
134.x: The 26-month duration, compared with the 60-day limit, illustrates chronic pendency and delay in investigation.
134.tq: Apply the numerical comparison to identify the underlying administrative problem.

134.s: Which authority conducted a State-level review in Vijayawada and issued guidelines concerning digital evidence and timely charge-sheets?
o: The State Vigilance and Monitoring Committee
The National Commission for Scheduled Castes
134.x: The Director of Prosecutions conducted the State-level review in Vijayawada and issued the guidelines.
134.tq: Identify the authority associated with the specific prosecutorial action, not the body responsible for general monitoring.

134.s:
Consider the following statements regarding institutional machinery for prevention of atrocities:
1. The State Vigilance and Monitoring Committee is chaired by the Chief Minister.
2. The District Vigilance and Monitoring Committee is chaired by the Collector.
3. A nodal officer is designated at the Secretary level in each State.
4. SC/ST Protection Cells function under an Inspector General or Additional Director General of Police.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
134.x: All four statements correctly describe the institutional machinery: State-level chairmanship by the Chief Minister, district-level chairmanship by the Collector, a Secretary-level nodal officer, and Protection Cells under an IG or ADGP.
134.tq: Verify the level, chairperson and police rank in each institutional arrangement.

134.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: District Vigilance and Monitoring Committee — Collector
SC/ST Protection Cell — chaired by the District Judge
State Vigilance and Monitoring Committee — Chief Minister
134.x: SC/ST Protection Cells function under an Inspector General or Additional Director General of Police, not under a District Judge.
134.tq: Find the institutional mismatch by checking the authority and its administrative level.

134.s: Which of the following correctly describes the institutional arrangement in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Fourteen Special Sessions Courts and one Exclusive Court at Amaravati, supported by Police and Judiciary alone
Fourteen Exclusive Courts and one Special Sessions Court at Vijayawada, supported only by the Police Department
One Special Sessions Court and fourteen Exclusive Courts at Laxmipet, Srikakulam, supported by the Revenue Department alone
Fourteen Special Sessions Courts and one Exclusive Court at Laxmipet, Srikakulam, supported by an SOP involving Police, Revenue, Judiciary and Welfare departments
134.x: Andhra Pradesh has 14 Special Sessions Courts and one Exclusive Court at Laxmipet in Srikakulam. The SOP involves the Police, Revenue, Judiciary and Welfare departments.
134.tq: Check the court count, location and participating departments as one integrated factual unit.

134.s: Which legislation prohibited the employment of manual scavengers and the construction of dry latrines?
o: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955
The Employment of Manual Scavengers and Construction of Dry Latrines (Prohibition) Act, 1993
The Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013
134.x: The 1993 Act prohibited employing manual scavengers and constructing dry latrines. The 2013 Act subsequently widened the prohibition and rehabilitation framework.
134.tq: Discriminate between the similarly named 1993 and 2013 enactments by their distinct scope.

134.s: Within what period must local authorities survey manual scavenging and build sanitary latrines under the 2013 manual scavenging law?
134.x: Local authorities are required to conduct surveys and build sanitary latrines within three years.
134.tq: Focus on the statutory time period and reject nearby duration distractors.

134.s: Which Ministry administers the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013?
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
134.x: The Act is administered by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
134.tq: Use the responsible-Ministry test and distinguish it from departments handling urban sanitation or labour.

134.s: The National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation was established in which year and serves as the nodal agency for which scheme?
o: 1997 — Self-Employment Scheme for Rehabilitation of Manual Scavengers
134.x: NSKFDC was established in 1997 and is the nodal agency for the Self-Employment Scheme for Rehabilitation of Manual Scavengers.
134.tq: Combine the founding year with the exact scheme name to avoid confusing it with later programmes.

134.s:
Consider the following statements regarding offences under the manual scavenging law:
1. The offences are cognizable.
2. The offences are non-bailable.
3. A first contravention may attract imprisonment up to one year or a fine up to ₹50,000.
4. Hazardous sewer cleaning may attract imprisonment up to two years or a fine up to ₹2 lakh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
134.x: All four statements are correct. The offences are cognizable and non-bailable, with the stated penalties for first contravention and hazardous sewer cleaning.
134.tq: Check the procedural classification and each separate punishment before selecting the comprehensive code.

134.s: Which body monitors the implementation of measures relating to manual scavenging and rehabilitation?
134.x: The National Commission for Safai Karamcharis monitors implementation in this field.
134.tq: Match the specialised statutory subject with the institution specifically associated with it.

134.s: In Safai Karamchari Andolan v. Union of India (2014), the Supreme Court directed compensation of what amount for each sewer death occurring since 1993?
134.x: The Supreme Court directed compensation of ₹10 lakh for each sewer death since 1993. The amount was raised to ₹30 lakh in 2023 in Balram Singh.
134.tq: Separate the original judicially directed amount from the later enhanced amount.

134.s: Which of the following correctly reflects the compensation developments relating to sewer deaths?
o: ₹10 lakh was ordered in 2014 and raised to ₹30 lakh in 2023
₹30 lakh was ordered in 2014 and reduced to ₹10 lakh in 2023
₹10 lakh was ordered in 1993 and raised to ₹50 lakh in 2014
₹5 lakh was ordered in 2014 and raised to ₹10 lakh in 2023
134.x: Safai Karamchari Andolan v. Union of India involved ₹10 lakh compensation, which was raised to ₹30 lakh in 2023 in Balram Singh.
134.tq: Track the sequence of the original ruling and the later enhancement rather than reversing the amounts.

134.s: NAMASTE, launched in 2023, is associated with which of the following objectives?
o: Replacing all State Vigilance and Monitoring Committees
Formalising sewer and septic-tank workers and achieving zero sanitation fatalities
Constructing only dry latrines in rural areas
Providing compensation exclusively for denial of public-space access
134.x: NAMASTE formalises sewer and septic-tank workers, subsumed the Self-Employment Scheme for Rehabilitation of Manual Scavengers, and aims at zero sanitation fatalities.
134.tq: Identify the programme through its worker-formalisation and safety objective, not through a general sanitation function.

134.s: The individual capital subsidy under the Swachhata Udyami Yojana was raised in 2026 from:
134.x: In 2026, the individual capital subsidy under the Swachhata Udyami Yojana was increased from ₹5 lakh to ₹7.5 lakh.
134.tq: Read the direction of change carefully and distinguish the old and revised subsidy amounts.

134.s: Under Section 4A of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, as introduced in 2018, which procedural requirement applies to registration of an FIR?
o: The FIR may be registered only after approval by the High Court
A preliminary inquiry must precede every FIR
The FIR can be registered only after completion of the departmental inquiry
The FIR must be registered immediately and no preliminary inquiry is required
134.x: Section 4A requires immediate registration of the FIR and does not permit a preliminary inquiry as a prerequisite.
134.tq: Discriminate between immediate FIR registration and the excluded preliminary-inquiry requirement.

134.s:
Consider the following statements regarding timelines under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act:
1. Investigation is to be completed within 60 days.
2. The charge-sheet is to be filed in the Special Court within 60 days.
3. The Special Court should, as far as possible, complete the trial within two months of the charge-sheet.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
134.x: Investigation and filing of the charge-sheet are subject to 60-day timelines, while the Special Court should, as far as possible, complete the trial within two months of the charge-sheet.
134.tq: Distinguish the two 60-day requirements from the separate two-month trial period.

134.s: An appeal from an order of a Special Court under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, including an order relating to bail, lies to the High Court within:
134.x: An appeal, including an appeal against a bail order, lies to the High Court within 90 days.
134.tq: Test the appellate time limit separately from the investigation and trial timelines.

134.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the measures that States must ensure for implementation of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act?
o: Travel and maintenance expenses for victims and witnesses
Abolition of Special Courts established under the Act
134.x: States must ensure legal aid, travel and maintenance for victims and witnesses, and identification of atrocity-prone areas. Abolition of Special Courts is not such a measure.
134.tq: Find the option that reverses an implementation duty into its opposite.

134.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched under the 2015 amendment to the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act?
o: Economic boycott and social boycott — defined and made atrocities
Economic boycott and social boycott — removed from the Act
Economic boycott — removed; social boycott — made a civil wrong only
Social boycott — defined only under the Protection of Civil Rights Act
134.x: The 2015 amendment defined economic boycott and social boycott and made them offences amounting to atrocities under the Act.
134.tq: Distinguish the two paired expressions and remember that both were added as atrocities by the amendment.

134.s:
With reference to the Centre's task force report of 31 July 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It proposed enhancement of relief for victims.
2. It recommended counselling and State-level relief cells.
3. It proposed that FIRs and charge-sheets be sent to the concerned authorities within 24 hours.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
134.x: The task force report proposed higher relief, counselling, State relief cells, and transmission of FIRs and charge-sheets to the authorities within 24 hours.
134.tq: Combine several recommendations and identify the option containing all the correct statements.

134.s: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes has advocated which combination of measures in cases involving alleged atrocities against tribals?
o: Counter-FIR scrutiny and protection of the livelihood of dispossessed tribals
Preliminary inquiry before every FIR and transfer of cases to civil courts
Abolition of counter-FIRs and withdrawal of livelihood assistance
Compulsory settlement of cases through village councils and suspension of relief
134.x: The NCST has sought scrutiny of counter-FIRs and protection of the livelihood of tribals who have been dispossessed.
134.tq: Match the institutional recommendation with the correct vulnerable-group concern.

134.s: The Madras High Court has held, in the context of offences under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, that:
o: A preliminary inquiry is mandatory before registration of every FIR.
An FIR may be registered only after approval by the State relief cell.
No preliminary inquiry is required before registration of an FIR.
A preliminary inquiry is required only where a counter-FIR is filed.
134.x: The Madras High Court held that a preliminary inquiry is not required before registration of an FIR in such cases.
134.tq: Test the judicial position by distinguishing a mandatory preliminary inquiry from direct FIR registration.

134.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the contemporary debate surrounding the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act:
1. Claims of misuse have been raised in the debate.
2. Low conviction rates have also been cited as a concern.
3. Counter-FIRs have been alleged to be used for intimidating complainants.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
134.x: The debate includes allegations of misuse, concerns regarding low convictions, and criticism that counter-FIRs may intimidate complainants.
134.tq: Use a three-part statement question to separate parallel criticisms from a single-sided view.

134.s: The Andhra Pradesh Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act, 1989 is primarily associated with prohibition of which practice?
134.x: The Andhra Pradesh Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act, 1989 was enacted against the Jogini system.
134.tq: Identify the legislation through its specific social practice rather than through a general rights category.

134.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the significance of the Supreme Court's decision in Sukanya Shantha (2024)?
o: Article 17 applies only to physical exclusion from public wells and temples.
Article 17 permits purity-based distinctions when followed by customary communities.
Article 17 concerns only untouchability imposed by private employers.
134.x: The Sukanya Shantha decision held that Article 17 bars caste-based purity stigma, expanding the understanding of untouchability beyond narrow physical exclusion.
134.tq: Apply the constitutional provision to the precise form of discrimination identified by the judgment.

134.s: A ritual described as post-rally 'shuddhikaran' revived a constitutional debate concerning which of the following?
o: Whether caste-based purity stigma constitutes untouchability
Whether relief under the PoA Act can be paid in cash
Whether Devadasi dedication is a form of bonded labour
Whether political rallies require prior judicial permission
134.x: The post-rally 'shuddhikaran' ritual revived the debate over whether caste-based purity stigma falls within the prohibition of untouchability under Article 17.
134.tq: Link the practical scenario to the constitutional issue it raises, avoiding unrelated social-law concepts.

134.s: A High Court questioned the police in a case where the investigation under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act had changed hands six times. Which additional circumstance led to judicial concern?
o: The accused had been acquitted six times by separate Special Courts.
The case had been transferred to six different High Courts within 60 days.
The investigation had been completed within 24 hours without recording statements.
The investigation had remained pending for 26 months beyond the prescribed 60-day limit.
134.x: The High Court noted that the probe had changed hands six times and was delayed by 26 months beyond the 60-day limit.
134.tq: Use the paired numerical clues—six transfers, 26 months and 60 days—to identify the correct procedural circumstance.

134.s: The 2018 development concerning the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act is commonly described as:
o: The Mahajan judgment followed by the legislative response through Section 18A
The Sukanya Shantha judgment followed by repeal of Article 17
The Devadasi judgment followed by insertion of Section 24A
The Madras High Court ruling followed by abolition of Special Courts
134.x: The 2018 episode refers to the Mahajan judgment and the subsequent legislative response through Section 18A of the PoA Act.
134.tq: Recognise the linked judicial-development and legislative-response sequence.

134.s: Which of the following is the principal rehabilitation-related objective associated with the Andhra Pradesh Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act, 1989?
o: Rehabilitation of government servants dismissed for misconduct
Rehabilitation of only displaced industrial workers
Rehabilitation of persons convicted under the PoA Act
134.x: The Andhra Pradesh measure is associated with the rehabilitation of women affected by the Jogini system.
134.tq: Distinguish the Act's rehabilitation focus from unrelated categories of beneficiaries.

134.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh support measure mentioned for 2024–25, free power for Scheduled Caste households is provided up to:
134.x: The measure provides free power up to 200 units for Scheduled Caste households, with an allocation of ₹300 crore for 2024–25.
134.tq: Test the exact numerical ceiling and avoid confusing it with the associated budget allocation.

134.s: The allocation mentioned for providing free power to Scheduled Caste households in Andhra Pradesh during 2024–25 was:
134.x: An allocation of ₹300 crore was mentioned for free power up to 200 units for Scheduled Caste households in 2024–25.
134.tq: Separate the monetary allocation from the electricity-unit limit in a paired numerical fact.

135.s: Which Constitutional Amendment inserted Article 15(4) into the Constitution of India following the Champakam Dorairajan case?
135.x: The First Constitutional Amendment Act of 1951 inserted Article 15(4), enabling special provisions for the advancement of socially and educationally backward classes and SCs and STs.
135.tq: Directly identify the amendment associated with a specific constitutional article.
135.sec: Constitutional amendments on reservation → content and bill numbers

135.s: Article 16(4A), relating to reservation in promotion for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, was inserted by the
135.x: The 77th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1995 inserted Article 16(4A) to provide reservation in promotion for SCs and STs, in response to the Indra Sawhney judgment.
135.tq: Use the article-number and amendment-number association to distinguish closely related reservation amendments.
135.sec: Constitutional amendments on reservation → content and bill numbers

135.s: The 85th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2001 provided for
o: identification of SEBCs by the States
consequential seniority in promotion and nullified the catch-up rule
reservation in private unaided educational institutions including minority institutions
135.x: The 85th Amendment provided consequential seniority along with promotion and nullified the catch-up rule.
135.tq: Use a distinctive legal consequence to identify the correct amendment.
135.sec: Constitutional amendments on reservation → content and bill numbers

135.s:
With reference to the 93rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2005, consider the following statements:
1. It inserted Article 15(5).
2. It enabled reservation in educational institutions, including private unaided institutions.
3. Minority educational institutions were excluded from its scope.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
135.x: The 93rd Amendment inserted Article 15(5) and enabled reservation in educational institutions, including private unaided institutions, while excluding minority institutions.
135.tq: Test the main provision together with its important constitutional exception.
135.sec: Constitutional amendments on reservation → content and bill numbers

135.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: 103rd Amendment — Constitutional status to the NCBC
135.x: The 102nd Amendment Act, 2018 gave constitutional status to the NCBC through Article 338B and inserted Article 342A. Article 15(5) belongs to the 93rd Amendment, EWS reservation to the 103rd, and restoration of States' power to the 105th.
135.tq: Trap article and amendment swaps by matching each amendment with its exact constitutional change.
135.sec: Constitutional amendments on reservation → content and bill numbers

135.s: The 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019 is associated with
o: 27 per cent reservation for OBCs in Central educational institutions
restoration of States' power to identify SEBCs
10 per cent reservation for Economically Weaker Sections and amendments to Articles 15 and 16
reservation in promotion for SCs and STs
135.x: The 103rd Amendment introduced 10 per cent reservation for EWS and amended Articles 15 and 16 for this purpose.
135.tq: Identify the famous policy measure associated with the amendment rather than a neighbouring reservation provision.
135.sec: Constitutional amendments on reservation → content and bill numbers

135.s: Which of the following correctly represents the amendment and the corresponding Constitutional Amendment Bill?
135.x: The 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act was enacted from the 124th Constitutional Amendment Bill. The 102nd and 105th Amendments corresponded to the 123rd and 127th Bills respectively.
135.tq: Distinguish the enacted amendment number from the preceding bill number.
135.sec: Constitutional amendments on reservation → content and bill numbers

135.s: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
o: The 82nd Amendment concerns relaxation of qualifying standards in promotion for SCs and STs.
The 81st Amendment deals with unfilled backlog vacancies.
The 89th Amendment introduced the relaxation of qualifying marks under Article 335.
The 77th Amendment deals with reservation in promotion for SCs and STs.
135.x: The 89th Amendment did not introduce the relaxation of qualifying marks; that change was made by the 82nd Amendment Act, 2000. The 89th Amendment is associated with the bifurcation of the SC/ST Commission.
135.tq: Find the wrong amendment-provision association among closely related reservation amendments.
135.sec: Constitutional amendments on reservation → content and bill numbers

135.s: Under Article 340 of the Constitution, a commission to investigate the conditions of socially and educationally backward classes is appointed by the
o: Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment
135.x: Article 340 empowers the President to appoint a commission to investigate the conditions of socially and educationally backward classes and recommend remedial measures.
135.tq: Apply the 'who would do this job?' method to identify the constitutional authority.

135.s: The Kaka Kalelkar Commission did not accept which of the following as the criterion for identifying backward classes?
o: Poor representation in trade and industry
135.x: The Kaka Kalelkar Commission did not accept caste as the criterion, although its broader criteria included educational and occupational disadvantage and inadequate representation.
135.tq: Test the crucial distinction between the criteria considered and the criterion rejected.

135.s: The Second Backward Classes Commission, popularly known as the Mandal Commission, was set up in 1979 by the
135.x: The B.P. Mandal Commission was established in 1979 by the Janata Government headed by Morarji Desai.
135.tq: Avoid the common trap of confusing the government that appointed a commission with the government that implemented its recommendations.

135.s: The Mandal Commission recommended reservation of what percentage of posts for Other Backward Classes?
135.x: The Mandal Commission recommended 27 per cent reservation for OBCs. Its estimate that OBCs constituted 52 per cent of the population was a population figure, not the recommended quota.
135.tq: Distinguish the recommended reservation percentage from the estimated share of the population.

135.s: Which of the following correctly describes the implementation of the Mandal Commission recommendations?
o: They were implemented by the V.P. Singh Government in 1990, and 27 per cent of Central civil posts were reserved in 1993.
They were implemented by the V.P. Singh Government in 1993, and posts were reserved in 1995.
They were implemented by the Morarji Desai Government in 1979, and posts were reserved in 1980.
They were implemented by the Nehru Government in 1955, and posts were reserved in 1990.
135.x: The V.P. Singh Government implemented the Mandal recommendations in 1990, and 27 per cent of Central civil posts were reserved for OBCs in 1993.
135.tq: Track the sequence of appointment, report, political implementation and operational reservation.

135.s: The Mandal Commission used how many indicators covering social, educational and economic factors?
135.x: The Mandal Commission used 11 indicators covering social, educational and economic dimensions of backwardness.
135.tq: Recall the exact quantitative detail attached to the commission's methodology.

135.s: Justice G. Rohini Commission was constituted in 2017 primarily for
o: identifying the first list of OBCs under Article 340
determining the constitutional validity of EWS reservation
preparing the list of Scheduled Tribes
135.x: The Justice G. Rohini Commission was constituted in 2017 to examine the sub-categorisation of OBCs.
135.tq: Match the commission's name and year with its specific mandate.

135.s: Which of the following observations is associated with the Justice G. Rohini Commission?
o: About 3 per cent of benefits went to 97 per cent of the sub-castes.
All OBC communities received an equal share of reservation benefits.
Nearly 52 per cent of the population received 27 per cent reservation.
Around 97 per cent of OBC benefits went to 25 per cent of the sub-castes, while about 1,000 communities received none.
135.x: The Rohini Commission's findings indicated that approximately 97 per cent of OBC benefits went to 25 per cent of the sub-castes, while about 1,000 communities received no benefits.
135.tq: Handle paired percentages and community counts without reversing their relationship.

135.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the two early Backward Classes Commissions is correct?
o: The Kaka Kalelkar Commission listed about 2,399 castes, whereas the Mandal Commission estimated OBCs at 52 per cent of the population.
The Kaka Kalelkar Commission was appointed in 1979 and the Mandal Commission in 1953.
Both commissions were appointed by the V.P. Singh Government.
Both commissions recommended 27 per cent reservation and were fully implemented.
135.x: The Kaka Kalelkar Commission's report listed about 2,399 castes, while the Mandal Commission estimated OBCs at 52 per cent of the population. The two commissions differed in date, government and outcome.
135.tq: Compare corresponding rows of the two commission profiles rather than memorising isolated names.

135.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Constitution expressly defines the term 'backward classes'.
2. Article 340 enables the President to appoint a commission to investigate the conditions of SEBCs.
3. The Mandal Commission was appointed under Article 340.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
135.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. The Constitution does not define the expression 'backward classes'; Article 340 provides for a commission to investigate their conditions and recommend remedies.
135.tq: Use the negative constitutional fact to eliminate the statement that sounds formally plausible but is incorrect.

135.s: Before the 102nd Constitutional Amendment, Article 338(10) provided that references to Scheduled Castes would include such backward classes as were specified by the
135.x: Before the 102nd Amendment, Article 338(10) treated references to Scheduled Castes as including such backward classes as the President specified. Consequently, complaints relating to backward classes could go to the SC Commission.
135.tq: Identify the constitutional authority named in the transitional provision.

135.s: The 102nd Constitutional Amendment added Article 366(26C), which defines Socially and Educationally Backward Classes by reference to
135.x: Article 366(26C), added by the 102nd Amendment, defines SEBCs by reference to Article 342A.
135.tq: Distinguish the defining provision from the related provisions on reservation, commissions and promotion.

135.s: The Supreme Court judgment in which case struck down the Madras Communal Government Order and led to the First Constitutional Amendment?
o: Indra Sawhney v. Union of India
M.R. Balaji v. State of Mysore
Champakam Dorairajan v. State of Madras
Ashoka Kumar Thakur v. Union of India
135.x: In Champakam Dorairajan (1951), the Madras Communal Government Order was struck down, leading to the First Constitutional Amendment.
135.tq: Identify the case from the specific constitutional consequence.

135.s:
With reference to M.R. Balaji v. State of Mysore, consider the following statements:
1. Caste cannot be the sole test for determining backwardness.
2. Reservation should generally remain below 50 per cent.
3. The case upheld reservation without prescribing any requirement of reasonableness.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
135.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The judgment emphasised that reservation must be reasonable and that caste cannot be the sole test; statement 3 is incorrect.
135.tq: Find the false statement by testing the omitted qualification of reasonableness.

135.s: In Indra Sawhney v. Union of India, the constitutional validity of the 27 per cent reservation for OBCs was upheld by a nine-judge Bench by what majority?
135.x: The nine-judge Bench decided Indra Sawhney by a 6:3 majority and upheld the 27 per cent OBC quota subject to exclusion of the creamy layer.
135.tq: Use the distinctive bench-strength and majority figures together.

135.s: Which one of the following was NOT a holding of the Supreme Court in Indra Sawhney (1992)?
o: A general ceiling of 50 per cent on reservations
Reservation in promotions for backward classes as a general rule
Exclusion of the creamy layer from OBC reservation
Establishment of a permanent body for backward classes
135.x: Indra Sawhney did not permit reservation in promotions as a general rule. It upheld 27 per cent OBC reservation, excluded the creamy layer, prescribed a 50 per cent ceiling subject to exceptional cases, and directed creation of a permanent backward-classes body.
135.tq: Eliminate the option that reverses the case’s principal limitation.

135.s:
The judgment in M. Nagaraj v. Union of India (2006) upheld the constitutional amendments relating to reservation in promotion subject to which conditions?
1. Backwardness must be established.
2. Inadequate representation must be supported by quantifiable data.
3. Administrative efficiency must be considered.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
135.x: All three conditions were recognised in M. Nagaraj: backwardness, inadequate representation supported by quantifiable data, and preservation of administrative efficiency.
135.tq: Treat a complete list of conditions as correct only when every condition belongs to the judgment.

135.s: M. Nagaraj v. Union of India is associated with upholding which of the following amendments, subject to conditions?
135.x: M. Nagaraj (2006) upheld the 77th and 85th Constitutional Amendments concerning reservation in promotion, subject to specified constitutional conditions.
135.tq: Match the case with the precise amendment pair.

135.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Ashoka Kumar Thakur v. Union of India (2008):
1. It upheld the 93rd Constitutional Amendment.
2. It upheld the 2006 law concerning reservation in State and aided institutions.
3. It held that the creamy layer among OBCs need not be excluded.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
135.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The creamy layer had to be excluded, so statement 3 is incorrect.
135.tq: Spot the reversed position on creamy-layer exclusion.

135.s:
With reference to Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India (November 2022), consider the following statements:
1. The EWS reservation was upheld by a 3:2 majority.
2. The 50 per cent ceiling was held to apply to backward-class reservations, but not to EWS reservation.
3. The judgment was delivered unanimously.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
135.x: The EWS reservation was upheld in Janhit Abhiyan by a 3:2 majority. The 50 per cent ceiling was treated as applicable to backward-class reservations and not to EWS; statement 3 is false because the Bench was divided.
135.tq: Use the majority figure to reject the absolute word in the third statement.

135.s: The Supreme Court’s decision in Jaishri Laxmanrao Patil v. State of Maharashtra (2021) primarily concerned which issue?
o: Validity of the Maratha reservation exceeding the 50 per cent ceiling
Validity of reservation for SC converts to Christianity
Exclusion of the creamy layer from EWS reservation
135.x: The Maratha quota was struck down for crossing the 50 per cent ceiling without exceptional circumstances.
135.tq: Identify the case from its distinctive reservation group and ceiling issue.

135.s: Which one of the following correctly states the effect of the 105th Constitutional Amendment (2021) in relation to the Maratha reservation judgment?
o: It removed the 50 per cent ceiling in all reservation matters.
It abolished the Central list of SEBCs.
It reversed the reading of the 102nd Amendment that had restricted the States’ power to identify SEBCs.
It prohibited States from maintaining backward-class lists.
135.x: The 105th Amendment reversed the interpretation of the 102nd Amendment in the Maratha case and restored the States’ power to identify socially and educationally backward classes.
135.tq: Test the constitutional amendment as a corrective response to a judicial interpretation.

135.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Case)
A. Champakam Dorairajan
B. M.R. Balaji
C. M. Nagaraj
D. Jarnail Singh

List-II (Principal issue)
1. Conditions for reservation in promotion
2. Madras Communal Government Order
3. Caste not being the sole test and reservation below 50 per cent
4. Creamy layer in SC/ST promotions

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
135.x: Champakam Dorairajan concerned the Communal Government Order; M.R. Balaji concerned caste and the 50 per cent principle; M. Nagaraj concerned promotional reservation conditions; Jarnail Singh concerned creamy layer in SC/ST promotions.
135.tq: Start from the sure case-issue pairs and eliminate incompatible codes.

135.s: In Andhra Pradesh, which group is associated with aboriginal tribes, Vimukta Jatis and nomadic groups?
135.x: BC-A comprises aboriginal tribes, Vimukta Jatis and nomadic groups and has a 7 per cent quota.
135.tq: Discriminate between closely related BC group labels and their social composition.
135.sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

135.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched in relation to the Andhra Pradesh BC groups?
o: BC-E — aboriginal tribes and nomadic groups
135.x: BC-D consists of other classes. BC-B comprises vocational or occupational groups, BC-C comprises SC converts to Christianity, and BC-E comprises socially and educationally backward Muslims.
135.tq: Use the group-composition pairs to detect swapped categories.
135.sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

135.s:
Consider the following pairs relating to BC reservation in Andhra Pradesh:
1. BC-A — 7 per cent
2. BC-B — 10 per cent
3. BC-C — 1 per cent
4. BC-D — 7 per cent
5. BC-E — 4 per cent
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
135.x: All five pairs are correct. The respective shares are BC-A 7 per cent, BC-B 10 per cent, BC-C 1 per cent, BC-D 7 per cent and BC-E 4 per cent.
135.tq: Check every numerical pair individually before selecting the complete combination.
135.sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

135.s: The BC-E category in Andhra Pradesh was added through which measure and in which year?
135.x: BC-E was added by the Andhra Pradesh Act of 2007. Earlier lists commonly included only BC-A to BC-D.
135.tq: Match the category’s introduction with the specific legal instrument and year.
135.sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

135.s:
Arrange the following developments relating to the Andhra Pradesh Muslim quota in chronological order:
A. The 2004 quota was struck down.
B. The 2005 quota was struck down.
C. The 2007 Act providing a 4 per cent quota was enacted.
D. The 2007 Act was struck down by the Andhra Pradesh High Court in 2010.
135.x: The 2004 and 2005 quotas were struck down first, followed by the 2007 Act providing 4 per cent reservation, which was struck down by the High Court in 2010.
135.tq: Fix the years first and then arrange the two earlier quota decisions.
135.sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

135.s: What was the effect of the Supreme Court’s interim order concerning the 4 per cent reservation for backward Muslim groups in Andhra Pradesh?
o: It permanently approved the quota without further judicial examination.
It allowed the quota to continue pending consideration by a Constitution Bench.
It converted the quota into an EWS reservation.
It abolished the quota immediately after the High Court judgment.
135.x: Although the Andhra Pradesh High Court struck down the 2007 Act in 2010, the Supreme Court permitted the 4 per cent quota to continue by an interim order pending a Constitution Bench.
135.tq: Distinguish an interim continuation from final constitutional approval.
135.sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

135.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the Kapu reservation proposal is correct?
1. The Justice Manjunatha Commission was constituted in 2016.
2. A 2017 Bill proposed 5 per cent reservation for Kapus as BC-F.
3. The proposal was approved by the Centre.
4. In 2019, Kapus received 5 per cent reservation within the 10 per cent EWS quota, which was later withdrawn by the succeeding government.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
135.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. The Centre never approved the 2017 BC-F proposal, so statement 3 is false.
135.tq: Find the wrong authority-action statement among otherwise connected facts.
135.sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

135.s: The combined quota shares of BC-A, BC-B, BC-C, BC-D and BC-E in Andhra Pradesh amount to:
135.x: The shares are 7 per cent, 10 per cent, 1 per cent, 7 per cent and 4 per cent respectively, totalling 29 per cent.
135.tq: Add the category-wise figures rather than confusing them with the local-body quota.
135.sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

135.s: After 1956, which arrangement was made in relation to backward-class lists in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Separate lists were prepared only for Rayalaseema and Coastal Andhra.
Separate BC lists were maintained for Andhra and Telangana, containing 86 castes for Andhra.
A single list was prepared for the entire State without regional distinction.
BC lists were abolished and replaced by the EWS list.
135.x: After 1956, separate backward-class lists existed for Andhra and Telangana; the Andhra list contained 86 castes.
135.tq: Test the regional administrative distinction and the associated number together.
135.sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

135.s: What was provided by the 1963 Government Order relating to backward classes in Andhra Pradesh?
o: 5 per cent reservation for Kapus as BC-F
4 per cent reservation for backward Muslims
20 per cent of local-body seats for BCs
25 per cent of medical seats for 139 castes
135.x: The 1963 Government Order provided 25 per cent of medical seats for 139 castes.
135.tq: Match the Government Order with its sector, percentage and caste count.
135.sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

135.s: The Sukhdev case concerning backward-class reservation in Andhra Pradesh resulted in which of the following conclusions?
o: Caste alone could not be the basis, and 112 classes were identified using poverty, residence and occupation.
All reservation for backward classes was unconstitutional.
Caste alone could be the basis for identifying backward classes.
Reservation could be based only on residence.
135.x: The High Court held in the Sukhdev case that caste alone could not be the basis; consequently, 112 classes were listed using poverty, residence and occupation as considerations.
135.tq: Link the judicial principle with the resulting classification exercise.
135.sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

135.s: Which commission was the first Andhra Pradesh Backward Classes Commission and framed the A-D grouping along with a 25 per cent quota?
135.x: The Anantharaman Commission was the first Andhra Pradesh Backward Classes Commission; its report was submitted in 1970 and it framed the A-D grouping and a 25 per cent quota.
135.tq: Identify the commission from its distinctive first-commission and grouping role.
135.sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

135.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Muralidhara Rao Commission?
o: It was constituted in 2016 to examine Kapu reservation only.
It decided the constitutional validity of EWS reservation in 2022.
It took charge on 27 January 1982, reviewed BC reservation and examined inclusion of minorities.
135.x: The Muralidhara Rao Commission took charge on 27 January 1982, reviewed BC reservation, examined minority inclusion and contributed to a higher total quota.
135.tq: Use the commission’s date and subject of inquiry to distinguish it from other bodies.
135.sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

135.s:
Consider the following statements regarding reservation for BCs in Andhra Pradesh local bodies:
1. NTR introduced a 20 per cent BC quota in 1984.
2. The quota was raised to 34 per cent for polls held in 1995, 2001, 2006 and 2013.
3. It was subsequently reduced to 24.15 per cent under Government Orders 176, 559 and 560.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
135.x: All three statements are correct: the quota began at 20 per cent in 1984, rose to 34 per cent for the specified elections, and was later reduced to 24.15 per cent under the cited Government Orders.
135.tq: Track the changing percentage chronologically and retain the order-specific details.
135.sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

135.s: According to the stated current arrangement for Andhra Pradesh local bodies, the BC quota is:
o: 34 per cent in rural and 33.33 per cent in urban local bodies
29 per cent in rural and 34 per cent in urban local bodies
33.33 per cent in rural and 34 per cent in urban local bodies
24.15 per cent in rural and 20 per cent in urban local bodies
135.x: The stated arrangement provides 34 per cent reservation in rural local bodies and 33.33 per cent in urban local bodies.
135.tq: Compare the rural and urban figures without reversing their order.
135.sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

135.s: G.O. Rt. No. 1065 dated 19 August 2026 relates to BC reservation in urban local-body elections under which laws?
o: The Representation of the People Act, 1951 and the Municipalities Act, 1965
The Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act, 1994 and the Municipalities Act, 1965
The AP Municipal Corporations Act, 1994 and the Municipalities Act, 1965
The AP Municipal Corporations Act, 1965 and the Panchayat Raj Act, 1994
135.x: G.O. Rt. No. 1065 dated 19 August 2026 concerns urban local-body polls under the AP Municipal Corporations Act, 1994 and the Municipalities Act, 1965.
135.tq: Match the Government Order with the correct pair of statutes and date.
135.sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

135.s:
The Supreme Court’s triple test for OBC reservation in local bodies requires:
1. A dedicated commission to examine backwardness.
2. Determination of the reservation proportion local-body-wise.
3. Keeping the total reservation within the 50 per cent ceiling.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
