135.x: All three requirements form the triple test: a dedicated commission, local-body-wise proportional determination, and compliance with the overall 50 per cent ceiling.
135.tq: Recognise a judicial test as a cumulative set of mandatory conditions.
135.sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

135.s: The earlier 34 per cent reservation for BCs in Andhra Pradesh local bodies was struck down primarily because it:
o: Was introduced through a Constitutional Amendment
Was confined to urban local bodies only
135.x: The earlier 34 per cent local-body reservation was struck down for breaching the overall reservation ceiling.
135.tq: Identify the constitutional limitation triggered by the percentage claimed.
135.sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

135.s: Which Constitutional Amendment inserted Articles 15(6) and 16(6) to provide reservation for Economically Weaker Sections?
135.x: The 103rd Constitutional Amendment, enacted in January 2019, inserted Articles 15(6) and 16(6) for EWS reservation.
135.tq: Use the amendment-number and provision pairing to distinguish closely related constitutional amendments.

135.s:
With reference to reservation for Economically Weaker Sections, consider the following statements:
1. It may extend up to 10 per cent.
2. It is available only to persons covered by SC, ST or OBC quotas.
3. It is in addition to the existing reservation quotas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
135.x: EWS reservation may extend up to 10 per cent and is additional to existing quotas. It is meant for persons not covered by SC, ST or OBC reservation.
135.tq: Split the options by checking the exclusion condition in statement 2.

135.s:
The constitutional provisions relating to EWS reservation are applicable to which of the following institutions or sectors?
1. Central educational institutions
2. Private educational institutions
3. Posts under the Central Government
4. State Governments on a compulsory basis
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
135.x: The 103rd Amendment provides EWS reservation in central educational institutions, including private institutions, and in posts. Its implementation is not mandatory for State Governments.
135.tq: Identify the statement that overstates the constitutional obligation by using a compulsory application to States.

135.s: For determining EWS eligibility, which one of the following combinations correctly represents the income and asset criteria stated for the purpose?
o: Annual family income below ₹5 lakh, land below 2 acres and flat below 800 sq ft
Annual family income below ₹8 lakh, agricultural land below 10 acres and flat below 1,000 sq ft
Annual family income below ₹8 lakh, agricultural land below 5 acres and flat below 1,000 sq ft
Annual family income below ₹10 lakh, agricultural land below 5 acres and flat below 1,500 sq ft
135.x: The stated EWS criteria include annual family income below ₹8 lakh, agricultural land below 5 acres and a flat below 1,000 square feet.
135.tq: Match the numerical threshold with the associated land and dwelling limits.

135.s: The Supreme Court judgment in Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India was delivered on which date?
135.x: The Supreme Court upheld the 103rd Amendment in Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India on 7 November 2022.
135.tq: Discriminate between the amendment year and the date of the later judicial decision.

135.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the decision in Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India:
1. The 103rd Constitutional Amendment was upheld by a 3:2 majority.
2. Chief Justice U.U. Lalit dissented.
3. Justice S. Ravindra Bhat dissented.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
135.x: The EWS amendment was upheld by a 3:2 majority, while Chief Justice U.U. Lalit and Justice S. Ravindra Bhat were among the dissenting judges.
135.tq: Check the judicial split first, then verify both named dissenting judges.

135.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the 50 per cent ceiling referred to in the context of reservation from EWS reservation?
o: The ceiling applies to backward-class reservations, whereas EWS reservation was provided additionally under Articles 15(6) and 16(6).
The ceiling applies only to reservations in promotions.
The ceiling applies exclusively to EWS reservation.
The ceiling was abolished by the 103rd Amendment.
135.x: The 50 per cent ceiling discussed in this context relates to backward-class reservations. EWS reservation was introduced additionally through Articles 15(6) and 16(6).
135.tq: Separate the general reservation ceiling from the constitutional source of EWS reservation.

135.s: Which of the following statements about the expression “Backward Classes” in the Constitution is correct?
o: It is exhaustively defined in Article 15.
It is defined in Article 340 itself.
It is defined only in the Fifth Schedule.
It is not defined in the Constitution.
135.x: The Constitution does not define the expression “Backward Classes”; constitutional provisions instead provide mechanisms concerning their identification and welfare.
135.tq: Test the exact constitutional status of a frequently misattributed definition.

135.s: The 27 per cent reservation for OBCs in Central Government jobs came into effect from which year?
135.x: The 27 per cent OBC quota in Central Government jobs came into effect from 1993.
135.tq: Distinguish the year of implementation in jobs from the later year of implementation in central educational institutions.

135.s: The Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006, providing 27 per cent OBC reservation, came into force in:
135.x: Although enacted in 2006, the Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act came into force in 2007.
135.tq: Separate the enactment year from the commencement year.

135.s: Which one of the following was the principal objective of the Oversight Committee headed by M. Veerappa Moily in 2006?
o: To prepare the Central List of Scheduled Tribes
To implement OBC reservation by expanding seats so that general-category seats did not shrink
To identify the creamy layer among SCs and STs
To abolish reservation in Central educational institutions
135.x: The Oversight Committee headed by M. Veerappa Moily planned implementation through expansion of seats, thereby protecting the existing number of general-category seats.
135.tq: Use the committee’s stated implementation purpose rather than its year alone.

135.s: The expansion of seats contemplated by the Oversight Committee for implementing OBC reservation was approximately:
135.x: The committee contemplated raising the total number of seats by about 54 per cent, in a phased manner, so that general-category seats would not be reduced.
135.tq: Match the committee’s implementation plan with its approximate quantitative figure.

135.s: The National Commission for Backward Classes examines requests relating principally to:
o: Appointment of judges to the Supreme Court
Inclusion in or exclusion from backward-class lists
135.x: The NCBC examines requests for inclusion in or exclusion from the lists of backward classes and advises on such matters.
135.tq: Ask which constitutional body would handle the specific administrative request.

135.s: Which of the following correctly describes Article 15(5)?
o: It provides for appointment of a commission on SEBC conditions.
It provides reservation in promotions for SCs and STs.
It provides for special provisions for SEBCs, SCs and STs in admissions, including private institutions, except minority institutions.
It provides for carry-forward of backlog vacancies.
135.x: Article 15(5), inserted by the 93rd Amendment, permits special provisions for SEBCs, SCs and STs in admission to educational institutions, including private aided and unaided institutions, while excluding minority institutions.
135.tq: Distinguish admission provisions from promotion, carry-forward and commission-related provisions.

135.s: The 93rd Constitutional Amendment is associated with which one of the following provisions?
o: Constitutional status for the NCBC under Article 338B
Reservation for EWS under Articles 15(6) and 16(6)
Identification of the Central List under Article 342A
Special provisions for admission under Article 15(5)
135.x: The 93rd Amendment inserted Article 15(5), enabling special provisions for admission of SEBCs, SCs and STs, including in private educational institutions other than minority institutions.
135.tq: Use the amendment–Article pairing to avoid confusing the 93rd, 102nd and 103rd Amendments.

135.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Article)
A. Article 15(4)
B. Article 16(4A)
C. Article 16(4B)
D. Article 340

List-II (Subject)
1. Carry-forward of backlog vacancies
2. Commission on conditions of SEBCs
3. Special provisions for SEBCs, SCs and STs
4. Reservation in promotion for SCs and STs with consequential seniority

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
135.x: Article 15(4) concerns special provisions for SEBCs, SCs and STs; Article 16(4A) concerns promotion for SCs and STs; Article 16(4B) concerns backlog vacancies; and Article 340 concerns a commission on SEBC conditions.
135.tq: Start with the sure Article 340–commission pair and then complete the reservation pairings.

135.s: Under Article 342A, which one of the following is correct?
o: The President specifies the Central List of SEBCs, while States retain their own lists.
The Governor specifies the Central List of SEBCs, while States have no separate lists.
The NCBC alone specifies both Central and State lists.
The Supreme Court specifies the Central List of SEBCs.
135.x: Article 342A provides for specification of SEBCs for the Central List by the President, while States retain their own lists.
135.tq: Use the authority–list distinction to separate Central List and State List powers.

135.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Article 15(6) — EWS reservation in education
2. Article 16(6) — EWS reservation in public employment
3. Article 338B — National Commission for Backward Classes
4. Article 342A — Central List of SEBCs
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
135.x: Articles 15(6) and 16(6) concern EWS reservation in education and public employment respectively; Article 338B concerns the NCBC; and Article 342A concerns the Central List of SEBCs.
135.tq: Verify each Article–subject pair independently before selecting the coded combination.

135.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indra Sawhney judgment:
1. Caste may be the main criterion for determining backwardness.
2. Total reservation should ordinarily not exceed 50 per cent.
3. The creamy layer among OBCs should be excluded.
4. Reservation for OBCs was extended to promotions as a general rule.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
135.x: Indra Sawhney accepted caste as a possible main criterion, prescribed the general 50 per cent ceiling and excluded the creamy layer. It confined reservation to initial appointments and did not extend it to promotions as a general rule.
135.tq: Locate the single reversal in the statement dealing with promotion.

135.s: According to the ruling in Indra Sawhney, the 50 per cent ceiling on reservation may be exceeded:
o: Whenever a State Government considers it desirable
135.x: The judgment laid down that total reservation should ordinarily not exceed 50 per cent, though extraordinary circumstances may justify an exception.
135.tq: Watch for the distinction between an ordinary rule and an absolute prohibition.

135.s: Which one of the following statements correctly reflects the ruling in Indra Sawhney regarding carry-forward vacancies?
o: Carry-forward is allowed, but it must operate within the 50 per cent ceiling on a year-by-year basis.
Carry-forward is prohibited in every situation.
Carry-forward applies only to EWS vacancies.
Carry-forward is unlimited and is calculated only once in a decade.
135.x: Indra Sawhney permitted carry-forward of vacancies, subject to the 50 per cent ceiling being applied year by year.
135.tq: Combine the carry-forward rule with the year-by-year ceiling rather than treating either as absolute.

135.s: The reservation contemplated in Indra Sawhney was confined primarily to:
o: Private employment, and not public employment
Political representation, and not public employment
135.x: The judgment confined the reservation policy under consideration to initial appointments and held that it did not apply to promotions.
135.tq: Discriminate between the two stages of public service—appointment and promotion.

135.s: The permanent statutory body for backward-class lists directed by the Supreme Court in Indra Sawhney subsequently became the:
135.x: The permanent statutory body directed for backward-class lists subsequently became the National Commission for Backward Classes.
135.tq: Match the judicially directed institutional role with the body that performs it.

135.s: The criteria for identifying the creamy layer among OBCs were framed through which of the following instruments and period?
o: The 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act, based on the Kalelkar Commission
The Ministry of Social Justice notification of 2004, based on the Justice G. Rohini Commission
The DoPT Office Memorandum of September 1993, based on the Justice R.N. Prasad Expert Committee
The DoPT Office Memorandum of 2017, based on the Mandal Commission
135.x: The creamy-layer criteria were framed through the DoPT Office Memorandum of September 1993, based on the Justice R.N. Prasad Expert Committee.
135.tq: Identify the correct instrument, year and associated committee together.
135.sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

135.s: Which one of the following is NOT a status-based category associated with exclusion from the OBC creamy layer?
o: Children of senior government and armed-forces officers
Children of all persons belonging to Scheduled Castes
135.x: Status-based exclusions include children of constitutional post-holders, senior government and armed-forces officers, and specified property owners. Automatic exclusion of all children of Scheduled Castes is not one of the listed criteria.
135.tq: Find the option that introduces a category outside the specified status-based exclusions.
135.sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

135.s:
Consider the following pairs relating to the OBC creamy-layer income ceiling:
1. 1993 — ₹1 lakh
2. 2004 — ₹2.5 lakh
3. 2008 — ₹4.5 lakh
4. 2013 — ₹6 lakh
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
135.x: The income ceiling rose from ₹1 lakh in 1993 to ₹2.5 lakh in 2004, ₹4.5 lakh in 2008 and ₹6 lakh in 2013.
135.tq: Verify each year-value pair rather than relying on the overall trend.
135.sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

135.s: The income ceiling for determining the OBC creamy layer, after the 2017 revision and described as still current, is
135.x: The income ceiling was revised to ₹8 lakh per annum in 2017 and is stated to remain current.
135.tq: Distinguish the latest threshold from earlier figures in the revision sequence.
135.sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

135.s: Which of the following statements regarding the application of the central creamy-layer threshold in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: Andhra Pradesh applies the threshold only to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
Andhra Pradesh has rejected the central threshold for all public-sector definitions.
Andhra Pradesh has fixed a separate threshold of ₹6 lakh for public-sector definitions.
Andhra Pradesh has aligned its State and public-sector definitions with the central threshold.
135.x: Andhra Pradesh aligned its State and public-sector definitions with the central creamy-layer threshold of ₹8 lakh.
135.tq: Test the State-level application of a central numerical standard.
135.sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

135.s:
With reference to Union of India v. Rohith Nathan, consider the following statements:
1. The Supreme Court held that parental salary alone cannot place a candidate in the creamy layer.
2. The Court ordered the creation of supernumerary posts.
3. In August 2026, the Centre sought clarification concerning 958 CSE-2025 candidates.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
135.x: The 11 March 2026 verdict held that parental salary alone cannot determine creamy-layer status and ordered supernumerary posts. In August 2026, the Centre sought clarification regarding 958 CSE-2025 candidates.
135.tq: Combine the judicial holding, consequential direction and subsequent administrative development.
135.sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

135.s: The Supreme Court decision in Union of India v. Rohith Nathan was delivered on
135.x: The decision in Union of India v. Rohith Nathan was delivered on 11 March 2026.
135.tq: Separate the date of the judgment from dates of later developments and other commissions.
135.sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

135.s: Who supported the introduction of a creamy-layer principle for Scheduled Castes in the debate mentioned in the context of 2025?
o: The Chief Justice of India, B.R. Gavai
The Chairman of the Kalelkar Commission
The Union Minister of Social Justice
135.x: Chief Justice of India B.R. Gavai supported the idea of applying a creamy-layer principle to Scheduled Castes.
135.tq: Match the public position with the correct constitutional functionary.
135.sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

135.s: The Union Government opposed applying the creamy-layer principle to SCs and STs on the ground that their status flows from
135.x: In August 2026, the Union Government opposed the proposal, stating that SC/ST status flows from Articles 341 and 342.
135.tq: Discriminate between closely related constitutional provisions concerning reservations and community identification.
135.sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

135.s: The creamy-layer principle for OBCs, which excludes socially advanced sections from reservation benefits, was introduced through the decision in
o: Union of India v. Rohith Nathan
State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan
135.x: The creamy-layer principle for excluding socially advanced OBCs was introduced through the Indra Sawhney decision.
135.tq: Use the landmark-case association rather than the later constitutional amendment association.
135.sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

135.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the categories associated with the OBC creamy layer under the Indra Sawhney framework?
o: All children of persons belonging to OBC communities, irrespective of social or economic status
Children whose parents are both Class-II officers
135.x: The framework identifies specified socially advanced categories, including children of Class-I officers and parents who are both Class-II officers. It does not exclude all OBC children irrespective of their circumstances.
135.tq: Reject the sweeping option that converts specified exclusions into a universal exclusion.
135.sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

135.s:
Consider the following statements about the Justice G. Rohini Commission:
1. It was constituted in October 2017.
2. It received 14 extensions.
3. It was concerned with sub-categorisation of about 3,000 Central-list OBC castes.
4. Its report was submitted to the President on 31 July 2023.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
135.x: The Justice G. Rohini Commission was constituted in October 2017, received 14 extensions, examined sub-categorisation of about 3,000 Central-list OBC castes, and submitted its report to the President on 31 July 2023.
135.tq: Check the complete chronology and mandate of the commission statement by statement.
135.sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

135.s: Which of the following findings was associated with the Justice G. Rohini Commission?
o: About 97% of OBC benefits were taken by 25% of the sub-castes, while about 1,000 communities had zero representation.
The Commission found that only 100 Central-list OBC communities required sub-categorisation.
About 25% of benefits went to 97% of the sub-castes, while no community lacked representation.
All Central-list OBC castes received an equal share of benefits.
135.x: The Commission found that approximately 97% of benefits had been taken by 25% of the sub-castes, while around 1,000 communities had zero representation.
135.tq: Watch for reversed percentages and population groups in a comparison-based finding.
135.sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

135.s: The Justice G. Rohini Commission is associated with a proposal to divide the Central-list OBCs into
135.x: The proposal associated with the Commission envisaged three to four sub-groups among the Central-list OBCs.
135.tq: Distinguish the proposed range from nearby numerical alternatives.
135.sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

135.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the 102nd Constitutional Amendment from the 105th Constitutional Amendment?
o: The 102nd introduced EWS reservation, while the 105th abolished Article 342A.
The 102nd created constitutional status for the NCBC and inserted Article 342A, while the 105th restored States’ power to identify and list SEBCs.
The 102nd restored State power over SEBC lists, while the 105th created the NCBC.
The 102nd created the first Backward Classes Commission, while the 105th repealed the NCBC Act, 1993.
135.x: The 102nd Amendment Act, 2018 inserted Articles 338B and 342A and gave constitutional status to the NCBC. The 105th Amendment Act, 2021 restored the power of States to identify and list SEBCs.
135.tq: Separate the institutional change made by the 102nd Amendment from the federal-list change made by the 105th.
135.sec: Amendments 102nd and 105th - NCBC status, State power over SEBC lists  [GROUP-II]

135.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the constitutional NCBC?
o: It is appointed by State Governors and exercises the powers of a tribunal.
It is appointed by the President and possesses powers of a civil court.
It is appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and possesses criminal-court powers.
It is appointed by the Prime Minister and functions only as an advisory body without legal powers.
135.x: The Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and members of the constitutional NCBC are appointed by the President, and the Commission has civil-court powers.
135.tq: Apply the ‘who appoints and what powers’ test to avoid authority and function swaps.
135.sec: Amendments 102nd and 105th - NCBC status, State power over SEBC lists  [GROUP-II]

135.s: Niranjan Jyoti was appointed as the Chairperson of the
135.x: Niranjan Jyoti was appointed Chairperson of the National Commission for Backward Classes.
135.tq: Match the named person with the correct commission rather than a similarly related body.
135.sec: Amendments 102nd and 105th - NCBC status, State power over SEBC lists  [GROUP-II]

135.s: Which of the following correctly compares the statutory NCBC under the 1993 Act with the present constitutional NCBC?
o: The statutory NCBC was constitutional, whereas the present NCBC is merely advisory and statutory.
The statutory NCBC had five members headed by a judge, whereas the constitutional NCBC has a Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and three members.
The statutory NCBC had three members headed by the President, whereas the constitutional NCBC has five judges.
Both bodies had identical composition and powers, but differed only in their names.
135.x: The 1993 statutory NCBC had five members and was headed by a judge. The present constitutional NCBC has a Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and three members.
135.tq: Compare composition and institutional status instead of focusing only on the common acronym.
135.sec: Amendments 102nd and 105th - NCBC status, State power over SEBC lists  [GROUP-II]

135.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. First Backward Classes Commission under Kalelkar
B. Creation of the statutory NCBC
C. Constitutional status to the NCBC through the 102nd Amendment
D. Restoration of State power over SEBC lists through the 105th Amendment
135.x: The Kalelkar Commission was established in 1953, the statutory NCBC was created in 1993, constitutional status came through the 102nd Amendment in 2018, and State power was restored by the 105th Amendment in 2021.
135.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two NCBC developments between them.

135.s: The first Backward Classes Commission in India was the
135.x: The first Backward Classes Commission was the Kalelkar Commission, constituted in 1953.
135.tq: Use the first-in-sequence clue to distinguish the foundational commission from later bodies.

135.s: Which of the following issues has been identified as a criticism or debate concerning reservation in central services?
o: Approximately 40–50% of reserved central posts lie vacant.
All reserved central posts are filled before unreserved posts.
Reserved posts are filled exclusively through State-level commissions.
No reservation is available in central services.
135.x: A criticism noted in the reservation debate is that approximately 40–50% of reserved central posts remain vacant.
135.tq: Select the stated range while rejecting absolute claims about reservation administration.

135.s: The 2027 Census has been discussed as potentially useful for
o: determining the composition of the NCBC by direct election
reassessing reservation quotas using caste enumeration
135.x: The 2027 Census, with caste enumeration, may be used to reassess reservation quotas.
135.tq: Link the proposed data exercise to its stated policy application without extending its purpose.

135.s: Which of the following represents a reservation-related issue specifically associated with Andhra Pradesh?
o: The creation of the constitutional NCBC by the State Legislature
The replacement of the Central List by a district-wise list
BC-E Muslim quota and the Kapu demand
The demand to abolish all BC-A to BC-E groups
135.x: BC-E Muslim quota and the Kapu demand are identified as live reservation issues in Andhra Pradesh.
135.tq: Separate State-specific reservation issues from national constitutional developments.

135.s: In Andhra Pradesh Social Welfare and Education Society residential school admissions for 2024–25, BC admissions continue to be organised through
o: only a single undivided BC category, with BC-E having 10 per cent
the Central List alone, without any State grouping
BC-A to BC-E groups, with BC-E having 4 per cent
four groups from BC-A to BC-D, with no BC-E category
135.x: APSES residential school admissions for 2024–25 continue to use BC-A to BC-E groups, with BC-E carrying 4 per cent.
135.tq: Read the category range and the associated percentage together.

135.s: Which of the following developments relates to the reservation debate in 2026?
o: The Telangana Assembly asked the Centre to include a BC/OBC column in Census 2027.
The Supreme Court directed that no caste enumeration could be considered in Census 2027.
The Union Government abolished the BC/OBC category in the Census.
The Telangana Assembly asked the Centre to remove caste-related questions from Census 2027.
135.x: On 12 September 2026, the Telangana Assembly asked the Centre to add a BC/OBC column in Census 2027.
135.tq: Identify the specific institutional demand and distinguish it from an opposite or absolute claim.

135.s: Which one of the following is correctly associated with the current debate on reservation for women?
o: Women's reservation has replaced all OBC reservation in central posts.
The NCBC has constitutional authority to impose a BC sub-quota in every State.
A BC sub-quota exists inside women's reservation throughout India.
There is no BC sub-quota inside women's reservation, which has been raised as a criticism.
135.x: The absence of a BC sub-quota within women's reservation has been identified as a criticism and debate.
135.tq: Watch for the reversal between an identified criticism and a claim that the arrangement already exists.

135.s: The Supreme Court’s reserved verdict mentioned in the context of August 2026 concerns Tamil Nadu’s BC (Muslim) quota for
135.x: The reserved Supreme Court verdict concerns Tamil Nadu’s BC (Muslim) quota in relation to persons who converted to Islam.
135.tq: Identify the precise community and issue rather than broadening the religious category.

136.s: The Kaka Kalelkar Commission, constituted in 1953, is associated with which of the following observations regarding Scheduled Tribes?
o: Tribal communities are identified exclusively on the basis of geographical isolation
Tribal communities are defined only by their economic backwardness
Tribes must profess a particular religion
Tribes generally lead a separate and exclusive existence and may belong to any religion
136.x: The Kaka Kalelkar Commission stated that Scheduled Tribes lived a separate and exclusive existence, while also recognising that tribes could belong to any religion.
136.tq: Use the mandate rather than confusing the commission with later committees on land alienation or ST criteria.
136.sec: Committees on tribal communities → chair and mandate  [APPSC]

136.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Committee)
a. Verrier Elwin Committee
b. U.N. Dhebar Commission
c. Lokur Committee
d. Dilip Singh Bhuria Committee

List-II (Associated subject or outcome)
i. Criteria for defining Scheduled Tribes
ii. Multi-Purpose Tribal Development Blocks
iii. PESA Act, 1996
iv. Tribal condition and land alienation

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
136.x: Verrier Elwin dealt with Multi-Purpose Tribal Development Blocks; Dhebar examined tribal conditions and land alienation; Lokur dealt with ST criteria; and Dilip Singh Bhuria was associated with PESA 1996.
136.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes containing a wrong committee-mandate association.
136.sec: Committees on tribal communities → chair and mandate  [APPSC]

136.s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Kaka Kalelkar — 1953
2. Verrier Elwin — 1959
3. U.N. Dhebar — 1960–61
4. Lokur — 1973

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
136.x: Kaka Kalelkar, Verrier Elwin and U.N. Dhebar are correctly matched with 1953, 1959 and 1960–61 respectively. The Lokur Committee was constituted in 1965, not 1973.
136.tq: Check the dates individually and identify the swapped-year trap in the last pair.
136.sec: Committees on tribal communities → chair and mandate  [APPSC]

136.s: The category of Primitive Tribal Groups, later termed Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups, followed the work of which commission in 1973?
136.x: The Primitive Tribal Group category followed the work of the U.N. Dhebar Commission, which examined tribal conditions and land alienation.
136.tq: Discriminate between committees by linking the later category to the commission’s mandate.
136.sec: Committees on tribal communities → chair and mandate  [APPSC]

136.s: Who chaired the committee that examined the criteria for defining Scheduled Tribes in 1965?
136.x: The 1965 Lokur Committee, headed by B.N. Lokur, examined the criteria for defining Scheduled Tribes.
136.tq: Test the chair separately from the committee’s subject to avoid confusing neighbouring tribal committees.
136.sec: Committees on tribal communities → chair and mandate  [APPSC]

136.s:
Consider the following statements regarding committees associated with tribal communities:

1. The Kalelkar Commission was constituted under Article 340.
2. The Bhuria Committee of 1991 was associated with the PESA Act, 1996.
3. The Bhuria Commission of 2002–04 dealt with tribal advancement, including land reform and the concerns of tribal women and children.
4. The Xaxa Committee was set up by the Planning Commission in 2013.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
136.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The Xaxa Committee was set up by the PMO, not the Planning Commission.
136.tq: The wrong-authority trap is used in statement 4 by replacing the PMO with a neighbouring central institution.
136.sec: Committees on tribal communities → chair and mandate  [APPSC]

136.s: The 2013 high-level committee chaired by Professor Virginius Xaxa primarily examined which of the following?
o: The socio-economic, health and educational status of tribal communities
The working of Multi-Purpose Tribal Development Blocks
136.x: The Xaxa Committee, set up by the PMO in 2013, examined the socio-economic, health and educational status of tribal communities and reported in 2014.
136.tq: Match the recent committee with its broad mandate rather than with an older constitutional subject.
136.sec: Committees on tribal communities → chair and mandate  [APPSC]

136.s:
Arrange the following committees in chronological order of their constitution:

A. Lokur Committee
B. Kaka Kalelkar Commission
C. Xaxa Committee
D. U.N. Dhebar Commission
136.x: The correct sequence is Kaka Kalelkar Commission (1953), U.N. Dhebar Commission (1960–61), Lokur Committee (1965) and Xaxa Committee (2013).
136.tq: Fix the earliest and latest items first, then place the two middle committees by year.
136.sec: Committees on tribal communities → chair and mandate  [APPSC]

136.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the two bodies associated with Dilip Singh Bhuria?
o: The 1991 Bhuria Committee examined tribal health, while the 2002–04 Commission examined Multi-Purpose Tribal Development Blocks
The 1991 Bhuria Committee was linked to PESA, while the 2002–04 Bhuria Commission addressed tribal advancement and related reforms
The 1991 Bhuria Committee dealt with forest rights, while the 2002–04 Commission dealt with ST identification
Both bodies were constituted in 2002–04 for the same mandate
136.x: The Bhuria Committee of 1991 led to PESA 1996, whereas the Bhuria Commission of 2002–04 focused on tribal advancement, funds, land reform, and tribal women and children.
136.tq: Separate similar names by comparing their years and distinct mandates.
136.sec: Committees on tribal communities → chair and mandate  [APPSC]

136.s: The nodal Ministry for implementation of the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 is the:
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
136.x: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs is the nodal ministry for the Forest Rights Act, 2006.
136.tq: Use the who-is-responsible test to distinguish the nodal ministry from ministries involved in implementation.
136.sec: Forest Rights Act 2006  [other exams]

136.s: Under Section 6 of the Forest Rights Act, 2006, which body initiates the process of determining the nature and extent of individual and community forest rights?
136.x: The Gram Sabha initiates the determination process and passes resolutions on claims under Section 6 of the Forest Rights Act.
136.tq: Apply the authority test: distinguish the initiating grassroots body from committees that subsequently examine claims.
136.sec: Forest Rights Act 2006  [other exams]

136.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the processing of claims under the Forest Rights Act, 2006:

1. The Gram Sabha passes resolutions on claims.
2. Claims are examined by Sub-Divisional and District Level Committees.
3. Each of these committees consists of six members.
4. The committees include representatives of revenue, tribal and forest authorities and elected panchayat members.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
136.x: All four statements are correct. The Gram Sabha initiates and resolves claims, while six-member Sub-Divisional and District Level Committees examine claims and issue titles.
136.tq: Check the complete institutional sequence from Gram Sabha initiation to committee examination and title issuance.
136.sec: Forest Rights Act 2006  [other exams]

136.s: Which of the following is NOT recognised as a forest right under the Forest Rights Act, 2006?

1. The State is also barred from leasing Scheduled Area land to non-tribals.

3. Private non-tribal mining companies may obtain leases if the Gram Sabha gives consent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
136.x: The State is also barred from leasing the land to non-tribals; the permissible institutional alternatives mentioned are State undertakings or tribal cooperatives. Gram Sabha consent does not make a private non-tribal lease valid under the stated rule.
136.tq: Separate the legal consequence from an apparently qualifying exception.
136.sec: Tribal land and displacement in AP

136.s: The background dispute in Samatha v. State of Andhra Pradesh was connected with mining leases in the:
136.x: The case arose against the background of mining leases in the Visakhapatnam Agency, where the AP Scheduled Area Land Transfer Regulation was enforced.
136.tq: Test the location associated with a landmark tribal-land case.
136.sec: Tribal land and displacement in AP

136.s: Which tribal communities are specifically mentioned as opposing the Polavaram project over land rights, compensation and rehabilitation?
136.x: The Koya and Kondh tribes are mentioned as opposing Polavaram over land rights, compensation and rehabilitation.
136.tq: Discriminate between the named communities and nearby tribal names.
136.sec: Tribal land and displacement in AP

136.s: G.O. No. 3 of 2000 in Andhra Pradesh provided for:
o: A ban on appointment of local ST teachers
Reservation of all Gram Sabha posts for non-tribals
Reservation of 100% of teacher posts in Scheduled Areas for local STs
Reservation of 50% of mining leases for private companies
136.x: G.O. No. 3 of 2000 reserved 100 per cent of teacher posts in Scheduled Areas for local Scheduled Tribes.
136.tq: Link the government order with its exact subject and percentage.
136.sec: Tribal land and displacement in AP

136.s: What was the judicial outcome concerning G.O. No. 3 of 2000?
o: It was converted into a PESA rule in 2011
It was upheld by the Supreme Court in 2020
It was struck down by the Supreme Court in 2020
It was repealed by the 1970 land regulation
136.x: The Supreme Court struck down G.O. No. 3 of 2000 in 2020.
136.tq: Distinguish the policy’s content from its later judicial outcome.
136.sec: Tribal land and displacement in AP

136.s: Which of the following statements regarding the AP Scheduled Areas Land Transfer Regulation is correct?
o: A challenge to Regulation 1 of 1970 is pending before the Supreme Court
The Supreme Court has already declared Regulation 1 of 1970 unconstitutional in every respect
Regulation 1 of 1970 was finally repealed by Regulation 1 of 1959
No legal challenge to Regulation 1 of 1970 has ever been made
136.x: A case challenging Regulation 1 of 1970 is pending in the Supreme Court.
136.tq: Test the distinction between a pending challenge and a final judicial decision.
136.sec: Tribal land and displacement in AP

136.s: In Scheduled Areas, Gram Sabhas can play which role in relation to tribal land?
o: They can suspend the Constitution’s Fifth Schedule
They can prevent alienation and restore illegally alienated ST land
They can transfer all tribal land to private companies
They can abolish the Scheduled Area designation
136.x: Gram Sabhas in Scheduled Areas can prevent alienation and restore illegally alienated land belonging to Scheduled Tribes.
136.tq: Apply the institutional power to a land-alienation situation.
136.sec: Tribal land and displacement in AP

136.s: In tribal usage, the term ‘Diku’ refers to:
o: An outsider-exploiter such as a moneylender, trader, landlord or contractor
136.x: Diku denotes an outsider-exploiter, including a moneylender, trader, landlord or contractor.
136.tq: Distinguish the exact social meaning of a culturally specific term.
136.sec: Tribal terms for outsiders and exploiters (Diku) - meaning

136.s: Birsa Munda’s Ulgulan was directed against:
o: Only forest conservation by tribal institutions
The Panchsheel principles of tribal development
136.x: Birsa’s Ulgulan was aimed at British land-grabbing and the exploitative dikus.
136.tq: Match the movement with its principal targets.
136.sec: Tribal terms for outsiders and exploiters (Diku) - meaning

136.s: Which one of the following combinations correctly identifies major causes and consequences of tribal indebtedness and land alienation?
o: Tribal indebtedness was caused exclusively by modern schools
Restrictive forest laws expanded tribal access to traditional habitats
Revenue farmers eliminated all non-tribal control over tribal land
Colonial moneylenders and revenue farmers contributed to indebtedness and land alienation
136.x: Colonial moneylenders and revenue farmers contributed to indebtedness and land alienation. Restrictive forest laws, on the contrary, cut tribals off from their habitats.
136.tq: Identify the historically correct cause-and-effect relationship.
136.sec: Tribal problems - land alienation, indebtedness, displacement, shifting cultivation, bonded labour

136.s:
Consider the following statements about the problems faced by Scheduled Tribes:
1. Restrictive forest laws cut many tribals off from their habitat.
2. Low literacy and language barriers are among the problems faced by them.
3. Malnutrition, forced labour and displacement are also identified as tribal problems.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
136.x: All three statements correctly identify problems associated with tribal communities: loss of habitat, educational and linguistic disadvantages, malnutrition, forced labour and displacement.
136.tq: Use the all-inclusive option when each listed problem is supported.
136.sec: Tribal problems - land alienation, indebtedness, displacement, shifting cultivation, bonded labour

136.s: Scheduled Tribes constitute about 9% of the population but account for over what proportion of people displaced by development projects?
136.x: Scheduled Tribes constitute about 9 per cent of the population but account for over 50 per cent of people displaced by development projects.
136.tq: Test a population-share versus displacement-share comparison.
136.sec: Tribal problems - land alienation, indebtedness, displacement, shifting cultivation, bonded labour

136.s: The Forest Conservation Rules, 2022 became a subject of dispute between the NCST and the Environment Ministry because they:
o: Added a compulsory tribal veto over every forest diversion
Dropped the forest-dwellers’ consent clause before forest diversion
Prohibited all development projects in forest areas
Transferred all forests to Gram Sabhas
136.x: The 2022 Rules dropped the consent clause of forest-dwellers before forest diversion, leading to a dispute between the NCST and the Environment Ministry.
136.tq: Identify the precise legal change behind an institutional dispute.
136.sec: Tribal problems - land alienation, indebtedness, displacement, shifting cultivation, bonded labour

136.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I: Approach
 a. Isolation
 b. Assimilation
 c. Integration

List-II: Associated idea or proponent
 i. Development while retaining tribal identity
 ii. Tribes treated as ‘backward Hindus’ and absorbed
 iii. Tribes kept apart to protect their culture

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
136.x: Isolation seeks to keep tribes apart for cultural protection; assimilation seeks their absorption as ‘backward Hindus’; integration combines development with retention of identity.
136.tq: Start from the clear idea-pair and complete the remaining matches.
136.sec: Approaches → proponent (isolation, assimilation, integration)

136.s: Who is associated with the isolation approach to tribal development, described in terms such as ‘museum’ or ‘national park’?
136.x: The isolation approach is associated with early Verrier Elwin and sought to keep tribes apart to protect their culture.
136.tq: Match the distinctive metaphor with its proponent.
136.sec: Approaches → proponent (isolation, assimilation, integration)

136.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the assimilation approach and its proponents?
o: It keeps tribes completely separate; it was proposed only by Nehru
It regards tribes as ‘backward Hindus’ to be absorbed; G.S. Ghurye and N.K. Bose are associated with it
It develops tribes while preserving identity; it was proposed only by Elwin
It rejects all cultural contact; it was formulated by Birsa Munda
136.x: Assimilation views tribes as ‘backward Hindus’ to be absorbed and is associated with G.S. Ghurye and N.K. Bose, including Bose’s Hindu method of tribal absorption.
136.tq: Combine the approach, its defining idea and its proponents.
136.sec: Approaches → proponent (isolation, assimilation, integration)

136.s:
With reference to Jawaharlal Nehru’s approach to tribal development, consider the following statements:
1. He favoured integration.
2. He worked with Verrier Elwin in developing this approach.
3. He rejected both isolation and forced assimilation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
136.x: Nehru favoured integration with Elwin and rejected both the isolationist approach and forced assimilation.
136.tq: Check whether all three statements consistently describe one approach.
136.sec: Approaches → proponent (isolation, assimilation, integration)

136.s: Which of the following is the correct first principle of Nehru’s Panchsheel for tribal development?
o: Measure success exclusively by money spent
Separate tribal people permanently from all institutions
Impose uniform administration on all tribal areas
Develop tribal communities along their own genius
136.x: The first principle is to develop tribal people along their own genius, respecting their distinct capacities and culture.
136.tq: Recall the exact wording of a foundational principle.
136.sec: Panchsheel for tribal development - principles and source

136.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Panchsheel principles for tribal development:
1. Tribal rights in land and forests should be respected.
2. Tribal people should be relied upon and trained for their own administration.
3. Administration should be minimised and conducted through tribal institutions.
4. Results should be judged by money spent rather than by the quality of human character evolved.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
136.x: The first three statements are Panchsheel principles. The fifth principle requires judging results by the quality of human character evolved, not by money spent, making statement 4 false.
136.tq: Spot the reversed standard of evaluating development.
136.sec: Panchsheel for tribal development - principles and source

136.s: Which of the following is the fifth principle of Panchsheel for tribal development?
o: To judge results by the quality of human character evolved, and not by money spent
To absorb tribal communities into the dominant society
To exclude tribal people from their own administration
To permit unrestricted exploitation of tribal forests
136.x: The fifth principle is to judge development by the quality of human character evolved rather than by the amount of money spent.
136.tq: Distinguish the qualitative evaluation principle from economic expenditure.
136.sec: Panchsheel for tribal development - principles and source

136.s: The standard formulation of Panchsheel places the encouragement of tribal languages:
o: Within the fifth principle concerning expenditure
Within the first principle concerning development along tribal genius
Only within the principle concerning forest rights
Outside the five principles as a sixth principle in every formulation
136.x: Although one listing presents encouragement of tribal languages separately, the standard wording keeps it within the first principle of developing tribal communities along their own genius.
136.tq: Resolve a wording distinction between a separate listing and the standard formulation.
136.sec: Panchsheel for tribal development - principles and source

136.s: The source of Nehru’s Panchsheel for tribal development is identified as:
o: Nehru’s foreword to Verrier Elwin’s A Philosophy for NEFA
136.x: The principles are sourced to Nehru’s foreword to Verrier Elwin’s work A Philosophy for NEFA.
136.tq: Match the doctrine with its literary and constitutional context.
136.sec: Panchsheel for tribal development - principles and source

136.s: Which one of the following statements correctly reflects the attribution of Panchsheel for tribal development?
o: Elwin is credited with formulating it under Nehru’s influence
It was formulated through the AP Scheduled Areas Land Transfer Regulation
Ghurye is credited with formulating it under Bose’s influence
Nehru formulated it under the exclusive influence of colonial revenue farmers
136.x: CDX credits Verrier Elwin with formulating Panchsheel under Nehru’s influence, while its stated source is Nehru’s foreword to A Philosophy for NEFA.
136.tq: Separate the credited formulator from the source text and reject swapped attributions.
136.sec: Panchsheel for tribal development - principles and source

136.s: The Santhal Hul of 1855–56 was primarily directed against which combination of groups?
o: Forest officials, contractors and military officers
Rajas, autonomous councils and Gram Sabhas
136.x: The Santhal Hul was directed against zamindars, moneylenders, referred to as dikus, and the police.
136.tq: Directly link the revolt with its principal targets.
136.sec: Tribal movements and revolts - issues raised

136.s: Who led the Santhal Hul of 1855–56?
o: Birsa Munda and Alluri Sitarama Raju
136.x: Sidhu and Kanhu were the leaders associated with the Santhal Hul of 1855–56.
136.tq: Use the leader–movement association to eliminate swapped-name options.
136.sec: Tribal movements and revolts - issues raised

136.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Birsa Munda’s Ulgulan:
1. It took place during 1899–1900.
2. It was associated with land-grabbing and forced labour.
3. Its objective included the establishment of Abua Raj.
4. It directly led to the enactment of the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act, 1908.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
136.x: All four statements are correct. Birsa’s Ulgulan occurred in 1899–1900, opposed land-grabbing and forced labour, sought Abua Raj, and led to the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act, 1908.
136.tq: Check the date, issue, objective and legislative consequence separately.
136.sec: Tribal movements and revolts - issues raised

136.s: Birsa Munda is also known by which title?
136.x: Birsa Munda is popularly known as Dharti Aaba.
136.tq: Test the exact title rather than the broader movement association.
136.sec: Tribal movements and revolts - issues raised

136.s:
Arrange the following tribal movements in chronological order:
A. Srikakulam Girijan movement
B. Santhal Hul
C. Rampa rebellion
D. Birsa’s Ulgulan
136.x: The correct sequence is Santhal Hul (1855–56), Birsa’s Ulgulan (1899–1900), Rampa rebellion (1922–24), and Srikakulam Girijan movement (1967–70).
136.tq: Place the events by their stated year ranges before checking the sequence options.
136.sec: Tribal movements and revolts - issues raised

136.s: The Rampa rebellion of 1922–24 was led by which of the following persons?
136.x: Alluri Sitarama Raju led the Rampa rebellion of 1922–24.
136.tq: Discriminate between leaders of different tribal movements.
136.sec: Tribal movements and revolts - issues raised

136.s: Which one of the following was NOT an issue associated with the Rampa rebellion?
o: Opposition to land-grabbing by zamindars as the principal recorded issue
Restrictions affecting tribal communities in the Agency area
Forced labour in the Godavari Agency
136.x: The Rampa rebellion is specifically associated with forest-law curbs on podu and forced labour in the Godavari Agency. Land-grabbing by zamindars was listed in relation to Birsa’s Ulgulan and the Santhal Hul, not as the principal issue stated for the Rampa rebellion.
136.tq: Find the issue belonging to another revolt rather than the named movement.
136.sec: Tribal movements and revolts - issues raised

136.s: The Srikakulam Girijan movement of 1967–70 is correctly associated with which statement?
o: It was led by Sidhu and Kanhu and opposed police action.
It was led by Alluri Sitarama Raju and sought Abua Raj.
It was led by Vempatapu Satyanarayana and Adibhatla Kailasam, and later turned Naxalite.
It was led by Birsa Munda and resulted in the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act.
136.x: The Srikakulam Girijan movement was led by Vempatapu Satyanarayana and Adibhatla Kailasam, raised issues of land alienation, moneylenders and forest officials, and later turned Naxalite.
136.tq: Match the movement with both its leaders and distinctive later development.
136.sec: Tribal movements and revolts - issues raised

136.s:
According to T. K. Oommen, modern tribal movements seek which of the following objectives?
1. Political autonomy
2. Recognition of identity
3. Control over resources
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
136.x: T. K. Oommen identified political autonomy, identity recognition and control over resources as objectives of modern tribal movements.
136.tq: Treat a three-part conceptual formulation as a complete list.
136.sec: Tribal movements and revolts - issues raised

136.s:
The Koya and Kondh communities oppose the Polavaram project mainly because of concerns relating to:
1. Land rights
2. Poor compensation
3. Displacement without proper rehabilitation
Which of the statements given above are correct?
136.x: The stated concerns of the Koya and Kondh communities include land rights, inadequate compensation and displacement without proper rehabilitation.
136.tq: Identify all components of a displacement-and-rehabilitation issue cluster.
136.sec: Displacement and rehabilitation - Polavaram, bauxite in Agency areas

136.s: Soil sampling for bauxite exploration was permitted in which mandals?
136.x: The permitted soil sampling was reported in Chintapalli and G.K. Veedhi mandals.
136.tq: Test the precise location pair; do not confuse exploration sites with project sites.
136.sec: Displacement and rehabilitation - Polavaram, bauxite in Agency areas

136.s: Private pumped-storage projects mentioned in connection with the Agency areas are located in which places?
136.x: The private pumped-storage projects were mentioned in Koyyuru, Hukumpeta and Ananthagiri in ASR district.
136.tq: Separate the three project locations from the two bauxite soil-sampling locations.
136.sec: Displacement and rehabilitation - Polavaram, bauxite in Agency areas

136.s: What was the outcome of the Niyamgiri bauxite-mining proposal in 2013?
o: It was approved after the Forest Rights Act process was waived.
It was approved after consent from the State legislature.
Dongria Kondh Gram Sabhas rejected the mining under the FRA, and the project was cancelled.
It was transferred to private pumped-storage projects.
136.x: In 2013, Dongria Kondh Gram Sabhas rejected bauxite mining under the Forest Rights Act, after which the project was cancelled.
136.tq: Apply the Gram Sabha consent principle to the Niyamgiri outcome.
136.sec: Displacement and rehabilitation - Polavaram, bauxite in Agency areas

136.s: Critical Wildlife Habitat under the Forest Rights Act refers to areas of national parks and sanctuaries that are to be:
o: Transferred exclusively to private conservation agencies
Kept inviolate after an open process involving affected communities
Opened for mining after approval by the Forest Department
136.x: Critical Wildlife Habitats are areas within national parks and sanctuaries to be kept inviolate, and they are notified after an open process with affected communities.
136.tq: Distinguish the legal definition from an assumed blanket exclusion of communities.
136.sec: FRA and forest/wildlife law linkages - CWH, MFP and bamboo, Indian Forest Act

136.s: Which one of the following statements regarding bamboo under the Forest Rights Act is correct?
o: Bamboo is a tree in every location and cannot be collected by forest dwellers.
Bamboo is a minor forest produce, and ownership is vested in forest dwellers.
Bamboo is excluded from minor forest produce and belongs only to the Forest Department.
Ownership of bamboo is vested only in Gram Panchayats.
136.x: The Forest Rights Act treats bamboo as a minor forest produce and vests its ownership in forest dwellers.
136.tq: Separate the FRA status of bamboo from its treatment under the Indian Forest Act amendment.
136.sec: FRA and forest/wildlife law linkages - CWH, MFP and bamboo, Indian Forest Act

136.s: The Indian Forest (Amendment) Act, 2017 did which of the following?
o: Removed bamboo grown outside forest areas from the definition of “tree”.
Granted an unrestricted right to fell bamboo in forest areas.
Removed all bamboo from the definition of minor forest produce.
Transferred ownership of all bamboo to private companies.
136.x: The 2017 amendment removed bamboo grown outside forest areas from the definition of “tree”. It did not confer a right to fell bamboo in forest areas.
136.tq: Watch for the false extension from bamboo outside forests to bamboo inside forests.
136.sec: FRA and forest/wildlife law linkages - CWH, MFP and bamboo, Indian Forest Act

136.s:
Which of the following is NOT correctly matched regarding forest diversion after the Forest Rights Act?
1. Completion of FRA processes — prerequisite before forest diversion under the FCA
2. Gram Sabha consent — relevant to the FRA process
3. Forest diversion — permissible before completion of FRA claims if the project is of public importance
4. Niyamgiri — Gram Sabha rejection of bauxite mining
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
136.x: Statement 3 is incorrect. MoEFCC guidelines barred forest diversion under the FCA until FRA processes, especially Gram Sabha consent, were complete; this position was repeatedly upheld by the Supreme Court.
136.tq: Locate the statement that reverses the prerequisite relationship between FRA and forest diversion.
136.sec: FRA and forest/wildlife law linkages - CWH, MFP and bamboo, Indian Forest Act

136.s: According to the Economic Survey 2025–26 figures cited, the national implementation of the Forest Rights Act covered:
o: 23.92 lakh individual titles and 1.22 lakh community titles covering 233.48 lakh acres
1.22 lakh individual titles and 23.92 lakh community titles covering 233.48 lakh acres
23.92 lakh claims and 1.22 lakh titles covering 42 lakh acres
136.x: The stated national figures are 23.92 lakh individual titles and 1.22 lakh community titles, covering 233.48 lakh acres.
136.tq: Keep claims, titles and acreage distinct when reading a three-part data figure.
136.sec: FRA implementation - claims vs titles, AP data, CFR

136.s: Which statement correctly describes the national status of Community Forest Resource Rights (CFR/CFRR)?
o: Exactly 47,900 villages received CFRR titles covering all eligible people.
Over 47,900 CFR/CFRR claims were rejected, while eligible forest-dependent villages and people number about 1.77 lakh and 20 crore respectively.
CFRR reached every eligible forest-dependent village.
About 1.77 lakh people and 20 crore villages were eligible for CFRR.
136.x: More than 47,900 CFR/CFRR claims were rejected. About 1.77 lakh forest-dependent villages and nearly 20 crore people were eligible, but CFRR reached only a fraction.
136.tq: Check the units carefully: villages and people, not the reverse.
136.sec: FRA implementation - claims vs titles, AP data, CFR

136.s:
Consider the following statements regarding FRA implementation in Andhra Pradesh during 2024–25:
1. Individual claims received numbered 2,85,087.
2. Community claims received numbered 3,294.
3. Individual titles approved numbered 2,26,651.
4. Community titles distributed numbered 1,822.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
136.x: All four numbers correspond to the APSES 2024–25 data: 2,85,087 individual claims, 3,294 community claims, 2,26,651 individual titles and 1,822 community titles.
136.tq: Read the claims-versus-titles categories without swapping individual and community figures.
136.sec: FRA implementation - claims vs titles, AP data, CFR

136.s: Which of the following correctly gives the extent associated with Andhra Pradesh FRA data for 2024–25?
o: Individual claims: 4,54,706 acres; community claims: 5,26,454 acres
Individual titles approved: 5,78,560 acres; community titles distributed: 6,23,678 acres
Individual claims: 6,23,678 acres; community claims: 5,78,560 acres
Individual claims: 5,78,560 acres; community claims: 6,23,678 acres
136.x: The extent of individual claims received was 5,78,560 acres, while community claims received covered 6,23,678 acres.
136.tq: Match each acreage with the correct claim category before considering title figures.
136.sec: FRA implementation - claims vs titles, AP data, CFR

136.s: The extent associated with individual titles approved and community titles distributed in Andhra Pradesh was, respectively:
136.x: Individual titles approved covered 4,54,706 acres, while community titles distributed covered 5,26,454 acres.
136.tq: Use the title category and its extent together; do not substitute claim figures.
136.sec: FRA implementation - claims vs titles, AP data, CFR

136.s: In the Andhra Pradesh context, RoFR in relation to forest rights is used to mean:
136.x: Although RoFR can expand to “Right of First Refusal” in another usage, the Andhra Pradesh usage here is “Recognition of Forest Rights”.
136.tq: Resolve a look-alike abbreviation by using the subject-specific expansion.
136.sec: FRA implementation - claims vs titles, AP data, CFR

136.s: How many RoFR cultivators were among Annadata Sukhibhava–PM Kisan beneficiaries in 2025–26?
136.x: There were 1,16,021 RoFR cultivators among Annadata Sukhibhava–PM Kisan beneficiaries in 2025–26.
136.tq: Retain the exact beneficiary count rather than confusing it with title or CFR figures.
136.sec: FRA implementation - claims vs titles, AP data, CFR

136.s:
Which of the following is NOT identified as a gap in Forest Rights Act implementation?
1. Excessive focus on individual titles over CFR
2. Gram Sabhas being bypassed
3. Strong MoTA capacity ensuring complete CFR implementation
4. Restrictive MFP transit permits
5. JFMC/CAMPA projects bypassing Gram Sabhas
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
136.x: Statement 3 is not a gap; the identified gap is weak MoTA capacity. The other statements describe reported implementation gaps.
136.tq: Find the positive statement that reverses the stated implementation weakness.
136.sec: FRA implementation - claims vs titles, AP data, CFR

136.s: The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 primarily operationalises which constitutional provision?
136.x: PESA operationalises Article 243M(4)(b) by extending Part IX relating to Panchayats to Fifth Schedule Areas, subject to exceptions.
136.tq: Match the statute with its specific constitutional enabling provision.
136.sec: PESA Act 1996 - Part IX in Fifth Schedule Areas

136.s:
With reference to PESA, consider the following statements:
1. It extends Part IX of the Constitution to Fifth Schedule Areas with exceptions.
2. It recognises governance through customary law.
3. It applies to Sixth Schedule tribal areas in the same manner as to Fifth Schedule Areas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
136.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. PESA applies only to Fifth Schedule Areas and not to Sixth Schedule tribal areas, making statement 3 incorrect.
136.tq: Use the Fifth Schedule–Sixth Schedule distinction as the decisive trap.
136.sec: PESA Act 1996 - Part IX in Fifth Schedule Areas

136.s:
Which of the following powers are associated with the Gram Sabha or Panchayat under PESA?
1. Consultation before land acquisition and resettlement
2. Ownership of minor forest produce
3. Prevention of land alienation and restoration of unlawfully alienated ST land
4. Regulation or prohibition of intoxicants
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
136.x: PESA recognises all four powers. It also covers management of village markets and control of money-lending.
136.tq: Treat the listed PESA powers as a combined authority package and check each item.
136.sec: PESA Act 1996 - Part IX in Fifth Schedule Areas

136.s: Which one of the following is NOT a power or function mentioned in relation to Gram Sabha/Panchayat under PESA?
o: Issuing licences for private pumped-storage projects
136.x: PESA assigns powers relating to village markets, money-lending and intoxicants, among others. Issuing licences for private pumped-storage projects is not one of the listed functions.
136.tq: Reject the unrelated project-licensing power while retaining the customary local-governance powers.
136.sec: PESA Act 1996 - Part IX in Fifth Schedule Areas

136.s: Which statement correctly reflects the reservation and nomination provisions under PESA?
o: The Union Government nominates all unrepresented tribes to State legislatures.
Seats are unrelated to population and chairperson posts are open to all categories.
Seats are in proportion to population, STs must have at least 50% representation, all chairperson posts go to STs, and the State may nominate unrepresented tribes to block or district bodies.
Only one-third of seats are reserved for STs and chairperson posts are reserved for women alone.
136.x: PESA provides for representation in proportion to population, at least 50% ST representation, all chairperson posts for STs, and possible State nomination of unrepresented tribes to block and district bodies.
136.tq: Check the combined effect of percentage, chairperson and nomination provisions.
136.sec: PESA Act 1996 - Part IX in Fifth Schedule Areas

136.s: A land acquisition proposal in a Fifth Schedule Area requires consultation with which local institution under PESA before acquisition and resettlement?
o: Only the State Public Service Commission
136.x: PESA provides for consultation with the Gram Sabha or Panchayat before land acquisition and resettlement in the relevant Scheduled Area.
136.tq: Ask which institution performs the locally rooted consultation function.
136.sec: PESA Act 1996 - Part IX in Fifth Schedule Areas

136.s: Under the RFCTLARR Act, 2013, Social Impact Assessment is:
o: Required only for private projects and never for public projects
Replaced by a census of affected families
136.x: The RFCTLARR Act, 2013 makes Social Impact Assessment mandatory.
136.tq: Identify the statutory requirement without being distracted by exceptions not stated in the law summary.
136.sec: Related laws - RFCTLARR 2013 consent and SIA in Scheduled Areas

136.s: Under the RFCTLARR Act, 2013, the consent requirement is what percentage of affected families for private projects and public-private partnership projects, respectively?
136.x: Consent of 80% of affected families is required for private projects and 70% for PPP projects.
136.tq: Keep the private-project and PPP thresholds in the correct order.
136.sec: Related laws - RFCTLARR 2013 consent and SIA in Scheduled Areas

136.s: In Scheduled Areas, acquisition under the RFCTLARR Act is treated as a last resort and requires consent of which body or bodies?
o: Only the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
Gram Sabha, Panchayat or Autonomous Council, as applicable
136.x: Acquisition in Scheduled Areas is a last resort and requires consent from the Gram Sabha, Panchayat or Autonomous Council, as applicable.
136.tq: Identify the local self-governing body rather than a supervisory or advisory institution.
136.sec: Related laws - RFCTLARR 2013 consent and SIA in Scheduled Areas

136.s: Which category receives specific legal protection under the RFCTLARR Act in the context of Scheduled Areas?
136.x: Habitats of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups receive legal protection under the RFCTLARR Act.

136.x: All three pairings are correct: 4,172 VDVKs were noted, EMRS received a raised allocation in Budget 2026-27, and diversion of sub-plan funds remains a criticism.
136.tq: Combine a numerical fact, a budget fact and a criticism while checking each pairing independently.
136.sec: Universal angles

136.s: Which one of the following correctly states the Andhra Pradesh figures given for Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Areas?
o: STs: 34 lakh, constituting 5.53 per cent of the State; Scheduled Areas: 27.39 per cent of the State
STs: 20 lakh, constituting 9 per cent of the State; Scheduled Areas: 10.15 per cent of the State
STs: 27.39 lakh, constituting 5.53 per cent of the State; Scheduled Areas: 10.15 per cent of the State
STs: 27.39 lakh, constituting 10.15 per cent of the State; Scheduled Areas: 5.53 per cent of the State
136.x: Scheduled Tribes in Andhra Pradesh were stated to number 27.39 lakh, constituting 5.53 per cent of the State’s population, while Scheduled Areas cover 10.15 per cent of the State.
136.tq: Keep the population figure, population share and area share in their correct columns.
136.sec: Universal angles

136.s: The Scheduled Tribes of Andhra Pradesh were stated to comprise how many communities?
136.x: The stated Andhra Pradesh figure is 34 Scheduled Tribe communities.
136.tq: Distinguish the State-specific community count from national programme counts.
136.sec: Universal angles

136.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. MoTA sought Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change funds for managing Community Forest Resource areas vested in Gram Sabhas.
2. Eviction orders in Agasthyamalai were criticised for ignoring the Forest Rights Act.
3. The debate reflects a tension between development and consent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
136.x: All three statements are correct. The issues concern funding for CFR management, alleged disregard of FRA in Agasthyamalai eviction orders, and the wider development-versus-consent debate.
136.tq: Link separate current-affairs developments through their common legal and policy issue.
