137.s: Section 12(1)(c) of the Right to Education Act relates to which of the following?
o: Reservation of 50% seats in private schools for all children
Reservation of 25% seats in all government colleges for girls
Reservation of 25% entry-level seats in unaided private schools for specified children
Reservation of 35% seats in aided schools for minorities
137.x: Section 12(1)(c) requires unaided private schools, excluding minority institutions, to reserve 25% of entry-level seats for children from weaker sections and disadvantaged groups.
137.tq: Identify the exact statutory provision by matching its percentage and institutional coverage.
137.sec: RTE Act 2009 - commencement, age group, 25% quota, PTR, teacher qualification, no-detention, SMCs  [APPSC]

137.s:
With reference to the 25% quota under Section 12(1)(c) of the RTE Act, consider the following statements:
1. It applies to entry-level seats.
2. Minority institutions are excluded from its coverage.
3. The State reimburses schools on the basis of per-child expenditure.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
137.x: All three statements are correct. The provision concerns entry-level seats in unaided private schools, excludes minority institutions, and provides reimbursement by the State on a per-child expenditure basis.
137.tq: Test the provision through its seat level, institutional exception and reimbursement mechanism.
137.sec: RTE Act 2009 - commencement, age group, 25% quota, PTR, teacher qualification, no-detention, SMCs  [APPSC]

137.s: The pupil-teacher ratio prescribed under the RTE norms is correctly matched as:
137.x: The prescribed pupil-teacher ratio is 30:1 at the primary level and 35:1 at the upper-primary level.
137.tq: Read the comparison in level-wise order and avoid reversing the two ratios.
137.sec: RTE Act 2009 - commencement, age group, 25% quota, PTR, teacher qualification, no-detention, SMCs  [APPSC]

137.s: Which authority lays down the minimum qualifications for appointment of teachers under the RTE framework?
o: State Council for Teacher Education alone
National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
137.x: The minimum teacher qualifications are laid down by the academic authority notified by the Central Government, namely the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE).
137.tq: Apply the 'who performs this function?' method to distinguish the national academic authority from monitoring bodies.
137.sec: RTE Act 2009 - commencement, age group, 25% quota, PTR, teacher qualification, no-detention, SMCs  [APPSC]

137.s: Teacher Eligibility Test under the RTE framework is conducted in accordance with guidelines of the:
137.x: Teacher Eligibility Test requirements operate according to guidelines issued by the NCTE.
137.tq: Separate teacher-qualification authority from child-rights monitoring institutions.
137.sec: RTE Act 2009 - commencement, age group, 25% quota, PTR, teacher qualification, no-detention, SMCs  [APPSC]

137.s:
Consider the following statements regarding detention under the RTE Act:
1. The original Act barred detention up to Class VIII.
2. The 2019 amendment permitted detention at certain stages subject to safeguards.
3. Re-examination is one of the safeguards associated with detention under the amended provision.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
137.x: All three statements are correct. The original no-detention provision extended up to Class VIII, while the 2019 amendment allowed detention at Classes V and VIII after regular examinations and a re-examination opportunity.
137.tq: Track the change from the original rule to the amended rule and its safeguard.
137.sec: RTE Act 2009 - commencement, age group, 25% quota, PTR, teacher qualification, no-detention, SMCs  [APPSC]

137.s: Under the amended no-detention framework, detention may be permitted at which stages, subject to safeguards?
137.x: The 2019 amendment permits detention at Classes V and VIII, subject to regular examination, re-examination and related safeguards.
137.tq: Focus on the exact class numbers rather than the broad phrase 'elementary education'.
137.sec: RTE Act 2009 - commencement, age group, 25% quota, PTR, teacher qualification, no-detention, SMCs  [APPSC]

137.s: The provision relating to School Management Committees under the RTE Act is found in:
137.x: School Management Committees are provided for under Section 21 of the RTE Act.
137.tq: Match the institutional mechanism with its statutory section.
137.sec: RTE Act 2009 - commencement, age group, 25% quota, PTR, teacher qualification, no-detention, SMCs  [APPSC]

137.s: In every government or aided school, what proportion of the members of the School Management Committee are parents or guardians?
137.x: Three-fourths of the members of the School Management Committee are parents or guardians.
137.tq: Test the exact composition percentage and reject the extreme claim that all members must be parents.
137.sec: RTE Act 2009 - commencement, age group, 25% quota, PTR, teacher qualification, no-detention, SMCs  [APPSC]

137.s:
Which of the following bodies are associated with monitoring and grievance redressal under the RTE Act?
1. National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
2. State Commissions for Protection of Child Rights
3. School Management Committees as statutory monitoring commissions
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
137.x: NCPCR and SCPCRs review, monitor and redress grievances under the RTE Act. School Management Committees are school-level bodies, not statutory child-rights commissions.
137.tq: Distinguish formal commissions from school-level participatory bodies.
137.sec: RTE Act 2009 - commencement, age group, 25% quota, PTR, teacher qualification, no-detention, SMCs  [APPSC]

137.s:
Consider the following statements about the 86th Constitutional Amendment:
1. It inserted Article 21A.
2. It rewrote Article 45 to address early childhood care up to six years.
3. It added Article 51A(k).
Which of the statements given above are correct?
137.x: The 86th Amendment inserted Article 21A, revised Article 45 regarding early childhood care up to six years, and added the parental duty in Article 51A(k).
137.tq: Use the three-part amendment bundle rather than treating Article 21A as its sole effect.
137.sec: RTE Act 2009 - commencement, age group, 25% quota, PTR, teacher qualification, no-detention, SMCs  [APPSC]

137.s: Which one of the following is NOT included within the principal coverage of the RTE Act as described?
o: Establishment of neighbourhood schools by the appropriate Government and local authority
Education at the pre-school and secondary levels as a statutory entitlement under the Act
A duty of parents or guardians to send the child to school
Free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years
137.x: The RTE Act does not include pre-school education below six years or secondary and higher education within its principal statutory entitlement.
137.tq: Find the option that extends the Act beyond its stated age and educational-stage coverage.
137.sec: Features of RTE Act - what is and is not included  [APPSC]

137.s: Which one of the following is NOT a correct feature of the RTE Act?
o: The Centre bears the sole financial responsibility for implementing the Act.
Parents or guardians have a duty to send the child to school.
The appropriate Government and local authority must establish neighbourhood schools.
Unaided private schools provide specified entry-level seats for weaker and disadvantaged groups.
137.x: The Centre does not bear sole financial responsibility; funds are shared by the Centre and the States. The other statements describe features of the Act.
137.tq: Identify the false financial-responsibility claim hidden among genuine statutory duties.
137.sec: Features of RTE Act - what is and is not included  [APPSC]

137.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the RTE Act?
1. Screening and capitation fee — prohibited
2. Physical punishment and mental harassment — prohibited
3. Private tuition by teachers — prohibited
4. Out-of-school child — admission to an age-appropriate class
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
137.x: All four are features of the RTE Act: it prohibits screening and capitation fee, physical punishment, mental harassment and private tuition by teachers, and provides age-appropriate admission for out-of-school children.
137.tq: Combine several statutory safeguards and inclusion measures before selecting the coded option.
137.sec: Features of RTE Act - what is and is not included  [APPSC]

137.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched?
1. RTE Act — prohibition of capitation fee
2. Article 51A(k) — duty of parent or guardian regarding education
3. Section 12(1)(c) — 25% provision in unaided private schools
4. Section 21 — School Management Committees
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
137.x: All four pairings are correct. They connect the RTE Act's safeguards and institutions with the relevant constitutional provisions and sections.
137.tq: Start with the sure section matches and verify each remaining constitutional or statutory pairing.
137.sec: Features of RTE Act - what is and is not included  [APPSC]

137.s: The Right to Education Act does NOT provide for coverage of which category under the 25% quota?
o: Children in minority institutions covered compulsorily by Section 12(1)(c)
Children in unaided private schools, subject to the provision
137.x: Minority institutions are excluded from the 25% quota provision under Section 12(1)(c). The provision concerns specified children in unaided private schools.
137.tq: Look for the institutional exception in a provision that otherwise appears broadly applicable.
137.sec: Features of RTE Act - what is and is not included  [APPSC]

137.s: The cost-sharing pattern mentioned for Samagra Shiksha is correctly stated as:
o: 100:0 generally and 90:10 for North-Eastern and hill States
40:60 generally and 10:90 for North-Eastern and hill States
60:40 generally and 90:10 for North-Eastern and hill States
50:50 generally and 75:25 for North-Eastern and hill States
137.x: The Centre-State sharing pattern is 60:40 generally and 90:10 for North-Eastern and hill States.
137.tq: Test both parts of a funding ratio and watch for reversed shares.
137.sec: RTE Act 2009 - commencement, age group, 25% quota, PTR, teacher qualification, no-detention, SMCs  [APPSC]

137.s:
The Supreme Court direction mentioned in relation to Section 12(1)(c) in January 2026 concerned which combination?
1. Framing of rules under Section 38
2. Monitoring by the NCPCR
3. Abolition of the 25% quota
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
137.x: The January 2026 direction concerned rules under Section 38 and NCPCR monitoring. It did not abolish the 25% quota.
137.tq: Reject the extreme negative option and isolate the two linked institutional directions.
137.sec: RTE Act 2009 - commencement, age group, 25% quota, PTR, teacher qualification, no-detention, SMCs  [APPSC]

137.s: According to the current figure specified, the 25% quota under Section 12(1)(c) operates in how many States and Union Territories?
137.x: The specified current figure is 16 States and Union Territories.
137.tq: Treat the current count as a distinct quantitative fact and avoid estimating from the total number of States and Union Territories.
137.sec: RTE Act 2009 - commencement, age group, 25% quota, PTR, teacher qualification, no-detention, SMCs  [APPSC]

137.s: The United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child was adopted by the United Nations General Assembly on:
137.x: The UN General Assembly adopted the UNCRC on 20 November 1989.
137.tq: Separate the adoption date from India’s accession date and the dates of the Optional Protocols.
137.sec: UNCRC - adoption, articles, India's ratification, rights and principles, protocols, Children's Day  [APPSC]

137.s: India’s accession to the UNCRC entails submission of periodic reports to the:
o: UN Committee on the Rights of the Child
137.x: States parties submit periodic reports to the UN Committee on the Rights of the Child.
137.tq: Match the reporting obligation with the specialised treaty-monitoring committee.
137.sec: UNCRC - adoption, articles, India's ratification, rights and principles, protocols, Children's Day  [APPSC]

137.s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the four broad categories of rights under the UNCRC?
137.x: The four categories are survival, development, protection and participation. Sovereignty is not one of the UNCRC rights categories.
137.tq: Identify the outsider by recalling the four-category classification.
137.sec: UNCRC - adoption, articles, India's ratification, rights and principles, protocols, Children's Day  [APPSC]

137.s:
Consider the following rights:
1. Right to development
2. Right to expression
3. Right to recreation
Which of the above are recognised as child rights under the UNCRC framework?
137.x: Right to development, expression and recreation are all recognised as child rights within the UNCRC framework.
137.tq: Avoid treating the four broad categories as an exhaustive list of individual rights.
137.sec: UNCRC - adoption, articles, India's ratification, rights and principles, protocols, Children's Day  [APPSC]

137.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four core principles of the UNCRC?
o: Compulsory state ownership of all child institutions
Right to life, survival and development
137.x: The four core principles include non-discrimination, best interests of the child, life-survival-development, and respect for the child’s views. Compulsory state ownership is not a core principle.
137.tq: Find the unrelated institutional claim among principles stated in rights language.
137.sec: UNCRC - adoption, articles, India's ratification, rights and principles, protocols, Children's Day  [APPSC]

137.s: The principle of respect for the views of the child is associated with which aspect of the UNCRC?
o: A condition for membership of the UN Security Council
A provision limited to armed conflict protocols
One of its four core principles
A financial provision for States parties
137.x: Respect for the views of the child is one of the four core principles of the UNCRC.
137.tq: Match the rights-based phrase with its proper conceptual category.
137.sec: UNCRC - adoption, articles, India's ratification, rights and principles, protocols, Children's Day  [APPSC]

137.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding the Optional Protocols to the UNCRC?
1. Involvement of children in armed conflict — 2000
2. Sale of children, child prostitution and child pornography — 2000
3. Communications procedure — 2011
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
137.x: The protocols concerning armed conflict and sale or exploitation of children were adopted in 2000, while the communications procedure protocol dates from 2011.
137.tq: Match each protocol with its subject and year before selecting the coded combination.
137.sec: UNCRC - adoption, articles, India's ratification, rights and principles, protocols, Children's Day  [APPSC]

137.s:
With reference to India and the Optional Protocols to the UNCRC, consider the following statements:
1. India ratified the two 2000 Optional Protocols in 2005.
2. India is not a party to the 2011 Communications Procedure Protocol.
3. India ratified all three Optional Protocols in 2005.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
137.x: India ratified the two 2000 Optional Protocols in 2005, but is not a party to the 2011 Communications Procedure Protocol. Therefore, statement 3 is false.
137.tq: Separate the two protocols ratified by India from the later protocol to which India is not a party.
137.sec: UNCRC - adoption, articles, India's ratification, rights and principles, protocols, Children's Day  [APPSC]

137.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Adoption of the UNCRC
B. India’s accession to the UNCRC
C. Adoption of the two Optional Protocols concerning armed conflict and exploitation
D. Adoption of the Communications Procedure Protocol
137.x: The sequence is 1989 adoption of the UNCRC, 1992 Indian accession, 2000 adoption of two Optional Protocols, and 2011 adoption of the Communications Procedure Protocol.
137.tq: Fix the earliest and latest dates first, then place the 1992 and 2000 events between them.
137.sec: UNCRC - adoption, articles, India's ratification, rights and principles, protocols, Children's Day  [APPSC]

137.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Universal Children’s Day from India’s Children’s Day?
o: Universal Children’s Day is 14 November and India’s Children’s Day is 20 November.
Universal Children’s Day is 20 November and India’s Children’s Day is 14 November.
Universal Children’s Day is 11 December and India’s Children’s Day is 20 November.
137.x: Universal Children’s Day or International Child Rights Day is observed on 20 November, while India’s Children’s Day is observed on 14 November.
137.tq: Discriminate between two closely associated observance dates instead of merging them.
137.sec: UNCRC - adoption, articles, India's ratification, rights and principles, protocols, Children's Day  [APPSC]

137.s:
Assertion (A): The UNCRC recognises participation as one of the broad categories of child rights.
Reason (R): Respect for the views of the child is one of the core principles of the UNCRC.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
137.x: Both statements are true. Participation is a broad rights category, while respect for the child’s views is a related core principle; the reason does not by itself explain the complete classification of rights.
137.tq: Check whether the true reason explains the full assertion or merely relates to it.
137.sec: UNCRC - adoption, articles, India's ratification, rights and principles, protocols, Children's Day  [APPSC]

137.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Article 24 — Prohibition of traffic in human beings
Article 39(e) — Duty of parents to provide education to children aged 6–14 years
Article 51A(k) — Fundamental duty of parent or guardian to provide education to children aged 6–14 years
137.x: Article 51A(k) makes it the duty of a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to children between 6 and 14 years. Article 24 concerns child employment, Article 39(e) concerns protection of tender age, and Article 45 concerns early childhood care and education.
137.tq: Use the article-subject match and eliminate swapped constitutional provisions.
137.sec: Child rights Articles number game → subject and amendment

137.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 39(e) requires that the tender age of children should not be abused.
2. Article 39(e) protects children from being forced by economic necessity to enter avocations unsuited to their age or strength.
3. Article 39(e) creates a fundamental duty upon parents to provide education to children aged 6–14 years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
137.x: Statements 1 and 2 correctly describe Article 39(e). Statement 3 is incorrect because the parental duty to provide education is contained in Article 51A(k).
137.tq: Find the statement that assigns a neighbouring article’s subject to Article 39(e).
137.sec: Child rights Articles number game → subject and amendment

137.s: Article 39(f), which concerns the healthy development of children in freedom and dignity and their protection from exploitation and abandonment, was reworded by the:
137.x: Article 39(f) was reworded by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976. The 86th Amendment is associated with Articles 21A, 45 and 51A(k).
137.tq: Separate the amendment connected with Article 39(f) from the later education amendment.
137.sec: Child rights Articles number game → subject and amendment

137.s: Which of the following constitutional provisions was substituted by the 86th Constitutional Amendment?
137.x: Article 45 was substituted by the 86th Amendment to provide for early childhood care and education until children attain six years of age. Article 51A(k) was added, rather than substituted, by the same amendment.
137.tq: Distinguish between a provision added by an amendment and one substituted by it.
137.sec: Child rights Articles number game → subject and amendment

137.s: The Child Labour Amendment Act, 2016 provides that:
o: All work by persons below 18 years is prohibited without exception
Children below 14 years may work in any occupation after school hours
Children below 14 years cannot work, except for helping in family work after school, while adolescents aged 14–18 years are barred from hazardous work
Only employment in mines is prohibited for children below 14 years
137.x: The 2016 amendment prohibits work by children below 14 years, subject to the stated family-help exception after school. It also prohibits adolescents aged 14–18 years from hazardous work.
137.tq: Watch for extreme words such as ‘all’ and identify the age-group distinction.
137.sec: Child rights Articles number game → subject and amendment

137.s: CHILDLINE 1098 is primarily intended to provide:
o: A portal for tracking school attendance
A legal aid service exclusively for women
137.x: CHILDLINE 1098 is a 24x7 emergency helpline for children. It is now integrated with ERSS-112 across all 36 States and Union Territories.
137.tq: Directly link the helpline number with its emergency function.
137.sec: Child helplines and portals → number/purpose

137.s:
With reference to child-protection helplines and portals, consider the following statements:
1. TrackChild is used for tracking missing and found children.
2. Khoya-Paya enables citizens to report missing or sighted children.
3. CARINGS is the Child Adoption Resource Information and Guidance System.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
137.x: All three statements are correct. TrackChild handles tracking of missing and found children, Khoya-Paya supports citizen reporting, and CARINGS relates to child adoption information and guidance.
137.tq: Match each portal with its distinctive purpose before selecting the coded combination.
137.sec: Child helplines and portals → number/purpose

137.s: Khoya-Paya has been integrated with which of the following platforms?
137.x: Khoya-Paya, the citizen portal for reporting missing or sighted children, has been integrated with TrackChild. ERSS-112 is associated with emergency response integration for CHILDLINE.
137.tq: Discriminate between similarly placed child-rights portals by their integration links.
137.sec: Child helplines and portals → number/purpose

137.s: e-Baal Nidan is associated with:
o: Online complaints regarding violation of child rights
Tracking children rescued from hazardous employment only
137.x: e-Baal Nidan is the NCPCR’s online complaint portal for violations of child rights. CARINGS is the adoption-related system, while CHILDLINE 1098 is the emergency helpline.
137.tq: Identify the portal by its institutional purpose rather than its name alone.
137.sec: Child helplines and portals → number/purpose

137.s: The composition of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights consists of:
o: Only a Chairperson and members nominated by the Supreme Court
A Chairperson and eight members, including three women
A Chairperson and six members, including at least two women
A Chairperson and four members, including one woman
137.x: The NCPCR consists of a Chairperson and six members, of whom at least two must be women. It is not composed solely of judicial nominees.
137.tq: Test the exact composition and the minimum representation requirement.
137.sec: NCPCR and SCPCR - parent Act, composition, powers, AP SCPCR

137.s: While inquiring into complaints, the NCPCR has the powers of a:
137.x: The NCPCR has powers of a civil court while inquiring into complaints. This power does not make it a constitutional or criminal court.
137.tq: Identify the exact legal status of the power instead of choosing a broader-sounding authority.
137.sec: NCPCR and SCPCR - parent Act, composition, powers, AP SCPCR

137.s: Which of the following Acts is NOT specifically included among those monitored by the NCPCR?
o: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
137.x: The specified monitoring mandate includes the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015, the POCSO Act, 2012 and the RTE Act, 2009. The Child Labour Amendment Act, 2016 is not included in that stated list.
137.tq: Find the one law outside the commission’s specifically stated monitoring list.
137.sec: NCPCR and SCPCR - parent Act, composition, powers, AP SCPCR

137.s: In Andhra Pradesh, V. Gandhi Babu directed the admission of migrant and fisherfolk children into nearby schools and hostels in:
137.x: V. Gandhi Babu of the AP SCPCR directed admission-related measures for migrant and fisherfolk children in Kolleru in Eluru district.
137.tq: Combine the person, vulnerable groups and precise location in an applied current-affairs fact.
137.sec: NCPCR and SCPCR - parent Act, composition, powers, AP SCPCR

137.s: The National Policy for Children, 2013 defines a child as a person:
o: Between 6 and 14 years of age only
137.x: The National Policy for Children, 2013 defines a child as a person below 18 years of age. The 6–14 age range is relevant to the constitutional right to education, not the policy’s general definition of a child.
137.tq: Separate the policy’s general age definition from the RTE age group.
137.sec: National Policy for Children 2013 and National Plan of Action for Children - priority areas

137.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four priority areas of the National Policy for Children, 2013?
137.x: The four priority areas are survival, health and nutrition; education and development; protection; and participation. Military training is not a priority area of the policy.
137.tq: Recall the complete four-part list and eliminate the unrelated option.
137.sec: National Policy for Children 2013 and National Plan of Action for Children - priority areas

137.s: The National Plan of Action for Children, 2016 primarily:
o: Introduced the constitutional right to education
Replaced the National Policy for Children, 2013
Limited child protection to the education sector
Operationalised the National Policy for Children, 2013
137.x: The National Plan of Action for Children, 2016 put the National Policy for Children, 2013 into operation. It follows the same four priority areas.
137.tq: Distinguish an implementation plan from the policy it operationalises.
137.sec: National Policy for Children 2013 and National Plan of Action for Children - priority areas

137.s: Which principle is expressly associated with the National Policy for Children, 2013?
o: The best interests of the child come first
Education is the sole priority of child policy
Participation is limited to children above 18 years
The interests of institutions come before those of children
137.x: The National Policy for Children, 2013 places the best interests of the child first. Its framework also includes survival, health and nutrition, education and development, protection and participation.
137.tq: Apply the policy principle to a child-centred decision-making scenario.
137.sec: National Policy for Children 2013 and National Plan of Action for Children - priority areas

137.s: The Supreme Court decision in Unni Krishnan v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1993) recognised that children below 14 years have:
o: A right to employment in non-hazardous industries
A statutory right to adoption under Article 24
A fundamental duty to provide education under Article 51A(k)
A fundamental right to free education under Article 21
137.x: Unni Krishnan recognised a fundamental right to free education for children below 14 years under Article 21. The decision formed the basis for the later insertion of Article 21A.
137.tq: Link the landmark case to the right and constitutional provision it developed.
137.sec: Child rights cases → issue

137.s: Which case upheld the 25 per cent quota in unaided private schools, while excluding unaided minority schools from its application?
o: Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India
Unni Krishnan v. State of AP
Pramati Educational and Cultural Trust v. Union of India
Society for Unaided Private Schools of Rajasthan v. Union of India
137.x: Society for Unaided Private Schools of Rajasthan v. Union of India (2012) upheld the 25 per cent quota in unaided private schools, but not in unaided minority schools.
137.tq: Discriminate between the two cases concerning RTE applicability to private and minority schools.
137.sec: Child rights cases → issue

137.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Pramati Educational and Cultural Trust v. Union of India held that the RTE Act does not apply to minority schools.
2. Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India concerned child trafficking and children working in circuses.
3. Bachpan Bachao Andolan later led to directions regarding registration of FIRs for missing children.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
137.x: All three statements are correct. Pramati excluded aided and unaided minority schools from the RTE Act, while Bachpan Bachao Andolan addressed trafficking, circus children and FIRs concerning missing children.
137.tq: Combine case names with their distinct issues and check all three propositions.
137.sec: Child rights cases → issue

137.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Unni Krishnan v. State of AP
B. Constitution Amendment Bill relating to the right to education
C. Enactment of the 86th Constitutional Amendment
D. Pramati Educational and Cultural Trust v. Union of India
137.x: The sequence is Unni Krishnan (1993), the Constitution Amendment Bill (July 1997), the 86th Amendment (December 2002), and Pramati (2014).
137.tq: Anchor the sequence with the case years and the 1997–2002 amendment milestones.
137.sec: Child rights cases → issue

137.s: According to the figures stated for child-related indicators, which pair is correctly matched?
o: Child sex ratio (0–6), Census 2011 — 914; NFHS-5 sex ratio at birth — 929

the introduction of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita
the difference between the age of marriage and voting age

o: It declared that Article 142 cannot be used in POCSO matters.
It removed the age threshold of 18 years from POCSO.
It urged consideration of a Romeo-Juliet clause and flagged misuse in consensual adolescent relationships.

138.s:

POCSO Act — subsumed entirely into the BNS from 1 July 2024
POCSO Act — law dealing exclusively with child labour

138.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the age categories under the amended child labour law:
1. A child is a person below 14 years of age.
2. An adolescent is a person between 14 and 18 years of age.
3. The category of adolescent was introduced only through the 2016 amendment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
138.x: All three statements are correct. The 2016 amendment introduced the adolescent category for persons aged 14 to 18 years.

138.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the position of a child below 14 years after the 2016 amendment?
o: Employment is banned in all occupations and processes, subject to specified exceptions
Employment is banned only in mines and factories
Employment is permitted in all non-hazardous occupations without restriction
Employment is regulated only through the Right to Education Act
138.x: After the 2016 amendment, employment of children below 14 years is prohibited in all occupations and processes, subject to specified exceptions.

138.sec: Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act 1986 and 2016 amendment - title, ages, hazardous list, exceptions

138.s: Before the 2016 amendment, the Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986 provided that children below 14 years could not be employed in:

o: Hazardous processes under the Factories Act
138.x: The retained hazardous categories are mines, inflammable substances and explosives, and hazardous processes under the Factories Act. All agricultural occupations are not included as a category of the hazardous list.
138.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the narrowed hazardous list.

138.s: Which authority may add or omit occupations from the hazardous list under the amended child labour law?

Permissible only if the child is above 18 years
Permissible only in mines and factories
138.x: Helping in a family or family enterprise after school hours is a specified exception, provided the conditions relating to schooling are satisfied.

A child artist is exempt even when schooling is affected

A child may work as an artist in audio-visual entertainment, excluding circus, if schooling is not affected

4. The Child and Adolescent Labour Rehabilitation Fund is established under the Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
138.x: All four statements are correct. The amendment made offences cognizable, prescribed imprisonment and fines, and provided for a Child and Adolescent Labour Rehabilitation Fund.

District Magistrate acting as a criminal court

A Chairperson and four members, all of whom must be social workers
A District Magistrate and five elected representatives

The Board handles children in conflict with law, while the Children's Court tries cases transferred to it
The Board tries all transferred cases, while the Children's Court conducts preliminary inquiries only

Detention in every case until adulthood
Retributive punishment as the primary objective

144.x: The Court held that the right under Article 30 is not absolute. The State may impose reasonable conditions relating to aid and recognition.
144.tq: Test the precise constitutional limitation rather than the extreme word 'absolute'.
144.sec: Minority rights cases → issue  [APPSC]

144.s: With reference to St. Stephen's College v. University of Delhi (1992), which one of the following statements is correct?
o: An aided minority college may prefer students of its own community up to about 50 percent
An aided minority college cannot admit students from its own community
Only unaided minority colleges may prefer their own community students
The State may reserve all seats in an aided minority college
144.x: The decision recognised that an aided minority college may prefer students belonging to its own community up to about 50 percent.
144.tq: Use the case-specific numerical limit to distinguish the ruling from broader Article 30 claims.
144.sec: Minority rights cases → issue  [APPSC]

144.s:
Consider the following statements regarding T.M.A. Pai Foundation v. State of Karnataka:
1. The case was decided by an 11-judge Bench.
2. The State is the unit for determining minority status.
3. The State may regulate, but not control, the administration of minority institutions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: All three statements are correct. The 2002 decision was delivered by an 11-judge Bench and adopted a State-wise approach to minority status while permitting regulation without administrative control.
144.tq: Combine bench strength, territorial unit and the distinction between regulation and control.
144.sec: Minority rights cases → issue  [APPSC]

144.s: The decision in Bal Patil v. Union of India (2005) is associated with which of the following?
o: Directing the Centre to notify Jains as a national minority
Imposing reservation quotas on unaided minority institutions
Declaring that minority status must be determined nationally
Declining to direct the Centre to notify Jains as a national minority and leaving the matter to the States
144.x: The Court declined to direct the Centre to notify Jains as a national minority, leaving the matter to the States and cautioning against the multiplication of minority claims.
144.tq: Discriminate between a judicial direction and a refusal to issue that direction.
144.sec: Minority rights cases → issue  [APPSC]

144.s: Which of the following statements about P.A. Inamdar (2005) is correct?
o: A 7-judge Bench held that the State may impose reservation quotas on all unaided institutions
A 7-judge Bench held that the State cannot impose reservation quotas on unaided institutions, whether minority or non-minority
The case dealt exclusively with notification of religious minorities
An 11-judge Bench held that only minority institutions are exempt from all regulation
144.x: P.A. Inamdar was decided by a 7-judge Bench, which held that the State cannot impose reservation quotas on unaided institutions, minority or non-minority.
144.tq: Match the correct bench size with the precise scope of the ruling.
144.sec: Minority rights cases → issue  [APPSC]

144.s:
Arrange the following cases in chronological order:
A. Kerala Education Bill
B. T.M.A. Pai Foundation
C. Bal Patil v. Union of India
D. St. Stephen's College
144.x: The correct sequence is Kerala Education Bill (1958), St. Stephen's College (1992), T.M.A. Pai Foundation (2002), and Bal Patil (2005).
144.tq: Fix the earliest and latest cases first, then place the 1992 and 2002 decisions.
144.sec: Minority rights cases → issue  [APPSC]

144.s: Which one of the following is NOT a function or power of the National Commission for Minority Educational Institutions?
o: Determining the minority status of an educational institution
Adjudicating disputes relating to affiliation with universities
Amending the Constitution to define the term minority
144.x: The Commission can determine minority status, decide affiliation disputes and issue minority certificates, and it has civil court powers. It has no power to amend the Constitution.
144.tq: Find the option outside the statutory and quasi-judicial jurisdiction of the body.
144.sec: National Commission for Minority Educational Institutions - Act, powers

144.s:
In relation to the National Commission for Minority Educational Institutions, consider the following statements:
1. It has powers of a civil court.
2. It decides disputes regarding affiliation to universities.
3. It is empowered to determine the minority status of institutions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: All three statements are correct. The Commission exercises civil court powers and handles minority status and university-affiliation matters.
144.tq: Test the three connected dimensions of a quasi-judicial institution's jurisdiction.
144.sec: National Commission for Minority Educational Institutions - Act, powers

144.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the constitutional treatment of minorities:
1. The Constitution uses the term 'minority' in Articles 29 and 30.
2. The term also occurs in Articles 350A and 350B.
3. The Constitution provides a comprehensive definition of minority.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: Articles 29, 30, 350A and 350B refer to minorities, but the Constitution does not define the term comprehensively. Therefore, statement 3 is incorrect.
144.tq: Separate constitutional usage of a term from constitutional definition of that term.
144.sec: Constitutional recognition - "minority" undefined; religious vs linguistic  [other exams, GROUP-II]

144.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes religious and linguistic minorities in India?
o: Religious minorities are associated with the National Commission for Minorities, while linguistic minorities are considered State-wise and linked with the Article 350B officer
Religious minorities are identified only by States, while linguistic minorities are identified by the Union
Both categories are determined exclusively on an all-India basis
Neither category is recognised under the Constitution
144.x: Religious minorities are dealt with through the National Commission for Minorities and the Ministry of Minority Affairs. Linguistic minorities are identified State-wise, with the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities under Article 350B.
144.tq: Split the comparison by authority and territorial basis.
144.sec: Constitutional recognition - "minority" undefined; religious vs linguistic  [other exams, GROUP-II]

144.s: Which of the following is NOT among the criteria used for identifying linguistic minorities?
o: Ownership of property in another State
144.x: Numerical inferiority, a non-dominant position in the State and distinct identity are relevant criteria. Property ownership in another State is not one of them.
144.tq: Eliminate the unrelated personal-status criterion from the three-part test.
144.sec: Constitutional recognition - "minority" undefined; religious vs linguistic  [other exams, GROUP-II]

144.s: National notification of a community as a minority primarily enables it to:
o: Obtain automatic reservation in every State legislature
Come within the National Commission for Minorities and central minority schemes
Avoid all regulation by State authorities
144.x: National notification brings a community within the National Commission for Minorities and makes it eligible under central minority schemes such as scholarships, PMJVK and PM VIKAS.
144.tq: Apply the practical consequences of notification instead of assuming it creates unrestricted rights.
144.sec: Constitutional recognition - "minority" undefined; religious vs linguistic  [other exams, GROUP-II]

144.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The National Commission for Minorities Act does not define the term 'minority'.
2. A community notified by the Centre is treated as a minority for the purposes of the Act.
3. States cannot notify minorities of their own for State purposes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. States can also notify their own minorities for State purposes, making statement 3 incorrect.
144.tq: Watch for the absolute word 'cannot' when comparing Union and State roles.
144.sec: Constitutional recognition - "minority" undefined; religious vs linguistic  [other exams, GROUP-II]

144.s: Which one of the following communities was added to India's nationally notified minority communities on 27 January 2014?
144.x: Jains were added on 27 January 2014, increasing the number of nationally notified minority communities from five to six.
144.tq: Use the exact date and the addition rather than the original five-community list.
144.sec: Notified minority communities - number, names, additions, population  [other exams, GROUP-II]

144.s: The nationally notified minority communities first notified in 1993 were:
o: Muslims, Sikhs, Jains, Parsis and Jews
Muslims, Christians, Jains, Buddhists and Parsis
Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains and Jews
Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists and Parsis
144.x: The five communities notified in 1993 were Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists and Parsis or Zoroastrians. Jains were added later in 2014.
144.tq: Distinguish the original notified group from the later addition of Jains.
144.sec: Notified minority communities - number, names, additions, population  [other exams, GROUP-II]

144.s: How many religious communities are nationally notified as minorities after the addition of Jains?
144.x: The notified communities number six after Jains were added to the five communities notified in 1993.
144.tq: Convert the change in the notified list into a direct count question.
144.sec: Notified minority communities - number, names, additions, population  [other exams, GROUP-II]

144.s: According to Census 2011 figures, which of the following correctly matches a notified minority community with its population?
144.x: The Census 2011 population figures given are Muslims 172.2 million, Christians 27.8 million, Sikhs 20.8 million and Jains 4.5 million.
144.tq: Start with the sure population figure and reject swapped numerical pairs.
144.sec: Notified minority communities - number, names, additions, population  [other exams, GROUP-II]

144.s: The six nationally notified minority communities together constitute approximately what share of India's population?
144.x: The six nationally notified minority communities together account for approximately 19 percent of India's population.
144.tq: Use the approximate share rather than confusing it with an individual community's population.
144.sec: Notified minority communities - number, names, additions, population  [other exams, GROUP-II]

144.s: PM Vishwakarma was launched on:
144.x: PM Vishwakarma was launched on 17 September 2023, coinciding with Vishwakarma Jayanti.
144.tq: Distinguish the scheme's launch date from dates associated with minority notification.
144.sec: PM Vishwakarma - target trades, benefits, implementing ministries  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

144.s: PM Vishwakarma primarily targets:
144.x: PM Vishwakarma is intended for artisans and craftspeople engaged in 18 traditional trades. It is not a fishermen's scheme.
144.tq: Discriminate between the target group and the tempting but incorrect fishermen association.
144.sec: PM Vishwakarma - target trades, benefits, implementing ministries  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

144.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with a benefit under PM Vishwakarma?
o: Registration — certificate and identity card through Common Service Centres
Toolkit — unrestricted loan of Rs 15 lakh
Credit — collateral-free credit only after compulsory property security
144.x: Registration through Common Service Centres provides a certificate and identity card. The scheme also provides training with a stipend, a Rs 15,000 toolkit incentive and collateral-free credit.
144.tq: Match the benefit with its delivery mechanism and reject altered amounts or conditions.
144.sec: PM Vishwakarma - target trades, benefits, implementing ministries  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

144.s: Under PM Vishwakarma, the credit support is structured as:
o: Rs 1 lakh followed by Rs 5 lakh without any interest
Rs 1 lakh followed by Rs 2 lakh at 5 percent interest
Rs 15,000 followed by Rs 2 lakh at 12 percent interest
Rs 2 lakh followed by Rs 1 lakh at 10 percent interest
144.x: The scheme provides collateral-free credit of Rs 1 lakh initially and an additional Rs 2 lakh, with the credit carrying a 5 percent interest rate.
144.tq: Read the staged amount and interest rate together to avoid reversing the figures.
144.sec: PM Vishwakarma - target trades, benefits, implementing ministries  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

144.s:
Consider the following statements about PM Vishwakarma:
1. The Ministry of MSME is the nodal ministry.
2. The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship also implements the scheme.
3. The Department of Financial Services is associated with its implementation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: All three statements are correct. MSME is the nodal ministry, while MSDE and the Department of Financial Services are also involved in implementation.
144.tq: Test nodal responsibility separately from the other implementing agencies.
144.sec: PM Vishwakarma - target trades, benefits, implementing ministries  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

144.s: The PM's New 15 Point Programme for the Welfare of Minorities was introduced in:
144.x: The PM's New 15 Point Programme for the Welfare of Minorities dates from 2006.
144.tq: Use the programme year as the distinguishing fact among nearby policy dates.
144.sec: Prime Minister's programme for welfare of minorities - name, focus areas, monitoring  [other exams, GROUP-II]

144.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the broad aims of the PM's New 15 Point Programme for the Welfare of Minorities?
144.x: The programme focuses on education, jobs and economic activity, living conditions, and prevention of communal riots. Privatisation of minority educational institutions is not one of its aims.
144.tq: Find the policy objective that does not belong to the programme's four focus areas.
144.sec: Prime Minister's programme for welfare of minorities - name, focus areas, monitoring  [other exams, GROUP-II]

144.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the PM's New 15 Point Programme:
1. It includes prevention of communal riots among its aims.
2. About 15 percent of targets and outlays in selected schemes are intended for minorities.
3. Review committees monitor its implementation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: All three statements are correct. The programme includes communal harmony, earmarks about 15 percent of targets and outlays in selected schemes, and is monitored by review committees.
144.tq: Combine objectives, earmarking and monitoring instead of treating the programme as a single-sector scheme.
144.sec: Prime Minister's programme for welfare of minorities - name, focus areas, monitoring  [other exams, GROUP-II]

144.s: The Ministry of Minority Affairs dates from:
144.x: The Ministry of Minority Affairs was established in 2006, the same year associated with the New 15 Point Programme.
144.tq: Link the ministry's establishment year with the relevant welfare programme without confusing it with the NCM Act year.
144.sec: Prime Minister's programme for welfare of minorities - name, focus areas, monitoring  [other exams, GROUP-II]

144.s: PM-YASASVI is administered by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and is intended for:
o: Only students belonging to notified religious minorities
Only SC students studying at IITs and IIMs
144.x: PM-YASASVI is a scholarship and educational support scheme for students belonging to OBC, EBC and DNT categories under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
144.tq: Separate the beneficiary categories of PM-YASASVI from minority scholarships and SHREYAS.
144.sec: Scholarships for OBC/EBC/DNT - PM YASASVI, SHREYAS, minority scholarships  [GROUP-II]

144.s: Which of the following correctly describes PM-YASASVI?
o: It was launched in 2021 and applies to families with income below Rs 2.5 lakh
It was launched in 2014 and has no income criterion
It was launched in 2006 and applies only to families above Rs 10 lakh
It was launched in 2023 exclusively for minority girls
144.x: PM-YASASVI was launched in 2021 for OBC, EBC and DNT students whose family income is below Rs 2.5 lakh.
144.tq: Pair the launch year with the income ceiling and reject substituted scheme profiles.
144.sec: Scholarships for OBC/EBC/DNT - PM YASASVI, SHREYAS, minority scholarships  [GROUP-II]

144.s: Under PM-YASASVI, the pre-matric scholarship for Classes IX and X is:
144.x: The pre-matric scholarship for Classes IX and X under PM-YASASVI is Rs 4,000.
144.tq: Distinguish the fixed pre-matric amount from the post-matric range.
144.sec: Scholarships for OBC/EBC/DNT - PM YASASVI, SHREYAS, minority scholarships  [GROUP-II]

144.s: The post-matric scholarship amount under PM-YASASVI is in the range of:
144.x: PM-YASASVI provides post-matric scholarship support ranging from Rs 5,000 to Rs 20,000.
144.tq: Use the range rather than mistaking the Class IX-X amount for the post-matric benefit.
144.sec: Scholarships for OBC/EBC/DNT - PM YASASVI, SHREYAS, minority scholarships  [GROUP-II]

144.s:
Consider the following statements about PM-YASASVI:
1. It supports top-class school and college education.
2. It includes hostel support.
3. Thirty percent of its slots are earmarked for girls.
4. Its cost-sharing ratio is 60:40.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: All four statements are correct. PM-YASASVI includes top-class education and hostel support, reserves 30 percent of slots for girls and follows a 60:40 cost-sharing ratio.
144.tq: Check both qualitative benefits and quantitative design features before selecting the coded option.
144.sec: Scholarships for OBC/EBC/DNT - PM YASASVI, SHREYAS, minority scholarships  [GROUP-II]

144.s: SHREYAS provides higher education support by funding:
o: 8,571 SC students at IITs and IIMs
144.x: The SHREYAS scheme supports higher education by funding 8,571 SC students studying at IITs and IIMs.
144.tq: Match the scheme with its beneficiary category, institution level and exact number.
144.sec: Scholarships for OBC/EBC/DNT - PM YASASVI, SHREYAS, minority scholarships  [GROUP-II]

144.s: Which of the following correctly describes the minority scholarship schemes administered by the Ministry of Minority Affairs?
o: They include pre-matric, post-matric and merit-cum-means scholarships, paid through DBT on NSP 2.0
They are restricted to SC students at IITs and IIMs
They provide only toolkit incentives to minority artisans
They include only post-matric scholarships, paid through Common Service Centres
144.x: Minority scholarships include pre-matric, post-matric and merit-cum-means scholarships. Payment is made through Direct Benefit Transfer on NSP 2.0.
144.tq: Distinguish the scholarship types and payment platform from other welfare schemes.
144.sec: Scholarships for OBC/EBC/DNT - PM YASASVI, SHREYAS, minority scholarships  [GROUP-II]

144.s: With reference to minority scholarships, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Thirty percent of the scholarships are reserved for boys
Payments are made only in cash through educational institutions
Thirty percent of the scholarships are reserved for girls
144.x: Thirty percent of the slots under the minority scholarship schemes are reserved for girls, and payments are made through DBT on NSP 2.0.
144.tq: Use the gender allocation figure and reject reversed or incompatible delivery mechanisms.
144.sec: Scholarships for OBC/EBC/DNT - PM YASASVI, SHREYAS, minority scholarships  [GROUP-II]

144.s: The National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) was established in which year?
144.x: NBCFDC was established in 1992. It is associated with financing development activities for backward classes.
144.tq: Use the year-based numerical recall approach and distinguish the three development finance corporations.
144.sec: Credit institutions - NBCFDC, NMDFC - loan schemes and channelling agencies  [GROUP-II]

144.s: The NBCFDC functions under which Union Ministry?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
144.x: NBCFDC functions under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
144.tq: Apply the ‘which ministry?’ trap by matching the institution with its beneficiary group and administrative department.
144.sec: Credit institutions - NBCFDC, NMDFC - loan schemes and channelling agencies  [GROUP-II]

144.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with reference to NBCFDC schemes?

1. New Swarnima — Women beneficiaries
2. Saksham — Young professionals
3. Virasat — Artisans

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
144.x: New Swarnima is intended for women and Saksham for young professionals. Virasat loans are associated with NMDFC and artisans, so statement 3 is incorrect in this context.
144.tq: Split the options by identifying the institution-specific scheme before checking the beneficiary group.
144.sec: Credit institutions - NBCFDC, NMDFC - loan schemes and channelling agencies  [GROUP-II]

144.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the National Minorities Development and Finance Corporation (NMDFC)?
o: A cooperative society under the Ministry of Finance
A Section 8 company under the Ministry of Minority Affairs
A statutory corporation under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs
A constitutional body under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
144.x: NMDFC is a Section 8 company under the Ministry of Minority Affairs.
144.tq: Test the exact institutional status and ministry rather than relying on the general word ‘corporation’.
144.sec: Credit institutions - NBCFDC, NMDFC - loan schemes and channelling agencies  [GROUP-II]

144.s:
Consider the following statements regarding NMDFC credit lines:

1. Credit Line-1 is available for families with income up to Rs 3 lakh.
2. Credit Line-2 is available for families with income up to Rs 8 lakh.
3. Term loans may extend up to Rs 20-30 lakh.
4. The funding pattern is 90:5:5.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: NMDFC Credit Line-1 has an income ceiling of Rs 3 lakh and Credit Line-2 of Rs 8 lakh. Term loans extend up to Rs 20-30 lakh and the stated funding pattern is 90:5:5.
144.tq: Check each numerical statement independently; the complete combination is correct.
144.sec: Credit institutions - NBCFDC, NMDFC - loan schemes and channelling agencies  [GROUP-II]

144.s: Which of the following is NOT listed as an additional NMDFC loan category?
o: Housing loans for all urban households
144.x: NMDFC provides education loans, micro-finance and Virasat loans for artisans. Housing loans for all urban households are not listed among the stated NMDFC loan categories.
144.tq: Find the option that falls outside the institution-specific list instead of selecting a generally plausible welfare activity.
144.sec: Credit institutions - NBCFDC, NMDFC - loan schemes and channelling agencies  [GROUP-II]

144.s: Through which agencies do NBCFDC and NMDFC primarily channel their loans?
144.x: Both NBCFDC and NMDFC lend through State Channelising Agencies.
144.tq: Discriminate between financial channelling agencies and local administrative bodies.
144.sec: Credit institutions - NBCFDC, NMDFC - loan schemes and channelling agencies  [GROUP-II]

144.s: Which one of the following correctly describes PMJVK?
o: It is a Central Sector Scheme limited to minority students pursuing higher education.
It is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme for area development in minority concentration areas.
It is a constitutional programme implemented by the Election Commission.
It is a State scheme restricted to urban minority households.
144.x: PMJVK is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme aimed at area development in minority concentration areas.
144.tq: Identify the scheme from its funding pattern and broad area-development objective.
144.sec: Area development for minorities - Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram, minority concentration areas  [GROUP-II]

144.s:
PMJVK covers which of the following combination of areas in its stated coverage?

1. 870 minority concentration blocks
2. 321 towns
3. All districts, including 112 Aspirational Districts

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
144.x: The stated coverage includes 870 minority concentration blocks and 321 towns, and has been extended to all districts, including 112 Aspirational Districts.
144.tq: Combine coverage figures with the later geographical expansion instead of treating them as alternatives.
144.sec: Area development for minorities - Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram, minority concentration areas  [GROUP-II]

144.s: Under PMJVK, what proportion of funds is earmarked for education, health and skills together?
144.x: Eighty percent of PMJVK funds go to education, health and skills.
144.tq: Separate the overall sectoral allocation from the distinct allocation intended for women.
144.sec: Area development for minorities - Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram, minority concentration areas  [GROUP-II]

144.s: The allocation under PMJVK for women is stated to be in the range of:
144.x: The allocation for women under PMJVK is stated to be 33-40 percent.
144.tq: Read the range precisely and avoid reversing it with the 80 percent sectoral allocation.
144.sec: Area development for minorities - Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram, minority concentration areas  [GROUP-II]

144.s: The Criminal Tribes Act, 1871, in relation to Denotified Tribes, was:
144.x: Denotified Tribes had been branded under the Criminal Tribes Act, 1871, which was repealed in 1952.
144.tq: Pair the historical enactment with its repeal year and beware of confusing repeal with replacement.
144.sec: Denotified, nomadic and semi-nomadic tribes - SEED scheme, Idate Commission  [GROUP-II]

144.s: Which commission was the first to examine the condition of Denotified Tribes among the commissions mentioned below?
144.x: The Renke Commission, whose report was submitted in 2008, was the first such commission mentioned for Denotified Tribes.
144.tq: Use the ‘first’ marker to distinguish the earlier Renke Commission from the later Idate Commission.
144.sec: Denotified, nomadic and semi-nomadic tribes - SEED scheme, Idate Commission  [GROUP-II]

144.s: The Idate Commission functioned during which period?
144.x: The Idate Commission functioned during 2014-17.
144.tq: Distinguish the commission’s period from the Renke Commission’s 2008 report and the SEED launch year.
144.sec: Denotified, nomadic and semi-nomadic tribes - SEED scheme, Idate Commission  [GROUP-II]

144.s:
Consider the following statements about the findings associated with the Idate Commission:

1. About 1,200 DNTs were already included in SC, ST or OBC lists.
2. About 267-268 DNTs had never been classified.
3. All DNTs were found to be included in the Scheduled Tribe list.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: The Commission found about 1,200 DNTs already in SC/ST/OBC lists and 267-268 never classified. It did not find that all DNTs were included in the Scheduled Tribe list.
144.tq: Reject the absolute statement and retain the two specific numerical findings.
144.sec: Denotified, nomadic and semi-nomadic tribes - SEED scheme, Idate Commission  [GROUP-II]

144.s:
Which of the following is the correct combination regarding the SEED scheme?

1. It was launched in 2022.
2. Its stated outlay is Rs 200 crore.
3. It covers coaching, health insurance, livelihoods and housing.
4. The income ceiling is below Rs 2.5 lakh.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
144.x: SEED was launched in 2022 with an outlay of Rs 200 crore, an income criterion below Rs 2.5 lakh, and provisions for coaching, health insurance, livelihoods and housing.
144.tq: Verify the year, amount, eligibility and objective separately before choosing the complete combination.
144.sec: Denotified, nomadic and semi-nomadic tribes - SEED scheme, Idate Commission  [GROUP-II]

144.s: What amount was reportedly spent under SEED in five years?
144.x: Only Rs 69.3 crore was spent in five years, against the stated Rs 200 crore outlay, reportedly because States did not issue DNT certificates.
144.tq: Distinguish actual expenditure from the sanctioned or announced outlay.
144.sec: Denotified, nomadic and semi-nomadic tribes - SEED scheme, Idate Commission  [GROUP-II]

144.s: The principal reason cited for the low expenditure under SEED was that:
o: States did not issue DNT certificates
the scheme covered only urban areas
the Union Government withdrew the scheme
beneficiaries were excluded from health insurance
144.x: Low expenditure was attributed to the failure of States to issue certificates for Denotified Tribes.
144.tq: Link the implementation shortfall to the administrative bottleneck rather than to the scheme’s objectives.
144.sec: Denotified, nomadic and semi-nomadic tribes - SEED scheme, Idate Commission  [GROUP-II]

144.s: According to the stated data, what proportion of Andhra Pradesh’s population comprises Backward Classes?
144.x: Backward Classes constitute 43.17 percent of Andhra Pradesh’s population according to the stated data.
144.tq: Recall the exact percentage and distinguish it from the separate 33.33 percent reservation figure.
144.sec: Andhra Pradesh BC and minority welfare - BC corporations, minority finance corporation, Imams and Muezzins honorarium  [GROUP-II]

144.s: The Backward Classes in Andhra Pradesh are organised into how many communities and groups, respectively?
144.x: The AP Backward Classes are stated to comprise 138 communities organised into Groups A-E.
144.tq: Keep the community count separate from the number of hostels and the number of groups.
144.sec: Andhra Pradesh BC and minority welfare - BC corporations, minority finance corporation, Imams and Muezzins honorarium  [GROUP-II]

144.s:
Which of the following statements regarding BC welfare infrastructure in Andhra Pradesh is correct?

1. There are 747 BC hostels.
2. The Swarnakara Welfare and Development Corporation has been set up.
3. The EWS department brings together only BC corporations.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
144.x: Andhra Pradesh has 747 BC hostels and has set up the Swarnakara Welfare and Development Corporation. The EWS department brings together specified EWS-related corporations, not only BC corporations.
144.tq: Identify the precise institutional scope and reject the restrictive word ‘only’.
144.sec: Andhra Pradesh BC and minority welfare - BC corporations, minority finance corporation, Imams and Muezzins honorarium  [GROUP-II]

144.s: Under G.O. 1065 of August 2026, the reservation for Backward Classes in urban local body polls in Andhra Pradesh is:
144.x: G.O. 1065 of August 2026 provides for 33.33 percent BC reservation in urban local body polls.
144.tq: Distinguish a reservation percentage from the broader BC population share and the rounded legislative demand.
144.sec: Andhra Pradesh BC and minority welfare - BC corporations, minority finance corporation, Imams and Muezzins honorarium  [GROUP-II]

144.s: The Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly resolved to seek what proportion of BC seats in legislatures?
144.x: The Assembly resolved to seek 33 percent BC seats in legislatures. This is distinct from the 33.33 percent reservation stated for urban local body polls.
144.tq: Discriminate between the exact ULB reservation figure and the rounded legislative demand.
144.sec: Andhra Pradesh BC and minority welfare - BC corporations, minority finance corporation, Imams and Muezzins honorarium  [GROUP-II]

145.x: All three statements are correct: contractors required licences, and migrant workers were entitled to displacement allowance and journey allowance. The displacement allowance was 50 per cent of monthly wages.
145.tq: Check each statutory protection separately before selecting the combined option.
145.sec: Inter-State Migrant Workmen Act 1979 - code, registration, displacement allowance, ONORC

145.s: Which of the following is NOT a feature mentioned in relation to migrant workers under the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020?
o: Coverage of workers who migrate on their own
Portability of PDS and social security across States
Abolition of all contractor licensing requirements
145.x: The OSH Code covers workers who migrate on their own, provides for annual travel allowance and supports portability of PDS and social security. Abolition of all contractor licensing requirements is not a stated feature.
145.tq: Find the option that goes beyond the stated provisions of the Code.
145.sec: Inter-State Migrant Workmen Act 1979 - code, registration, displacement allowance, ONORC

145.s: The One Nation One Ration Card system enables migrant workers to:
o: receive wages directly from the Central Government
draw NFSA rations anywhere in India
transfer their domicile permanently to another State
145.x: ONORC provides portability under the National Food Security Act, enabling migrants to draw rations anywhere in India.
145.tq: Link the portability mechanism with the specific benefit made portable.
145.sec: Inter-State Migrant Workmen Act 1979 - code, registration, displacement allowance, ONORC

145.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched under the Code on Social Security, 2020?
o: Gig worker — work exclusively under a traditional employer-employee relationship
Platform worker — work through online platforms
Aggregator — worker registered only under EPFO
Gig worker — worker entitled automatically to government employment
145.x: A platform worker is one who works through online platforms. Gig work is performed outside a traditional employer-employee relationship, while aggregators are recognised entities under the Code.
145.tq: Separate the definitions of gig workers, platform workers and aggregators.
145.sec: Gig and platform workers - Social Security Code definitions, state laws

145.s:
With reference to the Code on Social Security, 2020, consider the following statements:
1. It is the first law to recognise aggregators, gig workers and platform workers.
2. Aggregators are required to contribute 1–2 per cent of annual turnover to a social-security fund.
3. Such contribution is capped at 5 per cent of the payments made to workers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
145.x: All three statements are correct. The Code recognises the three categories, and aggregator contributions are 1–2 per cent of annual turnover subject to a cap of 5 per cent of payments to workers.
145.tq: Retain both the contribution rate and the separate statutory ceiling.
145.sec: Gig and platform workers - Social Security Code definitions, state laws

145.s: Which one of the following is correct regarding gig workers under the Social Security framework described?
o: They automatically acquire employee status upon registration.
They are guaranteed a minimum wage under the Code.
They can register from the age of 16, and National and State Social Security Boards are provided for.
They can register only after attaining 18 years of age.
145.x: Gig workers can register from the age of 16, and the framework provides for National and State Social Security Boards. It does not automatically confer employee status or guarantee a minimum wage.
145.tq: Use the positive provision and reject the overbroad employee-status claims.
145.sec: Gig and platform workers - Social Security Code definitions, state laws

145.s: Which of the following is NOT presently assured to gig workers under the limitations described?
o: Consideration under National and State Social Security Boards
145.x: Gig workers do not receive employee status as an automatic entitlement. The framework does provide for registration from age 16 and National and State Social Security Boards.
145.tq: Identify the option that converts a limited social-security recognition into full employee status.
145.sec: Gig and platform workers - Social Security Code definitions, state laws

145.s: Which of the following State-level measures is correctly matched?
o: Rajasthan — Platform-Based Gig Workers (Registration and Welfare) Act, 2023, with a welfare board funded by a transaction cess
Karnataka — enacted a 2023 national gig-workers law
Telangana — established the Central Social Security Board through a State Act
Rajasthan — abolished registration requirements for platform workers
145.x: Rajasthan enacted the Platform-Based Gig Workers (Registration and Welfare) Act, 2023, creating a welfare board funded by a cess on transactions. Karnataka's 2024 measure and Telangana's measure were described as proposed laws.
145.tq: Distinguish an enacted State law from proposed measures in other States.
145.sec: Gig and platform workers - Social Security Code definitions, state laws

145.s:
According to the NITI Aayog estimate, the number of gig and platform workers was projected as follows:
1. 77 lakh in 2020–21
2. 1.27 crore in 2024–25
3. 1.43 crore in 2025–26
Which of the statements given above are correct?
145.x: The NITI Aayog 2022 report gave the sequence of 77 lakh in 2020–21, 1.27 crore in 2024–25 and 1.43 crore in 2025–26.
145.tq: Verify each figure in the time series rather than relying only on its upward trend.
145.sec: Gig and platform workers - Social Security Code definitions, state laws

145.s: Which one of the following correctly reflects the Economic Survey 2025–26 assessment of gig and platform workers?
o: 1.43 crore workers, with no projected change in workforce share
120 crore workers, with a 55 per cent decline during FY21–FY25
77 lakh workers, constituting 1.27 per cent of the workforce by 2029–30
120 lakh workers, with a 55 per cent rise during FY21–FY25 and 6.7 per cent of the workforce by 2029–30
145.x: The Economic Survey 2025–26 estimated 120 lakh gig and platform workers, reported a 55 per cent rise from FY21 to FY25, and projected a 6.7 per cent workforce share by 2029–30.
145.tq: Keep the estimate, growth rate and projected workforce share together as one data cluster.
145.sec: Gig and platform workers - Social Security Code definitions, state laws

145.s: Article 23 of the Constitution prohibits:
o: child labour in hazardous industries only
trafficking in persons and bonded labour only
145.x: Article 23 prohibits trafficking in human beings and begar and other similar forms of forced labour; the stated connection here is its ban on begar and forced labour.
145.tq: Match the constitutional provision with its core prohibition.
145.sec: Bonded labour - 1976 Act, rehabilitation

145.s: At the district level, which body is responsible for identifying and releasing bonded labourers under the Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976?
145.x: District-level Vigilance Committees are responsible for identifying and releasing bonded labourers under the 1976 Act.
145.tq: Identify the authority assigned the specific enforcement function.
145.sec: Bonded labour - 1976 Act, rehabilitation

145.s: The Central Sector Scheme for Rehabilitation of Bonded Labourers was introduced in:
145.x: The Central Sector Scheme for Rehabilitation of Bonded Labourers was introduced in 2016.
145.tq: Distinguish the rehabilitation scheme year from the year of the abolition legislation.
145.sec: Bonded labour - 1976 Act, rehabilitation

145.s:
Which of the following statements correctly reflects the contemporary concerns associated with labour and migrant-worker protection?
1. The Indian Labour Conference has not been held since 2015.
2. Weaker collective bargaining is identified as a concern.
3. Digital exclusion is identified as a concern.
4. Idle welfare boards are part of the debate.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
145.x: All four statements reflect the listed criticisms and debates: the absence of the Indian Labour Conference since 2015, weaker collective bargaining, idle welfare boards and digital exclusion.
145.tq: Treat each listed criticism as an independent statement and select the complete combination.
145.sec: Universal angles

145.s: Which of the following statements about social-protection coverage is correct?
o: It remained at 19 per cent between 2015 and 2025.
It rose from 19 per cent in 2015 to 64.3 per cent in 2025, placing India first after China.
It fell from 64.3 per cent in 2015 to 19 per cent in 2025, placing India second after China.
It rose from 19 per cent in 2015 to 64.3 per cent in 2025, placing India second after China.
145.x: Social-protection coverage rose from 19 per cent in 2015 to 64.3 per cent in 2025, and India was ranked second after China.
145.tq: Check both the direction of change and the rank in the comparison.
145.sec: Universal angles

145.s: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the current relevance of e-Shram and gig-worker registration?
o: e-Shram completed five years in 2026, while most gig workers were still outside the portal.
e-Shram completed ten years in 2026, and all gig workers were registered.
e-Shram completed five years in 2021, and most gig workers were already covered.
e-Shram was launched in 2026, while gig workers were excluded by law.

145.sec: Universal angles

146.s: The UN Guidelines for Consumer Protection were first adopted by the United Nations General Assembly in which year?
146.x: The UN Guidelines for Consumer Protection were first adopted by the UN General Assembly in 1985.

146.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the development of the UN Guidelines for Consumer Protection?
o: Adopted in 1985, expanded in 1999 and revised in 2015
Adopted in 1999, expanded in 2005 and revised in 2015
Adopted in 1985, expanded in 2005 and revised in 2020
Adopted in 1991, expanded in 1999 and revised in 2015
146.x: The Guidelines were first adopted in 1985, expanded in 1999 to include sustainable consumption and revised in 2015.
146.tq: Use the chronological sequence to distinguish closely related revision years.
146.sec: International consumer protection - UN Guidelines, World Consumer Rights Day, Consumers International

146.s: World Consumer Rights Day commemorates the consumer-rights speech delivered by:
146.x: The day marks John F. Kennedy's 1962 speech on consumer rights.
146.tq: Discriminate between closely related political figures and years.
146.sec: International consumer protection - UN Guidelines, World Consumer Rights Day, Consumers International

146.s:
Consider the following statements about Consumers International:
1. It is a global federation of consumer groups.
2. It was founded in 1960 as the International Organisation of Consumers Unions.
3. Its headquarters is based in London.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
146.x: All three statements are correct. Consumers International was founded in 1960 as IOCU and is based in London.
146.tq: Combine organisation, origin and location facts in a coded statement question.
146.sec: International consumer protection - UN Guidelines, World Consumer Rights Day, Consumers International

146.s: National Consumer Day in India is observed on 24 December because that date marks:
o: The commencement of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019
The establishment of the National Consumer Commission
The adoption of the UN Guidelines for Consumer Protection
The enactment of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986
146.x: National Consumer Day is observed on 24 December, the date associated with the Consumer Protection Act, 1986.
