146.sec: International consumer protection - UN Guidelines, World Consumer Rights Day, Consumers International

146.s:
With reference to consumer redressal mechanisms, consider the following statements:
1. India has District, State and National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions.
2. These bodies were called Consumer Forums under the Consumer Protection Act, 1986.
3. They are ordinary civil courts established under the Code of Civil Procedure.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
146.x: India has a three-tier quasi-judicial structure of District, State and National Commissions. Under the 1986 Act, they were known as Consumer Forums; they are not ordinary civil courts under the Code of Civil Procedure.
146.tq: Identify the correct institutional description and reject the wrong-body trap.
146.sec: Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions - pecuniary jurisdiction, appeals, e-Daakhil

146.s: Under the revised pecuniary jurisdiction applicable from 2021, a complaint involving consideration paid up to ₹50 lakh ordinarily lies before the:
146.x: The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has original jurisdiction for consideration paid up to ₹50 lakh under the 2021 revision.
146.tq: Apply the revised slab rather than the older ₹1 crore threshold.
146.sec: Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions - pecuniary jurisdiction, appeals, e-Daakhil

146.s: The State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has original jurisdiction over complaints involving consideration paid:
o: Above ₹2 crore and up to ₹10 crore
Above ₹50 lakh and up to ₹2 crore
146.x: The State Commission has original jurisdiction from above ₹50 lakh up to ₹2 crore under the revised 2021 limits.
146.tq: Distinguish the revised middle-tier pecuniary range from the original 2019 slabs.
146.sec: Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions - pecuniary jurisdiction, appeals, e-Daakhil

146.s: A District Commission order is appealable to the State Commission within:
146.x: An appeal from the District Commission lies to the State Commission within 45 days.
146.tq: Direct recall of the appellate limitation period.
146.sec: Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions - pecuniary jurisdiction, appeals, e-Daakhil

146.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: State Commission — appeal to District Commission within 45 days
State Commission — appeal to National Commission within 30 days
District Commission — appeal to Supreme Court within 45 days
National Commission — appeal to State Commission within 30 days
146.x: An appeal from the State Commission lies to the National Commission within 30 days. Appeals from the District Commission go to the State Commission, while appeals from the National Commission go to the Supreme Court.
146.tq: Use the appellate hierarchy and authority trap to eliminate reversed relationships.
146.sec: Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions - pecuniary jurisdiction, appeals, e-Daakhil

146.s: An appeal against an order of the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission lies to the Supreme Court within:
146.x: An appeal from the National Commission lies to the Supreme Court within 30 days.
146.tq: Direct recall of the final appellate route and limitation period.
146.sec: Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions - pecuniary jurisdiction, appeals, e-Daakhil

146.s: For determining the pecuniary jurisdiction of a Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, the relevant criterion is:
o: The annual income of the complainant
The compensation claimed by the complainant
The market value of the goods at the time of filing
The value of consideration paid for the goods or services
146.x: Jurisdiction is determined by the value of consideration paid for the goods or services, not by the compensation claimed.
146.tq: Apply the governing criterion to distinguish consideration from compensation.
146.sec: Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions - pecuniary jurisdiction, appeals, e-Daakhil

146.s: Which one of the following pairs correctly describes the original and revised pecuniary jurisdiction limits?
o: Original 2019 slabs: ₹5 lakh and ₹50 lakh; revised 2021 upper threshold: above ₹2 crore
Original 2019 slabs: ₹50 lakh and ₹2 crore; revised 2021 upper threshold: above ₹10 crore
Original 2019 slabs: ₹2 crore and ₹10 crore; revised 2021 upper threshold: above ₹1 crore
Original 2019 slabs: ₹1 crore and ₹10 crore; revised 2021 upper threshold: above ₹2 crore
146.x: The original Consumer Protection Act 2019 slabs were ₹1 crore and ₹10 crore. They were revised in 2021, with the National Commission threshold becoming above ₹2 crore.
146.tq: Compare the older statutory slabs with the revised jurisdictional limits.
146.sec: Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions - pecuniary jurisdiction, appeals, e-Daakhil

146.s: A complaint before a Consumer Commission is deemed to have been admitted if it is not decided within:

146.tq: Direct recall of a procedural time limit.
146.sec: Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions - pecuniary jurisdiction, appeals, e-Daakhil

146.s: The e-Daakhil facility for online filing has been merged into which portal?
146.x: The e-Daakhil online filing facility has been merged into the e-Jagriti portal.
146.tq: Discriminate between similarly named digital public-service portals.
146.sec: Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions - pecuniary jurisdiction, appeals, e-Daakhil

146.s: In August 2026, the Supreme Court directed the NCDRC to report on pendency and vacancies. The number of cases pending across the consumer redressal system was reported to be approximately:
146.x: Approximately 5.7 lakh cases were pending across the consumer redressal system when the direction was issued.
146.tq: Recall the current-affairs figure associated with pendency and vacancies.
146.sec: Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions - pecuniary jurisdiction, appeals, e-Daakhil

146.s: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 1986, a District Consumer Forum consisted of:
o: A President and two members, one of whom was a woman
A President and three members, all of whom were judges
A President and four members, two of whom were women
146.x: The old District Forum consisted of a President and two members, one of whom had to be a woman.

146.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the six consumer rights recognised under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019?
146.x: The six rights include safety, information, choice, hearing, redressal and consumer awareness. A right to private ownership is not included in this list.

146.s: Which one of the following sets contains only rights recognised under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019?
o: Safety, information, choice, hearing, redressal and consumer awareness
Safety, privacy, ownership, hearing, compensation and awareness
Information, taxation, choice, employment, redressal and privacy
Choice, property, education, hearing, ownership and awareness
146.x: The six recognised rights are the right to safety, information, choice, hearing, redressal and consumer awareness.
146.tq: Use the complete statutory list to reject substituted rights.
146.sec: Consumer Protection Act 2019 - six rights, replaced Act, consumer definition, fees, product liability

146.s: Which one of the following persons would generally be treated as a consumer under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019?
o: A person purchasing services for commercial exploitation
A person purchasing goods solely for a large-scale business activity
A person purchasing goods for resale
A person making an online purchase for personal use
146.x: The definition includes online and electronic purchases for personal use. A person buying for resale or commercial use is generally excluded.
146.tq: Apply the personal-use and commercial-purpose distinction to a factual situation.
146.sec: Consumer Protection Act 2019 - six rights, replaced Act, consumer definition, fees, product liability

146.s: Under the expanded consumer-protection framework, the term 'advertisement' includes communication through:
o: Electronic media, the internet and websites
146.x: The definition of advertisement includes electronic media, the internet and websites.
146.tq: Test the scope-expansion trap created by digital modes of communication.
146.sec: Consumer Protection Act 2019 - six rights, replaced Act, consumer definition, fees, product liability

146.s: A consumer complaint may be filed before the appropriate Commission at the place where the complainant:
146.x: A complaint can be filed where the complainant resides or works, subject to the applicable jurisdictional requirements.
146.tq: Apply territorial jurisdiction to distinguish residence-or-work from purchase-only rules.
146.sec: Consumer Protection Act 2019 - six rights, replaced Act, consumer definition, fees, product liability

146.s:
Which of the following was introduced or strengthened as a feature of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019?
1. Central Consumer Protection Authority
2. Product liability of manufacturers, sellers and service providers
3. Rules relating to e-commerce
4. Penalties for adulterated and spurious goods
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
146.x: All four are features associated with the 2019 framework. It also provided for online filing and video hearings.

146.s: Eco Mark is associated with:

Agricultural produce and was introduced in 1937 through the Agriculture Ministry
Gold jewellery and was introduced in 2021 through RBI
Eco-friendly products and was introduced in 1991 through BIS
146.x: Eco Mark relates to eco-friendly products and was introduced in 1991 through BIS.

146.sec: Standards, marks and food laws → product/year

146.s: Under the Jan Vishwas Act, 2023, the Legal Metrology Act, 2009 had:
o: 7 sections repealed, with no further changes proposed
12 sections decriminalised, with 7 more proposed under Jan Vishwas 2.0
7 sections decriminalised, with 12 more proposed under Jan Vishwas 2.0
146.x: Seven sections of the Legal Metrology Act, 2009 were decriminalised through the Jan Vishwas Act, 2023, while 12 more were proposed under Jan Vishwas 2.0.

146.s: The Central Consumer Protection Authority is best described as:
o: An executive agency established under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019
A private federation of consumer organisations
A constitutional court established under Article 32
A department of the Supreme Court Registry
146.x: The CCPA is an executive agency created under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

146.s: The Central Consumer Protection Authority came into existence on:
146.x: The CCPA came into existence on 24 July 2020.

146.sec: Central Consumer Protection Authority - powers, class action, misleading ads, endorsers

146.s: The core mandate of the Central Consumer Protection Authority is to:
o: Regulate monetary policy and consumer credit
Set all retail prices in the country
Prevent and regulate false or misleading advertisements
146.x: The core mandate of the CCPA is to prevent and regulate false or misleading advertisements.

146.s:
Which of the following powers may be exercised by the Central Consumer Protection Authority?
1. Inquiring into violations of consumer rights
2. Ordering recalls and refunds
3. Filing class-action complaints
4. Imposing penalties
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
146.x: The CCPA can inquire into violations, order recalls and refunds, file class-action complaints and impose penalties.
146.tq: Test the complete range of powers through an all-inclusive coded option.
146.sec: Central Consumer Protection Authority - powers, class action, misleading ads, endorsers

146.s: Under Section 21, the maximum penalty for a misleading advertisement is ₹10 lakh for a first offence and may extend to ₹50 lakh for:
o: An offence appealed to the Supreme Court
An offence involving a foreign company only
146.x: The penalty may be up to ₹10 lakh for the initial offence and up to ₹50 lakh for a repeat offence.
146.tq: Distinguish first-offence and repeat-offence penalty limits.
146.sec: Central Consumer Protection Authority - powers, class action, misleading ads, endorsers

146.s: An endorser found liable in relation to a misleading advertisement may be prohibited from endorsing advertisements for up to:
o: Six months for a first offence and one year for a repeat offence
One year for a first offence and three years for a repeat offence
Three years for a first offence and permanently for a repeat offence
Two years for a first offence and five years for a repeat offence

146.sec: Central Consumer Protection Authority - powers, class action, misleading ads, endorsers

146.s: Under the June 2022 guidelines on misleading advertisements and endorsements, an endorsement should:
o: Be permitted only when the product is sold offline
Be based only on the popularity of the endorser, without disclosure
Reflect a genuine opinion, with any material connection disclosed
Conceal commercial relationships to preserve credibility

146.sec: Central Consumer Protection Authority - powers, class action, misleading ads, endorsers

146.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The CCPA issued advisories against celebrity endorsements of betting applications.
2. The CCPA fined Meta ₹10 lakh over walkie-talkie listings.
3. Meta challenged that order in the Delhi High Court.

146.s: Which one of the following comparisons between the EU framework and India's framework for representative consumer actions is correct?
o: The EU framework prohibits collective redress, whereas India's framework is completely centralised.

146.s:
Consider the following requirements under the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules, 2026:
1. Disclosure of the importer and country of origin for imported goods.
2. Display of the legal name, headquarters and branch addresses of the entity.
3. Disclosure of customer-care and grievance-officer details.
4. Concealment of the legal identity of the seller to protect commercial confidentiality.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
146.x: The 2026 Rules require disclosure of import details, the entity's legal identity and addresses, and customer-care and grievance-officer details. Statement 4 is false because concealment of legal identity is not a requirement.
146.tq: Find the statement that reverses a transparency requirement.
146.sec: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules 2020 - marketplace vs inventory, grievance officer, dark patterns

146.s:
Under the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules, 2026, e-commerce entities are required to do which of the following in relation to grievances?
1. Join the National Consumer Helpline convergence process.
2. Give complainants copies of their complaints.
3. Transfer every complaint directly to the National Commission without examination.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
146.x: The Rules require participation in the NCH convergence process and provision of complaint copies to complainants. They do not require every complaint to be transferred directly to the National Commission.
146.tq: Reject the extreme institutional-transfer claim and retain the two stated grievance duties.
146.sec: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules 2020 - marketplace vs inventory, grievance officer, dark patterns

146.s: Which of the following statements regarding search results and discounts under the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules, 2026 is correct?
o: Search results may be manipulated where the entity discloses its legal name.
Sponsored listings may be displayed without disclosure if the price is reduced.
The prior price is necessarily the maximum price charged during the preceding 30 days.
Reduced and prior prices must be shown, and the prior price is the lowest price in the preceding 30 days.
146.x: The Rules prohibit manipulated search results, require clear disclosure of sponsored listings, and require display of the reduced price and the prior price, defined as the lowest price in the preceding 30 days.
146.tq: Check both halves of the requirement: search transparency and the precise price baseline.
146.sec: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules 2020 - marketplace vs inventory, grievance officer, dark patterns

146.s: Which one of the following is NOT a requirement relating to dark patterns under the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules, 2026?
o: Exemption from the 2023 Guidelines after completing the annual self-audit
146.x: The Rules require compliance with the 2023 Guidelines, an annual self-audit and display of the compliance certificate. An annual self-audit does not exempt an entity from the Guidelines.
146.tq: Identify the option that changes a continuing compliance duty into an exemption.
146.sec: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules 2020 - marketplace vs inventory, grievance officer, dark patterns

146.s: Which of the following best describes the consent requirement for using consumer data under the e-commerce framework?
o: Consent is required only for imported goods and not for domestic transactions.
Consumer data may be used without consent when unrelated fees are bundled separately.
Implied consent is sufficient for all uses of consumer data.
Express and affirmative consent is required, and unrelated bundled fees are curbed.
146.x: Use of consumer data requires express, affirmative consent, and the framework curbs unrelated fees bundled with a transaction.
146.tq: Apply the consent rule to distinguish affirmative permission from implied permission.

3. National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission

Appealable before the National Commission as of right

146.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the National Consumer Helpline?
o: It deals exclusively with complaints relating to imported goods.
It has convergence partners such as e-commerce companies.
It is a consumer court attached only to the National Commission.
It operates without convergence partners from the e-commerce sector.
146.x: The National Consumer Helpline has convergence partners, including e-commerce companies; it is not itself a consumer court.

146.s:
Consider the following statements:

2. “Jagriti” is the brand ambassador or mascot of the campaign.
3. National Consumer Day is observed on 15 March.
4. World Consumer Rights Day is observed on 15 March.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
146.x: Jago Grahak Jago is the flagship awareness campaign of the Department of Consumer Affairs and Jagriti is its mascot. National Consumer Day is observed on 24 December, whereas World Consumer Rights Day is observed on 15 March; therefore, statement 3 is false.

146.s: In Indian Medical Association v. V.P. Shantha (1995), the Supreme Court held that:
o: All medical services, including wholly free services, are outside consumer law.
Medical services paid for, including services in hospitals charging some patients, constitute “service” under the Consumer Protection Act.
Medical negligence can never be considered by consumer fora.
Only services provided in government hospitals are covered by consumer law.
146.x: The 1995 decision held that paid medical services, including services in hospitals that charge some patients, fall within the definition of service under consumer law. Wholly free services are excluded.
146.tq: Use the paid-versus-wholly-free distinction to identify the holding.

146.s:
With reference to consumer remedies, consider the following statements:
1. A consumer may get food samples tested.
2. The legal heir of a deceased consumer may file a consumer complaint.
3. A legal heir can file a complaint only when the deceased consumer had received wholly free medical services.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
146.x: Consumers may get food samples tested, and the legal heir of a deceased consumer may file a complaint. Statement 3 is false because the right is not confined to wholly free medical services.
146.tq: Retain the two recognised consumer remedies and reject the restrictive condition.

146.s: Which one of the following statements correctly reflects the current consumer-protection context in India?
o: Andhra Pradesh was ranked first nationally in consumer justice delivery in the India Justice Report 2026.
E-commerce platforms uniformly accepted the jurisdiction of the Central Consumer Protection Authority.
There were no concerns regarding vacancies or pendency in consumer commissions.
The National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission had no backlog requiring judicial scrutiny in 2026.
146.x: Andhra Pradesh was ranked first nationally in consumer justice delivery in the India Justice Report 2026. The current context also includes scrutiny of a 5.7 lakh-case NCDRC backlog, concerns over vacancies and pendency, and disputes by platforms regarding CCPA jurisdiction.
146.tq: Identify the precise positive current-affairs fact while rejecting absolute claims about institutional performance and consensus.

157.sec: Heads of institutions and persons of Indian origin

157.s: Which one of the following statements about the presidency of the New Development Bank is correct?
o: The presidency is permanently held by Brazil
The presidency rotates only among non-BRICS members
The presidency is appointed for a lifetime by the IMF
The presidency rotates among the founding members; Russia gave up its turn and the Brazilian incumbent's term runs to 2030
157.x: The NDB presidency rotates among its founding members. Russia gave up its turn, and the Brazilian incumbent's term runs to 2030.
157.tq: Distinguish a rotating institutional arrangement from permanent or externally appointed leadership.
157.sec: Heads of institutions and persons of Indian origin

157.s: The traditional nationality associated with the presidency of the Asian Development Bank is:
157.x: The President of the Asian Development Bank is traditionally Japanese.
157.tq: Test the institutional convention rather than a particular office-holder.
157.sec: Heads of institutions and persons of Indian origin

157.s: IMF members' quotas determine all of the following EXCEPT:
o: Appointment of every national finance minister
157.x: Quotas determine members' financial contributions, borrowing access and voting power. They do not appoint national finance ministers.
157.tq: Find the option outside the three functions directly linked to IMF quotas.
157.sec: IMF - quota, SDR, IMFC, Article IV, facilities

157.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the weights in the IMF quota formula?
157.x: The quota formula assigns weights of GDP 50%, openness 30%, variability 15% and reserves 5%.
157.tq: Preserve the exact order and percentages in the quota formula.
157.sec: IMF - quota, SDR, IMFC, Article IV, facilities

157.s: The quota of an IMF member is reviewed:
o: Only once, at the time of admission
157.x: IMF quotas are reviewed periodically.
157.tq: Distinguish a periodic institutional review from a one-time or crisis-only review.
157.sec: IMF - quota, SDR, IMFC, Article IV, facilities

157.s: Since October 2016, the IMF's Special Drawing Rights basket has consisted of:
o: The US dollar, euro, Indian rupee, yen and pound
The US dollar, euro, Swiss franc, yen and pound
The US dollar, euro, Chinese renminbi, yen and pound
The US dollar, pound, ruble, yen and Canadian dollar
157.x: Since October 2016, the SDR basket has contained the US dollar, euro, Chinese renminbi, Japanese yen and pound sterling.
157.tq: Use the exact five-currency composition and avoid substituting a prominent but non-member currency.
157.sec: IMF - quota, SDR, IMFC, Article IV, facilities

157.s: Which of the following statements regarding SDRs is correct?
o: They are physical gold reserves held only by the World Bank
They are a single currency replacing all national currencies
They are loans issued exclusively to private corporations
They are commonly described as 'paper gold', and India's allocation can be used for balance-of-payments needs
157.x: SDRs are described as 'paper gold'. India's allocated SDRs may be used for balance-of-payments needs.
157.tq: Identify the functional meaning of SDRs rather than treating them as a physical commodity or national currency.
157.sec: IMF - quota, SDR, IMFC, Article IV, facilities

157.s: The International Monetary and Financial Committee primarily:
o: Advises the IMF Board of Governors
Settles disputes between private investors and states
Insures foreign investments against political risk
Prepares the World Bank's Human Capital Index
157.x: The IMFC advises the IMF Board of Governors.
157.tq: Match the committee to its advisory role within the IMF governance structure.
157.sec: IMF - quota, SDR, IMFC, Article IV, facilities

157.s: Article IV consultations of the IMF refer to:
o: A review of the World Bank's infrastructure loans
A compulsory annual revision of every member's currency
Annual bilateral surveillance of each member's economy
157.x: Article IV consultations involve annual bilateral surveillance of each IMF member's economy.
157.tq: Distinguish economic surveillance from lending, dispute settlement and exchange-rate revision.
157.sec: IMF - quota, SDR, IMFC, Article IV, facilities

157.s: Which of the following is NOT an IMF lending or financing facility mentioned in the institutional framework?
157.x: Stand-By Arrangement, Extended Fund Facility and Rapid Financing Instrument are IMF facilities. Political-risk guarantees are associated with MIGA, not an IMF facility listed here.
157.tq: Separate IMF financing facilities from a World Bank Group risk-insurance function.
157.sec: IMF - quota, SDR, IMFC, Article IV, facilities

157.s: Which IMF facility had the softest servicing terms?
157.x: The Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility, or ESAF, had the softest servicing terms among the facilities identified.
157.tq: Recall the distinctive concessional feature attached to ESAF.
157.sec: IMF - quota, SDR, IMFC, Article IV, facilities

157.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the distribution of influence in the IMF and World Bank:
1. The Global North accounts for about 15% of the population but holds approximately 60% of the votes.
2. The United States alone holds a veto.
3. The BRICS New Delhi Declaration of September 2026 demanded quota and voting reform.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
157.x: All three statements are correct. The declaration demanded reform in the context of the unequal distribution of population and voting power.
157.tq: Combine numerical inequality, veto power and the reform demand into one institutional-governance question.
157.sec: IMF - quota, SDR, IMFC, Article IV, facilities

157.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
157.x: The World Economic Outlook is an IMF report. Global Economic Prospects, World Development Report and Human Capital Index are associated with the World Bank.
157.tq: Begin with the sure report-institution pair and eliminate reports belonging to neighbouring institutions.

157.s: Which report is published by the United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs?
157.x: The World Economic Situation and Prospects 2026 is associated with UN DESA.
157.tq: Distinguish the UN DESA report from similarly titled IMF, World Bank and UNCTAD reports.

157.s: The Global Investment Trends Monitor is associated with:
o: UN DESA, which reported India's FDI rising 47% to $73 billion in 2025
IMF, which reported India's FDI rising 73% to $47 billion in 2025
World Bank, which reported India's FDI rising 37% to $74 billion in 2025
UNCTAD, which reported India's FDI rising 73% to $47 billion in 2025
157.x: The Global Investment Trends Monitor is a UNCTAD publication; it reported India's FDI rising 73% to $47 billion in 2025.
157.tq: Match the report, institution and two-part numerical figure together.

157.s: Which one of the following statements about the World Bank's reports is correct?
o: Global Economic Prospects is issued in January and June, and India's FY26 forecast was raised to 7.2% from 6.3%
World Development Report 2025 is titled Standards for Development and is an IMF report
Human Capital Index is a report of UNCTAD
Global Economic Prospects is issued only once every five years
157.x: Global Economic Prospects is issued in January and June, and the cited India FY26 forecast was raised from 6.3% to 7.2%. World Development Report 2025 is titled Standards for Development and is also associated with the World Bank.
157.tq: Check both the publication frequency and the forecast figures before accepting the complete statement.

157.s:
Arrange the following events relating to the New Development Bank in chronological order:
A. NDB began operations
B. Idea proposed at the 4th BRICS Summit in New Delhi
C. Agreement signed at the 6th BRICS Summit in Fortaleza
D. Uzbekistan became the 10th member
157.x: The idea was proposed in 2012, the agreement was signed in 2014, operations began in 2015, and Uzbekistan became the 10th member in 2026.
157.tq: Fix the first three events by their summit and operational years, then place the 2026 membership event last.

157.s: The agreement establishing the New Development Bank was signed at the:
157.x: The agreement was signed at the 6th BRICS Summit in Fortaleza, Brazil, in 2014; it is associated with the Fortaleza Declaration.
157.tq: Distinguish the summit where the idea originated from the summit where the agreement was signed.

157.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the New Development Bank's institutional structure?
o: Its headquarters is in Fortaleza and it has no regional offices
Its headquarters is in Washington, D.C. and it has regional offices only in Europe
Its headquarters is in Shanghai and it has regional offices in Johannesburg, São Paulo, Ahmedabad/GIFT City and Moscow
Its headquarters is in New Delhi and all regional offices are in BRICS capitals
157.x: The NDB is headquartered in Shanghai and has regional offices in Johannesburg, São Paulo, India's Ahmedabad/GIFT City and Moscow.
157.tq: Use the headquarters–regional office combination to distinguish NDB from Bretton Woods institutions.

157.s:
Consider the following statements about the New Development Bank:
1. The founding members have equal voting rights.
2. No founding member has a veto.
3. The Bank is open to all United Nations members.
4. Uzbekistan became its tenth member and the first Central Asian member in 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
157.x: All four statements correctly describe the voting structure, membership policy and Uzbekistan's 2026 status.
157.tq: Check each institutional feature separately, especially the contrast between equal voting and absence of veto.

157.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched with the New Development Bank's record as of September 2026?
157.x: Russia-linked operations were frozen in March 2022, not March 2015. The Bank had 139 projects, approximately $43 billion approved and approximately $20 billion disbursed.
157.tq: Use the institutional record figures and detect the altered year in the final option.

157.s: The New Development Bank froze Russia-linked operations in March 2022. This was significant because:
o: Russia was a 20% shareholder of the Bank
Russia was the sole shareholder of the Bank
Russia held a permanent veto over all NDB decisions
Russia had no connection with the Bank's founding structure
157.x: Russia was a 20% shareholder of the NDB. The Bank froze Russia-linked operations in March 2022.
157.tq: Connect the operational decision with the precise shareholder relationship, not with an invented veto power.

157.s: The Asian Development Bank was established in which year?
157.x: The Asian Development Bank was established in 1966.
157.tq: Use the direct year-recall approach and distinguish nearby dates.

157.s: The headquarters of the Asian Development Bank is located at
157.x: The headquarters of the Asian Development Bank is in Manila, Philippines.
157.tq: Test the headquarters-location fact directly.

157.s: The Asian Development Bank was created at the initiative of which organisation?
157.x: The Asian Development Bank was created at the initiative of the United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (UN-ESCAP).
157.tq: Use the institutional-origin trap by distinguishing related United Nations bodies.

157.s:
With reference to India and the Asian Development Bank, consider the following statements:
1. India was a founding member of the Asian Development Bank.
2. India holds a voting share of 6.3 per cent in the Asian Development Bank.
3. India has a higher voting share than China in the Asian Development Bank.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
157.x: India was a founding member and has a 6.3 per cent voting share. Since China's share is 6.4 per cent, India does not have a higher share than China; therefore statement 3 is false.
157.tq: Compare the exact percentages and identify the reversed-comparison trap.

157.s:
Consider the following pairs relating to voting shares in the Asian Development Bank:

Shareholder — Voting share
1. Japan — 15.7%
2. United States of America — 15.7%
3. China — 6.4%
4. India — 6.3%

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
157.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Japan and the United States each hold 15.7 per cent, China holds 6.4 per cent and India holds 6.3 per cent.
157.tq: Check each numerical pair separately before selecting the combined code.

157.s: As of 2025, the Asian Development Bank had how many members, comprising how many Asia-Pacific and non-regional members respectively?
157.x: The Asian Development Bank had 69 members: 49 from the Asia-Pacific region and 20 non-regional members.
157.tq: Match the total with its exact component numbers.

157.s: Which one of the following countries was the newest member of the Asian Development Bank in 2025?
157.x: Türkiye was the newest member of the Asian Development Bank in 2025.
157.tq: Test the newest-member fact against established member countries.

157.s: In December 2025, the Asian Development Bank raised India's FY26 growth forecast from 6.5 per cent to
157.x: The Asian Development Bank raised India's FY26 growth forecast to 7.2 per cent from 6.5 per cent in December 2025.
157.tq: Read the revised figure together with the original baseline.

157.s: The Articles of Agreement of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank were signed in which year?
157.x: The Articles of Agreement of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank were signed in 2015.
157.tq: Distinguish the signing year from the year of commencement of operations.

157.s: The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank commenced its operations in
157.x: The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank began operations in January 2016.
157.tq: Use the precise month-year combination rather than the nearby Articles-signing year.

157.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank?
o: It is headquartered in Beijing, China, with India as its largest shareholder and China as its second-largest shareholder.
It is headquartered in Beijing, China, with China as its largest shareholder and India as its second-largest shareholder.
It is headquartered in Tokyo, Japan, with Japan as its largest shareholder and India as its second-largest shareholder.
It is headquartered in Manila, Philippines, with India as its largest shareholder and China as its second-largest shareholder.
157.x: The AIIB is headquartered in Beijing. China is its largest shareholder and India is its second-largest shareholder.
157.tq: Separate headquarters, largest shareholder and second-largest shareholder instead of swapping their relationships.

157.s: According to the stated September 2026 position, which of the following correctly represents the AIIB's scale and rating?
o: 120 approved members, approximately 70 billion dollars across 350 projects, and an AAA rating
111 approved members, approximately 59 billion dollars across 300 projects, and an AAA rating
111 approved members, approximately 69 billion dollars across 350 projects, and an AAA rating
110 approved members, approximately 69 billion dollars across 350 projects, and an AA rating
157.x: The AIIB had 111 approved members, approximately 69 billion dollars committed across 350 projects, and an AAA rating.
157.tq: Verify all components of a compound numerical description.

157.s:
Which of the following projects are co-funded by the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank?
1. Mumbai MUTP-III
2. NIIF Phase II
3. Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor
4. AP Disaster Recovery Project
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
157.x: The AIIB co-funds Mumbai MUTP-III and NIIF Phase II. The Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor is identified with ADB, while the AP Disaster Recovery Project is identified with the World Bank.
157.tq: Identify the correct lender by eliminating projects assigned to neighbouring institutions.

157.s:
The Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor in Andhra Pradesh is associated with which of the following descriptions?
1. It includes the nodes of Visakhapatnam, Chittoor and Kopparthy.
2. It covers 33,000 acres.
3. It is funded by an ADB loan of ₹3,300 crore in two tranches.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
157.x: The VCIC includes the Visakhapatnam, Chittoor and Kopparthy nodes, covers 33,000 acres and receives an ADB loan of ₹3,300 crore in two tranches.
157.tq: Combine project geography, area and financing details without confusing the lender.

157.s: The AP Road Sector Project, associated with the World Bank, covers approximately how much of the road network comprising major district roads and State highways?
157.x: The AP Road Sector Project covers 850 km of major district roads and State highways and is associated with the World Bank.
157.tq: Test the exact project coverage figure and avoid nearby rounded values.

157.s: The AP Disaster Recovery Project funded by the World Bank was associated with recovery after
157.x: The AP Disaster Recovery Project was associated with post-Hudhud recovery.
157.tq: Use the event-project linkage rather than the lender alone.

157.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. VCIC — ADB
2. AP Road Sector Project — World Bank
3. AP Rural Roads Project — AIIB
4. AP Disaster Recovery Project — World Bank
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
157.x: All four pairs are correctly matched: VCIC with ADB, the AP Road Sector Project with the World Bank, the AP Rural Roads Project with AIIB and the AP Disaster Recovery Project with the World Bank.
157.tq: Start from the sure lender-project pairs and verify the complete combination.

157.s: The 18th BRICS Summit New Delhi Declaration, referred to in the stated September 2026 context, sought reform of which institutions?
o: United Nations Security Council institutions only
157.x: The 18th BRICS Summit New Delhi Declaration sought reform of the Bretton Woods institutions.
157.tq: Link the declaration with its stated institutional reform agenda.

157.s: Which one of the following statements best reflects the stated comparison between the New Development Bank and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank?
o: The New Development Bank's lending was described as slower than that of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank.
The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank's lending was described as slower than that of the New Development Bank.
Both institutions were described as having identical lending speeds.
Neither institution was associated with infrastructure lending.
157.x: The stated comparison described the New Development Bank's lending as slow in contrast with the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank.
157.tq: Focus on the direction of the comparison and avoid reversing the two institutions.

157.s:
Which of the following have been identified as criticisms or areas of debate concerning Bretton Woods institutions?
1. Structural adjustment conditions
2. Sovereign immunity
3. Northern control of votes
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
157.x: Structural adjustment conditions, sovereign immunity and Northern control of votes are all identified as criticisms or areas of debate concerning Bretton Woods institutions.
157.tq: Treat each listed criticism as an independent statement before choosing the combined code.

158.s: The World Trade Organization was established on 1 January 1995 under which agreement?
o: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade
158.x: The WTO was established on 1 January 1995 under the Marrakesh Agreement after the Uruguay Round.
158.tq: Use the founding agreement and date as the identifying pair.
158.sec: WTO - establishment, predecessor, HQ, membership

158.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the relationship between GATT and the WTO?
o: The WTO deals only with goods, whereas GATT deals with services and intellectual property.
The WTO replaced the GATT system, while GATT survived as an integral WTO agreement.
GATT replaced the WTO after the Uruguay Round.
GATT and the WTO are completely unrelated institutions.
158.x: The WTO replaced the GATT 1947/48 system, but GATT continues as an integral WTO agreement.
158.tq: Discriminate between an institutional predecessor and an agreement retained within the successor framework.
158.sec: WTO - establishment, predecessor, HQ, membership

158.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the WTO:
1. Its decision-making is based on consensus.
2. It follows the principle of one-country-one-vote.
3. Its governance covers goods, services and intellectual property.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
158.x: All three statements are correct. The WTO uses consensus-based, one-country-one-vote decision-making and covers goods, services and intellectual property.
158.tq: Combine institutional principles with the WTO’s expanded subject coverage.
158.sec: WTO - establishment, predecessor, HQ, membership

158.s: As of March 2026, the membership of the World Trade Organization is:
158.x: The WTO has 166 members as of March 2026.
158.tq: Distinguish the latest figure from the older membership figure of 164.
158.sec: WTO - establishment, predecessor, HQ, membership

158.s: Which pair was admitted as the latest members of the WTO in 2024?
158.x: Comoros and Timor-Leste became the latest WTO members in 2024.
158.tq: Match the latest membership fact rather than the older accession examples.
158.sec: WTO - establishment, predecessor, HQ, membership

158.s: Which WTO body is the highest decision-making body and is required to meet at least once every two years?
158.x: The Ministerial Conference is the WTO’s highest decision-making body and must meet at least once every two years.
158.tq: Identify the highest authority by its formal meeting requirement.
158.sec: Structure - Ministerial Conference, General Council, DSB, TPRB

158.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (WTO body)
A. General Council
B. Dispute Settlement Body
C. Trade Policy Review Body
D. Ministerial Conference

List-II (Function)
1. Periodic review of members’ trade policies
2. Highest decision-making body
3. Operates between Ministerial Conferences
4. Deals with panels and Appellate Body rulings

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
158.x: The General Council runs the WTO between Ministerial Conferences; the DSB handles dispute rulings; the TPRB reviews trade policies; and the Ministerial Conference is the highest decision-making body.
158.tq: Start from the sure pair of each body with its distinctive function.
158.sec: Structure - Ministerial Conference, General Council, DSB, TPRB

158.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Dispute Settlement Body — Panels and Appellate Body rulings
Trade Policy Review Body — Periodic review of members’ trade policies
Ministerial Conference — Investigation of anti-dumping cases in India
Council for Trade in Goods — Oversight of GATT
158.x: The Ministerial Conference is the WTO’s highest decision-making body; investigation of anti-dumping cases in India is not its function.
158.tq: Find the body-function mismatch by separating WTO governance from domestic investigation.
158.sec: Structure - Ministerial Conference, General Council, DSB, TPRB

158.s:
Which of the following is the correct chronological order of the WTO Ministerial Conferences and events?
A. Singapore Ministerial Conference
B. Seattle Ministerial Conference
C. Cancún Ministerial Conference
D. MC12 at Geneva
E. MC13 at Abu Dhabi
158.x: The sequence is Singapore in 1996, Seattle in 1999, Cancún in 2003, Geneva in 2022 and Abu Dhabi in 2024.
158.tq: Fix the first and last events, then place the intermediate conferences by year.
158.sec: Structure - Ministerial Conference, General Council, DSB, TPRB

158.s: Which one of the following combinations is correctly matched?
158.x: The first WTO Ministerial Conference was held at Singapore in 1996. Seattle was in 1999, Cancún in 2003 and MC12 was held at Geneva in 2022.
158.tq: Use date-location discrimination among closely related Ministerial Conferences.
158.sec: Structure - Ministerial Conference, General Council, DSB, TPRB

158.s: Which WTO Ministerial Conferences are specifically associated with a breakdown of negotiations?
158.x: The Seattle Ministerial Conference of 1999 and the Cancún Ministerial Conference of 2003 broke down.
158.tq: Separate failed negotiating conferences from conferences identified mainly by their locations or dates.
158.sec: Structure - Ministerial Conference, General Council, DSB, TPRB

158.s: The Council for Trade in Goods oversees which agreement, and which committees are associated with it?
o: GATS; banking, insurance and tourism committees
GATT; agriculture, market access, TBT and SPS committees
TRIPS; patents, copyright and trademarks committees
TRIMS; investment, taxation and exchange-control committees
158.x: The Council for Trade in Goods oversees GATT and includes committees dealing with agriculture, market access, TBT and SPS.
158.tq: Link the council to its principal agreement and its listed committees.
158.sec: Structure - Ministerial Conference, General Council, DSB, TPRB

158.s:
Match the following WTO agreements with their principal subjects:

A. AoA
B. SPS
C. TBT
D. GATS

1. Trade in services
2. Food safety and animal and plant health
3. Agricultural market access, domestic support and export subsidies
4. Technical regulations and standards

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
158.x: AoA concerns agriculture; SPS concerns food, animal and plant health; TBT concerns technical regulations and standards; and GATS concerns services.
158.tq: Start with the distinctive subject of each agreement and eliminate crossed codes.
158.sec: Agreements → subject

158.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Anti-dumping — Duties on goods sold below normal value
TRIPS — Minimum standards for all forms of intellectual property rights
TRIMS — Investment measures that distort trade
GATS — Subsidies that are prohibited, actionable and non-actionable
158.x: GATS deals with trade in services. The classification of subsidies as prohibited, actionable and non-actionable belongs to the SCM Agreement.
158.tq: Detect the agreement-subject swap among neighbouring WTO agreements.
158.sec: Agreements → subject

158.s: Under the SCM Agreement, which of the following categories of subsidies are recognised?
158.x: The SCM Agreement identifies prohibited, actionable or countervailable, and non-actionable subsidies, including certain R&D, regional and environmental subsidies.
158.tq: Distinguish the SCM subsidy classification from the agricultural box classification.
158.sec: Agreements → subject

158.s: In India, which body handles anti-dumping, countervailing and safeguard investigations under WTO rules?
158.x: The Directorate General of Trade Remedies handles anti-dumping, countervailing and safeguard investigations in India.
158.tq: Ask which domestic authority performs the specified trade-remedy function.
158.sec: Agreements → subject

158.s: Which two agreements are identified as the only new WTO agreements concluded in the first 30 years of the organisation?
o: Trade Facilitation Agreement and Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies
158.x: The Trade Facilitation Agreement and the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies are identified as the only new WTO agreements in that period.
158.tq: Use the word “only” carefully to identify the complete pair rather than older Uruguay Round agreements.
158.sec: Agreements → subject

158.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched with the WTO’s agricultural support boxes?

1. Green Box — support regarded as non-trade-distorting and having no limit
2. Blue Box — direct payments that limit production
3. Amber Box — measures such as output-linked MSP and input subsidies subject to reduction commitments
158.x: All three statements are correct. Green Box support has no reduction limit, Blue Box payments are linked to production-limiting conditions, and Amber Box measures are subject to reduction commitments.
158.tq: Separate the three agricultural boxes by both content and regulatory treatment.
158.sec: Agreement on Agriculture - boxes, de minimis, Peace Clause, PSH

158.s: Which one of the following is an example of Green Box support under the Agreement on Agriculture?
o: Minimum Support Price linked to production
Input subsidy on fertiliser tied to output
158.x: Research and disease control are Green Box measures, along with infrastructure, food security and decoupled income support.
158.tq: Classify the policy by checking whether it is decoupled and non-trade-distorting.
158.sec: Agreement on Agriculture - boxes, de minimis, Peace Clause, PSH

158.s: Which of the following is included in the Amber Box under the Agreement on Agriculture?
o: Input subsidies for power, fertiliser, seeds and irrigation tied to output
158.x: Amber Box measures include MSP and output-linked input subsidies such as power, fertiliser, seeds and irrigation, and are subject to reduction commitments.
158.tq: Identify the output-linked support rather than exempt Green Box measures.
158.sec: Agreement on Agriculture - boxes, de minimis, Peace Clause, PSH

158.s: The de minimis limit for agricultural domestic support is what percentage of production value for developed and developing countries, respectively?
158.x: The de minimis limit is 5% of production value for developed countries and 10% for developing countries.
158.tq: Read the paired percentages in the correct developed-country/developing-country order.
158.sec: Agreement on Agriculture - boxes, de minimis, Peace Clause, PSH

158.s: The Peace Clause adopted at Bali in 2013 provides protection to developing countries from disputes concerning:
o: Trade in banking and insurance services
158.x: The Bali Peace Clause shields developing-country public stockholding programmes from disputes until a permanent solution is found.
158.tq: Link the clause to its conference, year and specific agricultural issue.
158.sec: Agreement on Agriculture - boxes, de minimis, Peace Clause, PSH

158.s: Which country first invoked the WTO Peace Clause for rice in 2020?
158.x: India was the first country to invoke the Peace Clause for rice in 2020.
158.tq: Distinguish the invoking country from countries associated with India’s sugar dispute.
158.sec: Agreement on Agriculture - boxes, de minimis, Peace Clause, PSH

158.s:
Consider the following statements regarding public stockholding at MC14 in 2026:
1. No permanent solution was reached on public stockholding.
2. India and the African Group sought a permanent shield for programmes such as the NFSA.
3. The issue was declared permanently settled at MC14.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
158.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. MC14 did not produce a permanent solution; India and the African Group continued to seek a permanent shield for programmes such as the NFSA.
158.tq: Reject the extreme finality of “permanently settled” when the issue remains unresolved.
158.sec: Agreement on Agriculture - boxes, de minimis, Peace Clause, PSH

158.s: India amended the Patents Act in 2005 primarily to comply with:
158.x: India amended the Patents Act in 2005 to bring its patent regime into compliance with TRIPS minimum intellectual-property standards.
158.tq: Match the domestic legislative change with the relevant WTO agreement.
158.sec: TRIPS - compulsory licensing, Doha Declaration, COVID waiver, GI

158.s: The Doha Declaration on TRIPS and public health affirmed that TRIPS:
o: Prevents members from regulating medicines in public interest
Must not stop members from protecting public health
Eliminates compulsory licensing by developing countries
158.x: The Doha Declaration of 2001 affirmed that TRIPS must not prevent members from taking measures to protect public health.
158.tq: Test the public-health flexibility principle against restrictive distractors.
158.sec: TRIPS - compulsory licensing, Doha Declaration, COVID waiver, GI

158.s: Which provision and mechanism were used by India to address public-health concerns under the TRIPS framework?
158.x: India used Section 3(d) of the Patents Act against evergreening and compulsory licensing as TRIPS flexibilities.
158.tq: Identify the domestic legal tools associated with the international flexibility.
158.sec: TRIPS - compulsory licensing, Doha Declaration, COVID waiver, GI

158.s: India’s first compulsory licence was granted in 2012 in the Natco-Bayer case. It concerned:
158.x: India’s first compulsory licence was the Natco-Bayer case in 2012 and concerned a pharmaceutical patent.
158.tq: Use the parties and year to identify the subject of the compulsory licence.
158.sec: TRIPS - compulsory licensing, Doha Declaration, COVID waiver, GI

20% of global GDP, 11% of trade and half of population

Exactly 46% of global trade and one-third of the world's population

Outcomes are automatically binding on all states.
A single state can block an agreed outcome.
Only nuclear-weapon states can block outcomes.
